examples.dm: Those who wish to overcome the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Those who wish to dispel the miseries of sentient beings, And those who wish to enjoy hundreds of manifold happinesses, Should never forsake the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Those who wish to destroy the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Who wish to dispel the unhappiness of sentient beings, And who wish to experience hundreds of great joys, Should never give up the mind of awakening.
examples.sa: भवदुःखशतानि तर्तुकामै-रपि सत्त्वव्यसनानि हर्तुकामैः। बहुसौख्यशतानि भोक्तुकामै-र्न विमोच्यं हि सदैव बोधिचित्तम्॥

examples.dm: The cause of joy for all wandering beings, The medicine for the suffering of sentient beings— How could the merit of such a precious mind Ever be measured?
examples.gm: The cause of joy for all transmigrating beings, The medicine for the suffering of sentient beings— The merit of that jewel-like mind, How could it ever be measured?
examples.sa: जगदानन्दबीजस्य जगद्दुःखौषधस्य च। चित्तरत्नस्य यत्पुण्यं तत्कथं हि प्रमीयताम्॥

examples.dm: If, while I have the fortune to practice virtue, I do not perform virtuous deeds, Then what shall I be able to do when I am completely bewildered By the sufferings of the lower realms?
examples.gm: Even when having the fortune to practice virtue, If I do not practice virtue, Completely bewildered by the suffering of the lower realms, At that time, what will I be able to do?
examples.sa: यदा कुशलयोग्योऽपि कुशलं न करोम्यहम्। अपायदुःखैः संमूढः किं करिष्याम्यहं तदा॥

examples.dm: Those who wish to overcome the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Those who wish to dispel the miseries of sentient beings, And those who wish to enjoy hundreds of manifold happinesses, Should never forsake the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Those who wish to destroy the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Who wish to dispel the unhappiness of sentient beings, And who wish to experience hundreds of great joys, Should never give up the mind of awakening.
examples.sa: भवदुःखशतानि तर्तुकामै-रपि सत्त्वव्यसनानि हर्तुकामैः। बहुसौख्यशतानि भोक्तुकामै-र्न विमोच्यं हि सदैव बोधिचित्तम्॥

examples.dm: From the moment one has correctly adopted that mind With an irreversible resolve In order to thoroughly liberate The infinite realms of sentient beings,
examples.gm: From the moment that, In order to completely free the infinite realms of beings, With a mind that does not turn back, One perfectly takes up that mind,
examples.sa: यतः प्रभृत्यपर्यन्तसत्त्वधातुप्रमोक्षणे। समाददाति तच्चित्तमनिवर्त्येन चेतसा॥

examples.dm: This is reasonable, and as it was Requested by Subāhu, For the sake of beings with lesser aspirations, The Tathāgata himself has spoken.
examples.gm: Along with the reasoning for this, In the Questions of Subāhu, For the sake of beings of lesser inclination, It was taught by the Tathāgata himself.
examples.sa: इदं सुबाहुपृच्छायां सोपपत्तिकमुक्तवान्। हीनाधिमुक्तिसत्त्वार्थं स्वयमेव तथागतः॥

examples.dm: If my body were to be burned for a long time By the unbearable fires of hell, There is no doubt that my mind would be tormented By the blazing fire of unbearable remorse.
examples.gm: If the unbearable fire of hell for a long time Burns my body, Due to the blazing fire of unbearable regret, My mind will doubtless be tormented.
examples.sa: चिरं धक्ष्यति मे कायं नारकाग्निः सुदुःसहः। पश्चात्तापानलश्चित्तं चिरं धक्ष्यत्यशिक्षितम्॥

examples.dm: To those who wish to guard their minds, I join my palms in prayer and say: "With all your effort, guard both mindfulness and introspective awareness!"
examples.gm: To those who wish to guard their minds, Mindfulness and introspection, Guard them both with all your effort! Thus I join my palms in prayer.
examples.sa: चित्तं रक्षितुकामानां मयैष क्रियतेऽञ्जलिः। स्मृतिं च संप्रजन्यं च सर्वयत्नेन रक्षत॥

examples.dm: For those whose minds lack introspective awareness, Even what has been heard, reflected upon, and meditated on, Will not remain in their memory, Like water in a leaking jar.
examples.gm: Of one who has a mind without introspection, Even hearing, thinking, and meditating, Like water in a leaky vase, Will not remain in memory.
examples.sa: असंप्रजन्यचित्तस्य श्रुतचिन्तितभावितम्। सच्छिद्रकुम्भजलवन्न स्मृताववतिष्ठते॥

examples.dm: Whatever harm I have done to the Three Jewels, To my parents, or to my teachers and others, Through the gateway of the afflictions By means of my body, speech, and mind,
examples.gm: To the Three Jewels, To parents, gurus, or others, Through afflictions, with body, speech, And mind, whatever harm I have done,
examples.sa: रत्नत्रयेऽपकारो यो मातपितृषु वा मया। गुरुष्वन्येषु वा क्षेपात् कायवाग्बुद्धिभिः कृतः॥

examples.dm: This powerful enemy, the mental afflictions, Can in a single instant cast me Into that fire which, upon meeting even Mount Meru, Would not leave even its ashes behind.
examples.gm: This powerful enemy of the afflictions, Upon meeting which, even Mount Meru Does not remain even as ashes, Casts me there in a single moment.
examples.sa: मेरोरपि यदासङ्गान्न भस्माप्युपलभ्यते। क्षणात् क्षिपन्ति मां तत्र बलिनः क्लेशशत्रवः॥

examples.dm: If those who wish to forcefully defeat in battle their enemies, Who are already miserable by nature and destined for death, Can disregard the pain of being struck by arrows and spears, And refuse to turn back until their goal is achieved,
examples.gm: Those afflicted ones who suffer and naturally die, When arrayed in battle, even those intensely desiring to forcefully destroy them, Having ignored the suffering of being struck by arrows, spears, and weapons, If they do not turn back and flee without accomplishing the goal,
examples.sa: प्रकृतिमरणदुःखितान्धकारान्। रणशिरसि प्रसभं निहन्तुमुग्राः। अगणितशरशक्तिघातदुःखा न विमुखतामुपयान्त्यसाधयित्वा॥

examples.dm: Since the sole Guide of beings, through his immeasurable intellect, Has thoroughly examined it and seen its great value, Those who wish to escape the realms of cyclic existence Should firmly grasp this precious awakening mind.
examples.gm: Since the sole captain of beings, with limitless intellect, Has thoroughly examined it and found it to be highly precious, Those who wish to be separated from the states of wandering Should perfectly and firmly hold the precious mind of awakening.
examples.sa: सुपरीक्षितमप्रमेयधीभि-र्बहुमूल्यं जगदेकसार्थवाहैः। गतिपत्तनविप्रवासशीलाःसुदृढं गृह्णत बोधिचित्तरत्नम्॥

examples.dm: The cause of joy for all wandering beings, The medicine for the suffering of sentient beings— How could the merit of such a precious mind Ever be measured?
examples.gm: The cause of joy for all transmigrating beings, The medicine for the suffering of sentient beings— The merit of that jewel-like mind, How could it ever be measured?
examples.sa: जगदानन्दबीजस्य जगद्दुःखौषधस्य च। चित्तरत्नस्य यत्पुण्यं तत्कथं हि प्रमीयताम्॥

examples.dm: For as long as there are beings who are ill, Until their diseases are cured, May I become their medicine, their physician, And their nurse.
examples.gm: As long as wanderers are sick, Until they are cured of illness, The medicine and the doctor themselves, and Their nurse, may I become.
examples.sa: ग्लानानामस्मि भैषज्यं भवेयं वैद्य एव च। तदुपस्थायकश्चैव यावद्रोगापुनर्भवः॥

examples.dm: My body, and likewise my possessions, And all my virtues of the three times, I shall give away without a sense of loss, To accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: My body and likewise my wealth, and All virtues of the three times, In order to accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings, I shall give away without regret.
examples.sa: आत्मभावांस्तथा भोगान् सर्वत्र्यध्वगतं शुभम्। निरपेक्षस्त्यजाम्येष सर्वसत्त्वार्थसिद्धये॥

examples.dm: If you still have doubts about such impurity, Even though it is plainly evident, Then observe other impure bodies Abandoned in the charnel grounds.
examples.gm: If such filth as this Is obvious, yet you doubt it, The bodies discarded in the charnel grounds, Look at that other filth as well.
examples.sa: यदि प्रत्यक्षमप्येतदमेध्यं नाधिमुच्यसे। श्मशाने पतितान् घोरान् कायान् पश्यापरानपि॥

examples.dm: If you do not wish to touch a patch of ground Because it is soiled with filth, How can you wish to touch the body From which that very filth arose?
examples.gm: A place smeared with filth, If you do not wish to touch, From which that filth arose, How can you wish to touch the body?
examples.sa: मृदाद्यमेध्यलिप्तत्वाद्यदि न स्प्रष्टुमिच्छसि। यतस्तन्निर्गतं कायात्तं स्प्रष्टुं कथमिच्छसि॥

examples.dm: Just as a flash of lightning in the darkness of a cloud-shrouded night Momentarily reveals everything in its brilliant light, So too, through the power of the Buddha, A virtuous mind occasionally and briefly arises in the world.
examples.gm: Just as on a dark night in the womb of clouds A flash of lightning brilliantly illuminates for an instant, In the same way, by the power of the Buddha, occasionally Worldly intelligence for merit arises for a moment.
examples.sa: रात्रौ यथा मेघघनान्धकारे विद्युत् क्षणं दर्शयति प्रकाशम्। बुद्धानुभावेन तथा कदाचि-ल्लोकस्य पुण्येषु मतिः क्षणं स्यात्॥

examples.dm: Although great fruits arise from the aspiring mind While wandering in cyclic existence, It does not produce a continuous flow of merit In the way that the engaging mind does.
examples.gm: From the mind aspiring to awakening, Great fruits arise while in cyclic existence, but Unlike the mind entering awakening, A continuous stream of merit does not arise.
examples.sa: बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तस्य संसारेऽपि फलं महत्। न त्वविच्छिन्नपुण्यत्वं यथा प्रस्थानचेतसः॥

examples.dm: The thieves of non-introspective awareness, Following upon the decline of mindfulness, Steal even the merits one has carefully accumulated, Leading one to the lower realms as if plundered by robbers.
examples.gm: The thieves of lacking introspection, Following upon the decline of mindfulness, Even when merits are accumulated, Robbed by thieves, one goes to the lower realms.
examples.sa: असंप्रजन्यचौरेण स्मृतिमोषानुसारिणा। उपचित्यापि पुण्यानि मुषिता यान्ति दुर्गतिम्॥

examples.dm: Homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: Homage to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas.

examples.dm: Just as a flash of lightning in the darkness of a cloud-shrouded night Momentarily reveals everything in its brilliant light, So too, through the power of the Buddha, A virtuous mind occasionally and briefly arises in the world.
examples.gm: Just as on a dark night in the womb of clouds A flash of lightning brilliantly illuminates for an instant, In the same way, by the power of the Buddha, occasionally Worldly intelligence for merit arises for a moment.
examples.sa: रात्रौ यथा मेघघनान्धकारे विद्युत् क्षणं दर्शयति प्रकाशम्। बुद्धानुभावेन तथा कदाचि-ल्लोकस्य पुण्येषु मतिः क्षणं स्यात्॥

examples.dm: By reflecting in this way, one should maintain A sense of shame, respect, and likewise fear. Consequently, the recollection of the Buddha Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.gm: Thinking like this, with shame, Respect, and fear, one should dwell. Thus, the recollection of the Buddhas, Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.sa: इति ध्यात्वा तथा तिष्ठेत् त्रपादरभयान्वितः। बुद्धानुस्मृतिरप्येवं भवेत्तस्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥

examples.dm: Then what need is there to mention the desire To dispel the infinite suffering of every single sentient being, And the desire to bring each one To immeasurable excellence?
examples.gm: The discomforts of each and every sentient being, Immeasurable as they are, one wishes to dispel; And for each, immeasurable good qualities One wishes to accomplish—what need is there to mention?
examples.sa: किमुताप्रतिमं शूलमेकैकस्य जिहीर्षतः। अप्रमेयगुणं सत्त्वमेकैकं च चिकीर्षतः॥

examples.dm: In order to fully embrace that precious mind, I make excellent offerings to the Tathāgatas, To the stainless Jewel of the sublime Dharma, And to the Sons of the Buddha, those oceans of virtue.
examples.gm: In order to take hold of that precious mind, To the Tathāgatas and the holy Dharma, The stainless Jewel, and the Children of the Buddhas, Who are oceans of qualities, I make excellent offerings.
examples.sa: तच्चित्तरत्नग्रहणाय सम्यक् पूजां करोम्येष तथागतानाम्। सद्धर्मरत्नस्य च निर्मलस्य बुद्धात्मजानां च गुणोदधीनाम्॥

examples.dm: To those who are oceans of excellence, I offer praise with oceans of melodic branches. May those clouds of melodious songs of praise Certainly arise in every way.
examples.gm: To those who are oceans of qualities, I Offer praise with oceans of limbs of melodious praise. May sweet clouds of songs of praise Certainly arise everywhere for them.
examples.sa: स्वराङ्गसागरैः स्तोत्रैः स्तौमि चाहं गुणोदधीन्। स्तुतिसंगीतिमेघाश्च संभवन्त्वेष्वनन्यथा॥

examples.dm: Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas
examples.gm: Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas

examples.dm: In the language of Tibet: *Byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa* (Engaging in the Bodhisattva Deeds).
examples.gm: In the Tibetan language: Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva.

examples.dm: Just as the Sugatas of former times Generated the mind of enlightenment, And in the Bodhisattva trainings Abided and trained in successive order,
examples.gm: Just as the previous Sugatas Generated the awakening mind, And in the trainings of the bodhisattvas, Just as they progressively abided,
examples.sa: यथा गृहीतं सुगतैर्बोधिचित्तं पुरातनैः। ते बोधिसत्त्वशिक्षायामानुपूर्व्या यथा स्थिताः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, virtue is always extremely weak, While sin is of great strength and utterly unbearable. Except for the mind of perfect enlightenment, What other virtue could ever overcome it?
examples.gm: Thus virtue is perpetually feeble, While evil is extremely powerful and unbearable; If it were not for the mind of perfect awakening, What other virtue could overcome it?
examples.sa: तस्माच्छुभं दुर्बलमेव नित्यं बलं तु पापस्य महत्सुघोरम्। तज्जीयतेऽन्येन शुभेन केन संबोधिचित्तं यदि नाम न स्यात्॥

examples.dm: Even if one has committed extremely unbearable sins, Just as one relies on a hero to escape great terror, Why would those who are conscientious not rely upon That which swiftly liberates them?
examples.gm: Even if one has committed extremely unbearable evils, Just as one relies on a hero when in great fear, By relying on it, one is liberated in an instant; Why do conscientious beings not rely upon it?
examples.sa: कृत्वापि पापानि सुदारुणानियदाश्रयादुत्तरति क्षणेन। शूराश्रयेणेव महाभयानि नाश्रीयते तत्कथमज्ञसत्त्वैः॥

examples.dm: However, if one develops a deeply devoted mind, Its fruit will increase even more than that; Even when great difficulties arise for the Bodhisattvas, No sin occurs, and their virtue naturally increases.
examples.gm: But if anyone gives rise to a mind of deep faith, Its fruit increases even more than that. Even in great adversity for the Children of the Conquerors, Non-virtue does not arise, and virtue naturally increases.
examples.sa: अथ यस्य मनः प्रसादमेति प्रसवेत्तस्य ततःऽधिकं फलम्। महता हि बलेन पापकं जिनपुत्रेषु शुभं त्वयत्नतः॥

examples.dm: The Benefits of Bodhicitta
examples.gm: Chapter One: Explaining the Benefits of Bodhicitta

examples.dm: Therefore, virtue is always extremely weak, While sin is of great strength and utterly unbearable. Except for the mind of perfect enlightenment, What other virtue could ever overcome it?
examples.gm: Thus virtue is perpetually feeble, While evil is extremely powerful and unbearable; If it were not for the mind of perfect awakening, What other virtue could overcome it?
examples.sa: तस्माच्छुभं दुर्बलमेव नित्यं बलं तु पापस्य महत्सुघोरम्। तज्जीयतेऽन्येन शुभेन केन संबोधिचित्तं यदि नाम न स्यात्॥

examples.dm: Those who wish to overcome the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Those who wish to dispel the miseries of sentient beings, And those who wish to enjoy hundreds of manifold happinesses, Should never forsake the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Those who wish to destroy the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Who wish to dispel the unhappiness of sentient beings, And who wish to experience hundreds of great joys, Should never give up the mind of awakening.
examples.sa: भवदुःखशतानि तर्तुकामै-रपि सत्त्वव्यसनानि हर्तुकामैः। बहुसौख्यशतानि भोक्तुकामै-र्न विमोच्यं हि सदैव बोधिचित्तम्॥

examples.dm: Just as a flash of lightning in the darkness of a cloud-shrouded night Momentarily reveals everything in its brilliant light, So too, through the power of the Buddha, A virtuous mind occasionally and briefly arises in the world.
examples.gm: Just as on a dark night in the womb of clouds A flash of lightning brilliantly illuminates for an instant, In the same way, by the power of the Buddha, occasionally Worldly intelligence for merit arises for a moment.
examples.sa: रात्रौ यथा मेघघनान्धकारे विद्युत् क्षणं दर्शयति प्रकाशम्। बुद्धानुभावेन तथा कदाचि-ल्लोकस्य पुण्येषु मतिः क्षणं स्यात्॥

examples.dm: Once the awakening mind has been generated, in that very instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Are called children of the Sugatas, And become objects of homage for the world, including its gods and humans.
examples.gm: If the mind of awakening is generated, in an instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Will be called children of the Sugatas, And will become worthy of reverence by the world's gods and humans.
examples.sa: भवचारकबन्धनो वराकः सुगतानां सुत उच्यते क्षणेन। सनरामरलोकवन्दनीयो भवति स्मोदित एव बोधिचित्ते॥

examples.dm: In vehicles, on beds, or in dwellings, Do not remain alone with another's wife. Having observed and inquired, Avoid everything that causes the world to lose faith.
examples.gm: In vehicles, beds, and seats, One should not be alone with another's woman. Everything that causes the world to lose faith, Having observed and inquired, one should abandon.
examples.sa: नैकयान्यस्त्रिया कुर्याद्यानं शयनमासनम्। लोकाप्रसादकं सर्वं दृष्ट्वा पृष्ट्वा च वर्जयेत्॥

examples.dm: Through this, the power of my faith to cultivate virtue may increase for a while; Furthermore, if others of equal fortune to myself should see this, It may prove meaningful for them as well.
examples.gm: In order to cultivate virtue, the force of my faith Will for a time increase because of this; And if others, equal in fortune to myself, Should see these words, they may be meaningful.
examples.sa: मम तावदनेन याति वृद्धिं कुशलं भावयितुं प्रसादवेगः। अथ मत्समधातुरेव पश्ये-दपरोऽप्येनमतोऽपि सार्थकोऽयम्॥

examples.dm: All other virtues are like the plantain tree; Once they have produced their fruit, they are exhausted. But the tree of the awakening mind perpetually bears fruit, And rather than being exhausted, it increases ever more.
examples.gm: All other virtues are just like the plantain tree: Having borne their fruit, they are exhausted; But the tree of the mind of awakening constantly Bears fruit, is not exhausted, and continually grows.
examples.sa: कदलीव फलं विहाय याति क्षयमन्यत् कुशलं हि सर्वमेव। सततं फलति क्षयं न याति प्रसवत्येव तु बोधिचित्तवृक्षः॥

examples.dm: If I have not performed virtuous deeds, And have instead thoroughly accumulated sins, Then for even a hundred million eons, I shall not even hear the sound of a happy rebirth.
examples.gm: Having not practiced virtues, And having accumulated sins, For even a hundred million eons, Even the sound of the happy realms will not be heard.
examples.sa: अकुर्वतश्च कुशलं पापं चाप्युपचिन्वतः। हतः सुगतिशब्दोऽपि कल्पकोटिशतैरपि॥

examples.dm: Although they have the desire to cast off suffering, They rush headlong into suffering itself. Although they desire happiness, through delusion They destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy.
examples.gm: Although having the wish to abandon suffering, They run directly toward suffering itself. Although desiring happiness, out of ignorance, They destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy.
examples.sa: दुःखमेवाभिधावन्ति दुःखनिःसरणाशया। सुखेच्छयैव संमोहात् स्वसुखं घ्नन्ति शत्रुवत्॥

examples.dm: What need is there to mention one who constantly bestows Upon an infinite number of sentient beings for an endless duration The unsurpassed bliss of the Sugatas, Which fulfills every heartfelt aspiration?
examples.gm: To limitless numbers of sentient beings for a long time, The unsurpassable bliss of the Sugatas, Which fulfills all the wishes in their minds, What need is there to mention constantly giving?
examples.sa: किमु निरवधिसत्त्वसंख्यया निरवधिकालमनुप्रयच्छतः। गगनजनपरिक्षयाक्षयं सकलमनोरथसंप्रपूरणम्॥

examples.dm: "I am the one who does the work, While this one remains in a state of ease. This one is renowned as great in the world, While I am known as lowly and without merit."
examples.gm: I do all the work, and This one abides in happiness itself. This one is great in the world, and I am known as inferior and without good qualities.
examples.sa: अहं करोमि कर्माणि तिष्ठत्येष तु सुस्थितः। अयं किल महांल्लोके नीचोऽहं किल निर्गुणः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, mindfulness should never be allowed To stray from the gateway of the mind. If it should stray, one should bring it back By recollecting the sufferings of the lower realms.
examples.gm: Therefore, mindfulness from the door of the mind, Should never be let go. Even if it departs, recalling the harms of the lower realms, It should be closely maintained.
examples.sa: तस्मात्स्मृतिर्मनोद्वारान्नापनेया कदाचन। गतापि प्रत्युपस्थाप्या संसंमृत्त्यापायिकीं व्यथाम्॥

examples.dm: Having thus examined the mind for afflictions And for strivings toward meaningless things, At that time, the heroic one should firmly Restrain it by means of the antidote.
examples.gm: Thus, completely afflicted, Having examined the mind striving for meaningless things, At that time, the hero, by means of an antidote, Should hold it firmly.
examples.sa: एवं संक्लिष्टमालोक्य निष्फलारम्भि वा मनः। निगृह्णीयाद् दृढं शूरः प्रतिपक्षेण तत्सदा॥

examples.dm: Just as an illusion is not true, So too is the mind that sees it; If cyclic existence were based on a real entity, It would otherwise be like empty space.
examples.gm: Just as an illusion, although not true, Is an object of sight, so is the perceiving mind. "If saṃsāra has a real basis, it functions; Otherwise, it would be like space."
examples.sa: असत्यपि यथा माया दृश्या द्रष्टृ तथा मनः । वस्त्वाश्रयश्चेत्संसारः सोऽन्यथाकाशवद्भवेत्॥

examples.dm: Once the awakening mind has been generated, in that very instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Are called children of the Sugatas, And become objects of homage for the world, including its gods and humans.
examples.gm: If the mind of awakening is generated, in an instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Will be called children of the Sugatas, And will become worthy of reverence by the world's gods and humans.
examples.sa: भवचारकबन्धनो वराकः सुगतानां सुत उच्यते क्षणेन। सनरामरलोकवन्दनीयो भवति स्मोदित एव बोधिचित्ते॥

examples.dm: To the Dharma realized within their hearts, Which dispels the terrors of cyclic existence, And likewise to the assembly of Bodhisattvas, I also go for refuge perfectly.
examples.gm: In the Dharma that they have realized, Which clears away the fears of saṃsāra, And in the assembly of Bodhisattvas, Likewise, I perfectly take refuge.
examples.sa: तैश्चाप्यधिगतं धर्मं संसारभयनाशनम्। शरणं यामि भावेन बोधिसत्त्वगणं तथा॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: The Sage has declared that whoever gives rise to a malicious thought Toward such a benefactor, a Son of the Conquerors, Will remain in hell for as many aeons As the number of malicious thoughts produced.
examples.gm: If anyone toward such a benefactor, a Child of the Conquerors, Generates an evil thought, that one For eons equal to the number of evil thoughts generated Will abide in hell, so the Capable One has taught.
examples.sa: इति सत्त्रपतौ जिनस्य पुत्रे कलुषं स्वे हृदये करोति यश्च। कलुषोदयसंख्यया स कल्पान् नरकेष्वावसतीति नाथ आह॥

examples.dm: Having somehow, by good fortune, found this state of benefit That is so extremely difficult to obtain, If I am led back to those same hells Even while possessing conscious awareness,
examples.gm: The state of benefit that is extremely difficult to find, Having found it by some chance, While I myself am possessed of understanding, If I am led back again into that hell,
examples.sa: कथंचिदपि संप्राप्तो हितभूमिं सुदुर्लभाम्। जानन्नपि च नीयेऽहं तानेव नरकान् पुनः॥

examples.dm: In all the world systems, However many hells there may be, May the embodied beings within them Rejoice in the happiness of Sukhavati.
examples.gm: In the realms of the world, the hells, However many there are, In them, may embodied beings Rejoice with the happiness of Sukhāvatī.
examples.sa: यावन्तो नरकाः केचिद्विद्यन्ते लोकधातुषु। सुखावतीसुखामोद्यैर्मोदन्तां तेषु देहिनः॥

examples.dm: To all the Buddhas of the three times, And to the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With as many bodies as there are atoms in the realms, I bow down and pay homage.
examples.gm: To all the Buddhas who have gone in the three times, Along with the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With bodies as numerous as all the atoms in the fields, Bowing down, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वक्षेत्राणुसंख्यैश्च प्रणामैः प्रणमाम्यहम्। सर्वत्र्यध्वगतान् बुद्धान् सहधर्मगणोत्तमान्॥

examples.dm: Do not teach the profound and vast to those of lesser inclination, Nor to a woman without a man present. Toward both the lesser and the supreme teachings, One should always act with equal respect.
examples.gm: Nor the profound and vast to the inferior, Nor to a woman without a man present. To the inferior and supreme Dharmas, One should apply equal respect in all cases.
examples.sa: गम्भीरोदारमल्पेषु न स्त्रीषु पुरुषं विना। हीनोत्कृष्टेषु धर्मेषु समं गौरवमाचरेत्॥

examples.dm: If, however, it exists after the object of knowledge, Then from what would consciousness arise? In this way, the arising of all phenomena Cannot be understood.
examples.gm: Or if it exists after the object of knowledge, Then from what does consciousness arise? In this way, of all phenomena, Arising cannot be realized.
examples.sa: अथ ज्ञेयाद्भवेत् पश्चात् तदा ज्ञानं कुतो भवेत्। एवं च सर्वधर्माणामुत्पत्तिर्नावसीयते॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: Although the conduct of Bodhisattvas Is said to be immeasurable, One should certainly practice those activities That serve to train the mind.
examples.gm: The practices of the Bodhisattvas Are taught to be limitless; The practice of purifying the mind, One should definitely practice at least that much.
examples.sa: आचारो बोधिसत्त्वानामप्रमेय उदाहृतः। चित्तशोधनमाचारं नियतं तावदाचरेत्॥

examples.dm: Three times during the day and three times at night, One should recite the Three Heaps Sūtra; By relying on the Victors and the spirit of awakening, One should pacify the remaining downfalls.
examples.gm: Three times during the day and night, One should recite the Triskandha; By relying on the Conquerors and the awakening mind, One should pacify the remainder of downfalls thereby.
examples.sa: रात्रिंदिवं च त्रिस्कन्धं त्रिष्कालं च प्रवर्तयेत्। शेषापत्तिशमस्तेन बोधिचित्तजिनाश्रयात्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, as long as I have not decisively destroyed this enemy before my very eyes, I shall not abandon my efforts in this regard; For those full of pride, who become enraged even at a minor, temporary harm, Will not sleep until they have defeated that enemy.
examples.gm: Thus, as long as I do not manifestly And certainly destroy this enemy, I will not forsake my effort here. When angered by even a slight temporary harm, Those full of pride do not sleep until they have destroyed it.
examples.sa: तस्मान्न तावदहमत्र धुरं क्षिपामि यावन्न शत्रव इमे निहताः समक्षम्। स्वल्पेऽपि तावदपकारिणि बद्धरोषा मानोन्नतास्तमनिहत्य न यान्ति निद्राम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should aspire to virtue, And cultivate it with genuine respect. Having undertaken the rite of the Vajradhvaja, One should cultivate the pride of self-confidence.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should aspire to the wholesome, And meditate upon it with reverence; According to the method of the Vajradhvaja, Having begun, one should meditate on self-confidence.
examples.sa: तस्मात्कार्यः शुभच्छन्दो भावयित्वैवमादरात्। वज्रध्वजस्थविधिना मानं त्वारभ्य भावयेत्॥

examples.dm: One should apply pride to these three: Actions, afflictions, and ability. Thinking, "I alone shall do it," This is the pride of action.
examples.gm: Actions, afflictions, and capacity: One should generate self-confidence regarding these three. Thinking, "I shall do this alone," This is the self-confidence of action.
examples.sa: त्रिषु मानो विधातव्यः कर्मोपक्लेशशक्तिषु। मयैवैकेन कर्तव्यमित्येषा कर्ममानिता॥

examples.dm: That which is desired as the "Primal Substance" And that which is imputed as the "Self," Do not arise by intentionally thinking, "I shall come into being."
examples.gm: Whatever is asserted as the "Primary Matter," and Whatever is imputed as the "Self"— Thinking, "I myself shall arise," They do not purposefully arise.
examples.sa: यत्प्रधानं किलाभीष्टं यत्तदात्मेति कल्पितम्। तदेव हि भवाभीति न संचिन्त्योपजायते॥

examples.dm: Īśvara is not space, because space is inert; He is not the self, as that has already been refuted. And if the creator is also inconceivable, What is the point of speaking of him as "inconceivable"?
examples.gm: Īśvara is not space, because it is devoid of movement; He is not the self, because it was already refuted before; And as for a creator who is inconceivable, What is the use of speaking of the inconceivable?
examples.sa: नाकाशमीशोऽचेष्टत्वात् नात्मा पूर्वनिषेधतः। अचिन्त्यस्य च कर्तृत्वमप्यचिन्त्यं किमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, what is it that he is asserted to produce? Are not the self, the earth, and so forth, And the nature of Īśvara himself, also eternal? Since consciousness arises from objects of knowledge,
examples.gm: And what is it that he wishes to produce? Are not the self, those such as earth, And the essence of Īśvara permanent? Consciousness arises from the object of knowledge, and
examples.sa: तेन किं स्रष्टुमिष्टं च आत्मा चेत् नन्वसौ ध्रुवः। क्ष्मादिस्वभाव ईशश्च ज्ञानं ज्ञेयादनादि च॥

examples.dm: Since one does not feel anger toward the great sources of suffering Such as bile and the like, Why be angry with sentient beings? They too are all impelled by conditions.
examples.gm: Towards bile and so forth, which are Great sources of suffering, without being angry, Why be angry at those with minds? They too are all incited by conditions.
examples.sa: पित्तादिषु न मे कोपो महादुःखकरेष्वपि। सचेतनेषु किं कोपः तेऽपि प्रत्ययकोपिताः॥

examples.dm: Nowhere is there any single condition That has the power to produce everything. If ultimate reality is nirvana And cyclic existence is the conventional, then
examples.gm: That a single condition has the capacity for everything Nowhere exists. "If the ultimate is nirvāṇa, And saṃsāra is the relative, in that case,
examples.sa: नैकस्य सर्वसामर्थ्यं प्रत्ययस्यास्ति कुत्रचित्। निर्वृतः परमार्थेन संवृत्या यदि संसरेत्॥

examples.dm: Craving is conditioned by feeling, and they also possess those feelings. A mind that possesses an object of observation will remain fixed upon something.
examples.gm: Craving occurs due to the condition of feeling; Those ones also have feelings. A mind that is endowed with apprehension Will rest upon something.
examples.sa: वेदनाप्रत्यया तृष्णा वेदनैषां च विद्यते। सालम्बनेन चित्तेन स्थातव्यं यत्र तत्र वा॥

examples.dm: All other virtues are like the plantain tree; Once they have produced their fruit, they are exhausted. But the tree of the awakening mind perpetually bears fruit, And rather than being exhausted, it increases ever more.
examples.gm: All other virtues are just like the plantain tree: Having borne their fruit, they are exhausted; But the tree of the mind of awakening constantly Bears fruit, is not exhausted, and continually grows.
examples.sa: कदलीव फलं विहाय याति क्षयमन्यत् कुशलं हि सर्वमेव। सततं फलति क्षयं न याति प्रसवत्येव तु बोधिचित्तवृक्षः॥

examples.dm: Although great fruits arise from the aspiring mind While wandering in cyclic existence, It does not produce a continuous flow of merit In the way that the engaging mind does.
examples.gm: From the mind aspiring to awakening, Great fruits arise while in cyclic existence, but Unlike the mind entering awakening, A continuous stream of merit does not arise.
examples.sa: बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तस्य संसारेऽपि फलं महत्। न त्वविच्छिन्नपुण्यत्वं यथा प्रस्थानचेतसः॥

examples.dm: Just as the result of generating a single clear mind Is birth as a Brahmā or the like, The results of body and speech are not such, Because their conduct is weak.
examples.gm: Whatever result is generated by a single clear mind, Such as Brahmā and so forth, The results of body and speech, Because of weak conduct, are not like that.
examples.sa: सहापि वाक्शरीराभ्यां मन्दवृत्तेर्न तत्फलम्। यत्पटोरेककस्यापि चित्तस्य ब्रह्मतादिकम्॥

examples.dm: From beginningless cyclic existence, In this life or in others, Whatever sins I have committed, Or caused others to commit,
examples.gm: Since beginningless cyclic existence, In this life or in others, Whatever non-virtue I have unwittingly committed, Or caused to be committed,
examples.sa: अनादिमति संसारे जन्मन्यत्रैव वा पुनः। यन्मया पशुना पापं कृतं कारितमेव वा॥

examples.dm: Even in this brief lifetime, Many friends and enemies have passed away; Yet the unbearable sins committed for their sake Remain before me.
examples.gm: Even during this brief life, Many friends and enemies have passed away. But the unbearable non-virtues committed for their sake Remain right before me.
examples.sa: इहैव तिष्ठतस्तावद्गता नैके प्रियाप्रियाः। तन्निमित्तं तु यत्पापं तत्स्थितं घोरमग्रतः॥

examples.dm: I pray that the Guides will regard my sins As the transgressions they are. Since this was not good, Henceforth, I shall never do it again.
examples.gm: I beseech the guides to accept my negative deeds As being faults. Since this is not good, From now on I will not do them.
examples.sa: अत्ययमत्ययत्वेन प्रतिगृह्णन्तु नायकाः। न भद्रकमिदं नाथा न कर्तव्यं पुनर्मया॥

examples.dm: Both his weapon and my body Are the causes of this suffering. Since he has drawn the weapon and I have provided the body, At whom should I be angry?
examples.gm: Their weapons and my body Are both causes of suffering; They produced the weapon and I the body, At which one should I be angry?
examples.sa: तच्छस्त्रं मम कायश्च द्वयं दुःखस्य कारणम्। तेन शस्त्रं मया कायो गृहीतः कुत्र कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: Since that which does not occur in the absence of something, But does occur when that thing is present, Is defined as its cause, How can it be called an obstacle?
examples.gm: If one thing does not arise without another, And comes to be when it is present, Since that very thing is its cause, How can it be called an obstacle?
examples.sa: यो हि येन विना नास्ति यस्मिंश्च सति विद्यते। स एव कारणं तस्य स कथं विघ्न उच्यते॥

examples.dm: If you ask what created the variety of causes, It is from the very variety of preceding causes. Why is a cause able to produce an effect? It is from the very power of the preceding cause.
examples.gm: If one asks, what made the variations of causes? From the variations of prior causes themselves. Why are causes able to produce effects? From the power of prior causes themselves.
examples.sa: किंकृतो हेतुभेदश्चेत् पूर्वहेतुप्रभेदतः। कस्माच्चेत्फलदो हेतुः पूर्वहेतुप्रभावतः॥

examples.dm: Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas
examples.gm: Engaging in the Conduct of the Bodhisattvas

examples.dm: In the language of Tibet: *Byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa* (Engaging in the Bodhisattva Deeds).
examples.gm: In the Tibetan language: Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva.

examples.dm: This is the first chapter, titled "Explaining the Benefits of the Awakening Mind," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, this is the first chapter, called Explaining the Benefits of the Awakening Mind.

examples.dm: If these guards of the prison of cyclic existence, Who become executioners in the hells and elsewhere, Dwell within the net of attachment in my mind, How could I ever find happiness?
examples.gm: The guards of the prison of saṃsāra, These which become the executioners that kill in hell and so forth— If, in the net of attachment residing in the mind, They remain, how can there be happiness for me?
examples.sa: भवचारकपालका इमे नरकादिष्वपि वध्यघातकाः। मतिवेश्मनि लोभपञ्जरे यदि तिष्ठन्ति कुतः सुखं मम॥

examples.dm: Since all is impermanent, who that is impermanent Would feel a true attachment to another? Because of that, for thousands of lifetimes, One will never again see the beloved.
examples.gm: What impermanent being Would be truly attached to the impermanent? Through that, for thousands of lifetimes, They will not see their loved ones.
examples.sa: कस्यानित्येष्वनित्यस्य स्नेहो भवितुमर्हति। येन जन्मसहस्राणि द्रष्टव्यो न पुनः प्रियः॥

examples.dm: Since you are attached to this when it is covered, Why do you not desire it when it is uncovered? If you have no need for it then, Why do you embrace it when it is covered?
examples.gm: If you are attached to it even when covered, Why do you not desire it when uncovered? If you have no need for it uncovered, Why do you embrace it when covered?
examples.sa: यत्र च्छन्नेऽप्ययं रागस्तदच्छन्नं किमप्रियम्। न चेत्प्रयोजनं तेन कस्माच्छन्नं विमृद्यते॥

examples.dm: Likewise, I am unable to turn back All external phenomena; But I shall turn back this mind of mine; What need is there to turn back anything else?
examples.gm: Likewise, external phenomena too, Cannot be turned back by me, But I will turn back this mind of mine; What need is there to turn back others?
examples.sa: बाह्या भावा मया तद्वच्छक्या वारयितुं न हि। स्वचित्तं वारयिष्यामि किं ममान्यैर्निवारितैः॥

examples.dm: In this way, everything is dependent on other factors, And because of those factors, it lacks independence. Knowing this, one will not become angry At any phenomena, which are like magical illusions.
examples.gm: Thus, everything is under the power of others, And that which has power is itself powerless. Having understood this, one will not get angry Towards all things, which are like emanations.
examples.sa: एवं परवशं सर्वं यद्वशं सोऽपि चावशः। निर्माणवदचेष्टेषु भावेष्वेवं क्व कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: If an illusion is not other than the mind, And yet you do not consider it to be the same, If it were a real entity, how could it not be other? If you say it is not other, then it cannot exist as a real entity.
examples.gm: "Illusion is not other than the mind, And if it is not conceived as being not other," If it is a real entity, how is it not other? If it is not other, it does not exist as an entity.
examples.sa: चित्तादन्या न माया चेन्नाप्यनन्येति कल्प्यते। वस्तु चेत्सा कथं नान्यानन्या चेन्नास्ति वस्तुतः॥

examples.dm: Whenever one's mind is affected by attachment Or the desire to be angry, One should not act and should not speak; One should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Whenever one's own mind has attachment, Or the desire to be angry—at that time, One should not act and should not speak; One should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: अनुनीतं प्रतिहतं यदा पश्येत्स्वकं मनः। न कर्तव्यं न वक्तव्यं स्थातव्यं काष्ठवत्तदा॥

examples.dm: Because of that, his friends will become weary of him; Even if gathered through generosity, they will not remain. In short, there is no one at all Who dwells in happiness while possessed by anger.
examples.gm: Because of it, friends become disheartened; Though gathered by generosity, they do not stay. In brief, an angry person who dwells in happiness— There is no such thing at all.
examples.sa: सुहृदोऽप्युद्विजन्तेऽस्माद् ददाति न च सेव्यते। संक्षेपान्नास्ति तत्किंचित् क्रोधनो येन सुस्थितः॥

examples.dm: The enemy of anger produces these And many other such sufferings. Those who strive to conquer anger Will find happiness in this life and the next.
examples.gm: The enemy of anger will create These and other such sufferings. Whoever applies effort and destroys anger, That one is happy in this life and the next.
examples.sa: एवमादीनि दुःखानि करोतीत्यरिसंज्ञया। यः क्रोधं हन्ति निर्बन्धात् स सुखीह परत्र च॥

examples.dm: The worldly perceive things and conceptualize them As being truly real, rather than like an illusion; It is on this point that The yogis and the worldly dispute.
examples.gm: People of the world see entities, And conceptualize them as truly real, Not as being like illusions; therefore, here, Yogis and the world dispute.
examples.sa: लोकेन भावा दृश्यन्ते कल्प्यन्ते चापि तत्त्वतः। न तु मायावदित्यत्र विवादो योगिलोकयोः॥

examples.dm: In killing an illusory person and the like, There is no sin because they lack a mind; But in the case of one who possesses an illusory mind, Merit and sin do arise.
examples.gm: In killing an illusory person and so forth, Because there is no mind, there is no sin; But regarding that which possesses an illusory mind, Merit and sin arise.
examples.sa: मायापुरुषघातादौ चित्ताभावान्न पापकम्। चित्तमायासमेते तु पापपुण्यसमुद्भवः॥

examples.dm: Since even a Buddha would be in cyclic existence, What would be the use of the conduct of enlightenment? As long as the continuity of conditions is not severed, Even an illusion will not cease;
examples.gm: Even a Buddha would cycle in saṃsāra, so What is the point of bodhisattva conduct?" If the continuum of conditions is not severed, Even an illusion is not reversed;
examples.sa: बुद्धोऽपि संसरेदेवं ततः किं बोधिचर्यया। प्रत्ययानामनुच्छेदे मायाप्युच्छिद्यते न हि॥

examples.dm: Once the awakening mind has been generated, in that very instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Are called children of the Sugatas, And become objects of homage for the world, including its gods and humans.
examples.gm: If the mind of awakening is generated, in an instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Will be called children of the Sugatas, And will become worthy of reverence by the world's gods and humans.
examples.sa: भवचारकबन्धनो वराकः सुगतानां सुत उच्यते क्षणेन। सनरामरलोकवन्दनीयो भवति स्मोदित एव बोधिचित्ते॥

examples.dm: Desiring results without exertion, And being thin-skinned, you are beset by many harms; Though seized by death, you act like an immortal; Alas, you are destroyed by your own sufferings!
examples.gm: Desiring the result without exerting effort, Being fragile and experiencing many harms, Yet acting like a god while seized by death— Alas, you will be destroyed by sufferings!
examples.sa: निरुद्यम फलाकाङ्क्षिन् सुकुमार बहुव्यथ। मृत्युग्रस्तोऽमराकार हा दुःखित विहन्यसे॥

examples.dm: Thinking, "If I give this away, what will I have to enjoy?" Is the way of a demon, thinking only of one's own benefit. Thinking, "If I use this myself, what will I have to give?" Is the Dharma of the gods, thinking of the welfare of others.
examples.gm: "If I give, what will I consume?"— Thinking of one's own purpose is the way of a demon. "If I consume, what will I give?"— Thinking of others' purpose is the quality of a deity.
examples.sa: यदि दास्यामि किं भोक्ष्ये इत्यात्मार्थे पिशाचता। यदि भोक्ष्ये किं ददामीति परार्थे देवराजता॥

examples.dm: Suppose one person experiences happiness for a hundred years in a dream and then wakes up, And another experiences happiness for just a brief moment and then wakes up;
examples.gm: Having experienced happiness in a dream for a hundred years, Whoever awakens, And having experienced happiness for just an instant, Whoever awakens—
examples.sa: स्वप्ने वर्षशतं सौख्यं भुक्त्वा यश्च विबुध्यते। मुहूर्तमपरो यश्च सुखी भूत्वा विबुध्यते॥

examples.dm: If you had performed this work in the past, It would be impossible for you to be in this present state, Lacking the perfect bliss of a Buddha.
examples.gm: If in former times You had performed this action, A state other than the perfect happiness of a Buddha, Such a situation as this could not possibly occur.
examples.sa: अभविष्यदिदं कर्म कृतं पूर्वं यदि त्वया। बौद्धं संपत्सुखं मुक्त्वा नाभविष्यदियं दशा॥

examples.dm: If the qualities do not exist, then even the existence Of sound and so forth becomes extremely remote. It is also impossible for pleasure and the like To exist in insentient things such as clothing.
examples.gm: If the qualities do not exist, sound and so forth Would be very far from existing. In insentient objects like cloth and so forth, It is impossible for pleasure and so forth to exist.
examples.sa: गुणाभावे च शब्दादेरस्तित्वमतिदूरतः। अचेतने च वस्त्रादौ सुखादेरप्यसंभवः॥

examples.dm: Like the supreme form of an alchemical elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it into the priceless Jewel of a Victor’s body; therefore, firmly grasp That which is called the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Like the supreme form of the gold-making elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it Into the priceless jewel of a Conqueror's body; Therefore, firmly hold to this so-called mind of awakening.
examples.sa: अशुचिप्रतिमामिमां गृहीत्वा जिनरत्नप्रतिमां करोत्यनर्घाम्। रसजातमतीव वेधनीयं सुदृढं गृह्णत बोधिचित्तसंज्ञम्॥

examples.dm: Just as Mañjughoṣa and the others Have made offerings to the Victors, So too do I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors, and their spiritual heirs.
examples.gm: Just as Mañjuśrī and others Made offerings to the Victorious Ones, Likewise, I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors along with their Children.
examples.sa: मञ्जुघोषप्रभृतयः पूजयन्ति यथा जिनान्। तथा तथागतान्नाथान् सपुत्रान् पूजयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, to the Victors, the protectors of beings, Who strive for the purpose of shielding all wanderers, And who, possessing great power, dispel every fear, From this very day, I go for refuge.
examples.gm: Therefore, in the Victors, the protectors of beings, Who strive for the purpose of protecting beings, The mighty ones who clear away all fear, From today onward, I take refuge.
examples.sa: अद्यैव शरणं यामि जगन्नाथान् महाबलान्। जगद्रक्षार्थमुद्युक्तान् सर्वत्रासहरान् जिनान्॥

examples.dm: Because I did not realize That I am merely a transient guest, Through ignorance, attachment, and hatred, I have committed many kinds of sins.
examples.gm: That my existence is so fleeting, Since I did not realize this, Through ignorance, attachment, and hatred, I have committed many kinds of non-virtue.
examples.sa: एवमागन्तुकोऽस्मीति न मया प्रत्यवेक्षितम्। मोहानुनयविद्वेषैः कृतं पापमनेकधा॥

examples.dm: When speaking, one should speak in a way that is agreeable, coherent, And clear in meaning, and pleasant; Free from attachment and aversion, One should speak gently and in moderation.
examples.gm: When speaking, comforting and coherent, Clear in meaning and pleasing to the mind, Having abandoned attachment and hatred, One should speak gently and in moderation.
examples.sa: विश्वस्तविन्यस्तपदं विस्पष्टार्थं मनोरमम्। श्रुतिसौख्यं कृपामूलं मृदुमन्दस्वरं वदेत्॥

examples.dm: Disregarding all suffering, To conquer the enemies of hatred and the like— These are the victorious heroes; The rest are merely slaying corpses.
examples.gm: Having disregarded all sufferings, Those who conquer enemies such as anger— They are the victorious heroes; The rest slay corpses.
examples.sa: उरसारातिघातान् ये प्रतीच्छन्तो जयन्त्यरीन्। ते ते विजयिनः शूराः शेषास्तु मृतमारकाः॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: If things were accomplished by one's own independent will, Then since no one desires to suffer, Suffering would never arise For any embodied being at all.
examples.gm: If things were accomplished by their own will, Since no one desires suffering, For all embodied beings, Suffering would not occur for anyone.
examples.sa: यदि तु स्वेच्छया सिद्धिः सर्वेषामेव देहिनाम्। न भवेत्कस्यचिद्दुःखं न दुःखं कश्चिदिच्छति॥

examples.dm: Since the mind is not a physical entity, No one can destroy it anywhere; Because of intense attachment to the body, The body is afflicted by sufferings.
examples.gm: Because the mind is bodiless, No one can destroy it anywhere; Because of deep attachment to the body, The body is harmed by sufferings.
examples.sa: मनो हन्तुममूर्तत्वान्न शक्यं केनचित्क्वचित्। शरीराभिनिवेशात्तु चित्तं दुःखेन बाध्यते॥

examples.dm: While dwelling within my own mind, They harm me at their pleasure; To not be angry at this and to remain patient Is misplaced patience, a state worthy of reproach.
examples.gm: While dwelling in my mind, Doing harm to me at their pleasure, Patiently not being angry even at that, Is inappropriate patience and an object of reproach.
examples.sa: मच्चित्तावस्थिता एव घ्नन्ति मामेव सुस्थिताः। तत्राप्यहं न कुप्यामि धिगस्थानसहिष्णुताम्॥

examples.dm: The Perfection of Patience
examples.gm: Chapter Six: Teaching Patience

examples.dm: Since harm is inflicted upon embodied beings By both those with minds and those without, Why single out and bear a grudge against those with minds? Therefore, you should endure all harm.
examples.gm: To embodied beings, animate And inanimate things both do harm; Why single out the animate and hold resentment? Therefore, be patient with harm.
examples.sa: चेतनाचेतनकृता देहिनां नियता व्यथा। सा व्यथा चेतने दृष्टा क्षमस्वैनां व्यथामतः॥

examples.dm: Just as people who are disturbed by illness Have no strength for any activity, So too, a mind disturbed by confusion Has no strength for any activity.
examples.gm: People who are disturbed by illness, Are powerless in all activities; Likewise, when the mind is disturbed by ignorance, One is powerless in all activities.
examples.sa: व्याध्याकुलो नरो यद्वन्न क्षमः सर्वकर्मसु। तथाभ्यां विकलं चित्तं न क्षमं सर्वकर्मसु॥

examples.dm: O deluded mind, why do you not grasp instead a clean wooden image? Why is it appropriate to guard this foul machine, This collection of impurities?
examples.gm: Deluded mind, for what reason Do you not grasp a clean wooden form? This machine of a collection of impurities, Guarding this rotten thing, what is the use?
examples.sa: न स्वीकरोषि हे मूढ काष्ठपुत्तलकं शुचिम्। अमेध्यघटितं यन्त्रं कस्माद्रक्षसि पूतिकम्॥

examples.dm: Some commit misdeeds out of delusion; If others, being deluded, become angry, Who among them is without fault, And who is the one who is at fault?
examples.gm: Some commit faults through ignorance, And some, being ignorant, become angry. Among them, who is to be considered faultless? And who is to be considered at fault?
examples.sa: मोहादेकेऽपराध्यन्ति कुप्यन्त्यन्ये विमोहिताः। ब्रूमः कमेषु निर्दोषं कम वा ब्रूमोऽपराधिनम्॥

examples.dm: The Lords of Sages, who have deeply contemplated for many eons, Have seen that this alone is beneficial. By this, the boundless multitudes of beings Will easily attain the supreme bliss.
examples.gm: The Lords of Sages, who have contemplated for many eons, Have seen that this alone is beneficial; By this, immeasurable multitudes of beings Will easily attain the supreme bliss.
examples.sa: कल्पाननल्पान् प्रविचिन्तयद्भि-र्दृष्टं मुनीन्द्रैर्हितमेतदेव। यतः सुखेनैव सुखं प्रवृद्ध-मुत्प्लावयत्यप्रमिताञ्जनौघान्॥

examples.dm: The Sage has declared that whoever gives rise to a malicious thought Toward such a benefactor, a Son of the Conquerors, Will remain in hell for as many aeons As the number of malicious thoughts produced.
examples.gm: If anyone toward such a benefactor, a Child of the Conquerors, Generates an evil thought, that one For eons equal to the number of evil thoughts generated Will abide in hell, so the Capable One has taught.
examples.sa: इति सत्त्रपतौ जिनस्य पुत्रे कलुषं स्वे हृदये करोति यश्च। कलुषोदयसंख्यया स कल्पान् नरकेष्वावसतीति नाथ आह॥

examples.dm: By raining down showers of food and drink, May I dispel the suffering of hunger and thirst; During the intermediate eon of famine, May I myself become food and drink.
examples.gm: Bringing down a rain of food and drink, May I dispel the suffering of hunger and thirst. During the intermediate eon of famine, May I myself become food and drink.
examples.sa: क्षुत्पिपासाव्यथां हन्यामन्नपानप्रवर्षणैः। दुर्भिक्षान्तरकल्पेषु भवेयं पानभोजनम्॥

examples.dm: It is the universal bridge that delivers All beings from the lower realms; It is the rising moon of the mind that dispels The heat of the afflictions of all beings.
examples.gm: For all wandering beings, from the lower realms It is the universal bridge that liberates. Dispelling the torment of the afflictions of wandering beings, It is the rising moon of the mind.
examples.sa: दुर्गत्युत्तरणे सेतुः सामान्यः सर्वयायिनाम्। जगत्क्लेशोपशमन उदितश्चित्तचन्द्रमाः॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, even for a single moment, Creates obstacles or hinders this merit, Diminishes the welfare of sentient beings, And for them, rebirth in lower realms is endless.
examples.gm: Whoever else, even for a mere moment, Creates an obstacle to this merit, Because the benefit of sentient beings is diminished, Their lower rebirths will be limitless.
examples.sa: योऽप्यन्यः क्षणमप्यस्य पुण्यविघ्नं करिष्यति। तस्य दुर्गतिपर्यन्तो नास्ति सत्त्वार्थघातिनः॥

examples.dm: One who desires high status for oneself Will be reborn in the lower realms, in wretchedness, and as a fool. If that very desire is transferred to others, One will attain good migrations and be honored.
examples.gm: Through wishing for oneself to be exalted, One will fall to bad migrations and become base and foolish. If that very thing is shifted to others, One will obtain happy migrations and respect.
examples.sa: दुर्गतिर्नीचता मौर्ख्यं ययैवात्मोन्नतीच्छया। तामेवान्यत्र संक्राम्य सुगतिः सत्कृतिर्मतिः॥

examples.dm: Even if one abandons the bodhicitta, The way in which those are liberated Is an inconceivable karmic process, Known only to the Omniscient One.
examples.gm: Even though some people give up the awakening mind, As for their being liberated, The way of karma is inconceivable; Only the Omniscient One knows.
examples.sa: वेत्ति सर्वज्ञ एवैतामचिन्त्यां कर्मणो गतिम्। यद्बोधिचित्तत्यागेऽपि मोचयत्येवं तां नरान्॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the guardians of hell And the forest of sword-leaves are produced By one's own karma, At whom should I be angry?
examples.gm: Like the guardians of hell, And the forest of sword-leaves, This is produced by my own karma, So at whom should I be angry?
examples.sa: असिपत्रवनं यद्वद्यथा नारकपक्षिणः। मत्कर्मजनिता एव तथेदं कुत्र कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: Impelled by my own past actions, Those who harm me have arisen; If by this they go to the hells, Have I not been the one to ruin them?
examples.gm: Instigated by my own karma, Those who harm me appear; If because of this they go to hell, Have I not ruined them?
examples.sa: मत्कर्मचोदिता एव जाता मय्यपकारिणः। येन यास्यन्ति नरकान्मयैवामी हता ननु॥

examples.dm: If the elephant of the mind is firmly bound With the rope of total mindfulness, All fears will vanish, And every virtue will fall into one's hands.
examples.gm: With the rope of mindfulness on all sides, If the elephant of the mind is tightly bound, All fears will cease to exist, And all virtues will come into one's hands.
examples.sa: बद्धश्चेच्चित्तमातङ्गः स्मृतिरज्ज्वा समन्ततः। भयमस्तंगतं सर्वं कृत्स्नं कल्याणमागतम्॥

examples.dm: For those whose minds lack introspective awareness, Even what has been heard, reflected upon, and meditated on, Will not remain in their memory, Like water in a leaking jar.
examples.gm: Of one who has a mind without introspection, Even hearing, thinking, and meditating, Like water in a leaky vase, Will not remain in memory.
examples.sa: असंप्रजन्यचित्तस्य श्रुतचिन्तितभावितम्। सच्छिद्रकुम्भजलवन्न स्मृताववतिष्ठते॥

examples.dm: If self-awareness does not exist, How can consciousness be remembered? Memory arises through a connection to the experience of something else, Just like the venom of a rat.
examples.gm: "If self-awareness does not exist, How is consciousness remembered?" It is remembered from its connection to experiencing another, Like the poison of a rat.
examples.sa: यदि नास्ति स्वसंवित्तिर्विज्ञानं स्मर्यते कथम्। अन्यानुभूते संबन्धात् स्मृतिराखुविषं यथा॥

examples.dm: If it is the nature of the childish To cause harm to others, It is inappropriate to be angry with them; It is like resenting fire for its nature to burn.
examples.gm: If doing harm to others Is the nature of the childish, It is illogical to become angry at them, Like resenting fire for its nature of burning.
examples.sa: यदि स्वभावो बालानां परोपद्रवकारिता। तेषु कोपो न युक्तो मे यथाग्नौ दहनात्मके॥

examples.dm: If the body’s natural state—with its long hair and nails, Yellowish teeth, and the stench of mud— Is a terrifying sight when left naked, Why do you take such pains to polish it?
examples.gm: If long hair and nails, Yellowish teeth, and a foul, muddy smell, Imbue the nature of the body, And make it terrifying indeed when naked,
examples.sa: यदि केशनखैर्दीर्घैर्दन्तैः समलपाण्डुरैः। मलपङ्कधरो नग्नः कायः प्रकृतिभीषणः॥

examples.dm: That which is not the body, nor something other than it, Neither mixed with it nor separate in any way, Is not even the slightest thing; therefore, Sentient beings are by nature in the state of nirvana.
examples.gm: That which is not in the body, nor anywhere else, Not mixed, nor apart from it anywhere, Is nothing whatsoever; therefore, Sentient beings are by nature in nirvāṇa.
examples.sa: यन्न काये न चान्यत्र न मिश्रं न पृथक् क्वचित्। तन्न किंचिदतः सत्त्वाः प्रकृत्या परिनिर्वृताः॥

examples.dm: The Sage has declared that whoever gives rise to a malicious thought Toward such a benefactor, a Son of the Conquerors, Will remain in hell for as many aeons As the number of malicious thoughts produced.
examples.gm: If anyone toward such a benefactor, a Child of the Conquerors, Generates an evil thought, that one For eons equal to the number of evil thoughts generated Will abide in hell, so the Capable One has taught.
examples.sa: इति सत्त्रपतौ जिनस्य पुत्रे कलुषं स्वे हृदये करोति यश्च। कलुषोदयसंख्यया स कल्पान् नरकेष्वावसतीति नाथ आह॥

examples.dm: I take up with my mind and offer them well to the Munis, the supreme beings, Together with their spiritual heirs; O sublime objects of offering, you who are filled with great compassion, Regard me with affection and accept these offerings of mine.
examples.gm: Taking them with my mind, to the Capable Ones, the supreme of beings, And to their Children, I make excellent offerings; May those holy objects of offering, the ones of great compassion, Think of me with love and accept these things of mine.
examples.sa: आदाय बुद्ध्या मुनिपुंगवेभ्यो निर्यातयाम्येष सपुत्रकेभ्यः। गृह्णन्तु तन्मे वरदक्षिणीया महाकृपा मामनुकम्पमानाः॥

examples.dm: The Sage has taught that all such things Are the result of a sinful mind. Thus, within the three worlds, There is no other fear besides the mind.
examples.gm: All such things Were taught by the Sage to be the sinful mind. Thus, in the three worlds, There is no fear other than the mind.
examples.sa: पापचित्तसमुद्भूतं तत्तत्सर्वं जगौ मुनिः। तस्मान्न कश्चित् त्रैलोक्ये चित्तादन्यो भयानकः॥

examples.dm: Just as Mañjughoṣa and the others Have made offerings to the Victors, So too do I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors, and their spiritual heirs.
examples.gm: Just as Mañjuśrī and others Made offerings to the Victorious Ones, Likewise, I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors along with their Children.
examples.sa: मञ्जुघोषप्रभृतयः पूजयन्ति यथा जिनान्। तथा तथागतान्नाथान् सपुत्रान् पूजयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: Just as the Protector lay when passing into nirvana, One should lie down in the desired direction; From the very beginning, firmly apply the intention To wake up quickly with alertness.
examples.gm: Just as the Lord lay when passing into nirvana, One should lie down in the desired direction; With clear comprehension and the thought of rising quickly, One should definitely set the mind from the very beginning.
examples.sa: नाथनिर्वाणशय्यावच्छयीतेप्सितया दिशा। संप्रजानंल्लघूत्थानः प्रागवश्यं नियोगतः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, In order to dispel the fears of beings in cyclic existence, Blessed even his own name.
examples.gm: Therefore, the protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, for transmigratory beings, In order to dispel the fears of the assembly, Blessed even his own name.
examples.sa: अध्यतिष्ठदतो नाथः स्वनामाप्यवलोकितः। पर्षच्छारद्यभयमप्यपनेतुं जनस्य हि॥

examples.dm: Just as the Sugatas of former times Generated the mind of enlightenment, And in the Bodhisattva trainings Abided and trained in successive order,
examples.gm: Just as the previous Sugatas Generated the awakening mind, And in the trainings of the bodhisattvas, Just as they progressively abided,
examples.sa: यथा गृहीतं सुगतैर्बोधिचित्तं पुरातनैः। ते बोधिसत्त्वशिक्षायामानुपूर्व्या यथा स्थिताः॥

examples.dm: Those who wish to guard their training Must guard the mind with great effort; If one does not guard this mind, One will be unable to guard the training.
examples.gm: Those who wish to guard the training Must strictly guard the mind; If this mind is not guarded, One will not be able to guard the training.
examples.sa: शिक्षां रक्षितुकामेन चित्तं रक्ष्यं प्रयत्नतः। न शिक्षा रक्षितुं शक्या चलं चित्तमरक्षता॥

examples.dm: There is nothing whatsoever That the Sons of the Victors should not learn; For the wise who abide in this way, There is no merit that does not accrue.
examples.gm: That which is not to be trained in by the Sons of the Conqueror, Does not exist at all; For the wise one who abides in this way, There is nothing that does not become merit.
examples.sa: न हि तद्विद्यते किंचिद्यन्न शिक्ष्यं जिनात्मजैः। न तदस्ति न यत्पुण्यमेवं विहरतः सतः॥

examples.dm: Chapter Five: Guarding Introspection
examples.gm: Chapter Five: Guarding Introspection

examples.dm: To those who wish to guard their minds, I join my palms in prayer and say: "With all your effort, guard both mindfulness and introspective awareness!"
examples.gm: To those who wish to guard their minds, Mindfulness and introspection, Guard them both with all your effort! Thus I join my palms in prayer.
examples.sa: चित्तं रक्षितुकामानां मयैष क्रियतेऽञ्जलिः। स्मृतिं च संप्रजन्यं च सर्वयत्नेन रक्षत॥

examples.dm: When mindfulness stands at the gateway of the mind For the purpose of guarding it, At that time alertness will arrive, And even that which had slipped away will return.
examples.gm: When mindfulness from the door of the mind, Remains for the sake of guarding, At that time introspection will come, And even what has gone will return.
examples.sa: संप्रजन्यं तदायाति न च यात्यागतं पुनः। स्मृतिर्यदा मनोद्वारे रक्षार्थमवतिष्ठते॥

examples.dm: As long as the compassionate intention is not pure, One should not give away this body; Rather, in this and other lives as well, It should be given as a cause for accomplishing the great purpose.
examples.gm: As long as the thought of compassion is impure, This body should not be given away; Rather, in this and other lives as well, It should be given as a cause to accomplish a great purpose.
examples.sa: त्यजेन्न जीवितं तस्मादशुद्धे करुणाशये। तुल्याशये तु तत्त्याज्यमित्थं न परिहीयते॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, the qualities of suffering are: Through weariness, it dispels arrogance, Compassion arises for those in cyclic existence, One avoids misdeeds and delights in virtue.
examples.gm: Furthermore, the quality of suffering is That through sorrow, arrogance is dispelled, Compassion arises for those in cyclic existence, Sin is shunned, and virtue is delighted in.
examples.sa: गुणोऽपरश्च दुःखस्य यत्संवेगान्मदच्युतिः। संसारिषु च कारुण्यं पापाद्भीतिर्जिने स्पृहा॥

examples.dm: Therefore, just as I protect myself From even the slightest unpleasantness, I should likewise cultivate a protective mind And a heart of compassion toward others.
examples.gm: Therefore, just as to a small degree I protect myself even from unpleasant words, Likewise, a mind of protecting others and A mind of compassion should be cultivated in this way.
examples.sa: तस्माद्यथान्तशोऽवर्णादात्मानं गोपयाम्यहम्। रक्षाचित्तं दयाचित्तं करोम्येवं परेष्वपि॥

examples.dm: The followers of Durgā and the people of Karṇapa Endure the sensations of being burned, cut, and so forth; Why then am I so cowardly, When my goal is liberation?
examples.gm: Devotees of asceticism and the Karṇapas Endure the sensations of burning, cutting, and so forth Pointlessly; for the sake of liberation, Why am I cowardly?
examples.sa: दुर्गापुत्रककर्णाटा दाहच्छेदादिवेदनाम्। वृथा सहन्ते मुक्त्यर्थमहं कस्मात्तु कातरः॥

examples.dm: Craving is conditioned by feeling, and they also possess those feelings. A mind that possesses an object of observation will remain fixed upon something.
examples.gm: Craving occurs due to the condition of feeling; Those ones also have feelings. A mind that is endowed with apprehension Will rest upon something.
examples.sa: वेदनाप्रत्यया तृष्णा वेदनैषां च विद्यते। सालम्बनेन चित्तेन स्थातव्यं यत्र तत्र वा॥

examples.dm: If it is argued that it is not experienced because it is overwhelmed by something more powerful, How can that which is not of the nature of experience Be a sensation?
examples.gm: If it is because it is overshadowed by something stronger That it is not experienced, How can that which is not of the nature of experience Be a feeling?
examples.sa: बलीयसाभिभूतत्वाद्यदि तन्नानुभूयते। वेदनात्वं कथं तस्य यस्य नानुभवात्मता॥

examples.dm: That mind which you desire Cannot be touched or seen, And that which can be touched is not consciousness; What is the use of such a meaningless embrace?
examples.gm: That mind which you desire Cannot be touched or seen, And whatever can be is not conscious; What is the point of a meaningless embrace?
examples.sa: यदिच्छसि न तच्चित्तं द्रष्टुं स्प्रष्टुं च शक्यते। यच्च शक्यं न तद्वेत्ति किं तदालिङ्गसे मुधा॥

examples.dm: If you say, "The lamp illuminates," Having known this through cognition, Then by what is it known that the mind is luminous, Such that you can say so?
examples.gm: That a lamp illuminates Is known by cognition and thus expressed; That the intellect itself is luminous, Having been known by what, is so expressed?
examples.sa: दीपः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वा ज्ञानेन कथ्यते। बुद्धिः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वेदं केन कथ्यते॥

examples.dm: If the consciousness of sound were permanent, Then sound would be apprehended at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it perceive? On what basis could it be called "consciousness"?
examples.gm: If the consciousness of sound is permanent, It would apprehend sound at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it cognize, And due to what is it called a consciousness?
examples.sa: शब्दज्ञानं यदि तदा शब्दो गृह्येत सर्वदा। ज्ञेयं विना तु किं वेत्ति येन ज्ञानं निरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: The creator of such things is an object of knowledge, For the latencies of the afflictions have not been abandoned. Therefore, when one sees that object, The latency for emptiness is very weak.
examples.gm: Her creator has not abandoned The latent tendencies of the afflictions toward objects of knowledge; Therefore, when he sees her, His latent tendencies for emptiness are weak.
examples.sa: अप्रहीणा हि तत्कर्तुर्ज्ञेयसंक्लेशवासना। तद्दृष्टिकाले तस्यातो दुर्बला शून्यवासना॥

examples.dm: If the consciousness of sound were permanent, Then sound would be apprehended at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it perceive? On what basis could it be called "consciousness"?
examples.gm: If the consciousness of sound is permanent, It would apprehend sound at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it cognize, And due to what is it called a consciousness?
examples.sa: शब्दज्ञानं यदि तदा शब्दो गृह्येत सर्वदा। ज्ञेयं विना तु किं वेत्ति येन ज्ञानं निरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, what is it that he is asserted to produce? Are not the self, the earth, and so forth, And the nature of Īśvara himself, also eternal? Since consciousness arises from objects of knowledge,
examples.gm: And what is it that he wishes to produce? Are not the self, those such as earth, And the essence of Īśvara permanent? Consciousness arises from the object of knowledge, and
examples.sa: तेन किं स्रष्टुमिष्टं च आत्मा चेत् नन्वसौ ध्रुवः। क्ष्मादिस्वभाव ईशश्च ज्ञानं ज्ञेयादनादि च॥

examples.dm: Respectfully bowing to the Sugatas who possess the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, and to all who are worthy of veneration, I shall describe the engagement in the vows of the Sugatas' heirs, Having condensed them in accordance with the scriptures.
examples.gm: To the Sugatas, endowed with the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, And to all who are worthy of homage, I respectfully bow down; Then, entering into the vows of the heirs of the Sugatas, I shall explain it concisely in accordance with scripture.
examples.sa: सुगतान् ससुतान् सधर्मकायान् प्रणिपत्यादरतोऽखिलांश्च वन्द्यान्। सुगतात्मजसंवरावतारं कथयिष्यामि यथागमं समासात्॥

examples.dm: Today, in the presence of all the Protectors, I invite the world to the state of the Sugatas and to temporal happiness; Since I have invited you as my guests to this bliss, May the gods, asuras, and all others rejoice!
examples.gm: Today, by me, in the presence of all the protectors, Wandering beings to Sugatahood itself, and Until then, to happiness, have been invited as guests; Let gods, asuras, and others rejoice!
examples.sa: जगदद्य निमन्त्रितं मया सुगतत्वेन सुखेन चान्तरा। पुरतः खलु सर्वतायिनामभिनन्दन्तु सुरासुरादयः॥

examples.dm: Abiding within the heart of a vast, fragrant, and cool lotus, Their splendor nourished by the food of the Victorious One's melodious speech, Possessing a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through their virtue they become a Son of the Sugata dwelling in the presence of the Victorious One.
examples.gm: Dwelling in the core of a vast, fragrant, and cooling lotus, Whose splendor is produced by the food of the Victor's sweet speech, With a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through wholesome deeds one becomes a son of the Sugata dwelling before the Victor.
examples.sa: विपुलसुगन्धिशीतलसरोरुहगर्भगता मधुरजिनस्वराशनकृतोपचितद्युतयः। मुनिकरबोधिताम्बुजविनिर्गतसद्वपुषः सुगतसुता भवन्ति सुगतस्य पुरः कुशलैः॥

examples.dm: Just as one understands the distinction Between the desire to go and the act of going, In the same way, the wise should understand The distinction between these two in proper sequence.
examples.gm: Just as one understands the difference Between wishing to go and actually going, Likewise, the wise should understand the difference Between these two in their respective order.
examples.sa: गन्तुकामस्य गन्तुश्च यथा भेदः प्रतीयते। तथा भेदोऽनयोर्ज्ञेयो याथासंख्येन पण्डितैः॥

examples.dm: Because non-virtue is abandoned, there is no suffering; Because of wisdom, there is no unhappiness. In this way, it is through distorted conceptions And non-virtue that the mind and body are harmed.
examples.gm: By abandoning misdeeds, there is no suffering; By being wise, there is no displeasure. Thus, wrong conceptualizations And misdeeds harm the mind and body.
examples.sa: न दुःखी त्यक्तपापत्वात्पण्डितत्वान्न दुर्मनाः। मिथ्याकल्पनया चित्ते पापात्काये यतो व्यथा॥

examples.dm: If the body is at ease through merit, And the mind is at ease through wisdom, Then even while remaining in samsara for the sake of others, Why would those with compassion ever be weary?
examples.gm: Through merit, the body is at ease, And through wisdom, the mind is at ease. Even while remaining in cyclic existence for the sake of others, Why would the compassionate ones become weary?
examples.sa: पुण्येन कायः सुखितः पाण्डित्येन मनः सुखि। तिष्ठन् परार्थं संसारे कृपालुः केन खिद्यते॥

examples.dm: And even dispels their delusion. Where is there any virtue equal to that? Where could there be such a friend? How could there ever be such merit?
examples.gm: And dispels even their ignorance. Where is there a virtue comparable to that? Where is there a friend like that? Where is there even merit like that?
examples.sa: नाशयत्यपि संमोहं साधुस्तेन समः कुतः। कुतो वा तादृशं मित्रं पुण्यं वा तादृशं कुतः॥

examples.dm: What is diligence? It is delighting in the virtuous. Its opposing factors should be explained: Laziness, attachment to what is base, And the despondency of self-contempt.
examples.gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.
examples.sa: किं वीर्यं कुशलोत्साहस्तद्विपक्षः क उच्यते। आलस्यं कुत्सितासक्तिर्विषादात्मावमन्यना॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should aspire to virtue, And cultivate it with genuine respect. Having undertaken the rite of the Vajradhvaja, One should cultivate the pride of self-confidence.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should aspire to the wholesome, And meditate upon it with reverence; According to the method of the Vajradhvaja, Having begun, one should meditate on self-confidence.
examples.sa: तस्मात्कार्यः शुभच्छन्दो भावयित्वैवमादरात्। वज्रध्वजस्थविधिना मानं त्वारभ्य भावयेत्॥

examples.dm: Because I did not realize That I am merely a transient guest, Through ignorance, attachment, and hatred, I have committed many kinds of sins.
examples.gm: That my existence is so fleeting, Since I did not realize this, Through ignorance, attachment, and hatred, I have committed many kinds of non-virtue.
examples.sa: एवमागन्तुकोऽस्मीति न मया प्रत्यवेक्षितम्। मोहानुनयविद्वेषैः कृतं पापमनेकधा॥

examples.dm: Likewise, when the mind becomes attached to something And the fire of hatred begins to spread, One should discard that immediately Out of fear that one's merit will be consumed.
examples.gm: Likewise, whatever the mind is attached to, If the fire of hatred spreads to it, Fearing that merit will be burned, It should be discarded instantly.
examples.sa: एवं चित्तं यदासङ्गाद्दह्यते द्वेषवह्निना। तत्क्षणं तत्परित्याज्यं पुण्यात्मोद्दाहशङ्कया॥

examples.dm: If it is naturally foul-smelling, Is it not better to be unattached to it? Why do those with meaningless worldly cravings Anoint it with sweet scents?
examples.gm: If its nature is foul-smelling, Is it not better to not be attached to it? Those who pointlessly burn with craving in the world, Why do they smear it with sweet scents?
examples.sa: यदि स्वभावदौर्गन्ध्याद्रागो नात्र शिवं ननु। किमनर्थरुचिर्लोकस्तं गन्धेनानुलिम्पति॥

examples.dm: To the Victors who intend to pass into nirvana, I join my palms and pray: Do not leave these beings in blindness, But please remain for countless eons.
examples.gm: To the Conquerors wishing to pass into nirvana, With joined palms I pray: So as not to leave these wanderers in blindness, I beseech you to remain for countless eons.
examples.sa: निर्वातुकामांश्च जिनान् याचयामि कृताञ्जलिः। कल्पाननन्तांस्तिष्ठन्तु मा भूदन्धमिदं जगत्॥

examples.dm: So too, for the benefit of all beings, Shall I generate the mind of enlightenment, And likewise, in those trainings, I shall train in successive order.
examples.gm: Likewise, for the benefit of wandering beings, I shall generate the awakening mind, And likewise, in the trainings too, I shall progressively train.
examples.sa: तद्वदुत्पादयाम्येष बोधिचित्तं जगद्धिते। तद्वदेव च ताः शिक्षाः शिक्षिष्यामि यथाक्रमम्॥

examples.dm: If you do not wish for them to have even this, How can you wish for them to attain enlightenment? Where is the bodhicitta in one Who becomes angry at the prosperity of others?
examples.gm: If you do not want this for wandering beings, How can you desire awakening for them? For one who is angry at another's prosperity, Where is the mind of awakening?
examples.sa: स किं नेच्छसि सत्त्वानां यस्तेषां बोधिमिच्छति। बोधिचित्तं कुतस्तस्य योऽन्यसंपदि कुप्यति॥

examples.dm: But that which has been examined by the Buddhas and their heirs With great wisdom, And which I myself have also examined again and again— What reason is there to delay in that?
examples.gm: By the Buddhas and their sons, Whatever has been examined with great wisdom, And which I myself have examined again and again, What is there to postpone regarding it?
examples.sa: विचारितं तु यद्बुद्धैर्महाप्राज्ञैश्च तत्सुतैः। मयापि च यथाशक्ति तत्र किं परिलम्ब्यते॥

examples.dm: The afflictions are abandoned by the eye of wisdom; Once dispelled from my mind, where will they go? Where will they dwell to return and harm me again? It is only that I, being weak-minded, lack persistence.
examples.gm: Afflictions, afflictions, abandoned by the eye of wisdom, Cleared from my mind, where will they go? Where will they stay to return and harm me? It is just that I, of weak mind, lack effort.
examples.sa: क्वासौ यायान्मन्मनःस्थो निरस्तः स्थित्वा यस्मिन् मद्वधार्थं यतेत। नोद्योगो मे केवलं मन्दबुद्धेः क्लेशाः प्रज्ञादृष्टिसाध्या वराकाः॥

examples.dm: First, with your own intellect, peel away this layer of skin; Then, with the blade of wisdom, Separate the flesh from the lattice of bones.
examples.gm: First, this layer of skin, Separate it with your own intellect. And the flesh from the network of bones, Separate it aside with the weapon of wisdom.
examples.sa: इमं चर्मपुटं तावत्स्वबुद्ध्यैव पृथक्कुरु। अस्थिपञ्जरतो मांसं प्रज्ञाशस्त्रेण मोचय॥

examples.dm: If these guards of the prison of cyclic existence, Who become executioners in the hells and elsewhere, Dwell within the net of attachment in my mind, How could I ever find happiness?
examples.gm: The guards of the prison of saṃsāra, These which become the executioners that kill in hell and so forth— If, in the net of attachment residing in the mind, They remain, how can there be happiness for me?
