examples.sa: भवचारकपालका इमे नरकादिष्वपि वध्यघातकाः। मतिवेश्मनि लोभपञ्जरे यदि तिष्ठन्ति कुतः सुखं मम॥

examples.dm: The afflictions do not reside in sense objects, nor in the collection of faculties, nor in between them; If they do not exist elsewhere either, then where do they dwell to harm the entire world? They are like an illusion; therefore, to abandon fear in your heart, apply yourself to understanding them. Why do you pointlessly inflict harm upon yourself in the hells and other such realms?
examples.gm: Afflictions do not reside in the objects, nor in the sense faculties, nor in between. Nor elsewhere; if so, where do they reside and harm all wandering beings? They are like an illusion; therefore, banish fear in the heart and rely on effort for the sake of knowledge. Why should I be harmed meaninglessly in hells and so forth?
examples.sa: न क्लेशा विषयेषु नेन्द्रियगणे नाप्यन्तराले स्थिता नातोऽन्यत्र कुह स्थिताः पुनरमी मथ्नन्ति कृत्स्नं जगत्। मायैवेयमतो विमुञ्च हृदयं त्रासं भजस्वोद्यमं प्रज्ञार्थं किमकाण्ड एव नरकेष्वात्मानमाबाधसे॥

examples.dm: That which has become so impure Cannot be obtained for free; By striving for its sake, one suffers exhaustion And is harmed by the torments of hell and the like.
examples.gm: That which has thus become filthy, Cannot be obtained without a price; Exhaustion from accomplishing that goal, And harm in hells and so forth will follow.
examples.sa: एवं चामेध्यमप्येतद्विना मूल्यं न लभ्यते। तदर्थमर्जनायासो नरकादिषु च व्यथा॥

examples.dm: The conventional and the ultimate: These are held to be the two truths. The ultimate is not an object of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the conventional.
examples.gm: The relative and the ultimate— These are asserted to be the two truths. The ultimate is not the domain of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the relative.
examples.sa: संवृतिः परमार्थश्च सत्यद्वयमिदं मतम्। बुद्धेरगोचरस्तत्त्वं बुद्धिः संवृतिरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: For the sake of engaging the world, The Protector taught these things as if they were real; If you object that they are not even momentary, And that this is contradictory even in conventional truth,
examples.gm: "For the sake of guiding the world, The Protector taught entities. In reality, They are not momentary." If one says, "This contradicts even the relative,"
examples.sa: लोकावतारणार्थं च भावा नाथेन देशिताः। तत्त्वतः क्षणिका नैते संवृत्या चेद्विरुध्यते॥

examples.dm: But since the continuity of conditions is severed, It does not arise even conventionally. When even the confusion itself does not exist, By what means can an illusion be perceived?
examples.gm: But because the continuum of conditions is severed, It does not arise even relatively. "When even the deceptive mind does not exist, By what is the illusion perceived?"
examples.sa: प्रत्ययानां तु विच्छेदात्संवृत्यापि न संभवः। यदा न भ्रान्तिरप्यस्ति माया केनोपलभ्यते॥

examples.dm: Likewise, for the realms of sentient beings Extending to the very ends of space, May I be the cause of their sustenance in every way, Until all have passed beyond sorrow.
examples.gm: Likewise, extending to the limits of space, For the realm of sentient beings in all ways, Until they all attain nirvana, May I also be the cause of their sustenance.
examples.sa: एवमाकाशनिष्ठस्य सत्त्वधातोरनेकधा। भवेयमुपजीव्योऽहं यावत्सर्वे न निर्वृताः॥

examples.dm: Just as the Protector lay when passing into nirvana, One should lie down in the desired direction; From the very beginning, firmly apply the intention To wake up quickly with alertness.
examples.gm: Just as the Lord lay when passing into nirvana, One should lie down in the desired direction; With clear comprehension and the thought of rising quickly, One should definitely set the mind from the very beginning.
examples.sa: नाथनिर्वाणशय्यावच्छयीतेप्सितया दिशा। संप्रजानंल्लघूत्थानः प्रागवश्यं नियोगतः॥

examples.dm: If they are nothing but skeletons and nothing else, And are neither independent nor a self, Why, after desiring them intensely and becoming thoroughly attached, Do you not go to the state beyond sorrow?
examples.gm: Are nothing but skeletons, nothing else. Being neither independent nor a self, Strongly desiring and fully clinging to them, Why do you not proceed to nirvāṇa?
examples.sa: तान्येवास्थीनि नान्यानि स्वाधीनान्यममानि च। प्रकामं संपरिष्वज्य किं न गच्छसि निर्वृतिम्॥

examples.dm: Then, having sincerely invited all beings To the unsurpassed bliss, If I were to deceive all those beings, How could I ever go to a happy realm?
examples.gm: To unsurpassable happiness, Having invited them from the depths of my heart, If I deceive all wandering beings, How will I go to the higher realms?
examples.sa: किमुतानुत्तरं सौख्यमुच्चैरुद्धुष्य भावतः। जगत्सर्वं विसंवाद्य का गतिर्मे भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: If I have not performed virtuous deeds, And have instead thoroughly accumulated sins, Then for even a hundred million eons, I shall not even hear the sound of a happy rebirth.
examples.gm: Having not practiced virtues, And having accumulated sins, For even a hundred million eons, Even the sound of the happy realms will not be heard.
examples.sa: अकुर्वतश्च कुशलं पापं चाप्युपचिन्वतः। हतः सुगतिशब्दोऽपि कल्पकोटिशतैरपि॥

examples.dm: One who desires high status for oneself Will be reborn in the lower realms, in wretchedness, and as a fool. If that very desire is transferred to others, One will attain good migrations and be honored.
examples.gm: Through wishing for oneself to be exalted, One will fall to bad migrations and become base and foolish. If that very thing is shifted to others, One will obtain happy migrations and respect.
examples.sa: दुर्गतिर्नीचता मौर्ख्यं ययैवात्मोन्नतीच्छया। तामेवान्यत्र संक्राम्य सुगतिः सत्कृतिर्मतिः॥

examples.dm: If the perfection of generosity Consisted in the removal of the world's poverty, Then since beings are still destitute today, How could the Protectors of the past have reached that perfection?
examples.gm: If by eliminating the poverty of wandering beings, The perfection of generosity is achieved, Since there are still destitute beings, how did the past Saviors achieve the perfection?
examples.sa: अदरिद्रं जगत्कृत्वा दानपारमिता यदि। जगद्दरिद्रमद्यापि सा कथं पूर्वतायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: If one is unable to do so due to involvement in dangers, festivities, and the like, one should act as is appropriate; For it is taught that at times such as when practicing generosity, the rules of discipline may be set aside in equanimity.
examples.gm: When involved with dangers and festivities and so forth, If one is unable, one should act at ease. Thus, at times of giving, It is taught to treat ethical discipline with equanimity.
examples.sa: भयोत्सवादिसंबन्धे यद्यशक्तो यथासुखम्। दानकाले तु शीलस्य यस्मादुक्तमुपेक्षणम्॥

examples.dm: The Guide first engages one in the giving of things such as vegetables; Once accustomed to that, one later gradually gives even one's own flesh.
examples.gm: Even in the giving of vegetables and so forth, The Guide initially engages one. Having become accustomed to that, later on, One will gradually give away even one's own flesh.
examples.sa: आदौ शाकादिदानेऽपि नियोजयति नायकः। तत्करोति क्रमात्पश्चाद्यत्स्वमांसान्यपि त्यजेत्॥

examples.dm: Even if one practices recitations and all kinds of austerities For a very long period of time, The Knower of Reality has said that if they are performed With a mind distracted elsewhere, they are useless.
examples.gm: All recitations and ascetic practices, Even if practiced for a long time, If done with a mind distracted elsewhere, Are taught by the Knower of Reality to be meaningless.
examples.sa: जपास्तपांसि सर्वाणि दीर्घकालकृतान्यपि। अन्यचित्तेन मन्देन वृथैवेत्याह सर्ववित्॥

examples.dm: Whether from the perspective of conventional or ultimate truth, The scriptures state that there is a result, Just as there is a result From offerings made to the actual Buddha.
examples.gm: Whether conventionally or in reality, It is suitable, for scriptures state that there is a result; For example, toward a true Buddha, Just as it is endowed with a result.
examples.sa: आगमाच्च फलं तत्र संवृत्या तत्त्वतोऽपि वा। सत्यबुद्धे कृता पूजा सफलेति कथं यथा॥

examples.dm: With the price of a garment, buy cotton seeds And wear them instead. If the world does not see this due to ignorance, Then those who know the truth have established this very fact.
examples.gm: With the price of a cotton cloth, Buy a cotton seed and wear it. If the ignorant world does not see it, It is established by the knowers of reality.
examples.sa: पटार्घेणैव कर्पासबीजं क्रीत्वा निवस्यताम्। मोहाच्चेन्नेक्षते लोकः तत्त्वज्ञस्यापि सा स्थितिः॥

examples.dm: When the intention to neglect the welfare of others, Or the desire to pursue one's own interests, Or the urge to speak arises, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Forsaking the benefit of others, And desiring to pursue one's own benefit, If a mind desiring to speak arises, Because of that, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: परार्थरूक्षं स्वार्थार्थि परिषत्काममेव वा। वक्तुमिच्छति मे चित्तं तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: If I were one who understood my own best interests, What benefit for myself would I find in those things? If it is mere mental pleasure that I seek, I might as well devote myself to gambling, alcohol, and the like.
examples.gm: If I recognize my own welfare, What welfare of mine is there in that? If I desire only mental happiness, I should rely on gambling, alcohol, and the like.
examples.sa: एतावांश्च भवेत्स्वार्थो धीमतः स्वार्थवेदिनः। मद्यद्यूतादि सेव्यं स्यान्मानसं सुखमिच्छता॥

examples.dm: This alone is what pleases the Tathāgatas, This is also the perfect accomplishment of one's own welfare, This alone dispels the suffering of the world; Therefore, I shall always make this my practice.
examples.gm: This alone is what pleases the Tathāgatas; This alone is also the perfect accomplishment of my own purpose; This alone is also what dispels the suffering of the world; Therefore, I should always practice this alone.
examples.sa: तथागताराधनमेतदेव स्वार्थस्य संसाधनमेतदेव। लोकस्य दुःखापहमेतदेव तस्मान्ममास्तु व्रतमेतदेव॥

examples.dm: Do not be weary of the conflicting Desires of the childish, But be compassionate, thinking, "These arise from their afflictions."
examples.gm: Of the childish who are mutually discordant, Not being disheartened by their desires, 'From these arisen afflictions, This mind has arisen,' thinking thus, being endowed with compassion, and
examples.sa: परस्परविरुद्धाभिर्बालेच्छाभिरखेदितम्। क्लेशोत्पादादिदं ह्येतदेषामिति दयान्वितम्॥

examples.dm: Childish beings do not desire suffering, Yet they crave the causes of suffering. Since they are harmed by their own faults, Why should they be resentful toward others?
examples.gm: Childish ones do not desire suffering, Yet they crave the causes of suffering; When harmed by my own faults, Why should I resent others?
examples.sa: दुःखं नेच्छामि दुःखस्य हेतुमिच्छामि बालिशः। स्वापराधागते दुःखे कस्मादन्यत्र कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: If one shares the same conduct as the foolish, One will certainly go to the lower realms. If they lead one to what is unwholesome, What is the use of relying on the childish?
examples.gm: If one acts with equal fortune to the childish, One will certainly go to the lower realms. If they lead one to what is unequal, What is the use of relying on the childish?
examples.sa: बालैः सभागचरितो नियतं याति दुर्गतिम्। नेष्यते विषभागश्च किं प्राप्तं बालसंगमात्॥

examples.dm: O deluded mind, why do you not grasp instead a clean wooden image? Why is it appropriate to guard this foul machine, This collection of impurities?
examples.gm: Deluded mind, for what reason Do you not grasp a clean wooden form? This machine of a collection of impurities, Guarding this rotten thing, what is the use?
examples.sa: न स्वीकरोषि हे मूढ काष्ठपुत्तलकं शुचिम्। अमेध्यघटितं यन्त्रं कस्माद्रक्षसि पूतिकम्॥

examples.dm: If you have no attachment to what is impure, Why do you embrace in your lap another, A cage of bones bound together by sinews, And plastered over with the mud of flesh?
examples.gm: If you have no attachment to filth, To a cage of bones tied together with sinews And plastered with the mud of flesh, Why do you embrace another in your lap?
examples.sa: यदि ते नाशुचौ रागः कस्मादालिङ्गसेऽपरम्। मांसकर्दमसंलिप्तं स्नायुबद्धास्थिपञ्जरम्॥

examples.dm: You yourself contain plenty of filth, And you constantly wallow in that; Yet, out of a craving for the impure, You also desire other bags of filth.
examples.gm: You yourself contain much filth, Which you continually make use of, Yet for other bags of filth as well, Out of a craving for filth, you desire them.
examples.sa: स्वमेव बह्वमेध्यं ते तेनैव धृतिमाचर। अमेध्यभस्त्रामपरां गूथघस्मर विस्मर॥

examples.dm: For the sake of my desires, I have experienced Being burned and so forth in the hells thousands of times, Yet I have accomplished neither my own benefit Nor the benefit of others.
examples.gm: For the sake of desires, burning and so forth, I have experienced in hell thousands of times, but I did not accomplish my own benefit, Nor did I accomplish the benefit of others.
examples.sa: कोपार्थमेवमेवाहं नरकेषु सहस्रशः। कारितोऽस्मि न चात्मार्थः परार्थो वा कृतो मया॥

examples.dm: If one is never sated by sensual desires, Which are like honey on the edge of a razor, Then how could one ever be sated by merit, Which ripens into peace and happiness?
examples.gm: Like honey smeared on a razor's edge, If one is not satiated by sensual desires, Having a ripening of happiness and peace, How could one ever be satiated with merit?
examples.sa: कामैर्न तृप्तिः संसारे क्षुरधारामधूपमैः। पुण्यामृतैः कथं तृप्तिर्विपाकमधुरैः शिवैः॥

examples.dm: Since a child is unable to increase wealth, What happiness is there when one reaches one's prime? If one's life is exhausted by the accumulation of wealth, Once old, what is the use of sensual desires?
examples.gm: Since as a child one cannot amass wealth, When coming of age, what happiness is there in this? If life is exhausted by amassing wealth, What can be done with desires in old age?
examples.sa: शिशोर्नार्जनसामर्थ्यं केनासौ यौवने सुखी। यात्यर्जनेन तारुण्यं वृद्धः कामैः करोति किम्॥

examples.dm: Through this, the power of my faith to cultivate virtue may increase for a while; Furthermore, if others of equal fortune to myself should see this, It may prove meaningful for them as well.
examples.gm: In order to cultivate virtue, the force of my faith Will for a time increase because of this; And if others, equal in fortune to myself, Should see these words, they may be meaningful.
examples.sa: मम तावदनेन याति वृद्धिं कुशलं भावयितुं प्रसादवेगः। अथ मत्समधातुरेव पश्ये-दपरोऽप्येनमतोऽपि सार्थकोऽयम्॥

examples.dm: Even many who possess learning and faith, And who apply themselves with great diligence, Become defiled by the stain of downfalls, Due to the fault of lacking introspective awareness.
examples.gm: Those who are learned and have faith, And many who dedicate themselves to effort, Because they incur the fault of lacking introspection, Will become tainted by downfalls.
examples.sa: अनेके श्रुतवन्तोऽपि श्राद्धा यत्नपरा अपि। असंप्रजन्यदोषेण भवन्त्यापत्तिकश्मलाः॥

examples.dm: Why do you discard your own merit, faith, and good qualities? Tell me, why are you not angry at yourself For failing to grasp the gains that have come?
examples.gm: Merit and faith, Or your own good qualities, why do you cast them away? Not taking hold of the gains that occur, Tell me, why do you not become angry?
examples.sa: किं वारयतु पुण्यानि प्रसन्नान् स्वगुणानथ। लभमानो न गृह्णातु वद केन न कुप्यसि॥

examples.dm: Once the awakening mind has been generated, in that very instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Are called children of the Sugatas, And become objects of homage for the world, including its gods and humans.
examples.gm: If the mind of awakening is generated, in an instant, The wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existence Will be called children of the Sugatas, And will become worthy of reverence by the world's gods and humans.
examples.sa: भवचारकबन्धनो वराकः सुगतानां सुत उच्यते क्षणेन। सनरामरलोकवन्दनीयो भवति स्मोदित एव बोधिचित्ते॥

examples.dm: I take up with my mind and offer them well to the Munis, the supreme beings, Together with their spiritual heirs; O sublime objects of offering, you who are filled with great compassion, Regard me with affection and accept these offerings of mine.
examples.gm: Taking them with my mind, to the Capable Ones, the supreme of beings, And to their Children, I make excellent offerings; May those holy objects of offering, the ones of great compassion, Think of me with love and accept these things of mine.
examples.sa: आदाय बुद्ध्या मुनिपुंगवेभ्यो निर्यातयाम्येष सपुत्रकेभ्यः। गृह्णन्तु तन्मे वरदक्षिणीया महाकृपा मामनुकम्पमानाः॥

examples.dm: I shall triumph over everything; None shall triumph over me. As a son of the Lion-like Conqueror, I shall abide in this pride.
examples.gm: I shall conquer all, And no one shall conquer me. I, a son of the Victorious Lion, Should abide in this self-confidence.
examples.sa: मया हि सर्वं जेतव्यमहं जेयो न केनचित्। मयैष मानो वोढव्यो जिनसिंहसुतो ह्यहम्॥

examples.dm: This is reasonable, and as it was Requested by Subāhu, For the sake of beings with lesser aspirations, The Tathāgata himself has spoken.
examples.gm: Along with the reasoning for this, In the Questions of Subāhu, For the sake of beings of lesser inclination, It was taught by the Tathāgata himself.
examples.sa: इदं सुबाहुपृच्छायां सोपपत्तिकमुक्तवान्। हीनाधिमुक्तिसत्त्वार्थं स्वयमेव तथागतः॥

examples.dm: In order to fully embrace that precious mind, I make excellent offerings to the Tathāgatas, To the stainless Jewel of the sublime Dharma, And to the Sons of the Buddha, those oceans of virtue.
examples.gm: In order to take hold of that precious mind, To the Tathāgatas and the holy Dharma, The stainless Jewel, and the Children of the Buddhas, Who are oceans of qualities, I make excellent offerings.
examples.sa: तच्चित्तरत्नग्रहणाय सम्यक् पूजां करोम्येष तथागतानाम्। सद्धर्मरत्नस्य च निर्मलस्य बुद्धात्मजानां च गुणोदधीनाम्॥

examples.dm: The appearance of a Tathāgata, the attainment of faith and a human body, And the fitness to cultivate virtue— Since such things are so rare, when will they ever be found again?
examples.gm: The appearance of the Tathāgatas, Faith, obtaining a human body, And the fitness to practice virtue, like this, Since they are rare, when will they be obtained?
examples.sa: कदा तथागतोत्पादं श्रद्धां मानुष्यमेव च। कुशलाभ्यासयोग्यत्वमेवं लप्स्येऽतिदुर्लभम्॥

examples.dm: Although they have the desire to cast off suffering, They rush headlong into suffering itself. Although they desire happiness, through delusion They destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy.
examples.gm: Although having the wish to abandon suffering, They run directly toward suffering itself. Although desiring happiness, out of ignorance, They destroy their own happiness as if it were an enemy.
examples.sa: दुःखमेवाभिधावन्ति दुःखनिःसरणाशया। सुखेच्छयैव संमोहात् स्वसुखं घ्नन्ति शत्रुवत्॥

examples.dm: Overwhelmed by the confusion of ignorance, And whatever I have rejoiced in— Having seen those faults, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.gm: And, overcome by the confusion of ignorance, Whatever I have rejoiced in, Having seen these mistakes, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.sa: यच्चानुमोदितं किंचिदात्मघाताय मोहतः। तदत्ययं देशयामि पश्चात्तापेन तापितः॥

examples.dm: Then the intention not to act according to the instructions Of the Omniscient Physician, who removes every pain, Is a state of extreme delusion And is truly contemptible.
examples.gm: In that case, of the omniscient physician Who draws out all pain— The intention not to act according to his commands Is utterly foolish and an object of reproach.
examples.sa: तत्र सर्वज्ञवैद्यस्य सर्वशल्यापहारिणः। वाक्यमुल्लङ्घयामीति धिङ् मामत्यन्तमोहितम्॥

examples.dm: I am destitute and lack merit, And have no other wealth for making offerings. Therefore, O Protectors who care for the welfare of others, Please accept this through your own power for my sake.
examples.gm: I am without merit and extremely destitute, And I have no other wealth for offering. Therefore, may the Protectors whose thoughts are for the welfare of others, By their own power, accept this for my sake.
examples.sa: अपुण्यवानस्मि महादरिद्रः पूजार्थमन्यन्मम नास्ति किंचित्। अतो ममार्थाय परार्थचित्ता गृह्णन्तु नाथा इदमात्मशक्त्या॥

examples.dm: When the intention to neglect the welfare of others, Or the desire to pursue one's own interests, Or the urge to speak arises, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Forsaking the benefit of others, And desiring to pursue one's own benefit, If a mind desiring to speak arises, Because of that, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: परार्थरूक्षं स्वार्थार्थि परिषत्काममेव वा। वक्तुमिच्छति मे चित्तं तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: If the body is at ease through merit, And the mind is at ease through wisdom, Then even while remaining in samsara for the sake of others, Why would those with compassion ever be weary?
examples.gm: Through merit, the body is at ease, And through wisdom, the mind is at ease. Even while remaining in cyclic existence for the sake of others, Why would the compassionate ones become weary?
examples.sa: पुण्येन कायः सुखितः पाण्डित्येन मनः सुखि। तिष्ठन् परार्थं संसारे कृपालुः केन खिद्यते॥

examples.dm: With various fine garments, thin and soft, And hundreds of those most sublime ornaments, I shall adorn the noble Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and the rest.
examples.gm: With various fine garments, thin and soft, And with hundreds of those supreme ornaments, The noble Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and others, I will adorn.
examples.sa: दिव्यैर्मृदुश्लक्ष्णविचित्रशोभै-र्वस्त्रैरलंकारवरैश्च तैस्तैः। समन्तभद्राजितमञ्जुघोष-लोकेश्वरादीनपि मण्डयामि॥

examples.dm: Just as Mañjughoṣa and the others Have made offerings to the Victors, So too do I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors, and their spiritual heirs.
examples.gm: Just as Mañjuśrī and others Made offerings to the Victorious Ones, Likewise, I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors along with their Children.
examples.sa: मञ्जुघोषप्रभृतयः पूजयन्ति यथा जिनान्। तथा तथागतान्नाथान् सपुत्रान् पूजयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: The crowns of a hundred gods offer worship to his lotus feet, His eyes are moist with compassion, and a rain of various flowers falls upon his head; Look at him, accompanied by the songs of praise from thousands of goddesses in lovely celestial palaces! Having seen such a Mañjughoṣa, may the denizens of hell now break into cries of joy.
examples.gm: See how the crowns of hundreds of gods make offerings to his lotus feet, His eyes moistened with compassion, and a rain of multitudes of flowers falling upon his head, In delightful tiered palaces containing thousands of goddesses proclaiming songs of praise!" Seeing Mañjughoṣa like this, may the hell beings now cry out in joy.
examples.sa: पश्यन्त्वेनं भवन्तः सुरशतमुकुटैरर्च्यमानाङ्घ्रिपद्मं कारूण्यादार्द्रदृष्टिं शिरसि निपतितानेकपुष्पौघवृष्टिम्। कूटागारैर्मनोज्ञैः स्तुतिमुखरसुरस्त्रीसहस्रोपगीतै-र्दृष्ट्वाग्रे मञ्जुघोषं भवतु कलकलः सांप्रतं नारकाणाम्॥

examples.dm: This Lord of Death is not to be trusted; He does not wait for what has or has not been done. Whether sick or healthy, No one can rely on this fleeting life.
examples.gm: This Lord of Death cannot be trusted; He does not wait for what is done or not done. Whether we are sick or not sick, None can trust this fleeting life.
examples.sa: कृताकृतापरीक्षोऽयं मृत्युर्विश्रम्भघातकः। स्वस्थास्वस्थैरविश्वास्य आकस्मिकमहाशनिः॥

examples.dm: Even if you guard it in this way, When the pitiless Lord of Death Snatches it away and gives it to the birds and dogs, What will you be able to do then?
examples.gm: Even though you guard it like this, By the merciless Lord of Death If it is snatched and given to birds and dogs, At that time what can you do?
examples.sa: एवं ते रक्षतश्चापि मृत्युराच्छिद्य निर्दयः। कायं दास्यति गृध्रेभ्यस्तदा त्वं किं करिष्यसि॥

examples.dm: With all paths of escape completely blocked, And while the Lord of Death is watching you, How can you take pleasure in eating, And how can you find such joy in sleeping?
examples.gm: When all paths are blocked, And the Lord of Death is watching, How can you enjoy eating, And how can you enjoy sleeping like this?
examples.sa: यमेनोद्वीक्ष्यमाणस्य बद्धमार्गस्य सर्वतः। कथं ते रोचते भोक्तुं कथं निद्रा कथं रतिः॥

examples.dm: When seized by the messengers of the Lord of Death, What help are kinsmen, and what help are friends? At that time, merit alone provides protection, Yet that is what I have failed to cultivate.
examples.gm: When seized by the messengers of Yama, What good are relatives, what good are friends? At that time, merit alone is a protection, But I have not relied upon it.
examples.sa: यमदूतैर्गृहीतस्य कुतो बन्धुः कुतः सुहृत्। पुण्यमेकं तदा त्राणं मया तच्च न सेवितम्॥

examples.dm: At the sight of whom, the messengers of Yama And other hostile beings flee in terror To the four directions, I go for refuge to the Wielder of the Vajra.
examples.gm: Seeing whom, the messengers of Yama And other malicious beings Flee in terror to the four directions, I take refuge in the Vajra-wielder.
examples.sa: यं दृष्ट्वैव च संत्रस्ताः पलायन्ते चतुर्दिशम्। यमदूतादयो दुष्टास्तं नमस्यामि वज्रिणम्॥

examples.dm: With their skin entirely flayed by the henchmen of Yama, they are utterly tormented, And molten copper, melted by a searing fire, is poured over their bodies; Pierced by flaming swords and spears until their flesh is torn into hundreds of pieces, They fall upon the intensely blazing iron ground as a result of their many non-virtues.
examples.gm: Utterly tormented by the henchmen of Yama stripping away one's skin entirely, Molten copper melted by intensely hot fire poured onto one's body, Pierced by blazing swords and short spears, one's flesh scattered in a hundred pieces, Through many unwholesome deeds, one falls onto a ground of intensely blazing iron.
examples.sa: यमपुरुषापनीतसकलच्छविरार्तरवो हुतवहतापविद्रुतकताम्रनिषिक्ततनुः। ज्वलदसिशक्तिघातशतशातितमांसदलःपतति सुतप्तलोहधरणीष्वशुभैर्बहुशः॥

examples.dm: I joyfully rejoice in the virtue that relieves The suffering of all sentient beings in the lower realms, And in the abiding in happiness of those who suffer, With a heart full of delight.
examples.gm: Of the lower realms of all sentient beings, In the virtue that relieves suffering, and In suffering beings abiding in happiness, With joy I rejoice.
examples.sa: अपायदुःखविश्रामं सर्वसत्त्वैः कृतं शुभम्। अनुमोदे प्रमोदेन सुखं तिष्ठन्तु दुःखिताः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, are those who are present To destroy my praise and the like Not actually engaged in protecting me From falling into the lower realms?
examples.gm: Therefore, regarding my praise and the like, Those who stand close by to destroy them— Are they not engaged in protecting me From falling into the lower realms?
examples.sa: तस्मात्स्तुत्यादिघाताय मम ये प्रत्युपस्थिताः। अपायपातरक्षार्थं प्रवृत्ता ननु ते मम॥

examples.dm: Thus, by behaving as if they will never grow old or die, They are first of all killed in these very places, And then the unbearable fall into the lower realms occurs.
examples.gm: Thus, as if there were no aging and death, To those who live behaving in such a way, First of all, having been killed, The unbearable fall into the lower realms will come.
examples.sa: अजरामरलीलानामेवं विहरतां सताम्। आयास्यन्त्यापदो घोराः कृत्वा मरणमग्रतः॥

examples.dm: Just as the great elements, such as earth, And like space itself, may I always be The basis for the various means of subsistence For immeasurable sentient beings.
examples.gm: Just like earth and the other great elements, And like space, permanently, For limitless sentient beings, May I also be the ground of manifold sustenance.
examples.sa: पृथिव्यादीनि भूतानि निःशेषाकाशवासिनाम्। सत्त्वानामप्रमेयाणां यथाभोगान्यनेकधा॥

examples.dm: If the self is immutable, What could consciousness possibly do to it? Thus, being unconscious and inactive, It would be as if space were made into the self.
examples.gm: But if the self has no change, What is done to it by consciousness? Thus, unconscious and devoid of activity, Space might as well be made into the self.
examples.sa: अथाविकृत एवात्मा चैतन्येनास्य किं कृतम्। अज्ञस्य निष्क्रियस्यैवमाकाशस्यात्मता मता॥

examples.dm: For the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings, Reaching to the very limits of space in the ten directions, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.
examples.gm: As far as the limits of space in the ten directions, In order to accomplish the aims of all sentient beings, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.
examples.sa: दशदिग्व्योमपर्यन्तसर्वसत्त्वार्थसाधने। यथा चरति मञ्जुश्रीः सैव चर्या भवेन्मम॥

examples.dm: For a bodhisattva, this is The gravest of all downfalls; For should it occur, The welfare of all sentient beings is diminished.
examples.gm: For a bodhisattva, this Is the heaviest among the downfalls; Thus, if this happens, The benefit of all sentient beings is diminished.
examples.sa: बोधिसत्त्वस्य तेनैवं सर्वापत्तिग्ररीयसी। यस्मादापद्यमानोऽसौ सर्वसत्त्वार्थहानिकृत्॥

examples.dm: When encountering a dying snake, Even a crow acts like a Garuda. If I am weak and feeble, Even a minor downfall will cause me harm.
examples.gm: When encountering a dead snake, Even a crow acts like a garuda. If I myself am weak, Even a minor downfall will cause harm.
examples.sa: मृतं दुण्डुभमासाद्य काकोऽपि गरुडायते। आपदाबाधतेऽल्पापि मनो मे यदि दुर्बलम्॥

examples.dm: Even many who possess learning and faith, And who apply themselves with great diligence, Become defiled by the stain of downfalls, Due to the fault of lacking introspective awareness.
examples.gm: Those who are learned and have faith, And many who dedicate themselves to effort, Because they incur the fault of lacking introspection, Will become tainted by downfalls.
examples.sa: अनेके श्रुतवन्तोऽपि श्राद्धा यत्नपरा अपि। असंप्रजन्यदोषेण भवन्त्यापत्तिकश्मलाः॥

examples.dm: First, with your own intellect, peel away this layer of skin; Then, with the blade of wisdom, Separate the flesh from the lattice of bones.
examples.gm: First, this layer of skin, Separate it with your own intellect. And the flesh from the network of bones, Separate it aside with the weapon of wisdom.
examples.sa: इमं चर्मपुटं तावत्स्वबुद्ध्यैव पृथक्कुरु। अस्थिपञ्जरतो मांसं प्रज्ञाशस्त्रेण मोचय॥

examples.dm: If you say, "The lamp illuminates," Having known this through cognition, Then by what is it known that the mind is luminous, Such that you can say so?
examples.gm: That a lamp illuminates Is known by cognition and thus expressed; That the intellect itself is luminous, Having been known by what, is so expressed?
examples.sa: दीपः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वा ज्ञानेन कथ्यते। बुद्धिः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वेदं केन कथ्यते॥

examples.dm: When one thinks that "nothing exists," And the substantial thing to be analyzed is not perceived, At that time, how can a non-entity, lacking any basis, Remain before the mind?
examples.gm: When one asserts, "Such and such does not exist," And the entity to be examined is not observed, At that time, how can a non-entity without a basis Remain before the mind?
examples.sa: यदा न लभ्यते भावो यो नास्तीति प्रकल्प्यते। तदा निराश्रयोऽभावः कथं तिष्ठेन्मतेः पुरः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, like a treasure appearing in one's home Without being sought through wearisome toil, Because he becomes a helper in my bodhisattva conduct, I should rejoice in my enemy.
examples.gm: Therefore, accomplished without toil, Like a treasure appearing in the house, Since they become my helper in bodhisattva conduct, I should delight in my enemies.
examples.sa: अश्रमोपार्जितस्तस्माद्गृहे निधिरिवोत्थितः। बोधिचर्यासहायत्वात् स्पृहणीयो रिपुर्मम॥

examples.dm: Since I have been born as a human with the right potential, And recognize what is beneficial and what is harmful, If I do not abandon the conduct of a Bodhisattva, Why should I not attain enlightenment?
examples.gm: Since someone like me is born as a human by birth, And recognizes what is beneficial and harmful, If I do not forsake the enlightenment conduct, Why should I not attain enlightenment?
examples.sa: किमुताहं नरो जात्या शक्तो ज्ञातुं हिताहितम्। सर्वज्ञनीत्यनुत्सर्गाद्बोधिं किं नाप्नुयामहम्॥

examples.dm: If Buddhahood could be accomplished with even a millionth part of such hardship, Then for those possessed by desire, compared to the conduct of enlightenment, There is great suffering but no enlightenment.
examples.gm: If by just a ten-millionth fraction of that Hardship, Buddhahood is accomplished, Those with desires have greater suffering than in the Bodhisattva's conduct, And yet they have no awakening.
examples.sa: ततः कोटिशतेनापि श्रमभागेन बुद्धता। चर्यादुःखानमहद्दुःखं सा च बोधिर्न कामिनाम्॥

examples.dm: Through savoring the taste of idle pleasure, And the craving that relies on sleep, One does not feel weariness for the suffering of cyclic existence; From these, laziness fully arises.
examples.gm: Tasting the pleasure of idleness, and Craving that relies on sleep; From feeling no weariness toward the sufferings of saṃsāra, Laziness comes to arise.
examples.sa: अव्यापारसुखास्वादनिद्रापाश्रयतृष्णया। संसारदुःखानुद्वेगादालस्यमुपजायते॥

examples.dm: If they are not seen, there is no joy, And the mind will not remain in meditative equipoise; Even if they are seen, there is no satisfaction, And one is tormented by craving just as before.
examples.gm: Not seeing them, one will not be joyful, And the mind will not rest in equipoise. Even seeing them, one will not be satisfied, And will be tormented by craving as before.
examples.sa: अपश्यन्नरतिं याति समाधौ न च तिष्ठति। न च तृप्यति दृष्ट्वापि पूर्ववद्बाध्यते तृषा॥

examples.dm: Craving is conditioned by feeling, and they also possess those feelings. A mind that possesses an object of observation will remain fixed upon something.
examples.gm: Craving occurs due to the condition of feeling; Those ones also have feelings. A mind that is endowed with apprehension Will rest upon something.
examples.sa: वेदनाप्रत्यया तृष्णा वेदनैषां च विद्यते। सालम्बनेन चित्तेन स्थातव्यं यत्र तत्र वा॥

examples.dm: Since a non-entity depends upon an entity, How could it possess the capacity for action? Your mind would then be without any companion, It would become entirely solitary.
examples.gm: "Since a non-entity depends on a real entity, How could it be endowed with a function?" Your mind, being without a companion, Would become entirely alone.
examples.sa: वस्त्वाश्रयेणाभावस्य क्रियावत्त्वं कथं भवेत्। असत्सहायमेकं हि चित्तमापद्यते तव॥

examples.dm: When neither entities nor non-entities Remain before the mind, Then, since there is no other aspect, It is thoroughly pacified in non-apprehension.
examples.gm: When both entities and non-entities Do not remain before the mind, At that time, since there is no other aspect, It is completely pacified, without an object of focus.
examples.sa: यदा न भावो नाभावो मतेः संतिष्ठते पुरः। तदान्यगत्यभावेन निरालम्बा प्रशाम्यति॥

examples.dm: Without contacting the imagined entity, Its non-existence cannot be apprehended. Therefore, whatever entity is false, Its non-existence is clearly false as well.
examples.gm: Without contacting the imputed entity, Its nonentity is not apprehended. Therefore, whatever entity is false, Its nonentity is clearly false.
examples.sa: कल्पितं भावमस्पृष्ट्वा तदभावो न गृह्यते। तस्माद्भावो मृषा यो हि तस्याभावः स्फुटं मृषा॥

examples.dm: The creator of such things is an object of knowledge, For the latencies of the afflictions have not been abandoned. Therefore, when one sees that object, The latency for emptiness is very weak.
examples.gm: Her creator has not abandoned The latent tendencies of the afflictions toward objects of knowledge; Therefore, when he sees her, His latent tendencies for emptiness are weak.
examples.sa: अप्रहीणा हि तत्कर्तुर्ज्ञेयसंक्लेशवासना। तद्दृष्टिकाले तस्यातो दुर्बला शून्यवासना॥

examples.dm: Liberation comes from seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness? Because the scriptures state that without this path, There is no enlightenment.
examples.gm: "One is liberated by seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness?" Because scriptures state that without this path, There is no awakening.
examples.sa: सत्यदर्शनतो मुक्तिः शून्यतादर्शनेन किम्। न विनानेन मार्गेण बोधिरित्यागमो यतः॥

examples.dm: To remain in cyclic existence for the sake of those suffering through delusion, Liberated from the extremes of attachment and fear, And having accomplished the state of abiding in cyclic existence— This is the fruit of emptiness.
examples.gm: For the sake of those who suffer due to ignorance, Being freed from the extremes of attachment and fear, Remaining in saṃsāra becomes established; This is the result of emptiness.
examples.sa: सक्तित्रासात्त्वनिर्मुक्त्या संसारे सिध्यति स्थितिः। मोहेन दुःखिनामर्थे शून्यताया इदं फलम्॥

examples.dm: If Īśvara is the cause of the world, Then for a start, explain who Īśvara is. If you say he is the elements, that may be so; But why weary yourself over a mere name?
examples.gm: If Īśvara is the cause of beings, Tell me, for now, what is Īśvara? If one says it is the elements, so be it; But what is the use of exhausting oneself over a mere name?
examples.sa: ईश्वरो जगतो हेतुः वद कस्तावदीश्वरः। भूतानि चेद्भवत्वेवं नाममात्रेऽपि किं श्रमः॥

examples.dm: Īśvara is not space, because space is inert; He is not the self, as that has already been refuted. And if the creator is also inconceivable, What is the point of speaking of him as "inconceivable"?
examples.gm: Īśvara is not space, because it is devoid of movement; He is not the self, because it was already refuted before; And as for a creator who is inconceivable, What is the use of speaking of the inconceivable?
examples.sa: नाकाशमीशोऽचेष्टत्वात् नात्मा पूर्वनिषेधतः। अचिन्त्यस्य च कर्तृत्वमप्यचिन्त्यं किमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: If he depends on something, then the collection of conditions Is the cause, and not Īśvara. When the collection is present, he has no power not to produce, And without it, he has no power to produce.
examples.gm: If he depends, then the collection itself Would be the cause, and not Īśvara. When assembled, there is no power not to produce, And without them, there is no power to produce.
examples.sa: अपेक्षते चेत्सामग्रीं हेतुर्न पुनरीश्वरः। नाकर्तुमीशः सामग्र्यां न कर्तुं तदभावतः॥

examples.dm: Respectfully bowing to the Sugatas who possess the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, and to all who are worthy of veneration, I shall describe the engagement in the vows of the Sugatas' heirs, Having condensed them in accordance with the scriptures.
examples.gm: To the Sugatas, endowed with the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, And to all who are worthy of homage, I respectfully bow down; Then, entering into the vows of the heirs of the Sugatas, I shall explain it concisely in accordance with scripture.
examples.sa: सुगतान् ससुतान् सधर्मकायान् प्रणिपत्यादरतोऽखिलांश्च वन्द्यान्। सुगतात्मजसंवरावतारं कथयिष्यामि यथागमं समासात्॥

examples.dm: Whether from the perspective of conventional or ultimate truth, The scriptures state that there is a result, Just as there is a result From offerings made to the actual Buddha.
examples.gm: Whether conventionally or in reality, It is suitable, for scriptures state that there is a result; For example, toward a true Buddha, Just as it is endowed with a result.
examples.sa: आगमाच्च फलं तत्र संवृत्या तत्त्वतोऽपि वा। सत्यबुद्धे कृता पूजा सफलेति कथं यथा॥

examples.dm: Liberation comes from seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness? Because the scriptures state that without this path, There is no enlightenment.
examples.gm: "One is liberated by seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness?" Because scriptures state that without this path, There is no awakening.
examples.sa: सत्यदर्शनतो मुक्तिः शून्यतादर्शनेन किम्। न विनानेन मार्गेण बोधिरित्यागमो यतः॥

examples.dm: Those who wish to overcome the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Those who wish to dispel the miseries of sentient beings, And those who wish to enjoy hundreds of manifold happinesses, Should never forsake the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Those who wish to destroy the hundreds of sufferings of existence, Who wish to dispel the unhappiness of sentient beings, And who wish to experience hundreds of great joys, Should never give up the mind of awakening.
examples.sa: भवदुःखशतानि तर्तुकामै-रपि सत्त्वव्यसनानि हर्तुकामैः। बहुसौख्यशतानि भोक्तुकामै-र्न विमोच्यं हि सदैव बोधिचित्तम्॥

examples.dm: Through the torments of accumulating, guarding, and losing, One should understand that wealth is an endless source of ruin. Those who are distracted by their attachment to wealth Have no opportunity to be liberated from the suffering of cyclic existence.
examples.gm: Through the torments of amassing, protecting, and losing it, Wealth should be known as endless ruin. Those who are distracted by attachment to wealth Have no opportunity for liberation from the miseries of existence.
examples.sa: अर्जनरक्षणनाशविषादै-रर्थमनर्थमनन्तमवेहि। व्यग्रतया धनसक्तमतीनां नावसरो भवदुःखविमुक्तेः॥

examples.dm: For the guests among beings who travel the path of existence And desire to enjoy the riches of happiness, This stands as the supreme bliss close at hand, Which brings total satisfaction to the great guests, the sentient beings.
examples.gm: For wandering beings, the guests traveling the path of existence, Who wish to experience the enjoyment of happiness, This is stationed nearby as the supreme happiness, Satisfying the great guests, sentient beings.
examples.sa: सुखभोगबुभुक्षितस्य वा जनसार्थस्य भवाध्वचारिणः। सुखसत्रमिदं ह्युपस्थितं सकलाभ्यागतसत्त्वतर्पणम्॥

examples.dm: I am destitute and lack merit, And have no other wealth for making offerings. Therefore, O Protectors who care for the welfare of others, Please accept this through your own power for my sake.
examples.gm: I am without merit and extremely destitute, And I have no other wealth for offering. Therefore, may the Protectors whose thoughts are for the welfare of others, By their own power, accept this for my sake.
examples.sa: अपुण्यवानस्मि महादरिद्रः पूजार्थमन्यन्मम नास्ति किंचित्। अतो ममार्थाय परार्थचित्ता गृह्णन्तु नाथा इदमात्मशक्त्या॥

examples.dm: May I be a protector for those without a protector, A guide for those traveling on the path, And for those who wish to cross over, May I be a boat, a ship, and a bridge.
examples.gm: May I be a protector for those without a protector, A guide for those who travel on the path, And a boat for those who wish to cross over, May I become a ship and a bridge.
examples.sa: अनाथानामहं नाथः सार्थवाहश्च यायिनाम्। पारेप्सूनां च नौभूतः सेतुः संक्रम एव च॥

examples.dm: Overwhelmed by the confusion of ignorance, And whatever I have rejoiced in— Having seen those faults, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.gm: And, overcome by the confusion of ignorance, Whatever I have rejoiced in, Having seen these mistakes, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.sa: यच्चानुमोदितं किंचिदात्मघाताय मोहतः। तदत्ययं देशयामि पश्चात्तापेन तापितः॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to the foundations of the awakening mind and to the reliquaries; I prostrate to the preceptors, the masters, And to those who maintain the supreme ascetic discipline.
examples.gm: To the bases of the awakening mind, And to the stūpas, I pay homage. To the preceptors and likewise the teachers, And to the supreme practitioners, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वचैत्यानि वन्देऽहं बोधिसत्त्वाश्रयांस्तथा। नमः करोम्युपाध्यायानभिवन्द्यान् यतींस्तथा॥

examples.dm: Through associating with a spiritual master, Following the instructions of a preceptor, And through fear, the fortunate who act with respect Will easily develop mindfulness.
examples.gm: From associating with gurus, And the instructions of preceptors, In the fortunate who act with respect out of fear, Mindfulness is easily generated.
examples.sa: उपाध्यायानुशासन्या भीत्याप्यादरकारिणाम्। धन्यानां गुरुसंवासात्सुकरं जायते स्मृतिः॥

examples.dm: This was translated, edited, and finalized from a Kashmiri manuscript by the Indian scholar Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator Bandé Paltseg.
examples.gm: Revised and finalized by the Indian preceptor Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator, the monk Paltsek, based on a Kashmiri manuscript;

examples.dm: I prostrate to the foundations of the awakening mind and to the reliquaries; I prostrate to the preceptors, the masters, And to those who maintain the supreme ascetic discipline.
examples.gm: To the bases of the awakening mind, And to the stūpas, I pay homage. To the preceptors and likewise the teachers, And to the supreme practitioners, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वचैत्यानि वन्देऽहं बोधिसत्त्वाश्रयांस्तथा। नमः करोम्युपाध्यायानभिवन्द्यान् यतींस्तथा॥

examples.dm: Therefore, I shall firmly grasp And properly guard this mind of mine. Apart from the ascetic discipline of guarding the mind, What is the use of many other disciplines?
examples.gm: Therefore, this mind of mine, I shall hold it well and guard it well. Except for the discipline of guarding the mind, What is the use of many disciplines?
examples.sa: तस्मात्स्वधिष्ठितं चित्तं मया कार्यं सुरक्षितम्। चित्तरक्षाव्रतं मुक्त्त्वा बहुभिः किं मम व्रतैः॥

examples.dm: One should share with those who have fallen into wrong paths, the protectorless, And those established in ascetic vows; One should eat only in moderation, And give away everything except for the three religious robes.
examples.gm: To those fallen into ruin, the unprotected, And those abiding in ascetic practice, one should share; One should eat only a moderate amount, And give away everything except the three Dharma robes.
examples.sa: विनिपातगतानाथव्रतस्थान् संविभज्य च। भुञ्जीत मध्यमां मात्रां त्रिचीवरबहिस्त्यजेत्॥

examples.dm: Until I reach the heart of enlightenment, I take refuge in the Buddhas; Likewise, I take refuge in the Dharma And in the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: Until reaching the essence of awakening, I go for refuge to the Buddhas; To the Dharma and the Bodhisattvas' Assembly, likewise, I go for refuge.
examples.sa: बुद्धं गच्छामि शरणं यावदा बोधिमण्डतः। धर्मं गच्छामि शरणं बोधिसत्त्वगणं तथा॥

examples.dm: Therefore, to the Victors, the protectors of beings, Who strive for the purpose of shielding all wanderers, And who, possessing great power, dispel every fear, From this very day, I go for refuge.
examples.gm: Therefore, in the Victors, the protectors of beings, Who strive for the purpose of protecting beings, The mighty ones who clear away all fear, From today onward, I take refuge.
examples.sa: अद्यैव शरणं यामि जगन्नाथान् महाबलान्। जगद्रक्षार्थमुद्युक्तान् सर्वत्रासहरान् जिनान्॥

examples.dm: In the past, I have transgressed your commands; Now, seeing this great fear, I come to you for refuge; Please, swiftly dispel my fears!
examples.gm: Previously I transgressed your commands, But now, seeing great fear, I take refuge in you, so Please swiftly clear away this fear.
examples.sa: अतीत्य युष्मद्वचनं सांप्रतं भयदर्शनात्। शरणं यामि वो भीतो भयं नाशयत द्रुतम्॥

examples.dm: Whatever harm I have done to the Three Jewels, To my parents, or to my teachers and others, Through the gateway of the afflictions By means of my body, speech, and mind,
examples.gm: To the Three Jewels, To parents, gurus, or others, Through afflictions, with body, speech, And mind, whatever harm I have done,
examples.sa: रत्नत्रयेऽपकारो यो मातपितृषु वा मया। गुरुष्वन्येषु वा क्षेपात् कायवाग्बुद्धिभिः कृतः॥

examples.dm: Of all that I have experienced in the past and which has vanished, What remains for me? Yet, through my obsessive attachment to such things, I have acted in opposition to the Guru's commands.
examples.gm: From what was previously experienced and perished, What remains for me? By being deeply attached to that, I have transgressed the gurus' commands.
examples.sa: पूर्वानुभूतनष्टेभ्यः किं मे सारमवस्थितम्। येषु मेऽभिनिविष्टेन गुरूणां लङ्घितं वचः॥

examples.dm: Through associating with a spiritual master, Following the instructions of a preceptor, And through fear, the fortunate who act with respect Will easily develop mindfulness.
examples.gm: From associating with gurus, And the instructions of preceptors, In the fortunate who act with respect out of fear, Mindfulness is easily generated.
examples.sa: उपाध्यायानुशासन्या भीत्याप्यादरकारिणाम्। धन्यानां गुरुसंवासात्सुकरं जायते स्मृतिः॥

examples.dm: For those who, focusing on me, Develop a mind of anger or of faith, May that very state always become The cause for the fulfillment of all their goals.
examples.gm: Focusing upon me, for those whose Minds of anger or faith arise, May that very thing always become for them The cause for accomplishing all their goals.
examples.sa: येषां क्रुद्धाप्रसन्ना वा मामालम्ब्य मतिर्भवेत्। तेषां स एव हेतुः स्यान्नित्यं सर्वार्थसिद्धये॥

examples.dm: If I am angry at the one who throws it Because they directly employed a stick or other weapon, Then since they too were incited by hatred, It is more appropriate to be angry at that hatred.
examples.gm: Although sticks and the like are directly utilized, If I become angry at the one who wields them, Since they too are impelled by hatred, It is logical to be angry at hatred.
examples.sa: मुख्यं दण्डादिकं हित्वा प्रेरके यदि कुप्यते। द्वेषेण प्रेरितः सोऽपि द्वेषे द्वेषोऽस्तु मे वरम्॥

examples.dm: This body is like a human-shaped abscess, Painful and unable to bear being touched. Since I, blinded by craving, have grasped it, At whom should I be angry when it is harmed?
examples.gm: Like a human-shaped ulcer, Painful and unable to bear being touched; When, blinded by craving, I have grasped it, When it is harmed, at whom should I be angry?
examples.sa: गण्डोऽयं प्रतिमाकारो गृहीतो घट्टनासहः। तृष्णान्धेन मया तत्र व्यथायां कुत्र कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: If even a sin committed in a single instant Leads to remaining in the Avīci hell for an eon, Then what need is there to mention that, due to sins Accumulated in beginningless saṃsāra, I shall not go to a happy rebirth?
examples.gm: Even by the sin committed in a single moment, If one dwells in Avīci for an eon, Due to the sins accumulated in beginningless saṃsāra, What need is there to mention not going to the happy realms?
examples.sa: एकक्षणकृतात् पापादवीचौ कल्पमास्यते। अनादिकालोपचितात् पापात् का सुगतौ कथा॥

examples.dm: By letting the elephant of the mind run wild, It inflicts the torments of the Incessant Hell; An untamed, mad elephant in this world Cannot cause such harm.
examples.gm: Letting the elephant of the mind wander loose Causes harm in the Avīci hell; An untamed, maddened elephant Does not cause such harm here.
examples.sa: अदान्ता मत्तमातङ्गा न कुर्वन्तीह तां व्यथाम्। करोति यामवीच्यादौ मुक्तश्चित्तमतङ्गजः॥

examples.dm: Since those who sacrifice their bodies and enter the Avīci hell Are repaid by benefiting these beings, Therefore, even if they cause me great harm, I shall act toward them all with nothing but goodness.
examples.gm: For those for whose sake they give up their bodies and enter the Avīci hell, Benefiting them becomes a repayment; Therefore, even if they cause great harm, I should act toward all with complete goodness.
examples.sa: भिन्दन्ति देहं प्रविशन्त्यवीचिं येषां कृते तत्र कृते कृतं स्यात्। महापकारिष्वपि तेन सर्वं कल्याणमेवाचरणीयमेषु॥

examples.dm: To what place could fish and other creatures be moved So that they would not be killed? The perfection of ethical discipline is explained As the attainment of the mind of renunciation.
examples.gm: Where could fish and so forth Be driven away so that they are not killed? From attaining the mind of renunciation, The perfection of moral discipline is explained.
examples.sa: मत्स्यादयः क्व नीयन्तां मारयेयं यतो न तान्। लब्धे विरतिचित्ते तु शीलपारमिता मता॥

examples.dm: If one is unable to do so due to involvement in dangers, festivities, and the like, one should act as is appropriate; For it is taught that at times such as when practicing generosity, the rules of discipline may be set aside in equanimity.
examples.gm: When involved with dangers and festivities and so forth, If one is unable, one should act at ease. Thus, at times of giving, It is taught to treat ethical discipline with equanimity.
examples.sa: भयोत्सवादिसंबन्धे यद्यशक्तो यथासुखम्। दानकाले तु शीलस्य यस्मादुक्तमुपेक्षणम्॥

examples.dm: The decline of my ethical discipline, views, and so forth, Is due to the power of the afflictions and is not under my control. I must be healed as much as possible, And I shall even accept the hardship involved.
examples.gm: The decline of discipline, view, and so forth Is due to the power of afflictions; it is not under my control. I should be healed as much as possible, and I will willingly accept even harm.
examples.sa: शीलदृष्टिविपत्त्यादिक्लेशशक्त्या न मद्वशात्। चिकित्स्योऽहं यथाशक्ति पीडाप्यङ्गीकृता मया॥

examples.dm: Better that my gains, honor, and body, And even my very life should perish, And better that my other virtues should decline, Than that I should ever let my mind degenerate.
examples.gm: My gain and honor, And body and livelihood had better perish, And other virtues had better decline, But the mind must never decline.
examples.sa: लाभा नश्यन्तु मे कामं सत्कारः कायजीवितम्। नश्यत्वन्यच्च कुशलं मा तु चित्तं कदाचन॥

examples.dm: If one desires gain, honor, or fame, Or if one seeks a circle of attendants, Or if one's mind desires to be served, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Desiring gain, honor, and fame, Or desiring to seek attendants and retinues, If one's mind desires to be served, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: लाभसत्कारकीर्त्यर्थि परिवारार्थि वा पुनः। उपस्थानार्थे मे चित्तं तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: For me, who seeks liberation, I do not need the shackles of gain and honor. How could I be angry with those Who act to release me from my bonds?
examples.gm: Since I seek liberation, I do not need the bonds of gain and honor. Those who free me from being bound— How could I be angry at them?
examples.sa: मुक्त्यर्थिनश्चायुक्तं मे लाभसत्कारबन्धनम्। ये मोचयन्ति मां बन्धाद्द्‍वेषस्तेषु कथं मम॥

examples.dm: Better that my gains, honor, and body, And even my very life should perish, And better that my other virtues should decline, Than that I should ever let my mind degenerate.
examples.gm: My gain and honor, And body and livelihood had better perish, And other virtues had better decline, But the mind must never decline.
examples.sa: लाभा नश्यन्तु मे कामं सत्कारः कायजीवितम्। नश्यत्वन्यच्च कुशलं मा तु चित्तं कदाचन॥

examples.dm: Even those who depend on a master's kindness, Having been provided for with wealth and honors, Will seek to kill that master If he is possessed by anger.
examples.gm: Those who, through wealth and honors, Have been favored and depend upon him, Even they, against the hate-filled Master, will rebel to kill him.
examples.sa: पूजयत्यर्थमानैर्यान् येऽपि चैनं समाश्रिताः। तेऽप्येनं हन्तुमिच्छन्ति स्वामिनं द्वेषदुर्भगम्॥

examples.dm: If I harbor such pride, thinking, "I have many gains and honors, And many people are fond of me," Then fear will arise after death.
examples.gm: "I have much gain and respect," "Many are fond of me"— If one harbors such conceit, Fear will arise after death.
examples.sa: लाभी च सत्कृतश्चाहमिच्छन्ति बहवश्च माम्। इति मर्त्यस्य संप्राप्तान्मरणाज्जायते भयम्॥

examples.dm: Whenever one's mind is affected by attachment Or the desire to be angry, One should not act and should not speak; One should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Whenever one's own mind has attachment, Or the desire to be angry—at that time, One should not act and should not speak; One should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: अनुनीतं प्रतिहतं यदा पश्येत्स्वकं मनः। न कर्तव्यं न वक्तव्यं स्थातव्यं काष्ठवत्तदा॥

examples.dm: Whenever one is intent on self-praise, Or on disparaging others, Or if one becomes abusive or filled with remorse, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Whenever one is devoted to self-praise, Or the very disparaging of others, Or becoming abusive and resentful, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: यदात्मोत्कर्षणाभासं परपंसनमेव वा। साधिक्षेपं ससंरम्भं स्थातव्यं काष्ठवत्तदा॥

examples.dm: If one desires gain, honor, or fame, Or if one seeks a circle of attendants, Or if one's mind desires to be served, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Desiring gain, honor, and fame, Or desiring to seek attendants and retinues, If one's mind desires to be served, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: लाभसत्कारकीर्त्यर्थि परिवारार्थि वा पुनः। उपस्थानार्थे मे चित्तं तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: In this, there is no loss for oneself, And in the next life, there will be great happiness; Through wrongdoing, one is unhappy and suffers, And in the next life, the suffering will be even greater.
examples.gm: In this, there is no loss for me here, And in the next life there is great happiness. Through faults there is unhappiness and suffering, And in the next life there is great suffering.
examples.sa: न चात्र मे व्ययः कश्चित्परत्र च महत्सुखम्। अप्रीतिदुःखं द्वेषैस्तु महद्दुःखं परत्र च॥

examples.dm: All faults, as many as there are, And various kinds of misdeeds, All arise through the power of conditions; They do not possess any independence.
examples.gm: All however many faults there are, and Various kinds of sins— All these arise from the power of conditions; They do not possess independence.
examples.sa: ये केचिदपराधाश्च पापानि विविधानि च। सर्वं तत्प्रत्ययबलात् स्वतन्त्रं तु न विद्यते॥

examples.dm: Just as poison spreads through the body By depending on the blood, So too will a fault pervade the mind If it finds an opportunity.
examples.gm: Just as poison, by relying on the blood, Spreads throughout the body, Likewise, if an opportunity is found, Faults will spread through the mind.
examples.sa: विषं रूधिरमासाद्य प्रसर्पति यथा तनौ। तथैव च्छिद्रमासाद्य दोषश्चित्ते प्रसर्पति॥

examples.dm: One should practice the perfections, such as generosity, In an ever-ascending degree of excellence. One should not sacrifice a great benefit for a small one; The primary consideration should be the welfare of others.
examples.gm: The perfection of generosity and the rest, Should be practiced, progressing higher and higher. One should not abandon the greater for the lesser. Principally, one should consider the benefit of others.
examples.sa: उत्तरोत्तरतः श्रेष्ठा दानपारमितादयः। नेतरार्थं त्यजेच्छ्रेष्ठामन्यत्राचारसेतुतः॥

examples.dm: For the sake of my desires, I have experienced Being burned and so forth in the hells thousands of times, Yet I have accomplished neither my own benefit Nor the benefit of others.
examples.gm: For the sake of desires, burning and so forth, I have experienced in hell thousands of times, but I did not accomplish my own benefit, Nor did I accomplish the benefit of others.
examples.sa: कोपार्थमेवमेवाहं नरकेषु सहस्रशः। कारितोऽस्मि न चात्मार्थः परार्थो वा कृतो मया॥

examples.dm: If one employs others for one's own benefit, One will experience servitude and the like. If one employs oneself for the benefit of others, One will experience lordship and the like.
examples.gm: If one employs others for one's own purpose, One will experience servitude and so forth. If one uses oneself for the purpose of others, One will experience lordship and so forth.
examples.sa: आत्मार्थं परमाज्ञप्य दासत्वाद्यनुभूयते। परार्थं त्वेनमाज्ञप्य स्वामित्वाद्यनुभूयते॥

examples.dm: One should never forsake a spiritual friend Who is learned in the meaning of the Mahāyāna And possesses the supreme conduct of a Bodhisattva, Even at the cost of one's own life.
examples.gm: Always, the virtuous spiritual friend, Who is skilled in the meaning of the Mahāyāna, And the supreme discipline of the bodhisattvas, Should not be given up even for the sake of one's life.
examples.sa: सदा कल्याणमित्रं च जीवितार्थेऽपि न त्यजेत्। बोधिसत्त्वव्रतधरं महायानार्थकोविदम्॥

examples.dm: If you accept that any speech which accords with the sutras is the word of the Buddha, Then why do you not accept the majority of the Mahayana, Which is similar to your own sutras?
examples.gm: If any speech that enters into the sūtras Is asserted to be spoken by the Buddha, Is it not asserted that the majority of the Mahāyāna Is equal to your sūtras?
examples.sa: यत्सूत्रेऽवतरेद्वाक्यं तच्चेद्बुद्धोक्तमिष्यते । महायानं भवत्सूत्रैः प्रायस्तुल्यं न किं मतम् ॥

examples.dm: If the Mahāyāna were not established, How would your own scriptures be established? Because this is established for both of us, Initially, this was not established for you.
examples.gm: "If the Mahāyāna is not established, How is your scripture established?" "Because this is established for both of us." "Initially, this was not established for you."
examples.sa: नन्वसिद्धं महायानं कथं सिद्धस्त्वदागमः। यस्मादुभयसिद्धोऽसौ न सिद्धोऽसौ तवादितः॥

examples.dm: If I am averse to this because it creates obstacles to my gain, My gains will be discarded in this world, But my sins will remain firm.
examples.gm: Because it hinders my gain, If I do not desire this, My gain will be left behind here, But my negative actions will remain steadfast.
examples.sa: लाभान्तरायकारित्वाद् यद्यसौ मेऽनभीप्सितः। नङ्क्ष्यतीहैव मे लाभः पापं तु स्थास्यति ध्रुवम्॥

examples.dm: Even if one acquires great wealth And enjoys happiness for a long time, Just like someone plundered by thieves, One will depart naked and empty-handed.
examples.gm: Even if I acquire abundant gains, And enjoy happiness for a long time, Just like being robbed by a thief, I will depart naked and empty-handed.
examples.sa: लब्ध्वापि च बहूंल्लाभान् चिरं भुक्त्वा सुखान्यपि। रिक्तहस्तश्च नग्नश्च यास्यामि मुषितो यथा॥

examples.dm: If you think, "I shall live on my gains And, while doing so, exhaust my sins and perform merit," Yet you become angry for the sake of that gain, Will your merit not be exhausted and will you not incur sin?
examples.gm: If you say, "By living on account of gains, I will exhaust negative actions and perform merit," If I become angry for the sake of gains, Will not merit be exhausted and negative actions created?
examples.sa: पापक्षयं च पुण्यं च लाभाज्जीवन् करोमि चेत्। पुण्यक्षयश्च पापं च लाभार्थं क्रुध्यतो ननु॥

examples.dm: The Perfection of Diligence
examples.gm: Chapter Seven: Teaching Joyous Effort

examples.dm: Thus, with patience, one should initiate diligence, For enlightenment dwells in those who strive in this way. Just as there is no movement without wind, Merit does not arise without diligence.
examples.gm: Thus, having patience, I should undertake diligence. For enlightenment abides in diligence. Just as there is no movement without wind, Merit does not arise without diligence.
examples.sa: एवं क्षमो भजेद्वीर्यं वीर्ये बोधिर्यतः स्थिता। न हि वीर्यं विना पुण्यं यथा वायुं विनागतिः॥

examples.dm: Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors, One should strive to increase diligence through the powers of aspiration, pride, joy, relinquishment, Earnest application, and mastery.
examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.
examples.sa: एवं विपक्षमुन्मूल्य यतेतोत्साहवृद्धये। छन्दमानरतित्यागतात्पर्यवशिताबलैः॥

examples.dm: Instead of taking delight in a pillow, Which is soft to the touch like cotton, The lustful are deluded regarding the impure, Claiming, "It does not leak a foul odor."
examples.gm: Of cotton, which is soft to the touch, You do not delight in a pillow, Saying it does not emit a foul odor; The lustful are deluded by filth.
examples.sa: तूलगर्भैर्मृदुस्पर्शै रमन्ते नोपधानकैः। दुर्गन्धं न स्रवन्तीति कामिनोऽमेध्यमोहिताः॥

examples.dm: Some wretched, lustful people, Utterly exhausted by a long day's work, Return home and lay their weary bodies Down to sleep like corpses.
examples.gm: Some miserable people with desires, Utterly exhausted by the day's work, Come home with worn-out bodies, And sleep exactly like corpses.
examples.sa: केचिद्दिनान्तव्यापारैः परिश्रान्ताः कुकामिनः। गृहमागत्य सायाह्ने शेरते स्म मृता इव॥

examples.dm: Some who are full of desire even have their bodies mutilated; Some are impaled on the points of stakes; Some are pierced by short spears; And some are even seen being burned.
examples.gm: Some with desires even have their bodies mutilated, Some are impaled on the points of stakes, Some are stabbed with short spears, And some are seen being burned.
examples.sa: छिद्यन्ते कामिनः केचिदन्ये शूलसमर्पिताः। दृश्यन्ते दह्यमानाश्च हन्यमानाश्च शक्तिभिः॥

examples.dm: The worldly perceive things and conceptualize them As being truly real, rather than like an illusion; It is on this point that The yogis and the worldly dispute.
examples.gm: People of the world see entities, And conceptualize them as truly real, Not as being like illusions; therefore, here, Yogis and the world dispute.
examples.sa: लोकेन भावा दृश्यन्ते कल्प्यन्ते चापि तत्त्वतः। न तु मायावदित्यत्र विवादो योगिलोकयोः॥

examples.dm: Since a non-entity depends upon an entity, How could it possess the capacity for action? Your mind would then be without any companion, It would become entirely solitary.
examples.gm: "Since a non-entity depends on a real entity, How could it be endowed with a function?" Your mind, being without a companion, Would become entirely alone.
examples.sa: वस्त्वाश्रयेणाभावस्य क्रियावत्त्वं कथं भवेत्। असत्सहायमेकं हि चित्तमापद्यते तव॥

examples.dm: When neither entities nor non-entities Remain before the mind, Then, since there is no other aspect, It is thoroughly pacified in non-apprehension.
examples.gm: When both entities and non-entities Do not remain before the mind, At that time, since there is no other aspect, It is completely pacified, without an object of focus.
examples.sa: यदा न भावो नाभावो मतेः संतिष्ठते पुरः। तदान्यगत्यभावेन निरालम्बा प्रशाम्यति॥

examples.dm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Exists by worldly renown, not by valid cognition. This is as false as the common renown Of purity in things that are actually impure.
examples.gm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Is through convention, not through valid cognition. That is false, just like the convention Of being clean and so forth regarding what is unclean and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रत्यक्षमपि रूपादि प्रसिद्ध्या न प्रमाणतः। अशुच्यादिषु शुच्यादिप्रसिद्धिरिव सा मृषा॥

examples.dm: If it is that very same consciousness that knows a form, Why at that time does it not also hear? If you say it is because the sound is not present, Then the consciousness of that sound is also absent.
examples.gm: If that very same consciousness cognizes form, Why is there no hearing at that time? If it is because sound is not nearby, Then the consciousness of it is also non-existent.
examples.sa: तदेव रूपं जानाति तदा किं न शृणोत्यपि। शब्दस्यासंनिधानाच्चेत्ततस्तज्ज्ञानमप्यसत्॥

examples.dm: Such being the case, what discerning person Would be attached to forms that are like a dream? When the body is thus non-existent, Then who is a man and who is a woman?
examples.gm: Thus, what intelligent person would be attached To form, which is like a dream? When the body does not exist in that way, Then what is a man and what is a woman?
examples.sa: एवं स्वप्नोपमे रूपे को रज्येत विचारकः। कायश्चैवं यदा नास्ति तदा का स्त्री पुमांश्च कः॥

examples.dm: If you say, "The lamp illuminates," Having known this through cognition, Then by what is it known that the mind is luminous, Such that you can say so?
examples.gm: That a lamp illuminates Is known by cognition and thus expressed; That the intellect itself is luminous, Having been known by what, is so expressed?
examples.sa: दीपः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वा ज्ञानेन कथ्यते। बुद्धिः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वेदं केन कथ्यते॥

examples.dm: Since it is never seen by anyone at all, Whether it is clear or not clear, Is like the graceful posturing of a barren woman's daughter; It is meaningless even to speak of it.
examples.gm: If it is not seen by anyone at all, Whether it is luminous or not luminous, Like the alluring pose of a barren woman's daughter, Expressing it is meaningless.
examples.sa: प्रकाशा वाप्रकाशा वा यदा दृष्टा न केनचित्। वन्ध्यादुहितृलीलेव कथ्यमानापि सा मुधा॥

examples.dm: If the coarse state is not other than the pleasure, Then the manifest pleasure is itself impermanent. If you claim that nothing non-existent can ever arise Because it lacks being,
examples.gm: If coarseness is not other than pleasure, Manifest pleasure is impermanent. If you assert that nothing nonexistent Arises, because it does not exist,
examples.sa: न स्थौल्यं चेत्सुखादन्यत् सुखस्यानित्यता स्फुटम्। नासदुत्पद्यते किंचिदसत्त्वादिति चेन्मतम्॥

examples.dm: If the consciousness of sound were permanent, Then sound would be apprehended at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it perceive? On what basis could it be called "consciousness"?
examples.gm: If the consciousness of sound is permanent, It would apprehend sound at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it cognize, And due to what is it called a consciousness?
examples.sa: शब्दज्ञानं यदि तदा शब्दो गृह्येत सर्वदा। ज्ञेयं विना तु किं वेत्ति येन ज्ञानं निरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: If it is that very same consciousness that knows a form, Why at that time does it not also hear? If you say it is because the sound is not present, Then the consciousness of that sound is also absent.
examples.gm: If that very same consciousness cognizes form, Why is there no hearing at that time? If it is because sound is not nearby, Then the consciousness of it is also non-existent.
examples.sa: तदेव रूपं जानाति तदा किं न शृणोत्यपि। शब्दस्यासंनिधानाच्चेत्ततस्तज्ज्ञानमप्यसत्॥

examples.dm: How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound Become that which apprehends form? One person being designated as both father and son Is not the ultimate reality.
examples.gm: How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound Become the apprehender of form? One being both father and son Is designated, but it is not ultimate reality.
examples.sa: शब्दग्रहणरूपं यत्तद्रूपग्रहणं कथम्। एकः पिता च पुत्रश्च कल्प्यते न तु तत्त्वतः॥

examples.dm: The Benefits of Bodhicitta
examples.gm: Chapter One: Explaining the Benefits of Bodhicitta

examples.dm: Like the fire at the end of an eon, it will surely Incinerate great sins in a single instant. Its immeasurable benefits were explained By the wise Protector Maitreya to Sudhana.
examples.gm: Like the fire at the end of time, it Certainly burns up great evils in a single instant; Its immeasurable benefits Were explained to Sudhana by the wise Lord Maitreya.
examples.sa: युगान्तकालानलवन्महान्ति पापानि यन्निर्दहति क्षणेन। यस्यानुशंसानमितानुवाच मैत्रेयनाथः सुधनाय धीमान्॥

examples.dm: This is the first chapter, titled "Explaining the Benefits of the Awakening Mind," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, this is the first chapter, called Explaining the Benefits of the Awakening Mind.

examples.dm: The Lords of Sages, who have deeply contemplated for many eons, Have seen that this alone is beneficial. By this, the boundless multitudes of beings Will easily attain the supreme bliss.
examples.gm: The Lords of Sages, who have contemplated for many eons, Have seen that this alone is beneficial; By this, immeasurable multitudes of beings Will easily attain the supreme bliss.
examples.sa: कल्पाननल्पान् प्रविचिन्तयद्भि-र्दृष्टं मुनीन्द्रैर्हितमेतदेव। यतः सुखेनैव सुखं प्रवृद्ध-मुत्प्लावयत्यप्रमिताञ्जनौघान्॥

examples.dm: With the finest perfumes, whose fragrance pervades The entire billion-fold world system, I shall anoint the bodies of all the Lords of Sages, Which blaze with a radiant luster like burnished, refined gold.
examples.gm: With fragrances whose scent wafts throughout the three thousandfold world systems, By these supreme perfumes, the bodies of all the Lords of Capable Ones, Like purified and polished refined gold, Radiant and blazing, I will anoint.
examples.sa: सर्वत्रिसाहस्रविसारिगन्धै-र्गन्धोत्तमैस्ताननुलेपयामि। सूत्तप्तसून्मृष्टसुधौतहेम-प्रभोज्ज्वलान् सर्वमुनीन्द्रकायान्॥

examples.dm: To the Lords of Sages, the supreme objects of veneration, I offer delightful Mandārava flowers, lotuses, Utpalas, and all other fragrant blossoms, As well as beautifully arranged and enchanting garlands.
examples.gm: To the Lords of Capable Ones, the supreme objects of offering, with pleasing Mandāra flowers and lotuses, Utpalas, and all fragrant things, And beautifully strung, pleasing garlands, I make offerings.
examples.sa: मान्दारवेन्दीवरमल्लिकाद्यैः सर्वैः सुगन्धैः कुसुमैर्मनोज्ञैः। अभ्यर्चयाभ्यर्च्यतमान् मुनीन्द्रान् स्रग्भिश्च संस्थानमनोरमाभिः॥

examples.dm: The Sage has declared that whoever gives rise to a malicious thought Toward such a benefactor, a Son of the Conquerors, Will remain in hell for as many aeons As the number of malicious thoughts produced.
examples.gm: If anyone toward such a benefactor, a Child of the Conquerors, Generates an evil thought, that one For eons equal to the number of evil thoughts generated Will abide in hell, so the Capable One has taught.
examples.sa: इति सत्त्रपतौ जिनस्य पुत्रे कलुषं स्वे हृदये करोति यश्च। कलुषोदयसंख्यया स कल्पान् नरकेष्वावसतीति नाथ आह॥

examples.dm: However, if one develops a deeply devoted mind, Its fruit will increase even more than that; Even when great difficulties arise for the Bodhisattvas, No sin occurs, and their virtue naturally increases.
examples.gm: But if anyone gives rise to a mind of deep faith, Its fruit increases even more than that. Even in great adversity for the Children of the Conquerors, Non-virtue does not arise, and virtue naturally increases.
examples.sa: अथ यस्य मनः प्रसादमेति प्रसवेत्तस्य ततःऽधिकं फलम्। महता हि बलेन पापकं जिनपुत्रेषु शुभं त्वयत्नतः॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to the bodies of those in whom That most precious and excellent mind has arisen; I take refuge in that source of happiness, Who brings about bliss even for those who cause them harm.
examples.gm: In whomever that supreme, precious mind Has been born, I bow to their body, and To those whom even doing harm connects one to happiness, I go for refuge to those sources of happiness.
examples.sa: तेषां शरीराणि नमस्करोमियत्रोदितं तद्वरचित्तरत्नम्। यत्रापकारोऽपि सुखानुबन्धीसुखाकरांस्तान् शरणं प्रयामि॥

examples.dm: Thinking, "Who can truly protect me from this great terror?" With eyes wide and bulging in panic, I will search in the four directions for a refuge.
examples.gm: "Who from this great terror Will perfectly protect me?" Opening my terrified eyes wide, I will search the four directions for protection.
examples.sa: कातरैर्दृष्टिपातैश्च त्राणान्वेषी चतुर्दिशम्। को मे महाभयादस्मात्साधुस्त्राणं भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: Seeing that there is no refuge in the four directions, I then fall into utter despair. If there is no refuge to be found in that place, What shall I do then?
examples.gm: Seeing no protection in the four directions, I will then become completely enveloped in despair. If there is no protection in that place, What shall I do at that time?
examples.sa: त्राणशून्या दिशो दृष्ट्वा पुनः संमोहमागतः। तदाहं किं करिष्यामि तस्मिन् स्थाने महाभये॥

examples.dm: In order to fully embrace that precious mind, I make excellent offerings to the Tathāgatas, To the stainless Jewel of the sublime Dharma, And to the Sons of the Buddha, those oceans of virtue.
examples.gm: In order to take hold of that precious mind, To the Tathāgatas and the holy Dharma, The stainless Jewel, and the Children of the Buddhas, Who are oceans of qualities, I make excellent offerings.
examples.sa: तच्चित्तरत्नग्रहणाय सम्यक् पूजां करोम्येष तथागतानाम्। सद्धर्मरत्नस्य च निर्मलस्य बुद्धात्मजानां च गुणोदधीनाम्॥

examples.dm: This body, which practices the sublime Dharma, Should not be harmed for the sake of something minor. By acting in this way, the aspirations Of sentient beings will be swiftly fulfilled.
examples.gm: The body that practices the sublime Dharma Should not be harmed for trivial reasons. If one acts thus, the wishes of sentient beings Will quickly be fulfilled.
examples.sa: सद्धर्मसेवकं कायमितरार्थं न पीडयेत्। एवमेव हि सत्त्वानामाशामाशु प्रपूरयेत्॥

examples.dm: If you say that this enemy should not be honored Because they have no intention for me to practice patience, Then why honor the sublime Dharma, Which is also a fit cause for accomplishment but lacks intention?
examples.gm: If you say, "Because they have no intention to accomplish my patience, This enemy is not to be venerated," Then since it is a suitable cause for accomplishment, Why do you venerate the sublime Dharma?
examples.sa: क्षमासिद्ध्याशयो नास्य तेन पूज्यो न चेदरिः। सिद्धिहेतुरचित्तोऽपि सद्धर्मः पूज्यते कथम्॥

examples.dm: In order to fully embrace that precious mind, I make excellent offerings to the Tathāgatas, To the stainless Jewel of the sublime Dharma, And to the Sons of the Buddha, those oceans of virtue.
examples.gm: In order to take hold of that precious mind, To the Tathāgatas and the holy Dharma, The stainless Jewel, and the Children of the Buddhas, Who are oceans of qualities, I make excellent offerings.
examples.sa: तच्चित्तरत्नग्रहणाय सम्यक् पूजां करोम्येष तथागतानाम्। सद्धर्मरत्नस्य च निर्मलस्य बुद्धात्मजानां च गुणोदधीनाम्॥

examples.dm: Today my life has become fruitful; I have well obtained this human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; I have now become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.gm: Today my life is fruitful; I have well obtained a human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; Today I have become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: अद्य मे सफलं जन्म सुलब्धो मानुषो भवः। अद्य बुद्धकुले जातो बुद्धपुत्रोऽस्मि सांप्रतम्॥

examples.dm: May all directions be filled with groves of wish-fulfilling trees, Resounding with the sweet Dharma proclaimed By the Buddhas and the sons of the Buddhas, And may they be filled with these.
examples.gm: With gardens of wish-fulfilling trees, Buddhas, and the children of buddhas Proclaiming the sweet sound of the Dharma, May all directions be filled.
examples.sa: रम्याः कल्पद्रुमोद्यानैर्दिशः सर्वा भवन्तु च। बुद्धबुद्धात्मजाकीर्णा धर्मध्वनिमनोहरैः॥

examples.dm: In the worlds of the gods and others, there are fragrances, Incense, wish-fulfilling trees, and jewel trees, Various kinds of harvests that grow without being sown, And all other ornaments worthy of being offered;
