examples.gm: Fragrances in the worlds of gods and others, Incense, wish-fulfilling trees, and jewel trees, Various crops that grow without being plowed, And other ornaments worthy of being offered,
examples.sa: देवादिलोकेषु च गन्धधूपाः कल्पद्रुमा रत्नमयाश्च वृक्षाः। सरांसि चाम्भोरुहभूषणानिहंसस्वनात्यन्तमनोहराणि॥

examples.dm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel or a wish-granting tree Completely fulfills all hopes, Likewise, through the power of the aspirations of those to be trained, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.gm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree Completely fulfill hopes, Likewise, due to those to be tamed and prayers of aspiration, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिः कल्पतरुर्यथेच्छापरिपूरणः। विनेयप्रणिधानाभ्यां जिनबिम्बं तथेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: May the forest of sword-leaves Become for them a dense sandalwood grove; May the Shalmali trees likewise Grow into wish-fulfilling trees.
examples.gm: May the forest of sword-leaves also Become a dense sandalwood forest for them. May the trunks of the śālmali trees also Grow as wish-fulfilling trees.
examples.sa: असिपत्रवनं तेषां स्यान्नन्दनवनद्युति। कूटशाल्मलिवृक्षाश्च जायन्तां कल्पपादपाः॥

examples.dm: I take up with my mind and offer them well to the Munis, the supreme beings, Together with their spiritual heirs; O sublime objects of offering, you who are filled with great compassion, Regard me with affection and accept these offerings of mine.
examples.gm: Taking them with my mind, to the Capable Ones, the supreme of beings, And to their Children, I make excellent offerings; May those holy objects of offering, the ones of great compassion, Think of me with love and accept these things of mine.
examples.sa: आदाय बुद्ध्या मुनिपुंगवेभ्यो निर्यातयाम्येष सपुत्रकेभ्यः। गृह्णन्तु तन्मे वरदक्षिणीया महाकृपा मामनुकम्पमानाः॥

examples.dm: To the noble Ākāśagarbha, And to Kṣitigarbha as well, And to all the great compassionate protectors, I cry out from my heart, seeking refuge.
examples.gm: To the noble Ākāśagarbha, And to Kṣitigarbha, And to all the greatly compassionate protectors, Seeking refuge, I call out from my heart.
examples.sa: आर्यमाकाशगर्भं च क्षितिगर्भं च भावतः। सर्वान् महाकृपांश्चापि त्राणान्वेषी विरौम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: Just as one whose body is completely ablaze Cannot find any mental pleasure through sensual gratifications, Likewise, when sentient beings are harmed, There is no way for the Great Compassionate Ones to be pleased.
examples.gm: Just as when one's body is completely engulfed in fire, No desirable things can make the mind happy, Likewise, when harm is done to sentient beings, There is no way for the greatly compassionate ones to be pleased.
examples.sa: आदीप्तकायस्य यथा समन्ता-न्न सर्वकामैरपि सौमनस्यम्। सत्त्वव्यथायामपि तद्वदेव न प्रीत्युपायोऽस्ति दयामयानाम्॥

examples.dm: To the Tathāgatas and their spiritual heirs, I offer a bath from many precious vases, Beautifully filled with delightful, scented water, Accompanied by manifold songs and music.
examples.gm: To the Tathāgatas and their Children, With many jeweled vases of scented water, Beautifully and perfectly filled, alongside songs And various music, I offer a bath.
examples.sa: मनोज्ञगन्धोदकपुष्पपूर्णैः कुम्भैर्महारत्नमयैरनेकैः। स्नानं करोम्येष तथागतानां तदात्मजानां च सगीतिवाद्यम्॥

examples.dm: Just as Mañjughoṣa and the others Have made offerings to the Victors, So too do I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors, and their spiritual heirs.
examples.gm: Just as Mañjuśrī and others Made offerings to the Victorious Ones, Likewise, I make offerings to the Tathāgatas, The Protectors along with their Children.
examples.sa: मञ्जुघोषप्रभृतयः पूजयन्ति यथा जिनान्। तथा तथागतान्नाथान् सपुत्रान् पूजयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: In order to please the Tathāgatas, From this day forth I shall remain a servant to the world. Even if many beings should kick me or trample upon my head, Or even kill me, I shall not retaliate; may the Protectors of the World be pleased.
examples.gm: In order to please the Tathāgatas, From today onward I shall be a servant to the world. Even if the multitudes of wandering beings strike my head with their feet, Or kill me, I will not retaliate; may the protectors of the world be pleased!
examples.sa: आराधनायाद्य तथागतानां सर्वात्मना दास्यमुपैमि लोके। कुर्वन्तु मे मूर्घ्नि पदं जनौघा विघ्नन्तु वा तुष्यतु लोकनाथः॥

examples.dm: Immeasurable palaces resonant with delightful songs of praise, Beautifully ablaze with hanging ornaments of pearls and jewels— These, which have become the ornaments of infinite space, I offer to those whose very nature is compassion.
examples.gm: Immeasurable palaces possessing pleasing songs of praise, Beautifully blazing with hanging ornaments of pearls and jewels, Which have become ornaments of boundless space, these too I will offer to those whose nature is compassion.
examples.sa: प्रलम्बमुक्तामणिहारशोभा-नाभास्वरान् दिङ्मुखमण्डनांस्तान्। विमानमेघान् स्तुतिगीतरम्यान् मैत्रीमयेभ्योऽपि निवेदयामि॥

examples.dm: To the protector Avalokiteśvara, Whose compassionate conduct is never mistaken, I cry out with a piteous voice: "Please protect this sinful one!"
examples.gm: Whose compassionate deeds are unerring, To the protector Avalokiteśvara as well, With an anguished cry, I call out: "Please protect me, a sinner!"
examples.sa: तं चावलोकितं नाथं कृपाव्याकुलचारिणम्। विरौम्यार्तरवं भीतः स मां रक्षतु पापिनम्॥

examples.dm: There is no doubt that those whose very nature is compassion Have taken all these beings as their own selves. Since these very beings are seen in the nature of the Protectors, Why do I not show respect to them?
examples.gm: Those possessing the nature of compassion Have made all these wandering beings into themselves; of this there is no doubt. These very ones seen in the form of sentient beings Are the protectors themselves; why do I not respect them?
examples.sa: आत्मीकृतं सर्वमिदं जगत्तैः। कृपात्मभिर्नैव हि संशयोऽस्ति। दृश्यन्त एते ननु सत्त्वरूपा- स्त एव नाथाः किमनादरोऽत्र॥

examples.dm: Upon all the jewels of the sublime Dharma, And upon the reliquaries and the sacred images, May a rain of precious flowers and the like Fall in a continuous, uninterrupted stream.
examples.gm: Upon all the rare and supreme holy Dharma, Stūpas, and images, May a rain of jewels, flowers, and the like, Fall without interruption.
examples.sa: सर्वसद्धर्मरत्नेषु चैत्येषु प्रतिमासु च। पुष्परत्नादिवर्षाश्च प्रवर्तन्तां निरन्तरम्॥

examples.dm: It is the great sun that completely dispels The dimness of ignorance of wandering beings; It is the essence of butter extracted From churning the milk of the sublime Dharma.
examples.gm: The dimness of ignorance of wandering beings, It is the great sun that uproots it. From churning the milk of the true Dharma, It is the essence of butter that has emerged.
examples.sa: जगदज्ञानतिमिरप्रोत्सारणमहारविः। सद्धर्मक्षीरमथनान्नवनीतं समुत्थितम्॥

examples.dm: Toward those who revile and destroy Sacred images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, It is not appropriate for me to feel hatred, For the Buddhas and the like cannot be harmed.
examples.gm: Towards images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, Even if someone disparages or destroys them, It is inappropriate for me to have anger, For the Buddhas and so forth suffer no harm.
examples.sa: प्रतिमास्तूपसद्धर्मनाशकाक्रोशकेषु च। न युज्यते मम द्वेषो बुद्धादीनां न हि व्यथा॥

examples.dm: Until I reach the heart of enlightenment, I take refuge in the Buddhas; Likewise, I take refuge in the Dharma And in the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: Until reaching the essence of awakening, I go for refuge to the Buddhas; To the Dharma and the Bodhisattvas' Assembly, likewise, I go for refuge.
examples.sa: बुद्धं गच्छामि शरणं यावदा बोधिमण्डतः। धर्मं गच्छामि शरणं बोधिसत्त्वगणं तथा॥

examples.dm: Since death will come very quickly, For as long as you can, gather the accumulations. Even if you abandon laziness at that time, What can you do when it is no longer the right time?
examples.gm: Because death will come very quickly, Until then, the accumulations should be gathered. Even if laziness is abandoned at that time, Being out of time, what can be done?
examples.sa: यावत्संभृतसंभारं मरणं शीघ्रमेष्यति। संत्यज्यापि तदालस्यमकाले किं करिष्यसि॥

examples.dm: What are called "continua" and "assemblies" Are false, like garlands, armies, and the like. Since there is no one who possesses suffering, Who could be the owner of this?
examples.gm: What are called a continuum and a collection Are false, like a rosary, an army, and so forth. Since there is no one who possesses suffering, Therefore, who will have control over this?
examples.sa: संतानः समुदायश्च पङ्क्तिसेनादिवन्मृषा। यस्य दुःखं स नास्त्यस्मात्कस्य तत्स्वं भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: Overwhelmed by the confusion of ignorance, And whatever I have rejoiced in— Having seen those faults, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.gm: And, overcome by the confusion of ignorance, Whatever I have rejoiced in, Having seen these mistakes, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.sa: यच्चानुमोदितं किंचिदात्मघाताय मोहतः। तदत्ययं देशयामि पश्चात्तापेन तापितः॥

examples.dm: Whatever sins I, a sinner stained by many faults, Have committed through my many transgressions, Those extremely unbearable deeds, I confess to all the Guides.
examples.gm: Defiled by many faults, Whatever non-virtues I, a sinner, Have committed that are extremely unbearable, I confess them all to the Guides.
examples.sa: अनेकदोषदुष्टेन मया पापेन नायकाः। यत्कृतं दारुणं पापं तत्सर्वं देशयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: In the presence of the Protectors, openly, With palms joined and a mind fearful of suffering, I prostrate again and again, And I confess all of these.
examples.gm: Directly in the presence of the protectors, With palms joined and a mind terrified of suffering, Bowing down again and again, I will confess all of them.
examples.sa: तत्सर्वं देशयाम्येष नाथानामग्रतः स्थितः। कृताञ्जलिर्दुःखभीतः प्रणिपत्य पुनः पुनः॥

examples.dm: Chapter Four: Demonstrating Conscientiousness
examples.gm: Chapter Four: Teaching Conscientiousness

examples.dm: This concludes the fourth chapter, "Showing Heedfulness," from the *Entering the Bodhisattva's Conduct*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the fourth chapter, called the Teaching on Conscientiousness.

examples.dm: In order to have the capacity for all activities Before starting any work, I should recall the discourse on heedfulness And make myself rise with alacrity.
examples.gm: So that before undertaking any task, One will have the capability for everything, Thus, recalling the teachings on heedfulness, One should make oneself rise lightly.
examples.sa: लघुं कुर्यात्तथात्मानमप्रमादकथां स्मरन्। कर्मागमाद्यथा पूर्वं सज्जः सर्वत्र वर्तते॥

examples.dm: Even if one practices recitations and all kinds of austerities For a very long period of time, The Knower of Reality has said that if they are performed With a mind distracted elsewhere, they are useless.
examples.gm: All recitations and ascetic practices, Even if practiced for a long time, If done with a mind distracted elsewhere, Are taught by the Knower of Reality to be meaningless.
examples.sa: जपास्तपांसि सर्वाणि दीर्घकालकृतान्यपि। अन्यचित्तेन मन्देन वृथैवेत्याह सर्ववित्॥

examples.dm: There is no evil like hatred, And no austerity like patience. Therefore, one should diligently practice patience In various ways.
examples.gm: There is no misdeed like hatred; There is no ascetic practice like patience. Therefore, earnestly upon patience, One should meditate in various ways.
examples.sa: न च द्वेषसमं पापं न च क्षान्तिसमं तपः। तस्मात्क्षान्तिं प्रयत्नेन भावयेद्विविधैर्नयैः॥

examples.dm: However, if I retaliate with harm, They will not be protected, And my own conduct will also be ruined; Thus, my ascetic practice will be destroyed.
examples.gm: But if I cause harm in return, They will not be protected, And my conduct will also decline; Thus my ascetic practice will be destroyed.
examples.sa: अथ प्रत्यपकारी स्यां तथाप्येते न रक्षिताः। हीयते चापि मे चर्या तस्मान्नष्टास्तपस्विनः॥

examples.dm: When impatience, laziness, or fear arise, And likewise when impudence or idle chatter, Or attachment to one's own side arises, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Intolerance, laziness, and fear, Likewise shamelessness and senseless talk, If a mind attached to one's own side arises, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: असहिष्ण्वलसं भीतं प्रगल्भं मुखरं तथा। स्वपक्षाभिनिविष्टं च तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: What is diligence? It is delighting in the virtuous. Its opposing factors should be explained: Laziness, attachment to what is base, And the despondency of self-contempt.
examples.gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.
examples.sa: किं वीर्यं कुशलोत्साहस्तद्विपक्षः क उच्यते। आलस्यं कुत्सितासक्तिर्विषादात्मावमन्यना॥

examples.dm: Through savoring the taste of idle pleasure, And the craving that relies on sleep, One does not feel weariness for the suffering of cyclic existence; From these, laziness fully arises.
examples.gm: Tasting the pleasure of idleness, and Craving that relies on sleep; From feeling no weariness toward the sufferings of saṃsāra, Laziness comes to arise.
examples.sa: अव्यापारसुखास्वादनिद्रापाश्रयतृष्णया। संसारदुःखानुद्वेगादालस्यमुपजायते॥

examples.dm: Having thus examined the mind for afflictions And for strivings toward meaningless things, At that time, the heroic one should firmly Restrain it by means of the antidote.
examples.gm: Thus, completely afflicted, Having examined the mind striving for meaningless things, At that time, the hero, by means of an antidote, Should hold it firmly.
examples.sa: एवं संक्लिष्टमालोक्य निष्फलारम्भि वा मनः। निगृह्णीयाद् दृढं शूरः प्रतिपक्षेण तत्सदा॥

examples.dm: Whether motivated by constant devotion Or by the application of an antidote, Great virtue arises toward those who possess qualities, Those who have been helpful, and those who are suffering.
examples.gm: Motivated by constant strong aspiration, Or motivated by the antidote, Towards the fields of qualities and benefactors, And the suffering, virtue becomes great.
examples.sa: सातत्याभिनिवेशोत्थं प्रतिपक्षोत्थमेव च। गुणोपकारिक्षेत्रे च दुःखिते च महच्छुभम्॥

examples.dm: Emptiness is the antidote To the darkness of the afflictive and cognitive obscurations. Why, then, would those who desire to swiftly attain omniscience Not meditate upon it?
examples.gm: Of the obscurations of afflictions and knowables, Emptiness is the antidote to the darkness. By one who wishes to quickly become omniscient, How could one not meditate on it?
examples.sa: क्लेशज्ञेयावृतितमःप्रतिपक्षो हि शून्यता। शीघ्रं सर्वज्ञताकामो न भावयति तां कथम्॥

examples.dm: One who has become a vessel for the vast Dharma Should not be applied to the lesser Dharma. One must not completely forsake proper conduct, Nor deceive others with Sutra or Mantra.
examples.gm: One who is a vessel for the vast Dharma Should not be engaged in the inferior Dharma; Conduct should not be completely cast aside, Nor should they be deceived with sutras and mantras.
examples.sa: नोदारधर्मपात्रं च हीने धर्मे नियोजयेत्। न चाचारं परित्यज्य सूत्रमन्त्रैः प्रलोभयेत्॥

examples.dm: Alternatively, for the time being, one should look at the concise Compendium of Sūtras; Both works composed by the noble Nāgārjuna should also be studied with diligence.
examples.gm: Or else, for the time being, the brief Sūtrasamuccaya should be looked at; And the two composed by the Noble Nāgārjuna Should also be looked at with effort.
examples.sa: संक्षेपेणाथवा तावत्पश्येत्सूत्रसमुच्चयम्। आर्यनागार्जुनाबद्धं द्वितीयं च प्रयत्नतः॥

examples.dm: If you accept that any speech which accords with the sutras is the word of the Buddha, Then why do you not accept the majority of the Mahayana, Which is similar to your own sutras?
examples.gm: If any speech that enters into the sūtras Is asserted to be spoken by the Buddha, Is it not asserted that the majority of the Mahāyāna Is equal to your sūtras?
examples.sa: यत्सूत्रेऽवतरेद्वाक्यं तच्चेद्बुद्धोक्तमिष्यते । महायानं भवत्सूत्रैः प्रायस्तुल्यं न किं मतम् ॥

examples.dm: If that self were permanent, It would clearly be inactive, like space. Even if it were to encounter other conditions, What could they do to something that is unchanging?
examples.gm: If that self is permanent, Like space, it is evidently inactive. Even if it meets with other conditions, What can be done to the unchanging?
examples.sa: नित्यो ह्यचेतनश्चात्मा व्योमवत् स्फुटमक्रियः। प्रत्ययान्तरसङ्गेऽपि निर्विकारस्य का क्रिया॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, what is it that he is asserted to produce? Are not the self, the earth, and so forth, And the nature of Īśvara himself, also eternal? Since consciousness arises from objects of knowledge,
examples.gm: And what is it that he wishes to produce? Are not the self, those such as earth, And the essence of Īśvara permanent? Consciousness arises from the object of knowledge, and
examples.sa: तेन किं स्रष्टुमिष्टं च आत्मा चेत् नन्वसौ ध्रुवः। क्ष्मादिस्वभाव ईशश्च ज्ञानं ज्ञेयादनादि च॥

examples.dm: If the consciousness of sound were permanent, Then sound would be apprehended at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it perceive? On what basis could it be called "consciousness"?
examples.gm: If the consciousness of sound is permanent, It would apprehend sound at all times. If there is no object of knowledge, what does it cognize, And due to what is it called a consciousness?
examples.sa: शब्दज्ञानं यदि तदा शब्दो गृह्येत सर्वदा। ज्ञेयं विना तु किं वेत्ति येन ज्ञानं निरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: The honors of praise and fame Do not become merit, nor do they become long life; They do not become strength, nor are they health, And they do not even bring physical comfort.
examples.gm: Praise, fame, and honor Will not become merit, nor will they become long life; Will not become my strength, and are not health; Nor will they make the body comfortable.
examples.sa: स्तुतिर्यशोऽथ सत्कारो न पुण्याय न चायुषे। न बलार्थं न चारोग्ये न च कायसुखाय मे॥

examples.dm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Exists by worldly renown, not by valid cognition. This is as false as the common renown Of purity in things that are actually impure.
examples.gm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Is through convention, not through valid cognition. That is false, just like the convention Of being clean and so forth regarding what is unclean and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रत्यक्षमपि रूपादि प्रसिद्ध्या न प्रमाणतः। अशुच्यादिषु शुच्यादिप्रसिद्धिरिव सा मृषा॥

examples.dm: If, for the sake of fame, I squander my wealth And even bring about my own death, What use are these mere syllables? Once dead, who is it that will experience pleasure from them?
examples.gm: For the sake of fame, losing wealth, And even getting myself killed, What is the use of mere syllables? When dead, who will be happy from them?
examples.sa: यशोर्थं हारयन्त्यर्थमात्मानं मारयन्त्यपि। किमक्षराणि भक्ष्याणि मृते कस्य च तत्सुखम्॥

examples.dm: Praise and the like distract me; They also destroy my sense of disillusionment. They cause envy toward those with good qualities, And they destroy my excellence as well.
examples.gm: Praise and the like distract me, And also destroy my disillusionment; They cause jealousy toward those with good qualities, And destroy excellence as well.
examples.sa: स्तुत्यादयश्च मे क्षेमं संवेगं नाशयन्त्यमी। गुणवत्सु च मात्सर्यं संपत्कोपं च कुर्वते॥

examples.dm: They are jealous of superiors and competitive with equals; They are arrogant toward inferiors and conceited when praised. If something unpleasant is said, they become angry; When could one ever receive benefit from a fool?
examples.gm: Envious of superiors, competitive with equals, Arrogant toward inferiors, conceited when praised, And prone to anger when spoken to unpleasantly— When is benefit ever obtained from the childish?
examples.sa: ईर्ष्योत्कृष्टात्समाद्द्‍वन्द्वो हीनान्मानः स्तुतेर्मदः। अवर्णात्प्रतिघश्चेति कदा बालाद्धितं भवेत्॥

examples.dm: "I am happy, but others are not; I am high, but others are low; I am the benefactor, but others are not"— Why do you not feel envy toward yourself in this way?
examples.gm: "I am happy, others are unhappy, I am high, others are low, I do what is beneficial, others do not." Why do you not feel jealous of yourself?
examples.sa: अयं सुस्थः परो दुःस्थो नीचैरन्योऽयमुच्चकैः। परः करोत्ययं नेति कुरुष्वेर्ष्यां त्वमात्मनि॥

examples.dm: What is diligence? It is delighting in the virtuous. Its opposing factors should be explained: Laziness, attachment to what is base, And the despondency of self-contempt.
examples.gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.
examples.sa: किं वीर्यं कुशलोत्साहस्तद्विपक्षः क उच्यते। आलस्यं कुत्सितासक्तिर्विषादात्मावमन्यना॥

examples.dm: One should not be discouraged, thinking, "How could I ever attain enlightenment?" For the Tathāgata, the Speaker of Truth, Has spoken this truth.
examples.gm: Thinking, "How could I attain enlightenment?" I should not be despondent, For in this way the Tathāgata, Who speaks the truth, has spoken this truth:
examples.sa: नैवावसादः कर्तव्यः कुतो मे बोधिरित्यतः। यस्मात्तथागतः सत्यं सत्यवादीदमुक्तवान्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, having mounted the horse of the awakening mind, Which dispels all weariness and fatigue, As one proceeds from joy to joy, What person of intelligence would ever succumb to despondency?
examples.gm: Therefore, riding the horse of the awakening mind, Which dispels all weariness and fatigue, Proceeding from happiness to happiness, Who with a knowing mind would fall into despair?
examples.sa: एवं सुखात्सुखं गच्छन् को विषीदेत्सचेतनः। बोधिचित्तरथं प्राप्य सर्वखेदश्रमापहम्॥

examples.dm: Through solitude of body and mind, Distractions will not arise. Therefore, one should renounce the world And completely cast aside discursive thoughts.
examples.gm: Through the isolation of body and mind, Distraction does not arise. Therefore, one should abandon the worldly life And completely discard discursive thoughts.
examples.sa: कायचित्तविवेकेन विक्षेपस्य न संभवः। तस्माल्लोकं परित्यज्य वितर्कान् परिवर्जयेत्॥

examples.dm: Thus, having become weary of desires, One should generate a delight in solitude, Within peaceful forests That are empty of strife and afflictions.
examples.gm: Having thus generated revulsion for desires, Generate joy for solitude. Empty of disputes and afflictions, In the peaceful forests,
examples.sa: एवमुद्विज्य कामेभ्यो विवेके जनयेद्रतिम्। कलहायासशून्यासु शान्तासु वनभूमिषु॥

examples.dm: May those monks who desire to train Also obtain the state of solitude. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with a workable mind.
examples.gm: May monks who desire to train Attain solitary places. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with pliable minds.
examples.sa: विवेकलाभिनः सन्तुः शिक्षाकामाश्च भिक्षवः। कर्मण्यचित्ता ध्यायन्तु सर्वविक्षेपवर्जिताः॥

examples.dm: Since all is impermanent, who that is impermanent Would feel a true attachment to another? Because of that, for thousands of lifetimes, One will never again see the beloved.
examples.gm: What impermanent being Would be truly attached to the impermanent? Through that, for thousands of lifetimes, They will not see their loved ones.
examples.sa: कस्यानित्येष्वनित्यस्य स्नेहो भवितुमर्हति। येन जन्मसहस्राणि द्रष्टव्यो न पुनः प्रियः॥

examples.dm: May they be freed from all states of non-leisure, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And possessing excellent food and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.gm: Freed from all unfree states, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And perfect in sustenance and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.sa: सर्वाक्षणविनिर्मुक्ताः श्रद्धाप्रज्ञाकृपान्विताः। आकाराचारसंपन्नाः सन्तु जातिस्मराः सदा॥

examples.dm: May I be sustained and live, Even on a diet of the simplest food. In all my lives, may I obtain Perfect circumstances for living in solitude.
examples.gm: May I, even with simple food, Live endowed with vitality. In all my lifetimes, May I attain the perfection of solitary places.
examples.sa: येन तेनासनेनाहं यापयेयं बलान्वितः। विवेकवाससामग्रीं प्राप्नुयां सर्वजातिषु॥

examples.dm: Seeing this heap of flesh being eaten by vultures and others, Why do you honor the food of others with flower garlands, Sandalwood, and ornaments?
examples.gm: Seeing this heap of flesh, When vultures and others eat it, Why do you offer to the food of others Garlands of flowers, sandalwood, and ornaments?
examples.sa: मांसोच्छ्रयमिमं दृष्ट्वा गृध्रैरन्यैश्च भक्षितम्। आहारः पूज्यतेऽन्येषां स्रक्‍चन्दनविभूषणैः॥

examples.dm: Even the fragrance applied to the body Is that of sandalwood and the like, not of anything else. Why then do you become attached to one thing Because of the fragrance of another?
examples.gm: That scent smeared on the body Is sandalwood and so forth, nothing else; Because of that scent of another thing, Why are you attached to another?
examples.sa: काये न्यस्तोऽप्यसौ गन्धश्चन्दनादेव नान्यतः। अन्यदीयेन गन्धेन कस्मादन्यत्र रज्यसे॥

examples.dm: If the fragrance is that of sandalwood, What part of it comes from the body? Why then do you become attached to one thing Because of the fragrance of another?
examples.gm: If the sweet scent belongs to sandalwood, What does that have to do with the body here? Because of the scent of another thing, Why are you attached to another?
examples.sa: कायस्यात्र किमायातं सुगन्धि यदि चन्दनम्। अन्यदीयेन गन्धेन कस्मादन्यत्र रज्यते॥

examples.dm: By means of these and other such aspects, Having reflected upon the virtues of solitude, One should completely pacify discursive thoughts, And meditate upon the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Through these and other ways, Having considered the qualities of solitude, With discursive thoughts fully pacified, One should cultivate the awakening mind.
examples.sa: एवमादिभिराकारैर्विवेकगुणभावनात्। उपशान्तवितर्कः सन् बोधिचित्तं तु भावयेत्॥

examples.dm: Having identified oneself with those who are inferior and so forth, And having identified others as oneself, With a mind free of conceptual doubt, Meditate on envy, rivalry, and pride.
examples.gm: Having made the lower and so forth into oneself, and Having made oneself into the other, With a mind free of conceptualization, I should meditate on jealousy, rivalry, and pride.
examples.sa: हीनादिष्वात्मतां कृत्वा परत्वमपि चात्मनि। भावयेर्ष्यां च मानं च निर्विकल्पेन चेतसा॥

examples.dm: This is the conceptualization of another's mind; It is not one's own conventional reality. If that is later ascertained, then it exists; Otherwise, the conventional simply does not exist.
examples.gm: This is the conception of another mind; It is not one's own conventional reality. If it is ascertained later, it exists; If not, conventional reality itself does not exist.
examples.sa: परचित्तविकल्पोऽसौ स्वसंवृत्या तु नास्ति सः। स पश्चान्नियतः सोऽस्ति न चेन्नास्त्येव संवृतिः॥

examples.dm: What are called "continua" and "assemblies" Are false, like garlands, armies, and the like. Since there is no one who possesses suffering, Who could be the owner of this?
examples.gm: What are called a continuum and a collection Are false, like a rosary, an army, and so forth. Since there is no one who possesses suffering, Therefore, who will have control over this?
examples.sa: संतानः समुदायश्च पङ्क्तिसेनादिवन्मृषा। यस्य दुःखं स नास्त्यस्मात्कस्य तत्स्वं भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: Thus, those whose mind-streams are habituated, Finding joy in the pacification of others' suffering, Will plunge even into the Avīci hell Like swans into a lotus pond.
examples.gm: Thus, those whose continuums are accustomed, Because they delight in pacifying others' suffering, Like a swan into a lotus pool, Will plunge even into the Avīci hell.
examples.sa: एवं भावितसंतानाः परदुःखसमप्रियाः। अवीचिमवगाहन्ते हंसाः पद्मवनं यथा॥

examples.dm: To see a cause existing simultaneously with its result Is not possible; It is by relying on a single continuum That the "agent" and "experiencer" are taught.
examples.gm: That the one possessing the cause also possesses the result— To see this is impossible. It is in dependence upon a single continuum That an agent and an experiencer are taught.
examples.sa: हेतुमान् फलयोगीति दृश्यते नैष संभवः। संतानस्यैक्यमाश्रित्य कर्ता भोक्तेति देशितम्॥

examples.dm: In this regard, two kinds of worlds are seen: The yogic and the ordinary. In that regard, the ordinary world Is invalidated by the yogic world;
examples.gm: In this regard, two kinds of world are seen: Yogis and ordinary people. In this regard, the ordinary world Is invalidated by the world of yogis.
examples.sa: तत्र लोको द्विधा दृष्टो योगी प्राकृतकस्तथा। तत्र प्राकृतको लोको योगिलोकेन बाध्यते॥

examples.dm: Even yogis are superseded by those at higher and higher levels Due to differences in their intellect. Both are accepted through examples they agree upon, Because they do not analyze for the sake of the result.
examples.gm: Even yogis, due to differences in intellect, Are invalidated by successively higher ones. Through examples accepted by both, Because they are unanalyzed, for the sake of the result.
examples.sa: बाध्यन्ते धीविशेषेण योगिनोऽप्युत्तरोत्तरैः। दृष्टान्तेनोभयेष्टेन कार्यार्थमविचारतः॥

examples.dm: For that very reason, one should meditate On this analytical investigation as its antidote; The meditative concentration arising from the field of such analysis Is the food of the yogi.
examples.gm: For this very reason, the antidote to this Is to meditate on this analytical discernment; That which arises from the field of analysis Is the food of the yogi's concentration.
examples.sa: अत एव विचारोऽयं प्रतिपक्षोऽस्य भाव्यते। विकल्पक्षेत्रसंभूतध्यानाहारा हि योगिनः॥

examples.dm: Thus, it is not reasonable To direct refutations toward the position of emptiness. Therefore, without harboring any doubt, One should meditate upon emptiness.
examples.gm: Thus, toward the side of emptiness, Refutation is not appropriate. Therefore, without hesitation, One should meditate on emptiness.
examples.sa: तदेवं शून्यतापक्षे दूषणं नोपपद्यते। तस्मान्निर्विचिकित्सेन भावनीयैव शून्यता॥

examples.dm: Emptiness is the antidote To the darkness of the afflictive and cognitive obscurations. Why, then, would those who desire to swiftly attain omniscience Not meditate upon it?
examples.gm: Of the obscurations of afflictions and knowables, Emptiness is the antidote to the darkness. By one who wishes to quickly become omniscient, How could one not meditate on it?
examples.sa: क्लेशज्ञेयावृतितमःप्रतिपक्षो हि शून्यता। शीघ्रं सर्वज्ञताकामो न भावयति तां कथम्॥

examples.dm: If a valid authority is not valid, Would that which is measured by it not be false? In that case, the meditation On emptiness would be untenable.
examples.gm: If valid cognition is not valid, Is what is measured by it not false? In reality, emptiness; Meditating on it therefore becomes untenable.
examples.sa: प्रमाणमप्रमाणं चेन्ननु तत्प्रमितं मृषा। तत्त्वतः शून्यता तस्माद्भावानां नोपपद्यते॥

examples.dm: If that other mode is not real, Then describe its own inherent nature. If you say it is consciousness itself, then in that case, It would follow that all beings are one.
examples.gm: If the different guise is not true, Then explain its own nature. If you say it is consciousness itself, then in that case, It would logically follow that all people are one.
examples.sa: अन्यद्रूपमसत्यं चेन्निजं तद्रूपमुच्यताम्। ज्ञानता चेत्ततः सर्वपुंसामैक्यं प्रसज्यते॥

examples.dm: If consciousness existed prior to the object of knowledge, Then directed toward what would it arise? If consciousness and the object of knowledge are simultaneous, Then directed toward what would it arise?
examples.gm: If consciousness exists before the object of knowledge, Directed towards what would it arise? If consciousness and the object of knowledge are simultaneous, Directed towards what would it arise?
examples.sa: ज्ञेयात्पूर्वं यदि ज्ञानं किमालम्ब्यास्य संभवः। ज्ञेयेन सह चेज्ज्ञानं किमालम्ब्यास्य संभवः॥

examples.dm: For those who hold that these two are real, Their position is extremely difficult to maintain. If the object is established through the power of consciousness, What basis is there for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.gm: According to those who hold these two to be true, That very position rests in great difficulty. If the object is established by the power of consciousness, What is the basis for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.sa: यस्य त्वेतद्द्वयं सत्यं स एवात्यन्तदुःस्थितः। यदि ज्ञेयवशादर्थो ज्ञानास्तित्वे तु का गतिः॥

examples.dm: Such being the case, what discerning person Would be attached to forms that are like a dream? When the body is thus non-existent, Then who is a man and who is a woman?
examples.gm: Thus, what intelligent person would be attached To form, which is like a dream? When the body does not exist in that way, Then what is a man and what is a woman?
examples.sa: एवं स्वप्नोपमे रूपे को रज्येत विचारकः। कायश्चैवं यदा नास्ति तदा का स्त्री पुमांश्च कः॥

examples.dm: Since seeing and even touching Are of the nature of dreams and illusions, And arise simultaneously with the mind, That feeling is not seen by it.
examples.gm: Seeing or even touching, Have a nature like a dream or an illusion. Because it arises simultaneously with the mind, Feeling is not perceived by it.
examples.sa: दृश्यते स्पृश्यते चापि स्वप्नमायोपमात्मना। चित्तेन सहजातत्वाद्वेदना तेन नेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: Thus, when a son dies in a dream, The conceptual thought that he does not exist Is an obstacle to the conceptual thought that he exists, And yet that [thought] is also false.
examples.gm: Thus, when a child dies in a dream, The conceptualization thinking, "He does not exist," For the conceptualization of his existence Is the block, and that is also false.

examples.dm: For that very reason, one should meditate On this analytical investigation as its antidote; The meditative concentration arising from the field of such analysis Is the food of the yogi.
examples.gm: For this very reason, the antidote to this Is to meditate on this analytical discernment; That which arises from the field of analysis Is the food of the yogi's concentration.
examples.sa: अत एव विचारोऽयं प्रतिपक्षोऽस्य भाव्यते। विकल्पक्षेत्रसंभूतध्यानाहारा हि योगिनः॥

examples.dm: When one analyzes with an analysis That is itself being analyzed, Then because that analysis is also to be analyzed, There is no end to it.
examples.gm: When analysis Is analyzed by analysis, Then that analysis too, Because it is analyzed, has no end.
examples.sa: विचारितेन तु यदा विचारोऽन्येन विचार्यते। तदानवस्था तस्यापि विचारस्य विचारणात्॥

examples.dm: Life passes by quickly and meaninglessly, And analytical discernment is extremely difficult to find. Moreover, when one is habituated to such distractions, Where is there any means to turn them back?
examples.gm: Life passes quickly and meaninglessly; Discernment is extremely hard to find. And there, as for habituation to distraction, Where is the method to reverse it?
examples.sa: वृथैवायुर्वहत्याशु विवेकस्तत्र दुर्लभः। तत्राप्यभ्यस्तविक्षेपनिवारणगतिः कुतः॥

examples.dm: Although great fruits arise from the aspiring mind While wandering in cyclic existence, It does not produce a continuous flow of merit In the way that the engaging mind does.
examples.gm: From the mind aspiring to awakening, Great fruits arise while in cyclic existence, but Unlike the mind entering awakening, A continuous stream of merit does not arise.
examples.sa: बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तस्य संसारेऽपि फलं महत्। न त्वविच्छिन्नपुण्यत्वं यथा प्रस्थानचेतसः॥

examples.dm: In the cycle of existence, through patience one attains beauty and the like, As well as health and renown, A very long life, And the extensive happiness of a universal monarch.
examples.gm: While in saṃsāra, through patience, beauty and the like, Health, and fame, An extremely long life, and The vast happiness of a universal monarch are attained.
examples.sa: प्रासादिकत्वमारोग्यं प्रामोद्यं चिरजीवितम्। चक्रवर्तिसुखं स्फीतं क्षमी प्राप्नोति संसरन्॥

examples.dm: In all the various circles of retinues, May many Bodhisattvas Dwell, having adorned the surface of the earth With their own excellence.
examples.gm: In all the circles of retinues that exist, May many bodhisattvas Adorn the surface of the earth with their excellence, And remain dwelling there.
examples.sa: बोधिसत्त्वमहापर्षन्मण्डलानि समन्ततः। निषीदन्तु स्वशोभाभिर्मण्डयन्तु महीतलम्॥

examples.dm: From this moment onward, even while sleeping or Becoming heedless, a force of merit Continuous and manifold Will arise, as vast as space.
examples.gm: From then on, even while asleep Or inattentive, a force of merit, Uninterrupted and manifold, Continually arises, equal to the sky.
examples.sa: ततःप्रभृति सुप्तस्य प्रमत्तस्याप्यनेकशः। अविच्छिन्नाः पुण्यधाराः प्रवर्तन्ते नभःसमाः॥

examples.dm: O Protectors, because I was heedless And did not recognize such terrors as these, For the sake of this transient life, I have committed many sins.
examples.gm: O Protectors, I, being careless, Unaware of such danger as this, For the sake of this impermanent life, Have committed many non-virtues.
examples.sa: अनित्यजीवितासङ्गादिदं भयमजानता। प्रमत्तेन मया नाथा बहु पापमुपार्जितम्॥

examples.dm: If, through heedlessness, you do not give yourself to sentient beings, You will certainly hand me over to the guardians of hell.
examples.gm: If, becoming careless, I do not give you to sentient beings, You will surely hand me over To the guards of hell.
examples.sa: त्वां सत्त्वेषु न दास्यामि यदि नाम प्रमोदतः। त्वं मां नरकपालेषु प्रदास्यसि न संशयः॥

examples.dm: In order to fully embrace that precious mind, I make excellent offerings to the Tathāgatas, To the stainless Jewel of the sublime Dharma, And to the Sons of the Buddha, those oceans of virtue.
examples.gm: In order to take hold of that precious mind, To the Tathāgatas and the holy Dharma, The stainless Jewel, and the Children of the Buddhas, Who are oceans of qualities, I make excellent offerings.
examples.sa: तच्चित्तरत्नग्रहणाय सम्यक् पूजां करोम्येष तथागतानाम्। सद्धर्मरत्नस्य च निर्मलस्य बुद्धात्मजानां च गुणोदधीनाम्॥

examples.dm: To those who are oceans of excellence, I offer praise with oceans of melodic branches. May those clouds of melodious songs of praise Certainly arise in every way.
examples.gm: To those who are oceans of qualities, I Offer praise with oceans of limbs of melodious praise. May sweet clouds of songs of praise Certainly arise everywhere for them.
examples.sa: स्वराङ्गसागरैः स्तोत्रैः स्तौमि चाहं गुणोदधीन्। स्तुतिसंगीतिमेघाश्च संभवन्त्वेष्वनन्यथा॥

examples.dm: Since they possess a share in accomplishing the qualities of a Buddha, They are therefore asserted to be equal. Yet no one is equal to the Buddhas, Who are infinite oceans of excellence.
examples.gm: Because they have a share in accomplishing a Buddha's qualities, Therefore they are asserted to be equal. Yet, regarding the boundless ocean of qualities, No one is equal to the Buddhas.
examples.sa: बुद्धधर्मागमांशेन तस्मात्सत्त्वा जिनैः समाः। न तु बुद्धैः समाः केचिदनन्तांशैर्गुणार्णवैः॥

examples.dm: To the Victors and their spiritual heirs, I offer my entire body forever. O Supreme Beings, please accept me completely; With devotion, I shall become your servant.
examples.gm: To the Conquerors and their Children, I Offer my entire body forever. Supreme Beings, please accept me completely; With devotion I will become your subject.
examples.sa: ददामि चात्मानमहं जिनेभ्यः सर्वेण सर्वं च तदात्मजेभ्यः। परिग्रहं मे कुरुताग्रसत्त्वा युष्मासु दासत्वमुपैमि भक्त्या॥

examples.dm: How can merit from an illusory Conqueror Be the same as if he were truly existent? If sentient beings are like illusions, Then how are they reborn after death?
examples.gm: Merit from a Victorious One who is like an illusion Is just as it is for one who truly exists. "If sentient beings are like illusions, How are they born after dying?"
examples.sa: मायोपमाज्जिनात्पुण्यं सद्भावेऽपि कथं यथा। यदि मायोपमः सत्त्वः किं पुनर्जायते मृतः॥

examples.dm: Three times during the day and three times at night, One should recite the Three Heaps Sūtra; By relying on the Victors and the spirit of awakening, One should pacify the remaining downfalls.
examples.gm: Three times during the day and night, One should recite the Triskandha; By relying on the Conquerors and the awakening mind, One should pacify the remainder of downfalls thereby.
examples.sa: रात्रिंदिवं च त्रिस्कन्धं त्रिष्कालं च प्रवर्तयेत्। शेषापत्तिशमस्तेन बोधिचित्तजिनाश्रयात्॥

examples.dm: To the Lords of Sages, the supreme objects of veneration, I offer delightful Mandārava flowers, lotuses, Utpalas, and all other fragrant blossoms, As well as beautifully arranged and enchanting garlands.
examples.gm: To the Lords of Capable Ones, the supreme objects of offering, with pleasing Mandāra flowers and lotuses, Utpalas, and all fragrant things, And beautifully strung, pleasing garlands, I make offerings.
examples.sa: मान्दारवेन्दीवरमल्लिकाद्यैः सर्वैः सुगन्धैः कुसुमैर्मनोज्ञैः। अभ्यर्चयाभ्यर्च्यतमान् मुनीन्द्रान् स्रग्भिश्च संस्थानमनोरमाभिः॥

examples.dm: Abiding within the heart of a vast, fragrant, and cool lotus, Their splendor nourished by the food of the Victorious One's melodious speech, Possessing a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through their virtue they become a Son of the Sugata dwelling in the presence of the Victorious One.
examples.gm: Dwelling in the core of a vast, fragrant, and cooling lotus, Whose splendor is produced by the food of the Victor's sweet speech, With a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through wholesome deeds one becomes a son of the Sugata dwelling before the Victor.
examples.sa: विपुलसुगन्धिशीतलसरोरुहगर्भगता मधुरजिनस्वराशनकृतोपचितद्युतयः। मुनिकरबोधिताम्बुजविनिर्गतसद्वपुषः सुगतसुता भवन्ति सुगतस्य पुरः कुशलैः॥

examples.dm: Having abandoned the young lotus Opened by the rays of a cloudless sun, Why does your mind, with its attachment to the impure, Take delight in a cage of filth?
examples.gm: Opened by the rays of a cloudless sun, Abandoning a fresh lotus, With a mind attached to filth, Why do you delight in a cage of filth?
examples.sa: विघनार्कांशुविकचं मुक्त्वा तरुणपङ्कजम्। अमेध्यशौण्डचित्तस्य का रतिर्गूथपञ्जरे॥

examples.dm: Upon all the jewels of the sublime Dharma, And upon the reliquaries and the sacred images, May a rain of precious flowers and the like Fall in a continuous, uninterrupted stream.
examples.gm: Upon all the rare and supreme holy Dharma, Stūpas, and images, May a rain of jewels, flowers, and the like, Fall without interruption.
examples.sa: सर्वसद्धर्मरत्नेषु चैत्येषु प्रतिमासु च। पुष्परत्नादिवर्षाश्च प्रवर्तन्तां निरन्तरम्॥

examples.dm: Toward those who revile and destroy Sacred images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, It is not appropriate for me to feel hatred, For the Buddhas and the like cannot be harmed.
examples.gm: Towards images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, Even if someone disparages or destroys them, It is inappropriate for me to have anger, For the Buddhas and so forth suffer no harm.
examples.sa: प्रतिमास्तूपसद्धर्मनाशकाक्रोशकेषु च। न युज्यते मम द्वेषो बुद्धादीनां न हि व्यथा॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to the foundations of the awakening mind and to the reliquaries; I prostrate to the preceptors, the masters, And to those who maintain the supreme ascetic discipline.
examples.gm: To the bases of the awakening mind, And to the stūpas, I pay homage. To the preceptors and likewise the teachers, And to the supreme practitioners, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वचैत्यानि वन्देऽहं बोधिसत्त्वाश्रयांस्तथा। नमः करोम्युपाध्यायानभिवन्द्यान् यतींस्तथा॥

examples.dm: To all the Buddhas of the three times, And to the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With as many bodies as there are atoms in the realms, I bow down and pay homage.
examples.gm: To all the Buddhas who have gone in the three times, Along with the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With bodies as numerous as all the atoms in the fields, Bowing down, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वक्षेत्राणुसंख्यैश्च प्रणामैः प्रणमाम्यहम्। सर्वत्र्यध्वगतान् बुद्धान् सहधर्मगणोत्तमान्॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to the foundations of the awakening mind and to the reliquaries; I prostrate to the preceptors, the masters, And to those who maintain the supreme ascetic discipline.
examples.gm: To the bases of the awakening mind, And to the stūpas, I pay homage. To the preceptors and likewise the teachers, And to the supreme practitioners, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वचैत्यानि वन्देऽहं बोधिसत्त्वाश्रयांस्तथा। नमः करोम्युपाध्यायानभिवन्द्यान् यतींस्तथा॥

examples.dm: In the presence of the Protectors, openly, With palms joined and a mind fearful of suffering, I prostrate again and again, And I confess all of these.
examples.gm: Directly in the presence of the protectors, With palms joined and a mind terrified of suffering, Bowing down again and again, I will confess all of them.
examples.sa: तत्सर्वं देशयाम्येष नाथानामग्रतः स्थितः। कृताञ्जलिर्दुःखभीतः प्रणिपत्य पुनः पुनः॥

examples.dm: Whatever sins I, a sinner stained by many faults, Have committed through my many transgressions, Those extremely unbearable deeds, I confess to all the Guides.
examples.gm: Defiled by many faults, Whatever non-virtues I, a sinner, Have committed that are extremely unbearable, I confess them all to the Guides.
examples.sa: अनेकदोषदुष्टेन मया पापेन नायकाः। यत्कृतं दारुणं पापं तत्सर्वं देशयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: The Guide first engages one in the giving of things such as vegetables; Once accustomed to that, one later gradually gives even one's own flesh.
examples.gm: Even in the giving of vegetables and so forth, The Guide initially engages one. Having become accustomed to that, later on, One will gradually give away even one's own flesh.
examples.sa: आदौ शाकादिदानेऽपि नियोजयति नायकः। तत्करोति क्रमात्पश्चाद्यत्स्वमांसान्यपि त्यजेत्॥

examples.dm: I pray that the Guides will regard my sins As the transgressions they are. Since this was not good, Henceforth, I shall never do it again.
examples.gm: I beseech the guides to accept my negative deeds As being faults. Since this is not good, From now on I will not do them.
examples.sa: अत्ययमत्ययत्वेन प्रतिगृह्णन्तु नायकाः। न भद्रकमिदं नाथा न कर्तव्यं पुनर्मया॥

examples.dm: When seized by the messengers of the Lord of Death, What help are kinsmen, and what help are friends? At that time, merit alone provides protection, Yet that is what I have failed to cultivate.
examples.gm: When seized by the messengers of Yama, What good are relatives, what good are friends? At that time, merit alone is a protection, But I have not relied upon it.
examples.sa: यमदूतैर्गृहीतस्य कुतो बन्धुः कुतः सुहृत्। पुण्यमेकं तदा त्राणं मया तच्च न सेवितम्॥

examples.dm: With eyes red and swollen from the force of grief, Tears will stream down your face; As your relatives lose all hope, You will gaze upon the faces of the messengers of the Lord of Death.
examples.gm: Swollen by the force of sorrow, Red eyes shedding tears upon their faces, Relatives having lost hope, And looking at the faces of Yama's messengers.
examples.sa: शोकवेगसमुच्छूनसाश्रुरक्तेक्षणाननान्। बन्धून्निराशान् संपश्यन् यमदूतमुखानि च॥

examples.dm: Seized by the messengers of the Lord of Death, who have such terrifying forms, And stricken by the great illness of fear, What need is there to mention my extreme distress?
examples.gm: Seized by the messengers of Yama With their terrifying physical appearances, And struck by the great terrifying disease, What need to mention my utter misery?
examples.sa: किं पुनर्भैरवाकारैर्यमदूतैरधिष्ठितः। महात्रासज्वरग्रस्तः पुरीषोत्सर्गवेष्टितः॥

examples.dm: O Protectors, because I was heedless And did not recognize such terrors as these, For the sake of this transient life, I have committed many sins.
examples.gm: O Protectors, I, being careless, Unaware of such danger as this, For the sake of this impermanent life, Have committed many non-virtues.
examples.sa: अनित्यजीवितासङ्गादिदं भयमजानता। प्रमत्तेन मया नाथा बहु पापमुपार्जितम्॥

examples.dm: Since all is impermanent, who that is impermanent Would feel a true attachment to another? Because of that, for thousands of lifetimes, One will never again see the beloved.
examples.gm: What impermanent being Would be truly attached to the impermanent? Through that, for thousands of lifetimes, They will not see their loved ones.
examples.sa: कस्यानित्येष्वनित्यस्य स्नेहो भवितुमर्हति। येन जन्मसहस्राणि द्रष्टव्यो न पुनः प्रियः॥

examples.dm: However, because earth and the others are multiple, Impermanent, inert, and not divine, And because they are things to be trodden upon and are impure, They are not Īśvara himself.
examples.gm: However, earth and so forth are multiple, Impermanent, devoid of movement, not divine, Objects to be stepped upon, and impure; They are not Īśvara himself.
examples.sa: अपि त्वनेकेऽनित्याश्च निश्चेष्टा न च देवताः। लङ्घ्याश्चाशुचयश्चैव क्ष्मादयो न स ईश्वरः॥

examples.dm: I joyfully rejoice in the virtue that relieves The suffering of all sentient beings in the lower realms, And in the abiding in happiness of those who suffer, With a heart full of delight.
examples.gm: Of the lower realms of all sentient beings, In the virtue that relieves suffering, and In suffering beings abiding in happiness, With joy I rejoice.
examples.sa: अपायदुःखविश्रामं सर्वसत्त्वैः कृतं शुभम्। अनुमोदे प्रमोदेन सुखं तिष्ठन्तु दुःखिताः॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: I joyfully rejoice in the ocean of virtue That is the generation of the mind of awakening, which brings happiness to all sentient beings, And in the deeds that benefit all sentient beings, With a heart full of delight.
examples.gm: Bringing happiness to all sentient beings, In the ocean of virtue of generating the awakening mind, and In the deeds that benefit sentient beings, With joy I rejoice.
examples.sa: चित्तोत्पादसमुद्रांश्च सर्वसत्त्वसुखावहान्। सर्वसत्त्वहिताधानाननुमोदे च शासिनाम्॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: If the perfection of generosity Consisted in the removal of the world's poverty, Then since beings are still destitute today, How could the Protectors of the past have reached that perfection?
examples.gm: If by eliminating the poverty of wandering beings, The perfection of generosity is achieved, Since there are still destitute beings, how did the past Saviors achieve the perfection?
examples.sa: अदरिद्रं जगत्कृत्वा दानपारमिता यदि। जगद्दरिद्रमद्यापि सा कथं पूर्वतायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: Today, in the presence of all the Protectors, I invite the world to the state of the Sugatas and to temporal happiness; Since I have invited you as my guests to this bliss, May the gods, asuras, and all others rejoice!
examples.gm: Today, by me, in the presence of all the protectors, Wandering beings to Sugatahood itself, and Until then, to happiness, have been invited as guests; Let gods, asuras, and others rejoice!
examples.sa: जगदद्य निमन्त्रितं मया सुगतत्वेन सुखेन चान्तरा। पुरतः खलु सर्वतायिनामभिनन्दन्तु सुरासुरादयः॥

examples.dm: By renouncing everything, one transcends suffering, And my mind seeks to achieve that transcendence; Since I must give everything away at once, It is best to give it to all sentient beings.
examples.gm: By giving up everything, nirvana is attained, And my mind seeks to accomplish nirvana. Since I must part with everything at once, It is best given to sentient beings.
examples.sa: सर्वत्यागश्च निर्वाणं निर्वाणार्थि च मे मनः। त्यक्तव्यं चेन्मया सर्वं वरं सत्त्वेषु दीयताम्॥

examples.dm: If the root of the teaching is the monkhood itself, Then even being a monk is a difficult state to maintain. For those whose minds are still directed toward objects, Even nirvana is a difficult state to maintain.
examples.gm: If being a monk is the root of the teaching, Even being a monk is difficult to establish. For those whose minds have apprehension, Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.
examples.sa: शासनं भिक्षुतामूलं भिक्षुतैव च दुःस्थिता। सावलम्बनचित्तानां निर्वाणमपि दुःस्थितम्॥

examples.dm: When the object of analysis is thoroughly analyzed, There is no basis remaining for the analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that is described as nirvana.
examples.gm: If the object of analysis has been analyzed, There is no basis for analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that too is expressed as nirvāṇa.
examples.sa: विचारिते विचार्ये तु विचारस्यास्ति नाश्रयः। निराश्रितत्वान्नोदेति तच्च निर्वाणमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: Today my life has become fruitful; I have well obtained this human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; I have now become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.gm: Today my life is fruitful; I have well obtained a human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; Today I have become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: अद्य मे सफलं जन्म सुलब्धो मानुषो भवः। अद्य बुद्धकुले जातो बुद्धपुत्रोऽस्मि सांप्रतम्॥

examples.dm: From now on, by any means necessary, I shall undertake actions befitting this lineage, And act in such a way that I do not defile This faultless and noble lineage.
examples.gm: Now I must, whatever happens, Undertake actions in accord with the family, And upon this flawless, noble family, Bring no stain—thus shall I act.
examples.sa: तथाधुना मया कार्यं स्वकुलोचितकारिणाम्। निर्मलस्य कुलस्यास्य कलङ्को न भवेद्यथा॥

examples.dm: It is said that this miserable one is even competing with me. But is he my equal in learning, wisdom, Physical appearance, lineage, or wealth?
examples.gm: This miserable one is even renowned To be contending together with me. Are his learning and wisdom, or Form, caste, and wealth equal to mine?
examples.sa: अस्यापि हि वराकस्य स्पर्धा किल मया सह। किमस्य श्रुतमेतावत् प्रज्ञा रूपं कुलं धनम्॥

examples.dm: If it is said that even regarding a minor, ordinary object, A person who intends in their mind to give it, But then does not give it, Will become a hungry ghost,
examples.gm: Even regarding a slight, ordinary thing, Having intended in one's mind to give it, Whatever person does not give it, If it is said that they will become a hungry ghost,
examples.sa: मनसा चिन्तयित्वापि यो न दद्यात्पुनर्नरः। स प्रेतो भवतीत्युक्तमल्पमात्रेऽपि वस्तुनि॥

examples.dm: May animals be free from the fear Of preying upon one another; And just like the people of the Northern Continent, May the hungry ghosts become happy.
examples.gm: May animals be freed From the fear of eating one another. Just like the humans of Uttarakuru, May the hungry ghosts become happy.
examples.sa: शाम्यन्तु वेदनास्तीव्रा नारकाणां भयानि च। दुर्गतिभ्यो विमुच्यन्तां सर्वदुर्गतिवासिनः॥

examples.dm: By the stream of milk flowing From the hand of the noble Avalokiteśvara, May the hungry ghosts be satisfied, And by bathing in it, may they be forever cooled.
examples.gm: Of noble Avalokiteśvara, By the stream of milk flowing from his hands, May the hungry ghosts be satisfied, And having bathed, may they always be cooled.
examples.sa: अन्योन्यभक्षणभयं तिरश्चामपगच्छतु। भवन्तु सुखिनः प्रेता यथोत्तरकुरौ नराः॥

examples.dm: Thus, if powerful downfalls and the power of bodhicitta alternate and contend within cyclic existence, It will take a very long time to attain the bodhisattva grounds.
examples.gm: Thus, with powerful downfalls, And the powerful awakening mind, If they alternate in saṃsāra, It will take a long time to attain the grounds.
examples.sa: एवमापत्तिबलतो बोधिचित्तबलेन च। दोलायमानः संसारे भूमिप्राप्तौ चिरायते॥११

examples.dm: However, because earth and the others are multiple, Impermanent, inert, and not divine, And because they are things to be trodden upon and are impure, They are not Īśvara himself.
examples.gm: However, earth and so forth are multiple, Impermanent, devoid of movement, not divine, Objects to be stepped upon, and impure; They are not Īśvara himself.
examples.sa: अपि त्वनेकेऽनित्याश्च निश्चेष्टा न च देवताः। लङ्घ्याश्चाशुचयश्चैव क्ष्मादयो न स ईश्वरः॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, what is it that he is asserted to produce? Are not the self, the earth, and so forth, And the nature of Īśvara himself, also eternal? Since consciousness arises from objects of knowledge,
examples.gm: And what is it that he wishes to produce? Are not the self, those such as earth, And the essence of Īśvara permanent? Consciousness arises from the object of knowledge, and
examples.sa: तेन किं स्रष्टुमिष्टं च आत्मा चेत् नन्वसौ ध्रुवः। क्ष्मादिस्वभाव ईशश्च ज्ञानं ज्ञेयादनादि च॥

examples.dm: It is as if I have been rendered senseless by a magic spell; I am here utterly without my mind. I do not even know what has deluded me, Or what it is that dwells within me.
examples.gm: As if bewildered by a mantra, I am reduced to having no mind here. Even I do not know what bewilders me; What is there inside me?
examples.sa: अत्र मे चेतना नास्ति मन्त्रैरिव विमोहितः। न जाने केन मुह्यामि कोऽत्रान्तर्मम तिष्ठति॥

examples.dm: One who has become a vessel for the vast Dharma Should not be applied to the lesser Dharma. One must not completely forsake proper conduct, Nor deceive others with Sutra or Mantra.
examples.gm: One who is a vessel for the vast Dharma Should not be engaged in the inferior Dharma; Conduct should not be completely cast aside, Nor should they be deceived with sutras and mantras.
examples.sa: नोदारधर्मपात्रं च हीने धर्मे नियोजयेत्। न चाचारं परित्यज्य सूत्रमन्त्रैः प्रलोभयेत्॥

examples.dm: Because mantras and such lack the capacity, An illusory mind does not arise from them. Arising from various conditions, That illusion is itself of various kinds.
examples.gm: Because mantras and so forth lack the capacity, Illusory minds do not arise. Arising from various conditions, Illusions themselves are also various.
examples.sa: मन्त्रादीनामसामर्थ्यान्न मायाचित्तसंभवः । सापि नानाविधा माया नानाप्रत्ययसंभवा॥

examples.dm: These enemies, such as hatred and craving, Possess neither hands, feet, nor other limbs; They are neither brave nor wise, yet somehow, They have made me their slave.
examples.gm: The enemies of hatred, craving, and so forth, Do not have arms, legs, and so forth, And though neither brave nor wise, how is it That they have made me like a slave?
examples.sa: हस्तपादादिरहितास्तृष्णाद्वेषादिशत्रवः। न शूरा न च ते प्राज्ञाः कथं दासीकृतोऽस्मि तैः॥

examples.dm: From what do happiness and suffering arise? What is there to be displeased with, and what is there to be pleased with? When searched for in that very reality, Who is it that craves, and for what do they crave?
examples.gm: From what are happiness and suffering? What is there to displease, what is there to please? If searched for in reality, Who is craving and for what do they crave?
examples.sa: कुतः सुखं वा दुःखं वा किं प्रियं वा किमप्रियम्। का तृष्णा कुत्र सा तृष्णा मृग्यमाणा स्वभावतः॥

examples.dm: This body is like a human-shaped abscess, Painful and unable to bear being touched. Since I, blinded by craving, have grasped it, At whom should I be angry when it is harmed?
examples.gm: Like a human-shaped ulcer, Painful and unable to bear being touched; When, blinded by craving, I have grasped it, When it is harmed, at whom should I be angry?
examples.sa: गण्डोऽयं प्रतिमाकारो गृहीतो घट्टनासहः। तृष्णान्धेन मया तत्र व्यथायां कुत्र कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: If the perfection of generosity Consisted in the removal of the world's poverty, Then since beings are still destitute today, How could the Protectors of the past have reached that perfection?
examples.gm: If by eliminating the poverty of wandering beings, The perfection of generosity is achieved, Since there are still destitute beings, how did the past Saviors achieve the perfection?
examples.sa: अदरिद्रं जगत्कृत्वा दानपारमिता यदि। जगद्दरिद्रमद्यापि सा कथं पूर्वतायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: One should practice the perfections, such as generosity, In an ever-ascending degree of excellence. One should not sacrifice a great benefit for a small one; The primary consideration should be the welfare of others.
examples.gm: The perfection of generosity and the rest, Should be practiced, progressing higher and higher. One should not abandon the greater for the lesser. Principally, one should consider the benefit of others.
examples.sa: उत्तरोत्तरतः श्रेष्ठा दानपारमितादयः। नेतरार्थं त्यजेच्छ्रेष्ठामन्यत्राचारसेतुतः॥

examples.dm: The perfection of generosity is said to be the mind Of relinquishing all possessions, together with their results, To all beings; Therefore, it is the mind itself.
examples.gm: All possessions together with their fruits, By the mind giving them to all people, The perfection of generosity is taught; Therefore, it is simply the mind itself.
examples.sa: फलेन सह सर्वस्वत्यागचित्ताज्जनेऽखिले। दानपारमिता प्रोक्ता तस्मात्सा चित्तमेव तु॥

examples.dm: If the perfection of generosity Consisted in the removal of the world's poverty, Then since beings are still destitute today, How could the Protectors of the past have reached that perfection?
examples.gm: If by eliminating the poverty of wandering beings, The perfection of generosity is achieved, Since there are still destitute beings, how did the past Saviors achieve the perfection?
examples.sa: अदरिद्रं जगत्कृत्वा दानपारमिता यदि। जगद्दरिद्रमद्यापि सा कथं पूर्वतायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: The perfection of generosity is said to be the mind Of relinquishing all possessions, together with their results, To all beings; Therefore, it is the mind itself.
examples.gm: All possessions together with their fruits, By the mind giving them to all people, The perfection of generosity is taught; Therefore, it is simply the mind itself.
examples.sa: फलेन सह सर्वस्वत्यागचित्ताज्जनेऽखिले। दानपारमिता प्रोक्ता तस्मात्सा चित्तमेव तु॥

examples.dm: To what place could fish and other creatures be moved So that they would not be killed? The perfection of ethical discipline is explained As the attainment of the mind of renunciation.
examples.gm: Where could fish and so forth Be driven away so that they are not killed? From attaining the mind of renunciation, The perfection of moral discipline is explained.
examples.sa: मत्स्यादयः क्व नीयन्तां मारयेयं यतो न तान्। लब्धे विरतिचित्ते तु शीलपारमिता मता॥

examples.dm: Having thus gained self-mastery, Always maintain a smiling countenance; Completely abandon frowning and scowling, And be a friend to all beings and speak sincerely.
examples.gm: Thus, since you are in control, Always bear a smiling face. Completely abandon frowns and grimaces, Be an honest friend to wandering beings.
examples.sa: एवं वशीकृतस्वात्मा नित्यं स्मितमुखो भवेत्। त्यजेद् भृकुटिसंकोचं पूर्वाभाषी जगत्सुहृत्॥

examples.dm: All faults, as many as there are, And various kinds of misdeeds, All arise through the power of conditions; They do not possess any independence.
examples.gm: All however many faults there are, and Various kinds of sins— All these arise from the power of conditions; They do not possess independence.
examples.sa: ये केचिदपराधाश्च पापानि विविधानि च। सर्वं तत्प्रत्ययबलात् स्वतन्त्रं तु न विद्यते॥

examples.dm: If they are nothing but skeletons and nothing else, And are neither independent nor a self, Why, after desiring them intensely and becoming thoroughly attached, Do you not go to the state beyond sorrow?
examples.gm: Are nothing but skeletons, nothing else. Being neither independent nor a self, Strongly desiring and fully clinging to them, Why do you not proceed to nirvāṇa?
examples.sa: तान्येवास्थीनि नान्यानि स्वाधीनान्यममानि च। प्रकामं संपरिष्वज्य किं न गच्छसि निर्वृतिम्॥

examples.dm: Learn the manner of relying on a guru As described in the life story of Śrīsambhava; This and other teachings of the Buddha Are to be understood by reading the sūtras.
examples.gm: From the liberation story of Śrīsaṃbhava, One should train in the manner of relying on the guru; This and other words spoken by the Buddha, Should be known after reading the sūtras.
examples.sa: श्रीसंभवविमोक्षाच्च शिक्षेद्यद्गुरुवर्तनम्। एतच्चान्यच्च बुद्धोक्तं ज्ञेयं सूत्रान्तवाचनात्॥

examples.dm: If you accept that any speech which accords with the sutras is the word of the Buddha, Then why do you not accept the majority of the Mahayana, Which is similar to your own sutras?
examples.gm: If any speech that enters into the sūtras Is asserted to be spoken by the Buddha, Is it not asserted that the majority of the Mahāyāna Is equal to your sūtras?
examples.sa: यत्सूत्रेऽवतरेद्वाक्यं तच्चेद्बुद्धोक्तमिष्यते । महायानं भवत्सूत्रैः प्रायस्तुल्यं न किं मतम् ॥

examples.dm: The trainings are revealed within the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, in particular, Should be looked at first of all.
examples.gm: The trainings appear in the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, Should be looked at from the very beginning.
examples.sa: शिक्षाः सूत्रेषु दृश्यन्ते तस्मात्सूत्राणि वाचयेत्। आकाशगर्भसूत्रे च मूलापत्तीर्निरूपयेत्॥

examples.dm: Whatever virtuous deeds have been accumulated, Such as generosity and offerings to the Sugatas, Over a thousand eons, A single moment of anger destroys them all.
examples.gm: Accumulated over a thousand eons, Generosity, offerings to the Sugatas, and so forth— Whatever good conduct there is, all of that, A single moment of anger destroys.
examples.sa: सर्वमेतत्सुचरितं दानं सुगतपूजनम्। कृतं कल्पसहस्रैर्यत्प्रतिघः प्रतिहन्ति तत्॥

examples.dm: They are jealous of superiors and competitive with equals; They are arrogant toward inferiors and conceited when praised. If something unpleasant is said, they become angry; When could one ever receive benefit from a fool?
examples.gm: Envious of superiors, competitive with equals, Arrogant toward inferiors, conceited when praised, And prone to anger when spoken to unpleasantly— When is benefit ever obtained from the childish?
examples.sa: ईर्ष्योत्कृष्टात्समाद्द्‍वन्द्वो हीनान्मानः स्तुतेर्मदः। अवर्णात्प्रतिघश्चेति कदा बालाद्धितं भवेत्॥

examples.dm: By following the dictates of the body, I have accumulated meaningless suffering; What is the use of attachment or anger Toward this thing that is just like a piece of wood?
examples.gm: By taking care of the body, Having accumulated meaningless suffering, Attachment and anger— What use are they for this thing similar to wood?
examples.sa: शरीरपक्षपातेन वृथा दुःखमुपार्ज्यते। किमस्य काष्ठतुल्यस्य द्वेषेणानुनयेन वा॥

examples.dm: That which is desired as the "Primal Substance" And that which is imputed as the "Self," Do not arise by intentionally thinking, "I shall come into being."
examples.gm: Whatever is asserted as the "Primary Matter," and Whatever is imputed as the "Self"— Thinking, "I myself shall arise," They do not purposefully arise.
examples.sa: यत्प्रधानं किलाभीष्टं यत्तदात्मेति कल्पितम्। तदेव हि भवाभीति न संचिन्त्योपजायते॥

examples.dm: Those who claim that atoms are eternal Have already been refuted previously. The Sāṃkhyas assert that a permanent Primal Substance Is the cause of the world.
examples.gm: As for those who assert permanent atoms, They have also already been refuted earlier. The permanent Pradhāna is the cause of beings; This is what the Sāṃkhyas assert.
examples.sa: येऽपि नित्यानणूनाहुस्तेऽपि पूर्वं निवारिताः। सांख्याः प्रधानमिच्छन्ति नित्यं लोकस्य कारणम्॥

examples.dm: The equilibrium of the qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas Is proclaimed to be the Primal Substance; Their disequilibrium is said to be the world.
examples.gm: The qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, Abiding in equilibrium, Are termed Pradhāna; In disequilibrium, they are said to be beings.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति गुणा अविषमस्थिताः। प्रधानमिति कथ्यन्ते विषमैर्जगदुच्यते॥

examples.dm: If that self were permanent, It would clearly be inactive, like space. Even if it were to encounter other conditions, What could they do to something that is unchanging?
examples.gm: If that self is permanent, Like space, it is evidently inactive. Even if it meets with other conditions, What can be done to the unchanging?
examples.sa: नित्यो ह्यचेतनश्चात्मा व्योमवत् स्फुटमक्रियः। प्रत्ययान्तरसङ्गेऽपि निर्विकारस्य का क्रिया॥

examples.dm: Even the parts are reduced to atoms, And those atoms are divided into directional facets. Since the directional facets are also devoid of parts, They are like space; therefore, even atoms do not exist.
examples.gm: And the part also by its division into particles, And that particle also by its division into directional parts, And since the division of directions is devoid of parts, It is like space; therefore, even particles do not exist.
examples.sa: अंशा अप्यणुभेदेन सोऽप्यणुर्दिग्विभागतः। दिग्विभागो निरंशत्वादाकाशं तेन नास्त्यणुः॥

examples.dm: Īśvara is not space, because space is inert; He is not the self, as that has already been refuted. And if the creator is also inconceivable, What is the point of speaking of him as "inconceivable"?
examples.gm: Īśvara is not space, because it is devoid of movement; He is not the self, because it was already refuted before; And as for a creator who is inconceivable, What is the use of speaking of the inconceivable?
examples.sa: नाकाशमीशोऽचेष्टत्वात् नात्मा पूर्वनिषेधतः। अचिन्त्यस्य च कर्तृत्वमप्यचिन्त्यं किमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the guardians of hell And the forest of sword-leaves are produced By one's own karma, At whom should I be angry?
examples.gm: Like the guardians of hell, And the forest of sword-leaves, This is produced by my own karma, So at whom should I be angry?
examples.sa: असिपत्रवनं यद्वद्यथा नारकपक्षिणः। मत्कर्मजनिता एव तथेदं कुत्र कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: This hook cast by the fisherman of the afflictions Is an unbearable barb; Having been caught by it, you will surely be boiled In the cauldrons of hell by the hell-guardians.
examples.gm: This hook, cast by the fisherman of the afflictions, Is an unbearable barb. Caught by it, in the cauldrons of hell, The guardians of hell will boil me.
examples.sa: एतद्धि बडिशं घोरं क्लेशबाडिशिकार्पितम्। यतो नरकपालास्त्वां क्रीत्वा पक्ष्यन्ति कुम्भिषु॥

examples.dm: For the guardians of hell and the compassionate ones are their allies. Therefore, just as subjects placate a fierce king, One should please all sentient beings.
examples.gm: Because the wardens of hell And the compassionate ones are their forces; Therefore, just as subjects please a fierce king, I should please sentient beings.
examples.sa: यस्मान्नरकपालाश्च कृपावन्तश्च तद्बलम्। तस्मादाराधयेत्सत्त्वान् भृत्यश्चण्डनृपं यथा॥

examples.dm: If the dislike that others have for me Does not consume me in this life or in other lives, Why should I be averse to it?
examples.gm: That others dislike me, Since that, in this life or another, Will not consume me, Why do I dislike it?
examples.sa: मय्यप्रसादो योऽन्येषां स मां किं भक्षयिष्यति। इह जन्मान्तरे वापि येनासौ मेऽनभीप्सितः॥

examples.dm: By thinking only of them, This life will pass away in vain. Through impermanent friendships, Even the eternal Dharma is destroyed.
examples.gm: By merely thinking about them, This life will pass away meaninglessly. Because of impermanent friends and relatives, Even the eternal Dharma will be destroyed.
examples.sa: तच्चिन्तया मुधा याति ह्रस्वमायुर्मुहुर्मुहुः। अशाश्वतेन धर्मेण धर्मो भ्रश्यति शाश्वतः॥

examples.dm: Setting aside the next life, Even the goals of this life will not be achieved, Just as a servant will not do his work And a master will not pay his wages.
examples.gm: Let alone the next world, With servants not doing their work and Masters not paying wages, Even the purpose of this life will not be accomplished.
examples.sa: आस्तां तावत्परो लोके दृष्टोऽप्यर्थो न सिध्यति। भृत्यस्याकुर्वतः कर्म स्वामिनोऽददतो भृतिम्॥

examples.dm: Since a lack of faith depends on others, If you can tolerate those who have no faith, Then since the arising of afflictions depends on others, Why can you not tolerate those who speak unpleasantly?
examples.gm: Because lack of faith depends on others, If you tolerate those without faith, Because it depends on the arising of afflictions, Why do you not tolerate those who speak unpleasant words?
examples.sa: परायत्ताप्रसादत्वादप्रसादिषु ते क्षमा। क्लेशात्पादपरायत्ते क्षमा नावर्णवादिनि॥

examples.dm: It is also not right to be angry with them, Thinking, "This person is an obstacle to my merit." Since there is no austerity equal to patience, Shall I not abide in that?
examples.gm: Thinking, "This one is an obstacle to my merit," It is also inappropriate to be angry at them. Since there is no austerity equal to patience, Should I not abide in it?
examples.sa: पुण्यविघ्नः कृतोऽनेनेत्यत्र कोपो न युज्यते। क्षान्त्या समं तपो नास्ति नन्वेतत्तदुपस्थितम्॥

examples.dm: If you say that this enemy should not be honored Because they have no intention for me to practice patience, Then why honor the sublime Dharma, Which is also a fit cause for accomplishment but lacks intention?
examples.gm: If you say, "Because they have no intention to accomplish my patience, This enemy is not to be venerated," Then since it is a suitable cause for accomplishment, Why do you venerate the sublime Dharma?
examples.sa: क्षमासिद्ध्याशयो नास्य तेन पूज्यो न चेदरिः। सिद्धिहेतुरचित्तोऽपि सद्धर्मः पूज्यते कथम्॥

examples.dm: For the sake of my desires, I have experienced Being burned and so forth in the hells thousands of times, Yet I have accomplished neither my own benefit Nor the benefit of others.
examples.gm: For the sake of desires, burning and so forth, I have experienced in hell thousands of times, but I did not accomplish my own benefit, Nor did I accomplish the benefit of others.
examples.sa: कोपार्थमेवमेवाहं नरकेषु सहस्रशः। कारितोऽस्मि न चात्मार्थः परार्थो वा कृतो मया॥

examples.dm: What need is there to say more? Observe the difference between these two: The childish who work for their own sake, And the Sages who work for the sake of others.
examples.gm: What need is there to say much? Childish beings act for their own purpose, and The Sage acts for the purpose of others. Look at the difference between these two!
examples.sa: बहुना वा किमुक्तेन दृश्यतामिदमन्तरम्। स्वार्थार्थिनश्च बालस्य मुनेश्चान्यार्थकारिणः॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, abandon the thought that you still have your own interests; I have sold you to others. Do not be distressed, but offer up your service.
examples.gm: "I still have my own purpose"— Cast away that thought which thinks it exists! Since I have sold you to others, Do not feel sorrow, offer your services.
examples.sa: अद्याप्यस्ति मम स्वार्थ इत्याशां त्यज सांप्रतम्। त्वं विक्रीतो मयान्येषु बहुखेदमचिन्तयन्॥

examples.dm: Since the Sages are delighted by the happiness of beings, And are displeased when they are harmed, By making them happy, all the Sages are delighted, And by harming them, one harms the Sages.
examples.gm: Those by whose happiness the Sages are pleased, And by harming whom displeasure arises; By bringing joy to them, all the Sages are pleased, And by harming them, harm is done to the Sages.
examples.sa: येषां सुखे यान्ति मुदं मुनीन्द्राः येषां व्यथायां प्रविशन्ति मन्युम्। तत्तोषणात्सर्वमुनीन्द्रतुष्टि - स्तत्रापकारेऽपकृतं मुनीनाम्॥

examples.dm: Abiding within the heart of a vast, fragrant, and cool lotus, Their splendor nourished by the food of the Victorious One's melodious speech, Possessing a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through their virtue they become a Son of the Sugata dwelling in the presence of the Victorious One.
examples.gm: Dwelling in the core of a vast, fragrant, and cooling lotus, Whose splendor is produced by the food of the Victor's sweet speech, With a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through wholesome deeds one becomes a son of the Sugata dwelling before the Victor.
examples.sa: विपुलसुगन्धिशीतलसरोरुहगर्भगता मधुरजिनस्वराशनकृतोपचितद्युतयः। मुनिकरबोधिताम्बुजविनिर्गतसद्वपुषः सुगतसुता भवन्ति सुगतस्य पुरः कुशलैः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, whatever harm I have done to beings, Which has caused displeasure to all the Great Compassionate Ones, I confess each and every one of those sins today; I pray the Sages will forgive whatever has displeased them.
examples.gm: Therefore, whatever harm I have done to wandering beings, Which has caused all the greatly compassionate ones to be displeased, I individually confess that negative deed today; I pray that the Sages forgive whatever displeasure I have caused.
examples.sa: तस्मान्मया यज्जनदुःखदेन दुःखं कृतं सर्वमहाकृपाणाम्। तदद्य पापं प्रतिदेशयामि यत्खेदितास्तन्मुनयः क्षमन्ताम्॥

examples.dm: Even if a king were to be pleased, He could not possibly bestow the state of Buddhahood, Which is what is attained By pleasing sentient beings.
examples.gm: Even if a king were to be pleased, Through having pleased sentient beings, Whatever is to be attained, He could not possibly grant Buddhahood itself.
examples.sa: तुष्टः किं नृपतिर्दद्याद्यद्बुद्धत्वसमं भवेत्। यत्सत्त्वसौमनस्येन कृतेन ह्यनुभूयते॥

examples.dm: If Buddhahood could be accomplished with even a millionth part of such hardship, Then for those possessed by desire, compared to the conduct of enlightenment, There is great suffering but no enlightenment.
examples.gm: If by just a ten-millionth fraction of that Hardship, Buddhahood is accomplished, Those with desires have greater suffering than in the Bodhisattva's conduct, And yet they have no awakening.
examples.sa: ततः कोटिशतेनापि श्रमभागेन बुद्धता। चर्यादुःखानमहद्दुःखं सा च बोधिर्न कामिनाम्॥

examples.dm: If one does not truly exchange One's own happiness for the suffering of others, Buddhahood will not be attained, And there will be no happiness even in cyclic existence.
examples.gm: One's own happiness and the sufferings of others, If one does not perfectly exchange them, One will not achieve Buddhahood, and Even in cyclic existence there will be no happiness.
examples.sa: न नाम साध्यं बुद्धत्वं संसारेऽपि कुतः सुखम्। स्वसुखस्यान्यदुःखेन परिवर्तमकुर्वतः॥
