examples.dm: Having abandoned the supreme joy of the sublime Dharma, Which is a boundless cause of delight, Why do you delight in distractions, Frivolity, and the like, which are the causes of suffering?
examples.gm: Which is a boundless cause of joy, Having abandoned the supreme joy of the holy Dharma, In distraction by the causes of suffering, And in frivolity and the like, why do you delight?
examples.sa: मुक्त्वा धर्मरतिं श्रेष्ठामनन्तरतिसंततिम्। रतिरौद्धत्यहास्यादौ दुःखहेतौ कथं तव॥

examples.dm: Therefore, in a forest that is exceedingly delightful, Free of hardship, blissful, and the pacifier Of all distractions, I shall dwell entirely alone.
examples.gm: Therefore, in exceptionally delightful Forests, with little trouble and happy, Pacifying all distractions, I shall dwell completely alone.
examples.sa: तस्मादेकाकिता रम्या निरायासा शिवोदया। सर्वविक्षेपशमनी सेवितव्या मया सदा॥

examples.dm: May those monks who desire to train Also obtain the state of solitude. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with a workable mind.
examples.gm: May monks who desire to train Attain solitary places. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with pliable minds.
examples.sa: विवेकलाभिनः सन्तुः शिक्षाकामाश्च भिक्षवः। कर्मण्यचित्ता ध्यायन्तु सर्वविक्षेपवर्जिताः॥

examples.dm: Because I lacked devotion to the Dharma In the past and even now, I have come to such a state of destitution; Who would ever abandon devotion to the Dharma?
examples.gm: Because previously and even now, I have been devoid of aspiration for the Dharma, Such destitution has come about; Who would forsake aspiration for the Dharma?
examples.sa: धर्मच्छन्दवियोगेन पौर्विकेण ममाधुना। विपत्तिरीदृशी जाता को धर्मे छन्दमुत्सृजेत्॥

examples.dm: The Sage has taught that aspiration is the root of all virtuous qualities; Its own root, in turn, is constant meditation upon the results of karmic ripening.
examples.gm: Of all wholesome factors, The Sage has stated that the root is aspiration, And its root constantly is Meditating on the ripened results.
examples.sa: कुशलानां च सर्वेषां छन्दं मूलं मुनिर्जगौ। तस्यापि मूलं सततं विपाकफलभावना॥

examples.dm: Since sentient beings have such diverse inclinations, Even the Victors cannot satisfy them all; What need is there to mention a wretched person like me? Therefore, I shall abandon concern for the world's opinions.
examples.gm: Sentient beings have diverse inclinations; If even the Victors cannot please them, What need to mention an inferior one like me? Therefore, I should abandon worldly thoughts.
examples.sa: नानाधिमुक्तिकाः सत्त्वा जिनैरपि न तोषिताः। किं पुनः मादृशैरज्ञैस्तस्मात्किं लोकचिन्तया॥

examples.dm: Chapter Eight: The Exposition of Meditative Concentration
examples.gm: Chapter Eight: Teaching Meditation

examples.dm: This concludes the eighth chapter, titled "The Explanation of Meditative Concentration," from the *Entering the Conduct of a Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the eighth chapter, called The Teaching on Meditative Concentration.

examples.dm: For that very reason, one should meditate On this analytical investigation as its antidote; The meditative concentration arising from the field of such analysis Is the food of the yogi.
examples.gm: For this very reason, the antidote to this Is to meditate on this analytical discernment; That which arises from the field of analysis Is the food of the yogi's concentration.
examples.sa: अत एव विचारोऽयं प्रतिपक्षोऽस्य भाव्यते। विकल्पक्षेत्रसंभूतध्यानाहारा हि योगिनः॥

examples.dm: If one is attached to sentient beings, The perfect reality is completely obscured. It destroys even a mind of disillusionment, And in the end, one will be tormented by grief.
examples.gm: If one forms attachments to sentient beings, Ultimate reality is completely obscured, The mind of disillusionment is also destroyed, And in the end, one will be tormented by sorrow.
examples.sa: न पश्यति यथाभूतं संवेगादवहीयते। दह्यते तेन शोकेन प्रियसंगमकाङ्क्षया॥

examples.dm: The worldly perceive things and conceptualize them As being truly real, rather than like an illusion; It is on this point that The yogis and the worldly dispute.
examples.gm: People of the world see entities, And conceptualize them as truly real, Not as being like illusions; therefore, here, Yogis and the world dispute.
examples.sa: लोकेन भावा दृश्यन्ते कल्प्यन्ते चापि तत्त्वतः। न तु मायावदित्यत्र विवादो योगिलोकयोः॥

examples.dm: How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound Become that which apprehends form? One person being designated as both father and son Is not the ultimate reality.
examples.gm: How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound Become the apprehender of form? One being both father and son Is designated, but it is not ultimate reality.
examples.sa: शब्दग्रहणरूपं यत्तद्रूपग्रहणं कथम्। एकः पिता च पुत्रश्च कल्प्यते न तु तत्त्वतः॥

examples.dm: If one is attached to sentient beings, The perfect reality is completely obscured. It destroys even a mind of disillusionment, And in the end, one will be tormented by grief.
examples.gm: If one forms attachments to sentient beings, Ultimate reality is completely obscured, The mind of disillusionment is also destroyed, And in the end, one will be tormented by sorrow.
examples.sa: न पश्यति यथाभूतं संवेगादवहीयते। दह्यते तेन शोकेन प्रियसंगमकाङ्क्षया॥

examples.dm: Having made myself free of friends and free of enemies, This body shall dwell alone in a secluded place; Regarding myself as already dead, There will be no mourning even when I actually die.
examples.gm: Having made no friends and no enemies, This body dwelling alone in solitude, Having considered it as already dead, Even when dying, there is no mourning.
examples.sa: असंस्तवाविरोधाभ्यामेक एव शरीरकः। पुर्वमेव मृतो लोके म्रियमाणो न शोचति॥

examples.dm: Since there is no one nearby To cause the harm of mourning, No one at all will distract me From such practices as the recollection of the Buddha.
examples.gm: Since there is no one staying nearby To cause grief or harm, By this, the recollection of the Buddha and so forth Will not be distracted by anyone.
examples.sa: न चान्तिकचराः केचिच्छोचन्तः कुर्वते व्यथाम्। बुद्धाद्यनुस्मृतिं चास्य विक्षिपन्ति न केचन॥

examples.dm: They are jealous of superiors and competitive with equals; They are arrogant toward inferiors and conceited when praised. If something unpleasant is said, they become angry; When could one ever receive benefit from a fool?
examples.gm: Envious of superiors, competitive with equals, Arrogant toward inferiors, conceited when praised, And prone to anger when spoken to unpleasantly— When is benefit ever obtained from the childish?
examples.sa: ईर्ष्योत्कृष्टात्समाद्द्‍वन्द्वो हीनान्मानः स्तुतेर्मदः। अवर्णात्प्रतिघश्चेति कदा बालाद्धितं भवेत्॥

examples.dm: I shall flee far away from the childish. If I encounter them, I shall please them with a joyful manner, Yet without becoming overly intimate, I shall maintain a polite and ordinary relationship.
examples.gm: One should flee far away from the childish. When meeting them, one should please them with joy, Without becoming very close, Interacting well as mere acquaintances.
examples.sa: बालाद्दूरं पलायेत प्राप्तमाराधयेत्प्रियैः। न संस्तवानुबन्धेन किं तूदासीनसाधुवत्॥

examples.dm: Even during that time, while living and free from illness, Through the hardships of activities, hunger, and fatigue, Through sleep and injury, and likewise Through meaningless association with the childish,
examples.gm: Even there, for livelihood and health, Through activities, the weariness of hunger and sickness, Sleep, harm, and likewise Meaningless association with fools,
examples.sa: तत्रापि जीवितारोग्यव्यापारेः क्षुत्क्लमश्रमैः। निद्रयोपद्रवैर्बालसंसर्गैर्निष्फलैस्तथा॥

examples.dm: Thus, relying on one another in such a way Will result in nothing but ruin; Since they do not accomplish my purpose, And I will not be of benefit to them either.
examples.gm: Thus, associating oneself with others Will merely lead to ruin. They will not accomplish my benefit, And I will not accomplish their benefit.
examples.sa: एवं तस्यापि तत्सङ्गात्तेनानर्थसमागमः। एकाकी विहरिष्यामि सुखमक्लिष्टमानसः॥

examples.dm: If there is a gap between the sense faculty and the object, Where would those two meet? If there is no gap, they are but one; What, then, could meet with what?
examples.gm: If there is a gap between the sense faculties and objects, Where would they meet? Even if there is no gap, they are a single entity, So what would meet with what?
examples.sa: सान्तराविन्द्रियार्थौ चेत्संसर्गः कुत एतयोः। निरन्तरत्वेऽप्येकत्वं कस्य केनास्तु संगतिः॥

examples.dm: For those who hold that these two are real, Their position is extremely difficult to maintain. If the object is established through the power of consciousness, What basis is there for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.gm: According to those who hold these two to be true, That very position rests in great difficulty. If the object is established by the power of consciousness, What is the basis for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.sa: यस्य त्वेतद्द्वयं सत्यं स एवात्यन्तदुःस्थितः। यदि ज्ञेयवशादर्थो ज्ञानास्तित्वे तु का गतिः॥

examples.dm: Having gone to a charnel ground, When shall I come to treat as equal My own body and the skeletal remains of others, Seeing them both as having the nature of decay?
examples.gm: Having gone to the charnel ground, The bones of others and my own body, As having the nature of perishing, When will I view them equally?
examples.sa: कायभूमिं निजां गत्वा कङ्कालैरपरैः सह। स्वकायं तुलयिष्यामि कदा शतनधर्मिणम्॥

examples.dm: If you still have doubts about such impurity, Even though it is plainly evident, Then observe other impure bodies Abandoned in the charnel grounds.
examples.gm: If such filth as this Is obvious, yet you doubt it, The bodies discarded in the charnel grounds, Look at that other filth as well.
examples.sa: यदि प्रत्यक्षमप्येतदमेध्यं नाधिमुच्यसे। श्मशाने पतितान् घोरान् कायान् पश्यापरानपि॥

examples.dm: If you feel revulsion in a charnel ground Upon seeing nothing but a heap of bones, Why do you delight in the "city charnel ground," Which is filled with moving skeletons?
examples.gm: Having seen just a skeleton, If you feel disgust in the charnel ground, Pervaded by moving skeletons, Are you delighted by the charnel ground of the city?
examples.sa: कङ्कालान् कतिचिद्दृष्ट्वा श्मशाने किल ते घृणा। ग्रामश्मशाने रमसे चलत्कङ्कालसंकुले॥

examples.dm: Having gone to a charnel ground, When shall I come to treat as equal My own body and the skeletal remains of others, Seeing them both as having the nature of decay?
examples.gm: Having gone to the charnel ground, The bones of others and my own body, As having the nature of perishing, When will I view them equally?
examples.sa: कायभूमिं निजां गत्वा कङ्कालैरपरैः सह। स्वकायं तुलयिष्यामि कदा शतनधर्मिणम्॥

examples.dm: Seeing it as nothing but a heap of bones, If you are terrified even when it is motionless, Why are you not afraid when it is moved by someone, Like a reanimated corpse?
examples.gm: Having seen it as merely a heap of bones, If you are terrified even when it does not move, When it was moved by something, like a zombie, Why were you not afraid?
examples.sa: निश्चलादपि ते त्रासः कङ्कालादेवमीक्षितात्। वेतालेनेव केनापि चाल्यमानाद्भयं न किम्॥

examples.dm: If you feel revulsion in a charnel ground Upon seeing nothing but a heap of bones, Why do you delight in the "city charnel ground," Which is filled with moving skeletons?
examples.gm: Having seen just a skeleton, If you feel disgust in the charnel ground, Pervaded by moving skeletons, Are you delighted by the charnel ground of the city?
examples.sa: कङ्कालान् कतिचिद्दृष्ट्वा श्मशाने किल ते घृणा। ग्रामश्मशाने रमसे चलत्कङ्कालसंकुले॥

examples.dm: Instead of taking delight in a pillow, Which is soft to the touch like cotton, The lustful are deluded regarding the impure, Claiming, "It does not leak a foul odor."
examples.gm: Of cotton, which is soft to the touch, You do not delight in a pillow, Saying it does not emit a foul odor; The lustful are deluded by filth.
examples.sa: तूलगर्भैर्मृदुस्पर्शै रमन्ते नोपधानकैः। दुर्गन्धं न स्रवन्तीति कामिनोऽमेध्यमोहिताः॥

examples.dm: There is no fault in the conventional truth of the yogis, For they see reality in relation to the world; Otherwise, the world's perception would invalidate The realization that a woman's body is impure.
examples.gm: There is no fault in the yogi's relative; In relation to the world, they see reality. Otherwise, the apprehension of women as unclean Would be invalidated by the world.
examples.sa: न दोषो योगिसंवृत्या लोकात्ते तत्त्वदर्शिनः। अन्यथा लोकबाधा स्यादशुचिस्त्रीनिरूपणे॥

examples.dm: However, because earth and the others are multiple, Impermanent, inert, and not divine, And because they are things to be trodden upon and are impure, They are not Īśvara himself.
examples.gm: However, earth and so forth are multiple, Impermanent, devoid of movement, not divine, Objects to be stepped upon, and impure; They are not Īśvara himself.
examples.sa: अपि त्वनेकेऽनित्याश्च निश्चेष्टा न च देवताः। लङ्घ्याश्चाशुचयश्चैव क्ष्मादयो न स ईश्वरः॥

examples.dm: If you have no attachment to what is impure, Then why do you embrace in your lap another Who was produced by that seed And arose from an impure field?
examples.gm: If you have no attachment to filth, Arisen from a field of filth, And generated by its seed, Why do you embrace another in your lap?
examples.sa: यदि ते नाशुचौ रागः कस्मादालिङ्गसे परम्। अमेध्यक्षेत्रसंभूतं तद्बीजं तेन वर्धितम्॥

examples.dm: Just as a sprout is produced from a seed, And the seed itself is known by that very sprout, Why is the existence of the object of knowledge not realized By the consciousness that arises from it?
examples.gm: A sprout arises from a seed, and Just as that very seed is known by it, By consciousness, which arises from the object of knowledge, Why is the existence of that [object] not known?
examples.sa: अङ्कुरो जायते बीजाद्बीजं तेनैव सूच्यते। ज्ञेयाज्ज्ञानेन जातेन तत्सत्ता किं न गम्यते॥

examples.dm: If a consciousness other than the sprout Realizes that the seed exists, Then by what means is the existence of that consciousness, Which realizes that object of knowledge, itself realized?
examples.gm: By a consciousness that is other than the sprout, If the existence of the seed is known, By which that object of knowledge is known, From what is the existence of the consciousness itself known?
examples.sa: अङ्कुरादन्यतो ज्ञानाद्बीजमस्तीति गम्यते। ज्ञानास्तित्वं कुतो ज्ञातं ज्ञेयं यत्तेन गम्यते॥

examples.dm: Just as the thought of "I" has arisen Toward this selfless body through habituation, Why should the thought of "I" not likewise Arise toward other sentient beings through habituation?
examples.gm: Just as towards this selfless body The mind of "I" has arisen through habituation, Likewise, towards other sentient beings as well, Why would the mind of "I" not arise through habituation?
examples.sa: यथात्मबुद्धिरभ्यासात्स्वकायेऽस्मिन्निरात्मके। परेष्वपि तथात्मत्वं किमभ्यासान्न जायते॥

examples.dm: The pride that is the cause of suffering Increases through the delusion of a self. If you say that this cannot be averted, Then meditating on selflessness is the supreme remedy.
examples.gm: Pride, which is the cause of suffering, Increases because of the delusion of a self. If you say, "Even that cannot be reversed," Meditating on selflessness is the best.
examples.sa: दुःखहेतुरहंकार आत्ममोहात्तु वर्धते। ततोऽपि न निवर्त्यश्चेत् वरं नैरात्म्यभावना॥

examples.dm: There is no experiencer at all, And therefore, feeling itself does not exist. Thus, how can this collection, Which is devoid of a self, be harmed by this?
examples.gm: There is no feeler at all, Therefore, feeling itself is not real. Thus, for this selfless aggregate, How could it be harmed by this?
examples.sa: न चास्ति वेदकः कश्चिद्वेदनातो न तत्त्वतः। निरात्मके कलापेऽस्मिन् क एवं बाध्यतेऽनया॥

examples.dm: Just as the thought of "I" has arisen Toward this selfless body through habituation, Why should the thought of "I" not likewise Arise toward other sentient beings through habituation?
examples.gm: Just as towards this selfless body The mind of "I" has arisen through habituation, Likewise, towards other sentient beings as well, Why would the mind of "I" not arise through habituation?
examples.sa: यथात्मबुद्धिरभ्यासात्स्वकायेऽस्मिन्निरात्मके। परेष्वपि तथात्मत्वं किमभ्यासान्न जायते॥

examples.dm: By habituating the latency for emptiness, The latency for substantial things will be abandoned; And by habituating the thought that "nothing exists," Even that will later be abandoned.
examples.gm: By familiarizing with the latent tendencies of emptiness, The latent tendencies of entities will be abandoned; By familiarizing with "there is nothing at all," That too will later be abandoned.
examples.sa: शून्यतावासनाधानाद्धीयते भाववासना। किंचिन्नास्तीति चाभ्यासात्सापि पश्चात्प्रहीयते॥

examples.dm: One should not turn back from hardships; For through the power of such habituation, Even that whose very name once caused fear, Becomes something one is unhappy to be without.
examples.gm: One should not turn back from difficulties, For by the power of habituation in this way, Even someone whose name one feared to hear, Without them, one becomes joyless.
examples.sa: दुष्करान्न निवर्तेत यस्मादभ्यासशक्तितः। यस्यैव श्रवणात्रासस्तेनैव न विना रतिः॥

examples.dm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Exists by worldly renown, not by valid cognition. This is as false as the common renown Of purity in things that are actually impure.
examples.gm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Is through convention, not through valid cognition. That is false, just like the convention Of being clean and so forth regarding what is unclean and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रत्यक्षमपि रूपादि प्रसिद्ध्या न प्रमाणतः। अशुच्यादिषु शुच्यादिप्रसिद्धिरिव सा मृषा॥

examples.dm: If that knowledge exists even in the world, Why is it not seen? If the world is not a valid authority, Then even seeing what is manifest is not true.
examples.gm: That knowledge is also in the world; Since it exists, why is it not seen? If the world is not a valid cognition, Seeing the manifest is also not true.
examples.sa: लोकस्यापि च तज्ज्ञानमस्ति कस्मान्न पश्यति। लोकाप्रमाणतायां चेत् व्यक्तदर्शनमप्यसत्॥

examples.dm: If a valid authority is not valid, Would that which is measured by it not be false? In that case, the meditation On emptiness would be untenable.
examples.gm: If valid cognition is not valid, Is what is measured by it not false? In reality, emptiness; Meditating on it therefore becomes untenable.
examples.sa: प्रमाणमप्रमाणं चेन्ननु तत्प्रमितं मृषा। तत्त्वतः शून्यता तस्माद्भावानां नोपपद्यते॥

examples.dm: As long as the conditions are assembled, For that long even an illusion will arise. How can a sentient being be truly existent Merely because their continuity lasts a long time?
examples.gm: As long as conditions are assembled, For that long, even illusions will occur. How, merely through a long continuum, Does a sentient being truly exist?
examples.sa: यावत्प्रत्ययसामग्री तावन्मायापि वर्तते। दीर्घसंतानमात्रेण कथं सत्त्वोऽस्ति सत्यतः॥

examples.dm: Since even a Buddha would be in cyclic existence, What would be the use of the conduct of enlightenment? As long as the continuity of conditions is not severed, Even an illusion will not cease;
examples.gm: Even a Buddha would cycle in saṃsāra, so What is the point of bodhisattva conduct?" If the continuum of conditions is not severed, Even an illusion is not reversed;
examples.sa: बुद्धोऽपि संसरेदेवं ततः किं बोधिचर्यया। प्रत्ययानामनुच्छेदे मायाप्युच्छिद्यते न हि॥

examples.dm: But since the continuity of conditions is severed, It does not arise even conventionally. When even the confusion itself does not exist, By what means can an illusion be perceived?
examples.gm: But because the continuum of conditions is severed, It does not arise even relatively. "When even the deceptive mind does not exist, By what is the illusion perceived?"
examples.sa: प्रत्ययानां तु विच्छेदात्संवृत्यापि न संभवः। यदा न भ्रान्तिरप्यस्ति माया केनोपलभ्यते॥

examples.dm: Just as the edge of a sword cannot Cut itself, so it is with the mind. Just as a lamp’s own nature Perfectly illuminates itself,
examples.gm: Just as the blade of a sword Does not cut itself, so too the mind. If [you say], "Just as a lamp Perfectly illuminates its own entity,"
examples.sa: न च्छिनत्ति यथात्मानमसिधारा तथा मनः। आत्मभावं यथा दीपः संप्रकाशयतीति चेत्॥

examples.dm: A lamp is not something to be illuminated, Because it is not obscured by darkness. Just as the blueness of a blue crystal Does not depend upon anything else,
examples.gm: A lamp is not something to be illuminated, Because it is not obscured by darkness. "Unlike a crystal, a blue thing Does not depend on another for its blueness;
examples.sa: नैव प्रकाश्यते दीपो यस्मान्न तमसावृतः। न हि स्फटिकवन्नीलं नीलत्वेऽन्यमपेक्षते॥

examples.dm: If you say, "The lamp illuminates," Having known this through cognition, Then by what is it known that the mind is luminous, Such that you can say so?
examples.gm: That a lamp illuminates Is known by cognition and thus expressed; That the intellect itself is luminous, Having been known by what, is so expressed?
examples.sa: दीपः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वा ज्ञानेन कथ्यते। बुद्धिः प्रकाशत इति ज्ञात्वेदं केन कथ्यते॥

examples.dm: If self-awareness does not exist, How can consciousness be remembered? Memory arises through a connection to the experience of something else, Just like the venom of a rat.
examples.gm: "If self-awareness does not exist, How is consciousness remembered?" It is remembered from its connection to experiencing another, Like the poison of a rat.
examples.sa: यदि नास्ति स्वसंवित्तिर्विज्ञानं स्मर्यते कथम्। अन्यानुभूते संबन्धात् स्मृतिराखुविषं यथा॥

examples.dm: Flesh and skin are not the self; Heat and wind are also not the self. The orifices are not the self in any way; The six consciousnesses are also not the self.
examples.gm: Flesh and skin are not the self, And warmth and wind are not the self. The cavities are not the self, and in all ways The six consciousnesses are not the self either.
examples.sa: नाहं मांसं न च स्नायु नोष्मा वायुरहं न च। न च च्छिद्राण्यहं नापि षड् विज्ञानानि सर्वथा॥

examples.dm: For a consciousness that is formless, Contact is not at all logical. A collection also lacks substantial reality, Just as was previously analyzed.
examples.gm: For consciousness, which has no body, Meeting is not reasonable at all. Neither is it for an aggregation, because it does not exist as a real entity, Just as was analytically examined before.
examples.sa: विज्ञानस्य त्वमूर्तस्य संसर्गो नैव युज्यते। समूहस्याप्यवस्तुत्वाद्यथा पूर्वं विचारितम्॥

examples.dm: If the root of the teaching is the monkhood itself, Then even being a monk is a difficult state to maintain. For those whose minds are still directed toward objects, Even nirvana is a difficult state to maintain.
examples.gm: If being a monk is the root of the teaching, Even being a monk is difficult to establish. For those whose minds have apprehension, Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.
examples.sa: शासनं भिक्षुतामूलं भिक्षुतैव च दुःस्थिता। सावलम्बनचित्तानां निर्वाणमपि दुःस्थितम्॥

examples.dm: May those monks who desire to train Also obtain the state of solitude. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with a workable mind.
examples.gm: May monks who desire to train Attain solitary places. Having abandoned all distractions, May they meditate with pliable minds.
examples.sa: विवेकलाभिनः सन्तुः शिक्षाकामाश्च भिक्षवः। कर्मण्यचित्ता ध्यायन्तु सर्वविक्षेपवर्जिताः॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, at a later time, the Indian scholar Sumatikīrti and the chief editor and translator, the monk Loden Sherab, accurately revised, translated, and thoroughly finalized it.
examples.gm: Still later, it was correctly revised, translated, and excellently finalized by the Indian preceptor Sumatikīrti and the chief editor-translator, the fully ordained monk Loden Sherab.

examples.dm: In this way, sattva, rajas, and tamas Are neither son nor father. They are not observed to have a nature That possesses the apprehension of sound.
examples.gm: Thus, sattva, rajas, and Tamas are neither son nor father; And it is not seen to have a nature Possessing the apprehension of sound.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमो वापि न पुत्रो न पिता यतः। शब्दग्रहणयुक्तस्तु स्वभावस्तस्य नेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: Even the parts are reduced to atoms, And those atoms are divided into directional facets. Since the directional facets are also devoid of parts, They are like space; therefore, even atoms do not exist.
examples.gm: And the part also by its division into particles, And that particle also by its division into directional parts, And since the division of directions is devoid of parts, It is like space; therefore, even particles do not exist.
examples.sa: अंशा अप्यणुभेदेन सोऽप्यणुर्दिग्विभागतः। दिग्विभागो निरंशत्वादाकाशं तेन नास्त्यणुः॥

examples.dm: The equilibrium of the qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas Is proclaimed to be the Primal Substance; Their disequilibrium is said to be the world.
examples.gm: The qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, Abiding in equilibrium, Are termed Pradhāna; In disequilibrium, they are said to be beings.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति गुणा अविषमस्थिताः। प्रधानमिति कथ्यन्ते विषमैर्जगदुच्यते॥

examples.dm: If you say that suffering exists in a subtle state And its gross form has merely been removed, Then that is simply a state of joy other than that; If you say it is subtle, then that too is of the same nature.
examples.gm: "Suffering exists in a subtle state; Has its gross state not been removed?" If you say, "That is merely a joy distinct from that," Then that subtle state too is [a state] of that [joy].
examples.sa: अस्ति सूक्ष्मतया दुःखं स्थौल्यं तस्य हृतं ननु। तुष्टिमात्रापरा चेत्स्यात्तस्मात् साप्यस्य सूक्ष्मता॥

examples.dm: By abandoning the coarse and becoming subtle, Those coarse and subtle states are themselves impermanent. Why, then, do you not accept that All things are likewise impermanent?
examples.gm: Since it becomes subtle after abandoning coarseness, That coarseness and subtlety are impermanent. Likewise, why do you not assert That all things are impermanent?
examples.sa: स्थौल्यं त्यक्त्वा भवेत्सूक्ष्ममनित्ये स्थौल्यसूक्ष्मते। सर्वस्य वस्तुनस्तद्वत्किं नानित्यत्वमिष्यते॥

examples.dm: If the coarse state is not other than the pleasure, Then the manifest pleasure is itself impermanent. If you claim that nothing non-existent can ever arise Because it lacks being,
examples.gm: If coarseness is not other than pleasure, Manifest pleasure is impermanent. If you assert that nothing nonexistent Arises, because it does not exist,
examples.sa: न स्थौल्यं चेत्सुखादन्यत् सुखस्यानित्यता स्फुटम्। नासदुत्पद्यते किंचिदसत्त्वादिति चेन्मतम्॥

examples.dm: When the object of analysis is thoroughly analyzed, There is no basis remaining for the analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that is described as nirvana.
examples.gm: If the object of analysis has been analyzed, There is no basis for analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that too is expressed as nirvāṇa.
examples.sa: विचारिते विचार्ये तु विचारस्यास्ति नाश्रयः। निराश्रितत्वान्नोदेति तच्च निर्वाणमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: For those who hold that these two are real, Their position is extremely difficult to maintain. If the object is established through the power of consciousness, What basis is there for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.gm: According to those who hold these two to be true, That very position rests in great difficulty. If the object is established by the power of consciousness, What is the basis for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.sa: यस्य त्वेतद्द्वयं सत्यं स एवात्यन्तदुःस्थितः। यदि ज्ञेयवशादर्थो ज्ञानास्तित्वे तु का गतिः॥

examples.dm: If, however, consciousness is established through the object of knowledge, What basis is there for the existence of the object of knowledge? If they exist through mutual dependence, Then both of them will be non-existent.
examples.gm: Or if consciousness is established from the object of knowledge, What is the basis for the existence of the object of knowledge? If they exist by the power of one another, Both also would not exist.
examples.sa: अथ ज्ञेयवशाज्ज्ञानं ज्ञेयास्तित्वे तु का गतिः। अथान्योन्यवशात्सत्त्वमभावः स्याद्द्वयोरपि॥

examples.dm: May those submerged in the fordless river, which is like a pit of fire, Their flesh all decayed and their skeletons the color of white kunda flowers, Attain celestial bodies through the power of my merit, And dwell with goddesses by the gently flowing waters.
examples.gm: May those sinking in the unfordable river that is like a fire pit, Their flesh all destroyed, with bones the color of jasmine flowers, By the power of my virtue attain the bodies of gods, And abide together with goddesses in the Mandākinī.
examples.sa: पतितसकलमांसाः कुन्दवर्णास्थिदेहा दहनसमजलायां वैतरण्यां निमग्नाः। मम कुशलबलेन प्राप्तदिव्यात्मभावाः सह सुरवनिताभिः सन्तु मन्दाकिनीस्थाः॥

examples.dm: May the blind see forms, And may the deaf always hear sounds; Just like the goddess Māyādevī, May pregnant women also give birth without harm.
examples.gm: May the blind see with their eyes, And the deaf always hear sounds. Just as with the goddess Māyā, May pregnant women give birth without harm.
examples.sa: संतर्प्यन्तां प्रेताः स्नाप्यन्तां शीतला भवन्तु सदा। आर्यावलोकितेश्वरकरगलितक्षीरधाराभिः॥

examples.dm: The crowns of a hundred gods offer worship to his lotus feet, His eyes are moist with compassion, and a rain of various flowers falls upon his head; Look at him, accompanied by the songs of praise from thousands of goddesses in lovely celestial palaces! Having seen such a Mañjughoṣa, may the denizens of hell now break into cries of joy.
examples.gm: See how the crowns of hundreds of gods make offerings to his lotus feet, His eyes moistened with compassion, and a rain of multitudes of flowers falling upon his head, In delightful tiered palaces containing thousands of goddesses proclaiming songs of praise!" Seeing Mañjughoṣa like this, may the hell beings now cry out in joy.
examples.sa: पश्यन्त्वेनं भवन्तः सुरशतमुकुटैरर्च्यमानाङ्घ्रिपद्मं कारूण्यादार्द्रदृष्टिं शिरसि निपतितानेकपुष्पौघवृष्टिम्। कूटागारैर्मनोज्ञैः स्तुतिमुखरसुरस्त्रीसहस्रोपगीतै-र्दृष्ट्वाग्रे मञ्जुघोषं भवतु कलकलः सांप्रतं नारकाणाम्॥

examples.dm: This was translated, edited, and finalized from a Kashmiri manuscript by the Indian scholar Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator Bandé Paltseg.
examples.gm: Revised and finalized by the Indian preceptor Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator, the monk Paltsek, based on a Kashmiri manuscript;

examples.dm: Later, the Indian scholar Dharmaśrībhadra and the chief editors and translators, the monks Rinchen Zangpo and Śākya Lodrö, revised, translated, and finalized it in accordance with a Central Indian manuscript and commentary.
examples.gm: Later, it was corrected, translated, and finalized by the Indian preceptor Dharmaśrībhadra and the chief editor-translators, the monk Rinchen Zangpo and Śākya Lodrö, in accordance with manuscripts and commentaries from the central region.

examples.dm: Furthermore, at a later time, the Indian scholar Sumatikīrti and the chief editor and translator, the monk Loden Sherab, accurately revised, translated, and thoroughly finalized it.
examples.gm: Still later, it was correctly revised, translated, and excellently finalized by the Indian preceptor Sumatikīrti and the chief editor-translator, the fully ordained monk Loden Sherab.

examples.dm: Respectfully bowing to the Sugatas who possess the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, and to all who are worthy of veneration, I shall describe the engagement in the vows of the Sugatas' heirs, Having condensed them in accordance with the scriptures.
examples.gm: To the Sugatas, endowed with the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, And to all who are worthy of homage, I respectfully bow down; Then, entering into the vows of the heirs of the Sugatas, I shall explain it concisely in accordance with scripture.
examples.sa: सुगतान् ससुतान् सधर्मकायान् प्रणिपत्यादरतोऽखिलांश्च वन्द्यान्। सुगतात्मजसंवरावतारं कथयिष्यामि यथागमं समासात्॥

examples.dm: Abiding within the heart of a vast, fragrant, and cool lotus, Their splendor nourished by the food of the Victorious One's melodious speech, Possessing a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through their virtue they become a Son of the Sugata dwelling in the presence of the Victorious One.
examples.gm: Dwelling in the core of a vast, fragrant, and cooling lotus, Whose splendor is produced by the food of the Victor's sweet speech, With a supreme body born from a lotus blossomed by the Sage's light, Through wholesome deeds one becomes a son of the Sugata dwelling before the Victor.
examples.sa: विपुलसुगन्धिशीतलसरोरुहगर्भगता मधुरजिनस्वराशनकृतोपचितद्युतयः। मुनिकरबोधिताम्बुजविनिर्गतसद्वपुषः सुगतसुता भवन्ति सुगतस्य पुरः कुशलैः॥

examples.dm: This leisure and endowment is extremely difficult to find. Having attained that which can accomplish the purpose of a human being, If one does not accomplish what is beneficial in this life, How could such a perfect opportunity ever be found again?
examples.gm: These freedoms and advantages are extremely hard to find; Since the attainment that fulfills human purpose has been found, If one does not accomplish what is beneficial in this life, How will such a perfect opportunity arise again later?
examples.sa: क्षणसंपदियं सुदुर्लभा प्रतिलब्धा पुरुषार्थसाधनी। यदि नात्र विचिन्त्यते हितंपुनरप्येष समागमः कुतः॥

examples.dm: For the sake of such a small benefit, which is not even rare for a beast to achieve, Those tormented by their karma destroy This precious human life of leisure and endowment, so difficult to find.
examples.gm: Which is not rare even when accomplished by beasts; For the sake of whatever is that small benefit, This hard-to-find, perfect freedom and endowment Is destroyed by those tormented by karma.
examples.sa: तस्यास्वादलवस्यार्थे यः पशोरप्यदुर्लभः। हता दैवहतेनेयं क्षणसंपत्सुदुर्लभा॥

examples.dm: All other virtues are like the plantain tree; Once they have produced their fruit, they are exhausted. But the tree of the awakening mind perpetually bears fruit, And rather than being exhausted, it increases ever more.
examples.gm: All other virtues are just like the plantain tree: Having borne their fruit, they are exhausted; But the tree of the mind of awakening constantly Bears fruit, is not exhausted, and continually grows.
examples.sa: कदलीव फलं विहाय याति क्षयमन्यत् कुशलं हि सर्वमेव। सततं फलति क्षयं न याति प्रसवत्येव तु बोधिचित्तवृक्षः॥

examples.dm: Wandering beings are like a dream; When analyzed, they are like a plantain tree. Between nirvāṇa and the state not passed beyond sorrow, In reality, there is no distinction.
examples.gm: Migrating beings are like a dream; When analyzed, they are like a plantain tree. Even passing into nirvana or not passing into nirvana, In reality, have no difference.
examples.sa: स्वप्नोपमास्तु गतयो विचारे कदलीसमाः। निर्वृतानिर्वृतानां च विशेषो नास्ति वस्तुतः॥

examples.dm: To summarize that awakening mind, It should be understood as being of two types: The mind that aspires for awakening, and The mind that engages in awakening.
examples.gm: In brief, that mind of awakening Should be understood as being of two types: The mind aspiring to awakening, and The mind entering awakening itself.
examples.sa: तद्बोधिचित्तं द्विविधं विज्ञातव्यं समासतः। बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तं च बोधिप्रस्थानमेव च॥

examples.dm: Although great fruits arise from the aspiring mind While wandering in cyclic existence, It does not produce a continuous flow of merit In the way that the engaging mind does.
examples.gm: From the mind aspiring to awakening, Great fruits arise while in cyclic existence, but Unlike the mind entering awakening, A continuous stream of merit does not arise.
examples.sa: बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तस्य संसारेऽपि फलं महत्। न त्वविच्छिन्नपुण्यत्वं यथा प्रस्थानचेतसः॥

examples.dm: If even the mere thought of being beneficial Excels the worship of the Buddhas, What need is there to mention striving For the welfare and happiness of every single being without exception?
examples.gm: If merely intending to be beneficial Is more exalted than making offerings to the Buddhas, Of all sentient beings without exception, What need is there to mention striving for their happiness and welfare?
examples.sa: हिताशंसनमात्रेण बुद्धपूजा विशिष्यते। किं पुनः सर्वसत्त्वानां सर्वसौख्यार्थमुद्यमात्॥

examples.dm: Whatever virtuous deeds have been accumulated, Such as generosity and offerings to the Sugatas, Over a thousand eons, A single moment of anger destroys them all.
examples.gm: Accumulated over a thousand eons, Generosity, offerings to the Sugatas, and so forth— Whatever good conduct there is, all of that, A single moment of anger destroys.
examples.sa: सर्वमेतत्सुचरितं दानं सुगतपूजनम्। कृतं कल्पसहस्रैर्यत्प्रतिघः प्रतिहन्ति तत्॥

examples.dm: Chapter Two: Confession of Negativities
examples.gm: Chapter Two: Confession of Sins

examples.dm: This concludes the second chapter, the Chapter on the Confession of Sin, from the Engaging in the Bodhisattva's Conduct.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the second chapter, Confession of Negative Deeds.

examples.dm: Upon all the jewels of the sublime Dharma, And upon the reliquaries and the sacred images, May a rain of precious flowers and the like Fall in a continuous, uninterrupted stream.
examples.gm: Upon all the rare and supreme holy Dharma, Stūpas, and images, May a rain of jewels, flowers, and the like, Fall without interruption.
examples.sa: सर्वसद्धर्मरत्नेषु चैत्येषु प्रतिमासु च। पुष्परत्नादिवर्षाश्च प्रवर्तन्तां निरन्तरम्॥

examples.dm: Toward those who revile and destroy Sacred images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, It is not appropriate for me to feel hatred, For the Buddhas and the like cannot be harmed.
examples.gm: Towards images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, Even if someone disparages or destroys them, It is inappropriate for me to have anger, For the Buddhas and so forth suffer no harm.
examples.sa: प्रतिमास्तूपसद्धर्मनाशकाक्रोशकेषु च। न युज्यते मम द्वेषो बुद्धादीनां न हि व्यथा॥

examples.dm: To all the Buddhas of the three times, And to the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With as many bodies as there are atoms in the realms, I bow down and pay homage.
examples.gm: To all the Buddhas who have gone in the three times, Along with the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With bodies as numerous as all the atoms in the fields, Bowing down, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वक्षेत्राणुसंख्यैश्च प्रणामैः प्रणमाम्यहम्। सर्वत्र्यध्वगतान् बुद्धान् सहधर्मगणोत्तमान्॥

examples.dm: My body, and likewise my possessions, And all my virtues of the three times, I shall give away without a sense of loss, To accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: My body and likewise my wealth, and All virtues of the three times, In order to accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings, I shall give away without regret.
examples.sa: आत्मभावांस्तथा भोगान् सर्वत्र्यध्वगतं शुभम्। निरपेक्षस्त्यजाम्येष सर्वसत्त्वार्थसिद्धये॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to the foundations of the awakening mind and to the reliquaries; I prostrate to the preceptors, the masters, And to those who maintain the supreme ascetic discipline.
examples.gm: To the bases of the awakening mind, And to the stūpas, I pay homage. To the preceptors and likewise the teachers, And to the supreme practitioners, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वचैत्यानि वन्देऽहं बोधिसत्त्वाश्रयांस्तथा। नमः करोम्युपाध्यायानभिवन्द्यान् यतींस्तथा॥

examples.dm: The *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*, composed by the master Śāntideva, is hereby completed.
examples.gm: Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, composed by the master Śāntideva, is complete.
examples.sa: ॥बोधिचर्यावतारे परिणामनापरिच्छेदो दशमः॥ ^10-a ॥समाप्तोऽयं बोधिचर्यावतारः। कृतिराचार्यशान्तिदेवस्य॥

examples.dm: To the fully enlightened Buddhas and Bodhisattvas Who dwell in all directions, And who possess great compassion, I join my palms and pray:
examples.gm: To those who reside in all directions, The perfect Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, Who possess great compassion, Joining my palms, I make this request:
examples.sa: विज्ञापयामि संबुद्धान् सर्वदिक्षु व्यवस्थितान्। महाकारुणिकांश्चापि बोधिसत्त्वान् कृताञ्जलिः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, In order to dispel the fears of beings in cyclic existence, Blessed even his own name.
examples.gm: Therefore, the protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, for transmigratory beings, In order to dispel the fears of the assembly, Blessed even his own name.
examples.sa: अध्यतिष्ठदतो नाथः स्वनामाप्यवलोकितः। पर्षच्छारद्यभयमप्यपनेतुं जनस्य हि॥

examples.dm: Whatever harm I have done to the Three Jewels, To my parents, or to my teachers and others, Through the gateway of the afflictions By means of my body, speech, and mind,
examples.gm: To the Three Jewels, To parents, gurus, or others, Through afflictions, with body, speech, And mind, whatever harm I have done,
examples.sa: रत्नत्रयेऽपकारो यो मातपितृषु वा मया। गुरुष्वन्येषु वा क्षेपात् कायवाग्बुद्धिभिः कृतः॥

examples.dm: If those who, for the sake of profit and honor, Kill even their own fathers and mothers, And steal the property of the Three Jewels, Will be burned in the Incessant Hell,
examples.gm: Whoever, for the sake of profit and respect, Kills even their father and mother, and, Having stolen the wealth of the Three Jewels, Will therefore burn in the Incessant Hell;
examples.sa: यो लाभसत्क्रियाहेतोः पितरावपि मारयेत्। रत्नत्रयस्वमादद्याद्येनावीचीन्धनो भवेत्॥

examples.dm: Terrified by fear, I offer myself to Samantabhadra; To Mañjuśrī, I also Offer my own body.
examples.gm: Terrified by fear, I offer myself to Samantabhadra; To Mañjuśrī, I myself Shall offer my body.
examples.sa: समन्तभद्रायात्मानं ददामि भयविह्वलः। पुनश्च मञ्जुघोषाय ददाम्यात्मानमात्मना॥

examples.dm: Thus, through my roots of virtue, may they see clouds of unobstructed Bodhisattvas such as Samantabhadra, Like clouds of bliss, raining down cool and fragrant showers; Upon seeing this, May those denizens of hell be filled with manifest joy.
examples.gm: Likewise, by my roots of virtue, seeing Samantabhadra and other Bodhisattvas' unobstructed pleasant clouds, Letting fall a cool and fragrant rain, May those sentient beings in hell become truly joyful.
examples.sa: इति मत्कुशलैः समन्तभद्र-प्रमुखानावृतबोधिसत्त्वमेघान्। सुखशीतसुगन्धवातवृष्टी-नभिनन्दन्तु विलोक्य नारकास्ते॥

examples.dm: Terrified by fear, I offer myself to Samantabhadra; To Mañjuśrī, I also Offer my own body.
examples.gm: Terrified by fear, I offer myself to Samantabhadra; To Mañjuśrī, I myself Shall offer my body.
examples.sa: समन्तभद्रायात्मानं ददामि भयविह्वलः। पुनश्च मञ्जुघोषाय ददाम्यात्मानमात्मना॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to Mañjughoṣa, Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises. I also prostrate to my spiritual friend, Through whose kindness I have flourished.
examples.gm: Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises, I prostrate to Mañjuśrī. Through whose kindness I have grown, I also prostrate to the spiritual friend.
examples.sa: मञ्जुघोषं नमस्यामि यत्प्रसादान्मतिः शुभे। कल्याणमित्रं वन्देऽहं यत्प्रसादाच्च वर्धते॥

examples.dm: To the protector Avalokiteśvara, Whose compassionate conduct is never mistaken, I cry out with a piteous voice: "Please protect this sinful one!"
examples.gm: Whose compassionate deeds are unerring, To the protector Avalokiteśvara as well, With an anguished cry, I call out: "Please protect me, a sinner!"
examples.sa: तं चावलोकितं नाथं कृपाव्याकुलचारिणम्। विरौम्यार्तरवं भीतः स मां रक्षतु पापिनम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, In order to dispel the fears of beings in cyclic existence, Blessed even his own name.
examples.gm: Therefore, the protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, for transmigratory beings, In order to dispel the fears of the assembly, Blessed even his own name.
examples.sa: अध्यतिष्ठदतो नाथः स्वनामाप्यवलोकितः। पर्षच्छारद्यभयमप्यपनेतुं जनस्य हि॥

examples.dm: To the noble Ākāśagarbha, And to Kṣitigarbha as well, And to all the great compassionate protectors, I cry out from my heart, seeking refuge.
examples.gm: To the noble Ākāśagarbha, And to Kṣitigarbha, And to all the greatly compassionate protectors, Seeking refuge, I call out from my heart.
examples.sa: आर्यमाकाशगर्भं च क्षितिगर्भं च भावतः। सर्वान् महाकृपांश्चापि त्राणान्वेषी विरौम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: The trainings are revealed within the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, in particular, Should be looked at first of all.
examples.gm: The trainings appear in the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, Should be looked at from the very beginning.
examples.sa: शिक्षाः सूत्रेषु दृश्यन्ते तस्मात्सूत्राणि वाचयेत्। आकाशगर्भसूत्रे च मूलापत्तीर्निरूपयेत्॥

examples.dm: Then the intention not to act according to the instructions Of the Omniscient Physician, who removes every pain, Is a state of extreme delusion And is truly contemptible.
examples.gm: In that case, of the omniscient physician Who draws out all pain— The intention not to act according to his commands Is utterly foolish and an object of reproach.
examples.sa: तत्र सर्वज्ञवैद्यस्य सर्वशल्यापहारिणः। वाक्यमुल्लङ्घयामीति धिङ् मामत्यन्तमोहितम्॥

examples.dm: Emptiness is the antidote To the darkness of the afflictive and cognitive obscurations. Why, then, would those who desire to swiftly attain omniscience Not meditate upon it?
examples.gm: Of the obscurations of afflictions and knowables, Emptiness is the antidote to the darkness. By one who wishes to quickly become omniscient, How could one not meditate on it?
examples.sa: क्लेशज्ञेयावृतितमःप्रतिपक्षो हि शून्यता। शीघ्रं सर्वज्ञताकामो न भावयति तां कथम्॥

examples.dm: Adopting the Bodhichitta
examples.gm: Chapter Three: Completely Taking Hold of Bodhicitta

examples.dm: From "Engaging in the Bodhisattva Deeds," this is the third chapter, entitled "Fully Adopting the Awakening Mind."
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the third chapter, called "Fully Taking Hold of the Awakening Mind."

examples.dm: To the Victors who intend to pass into nirvana, I join my palms and pray: Do not leave these beings in blindness, But please remain for countless eons.
examples.gm: To the Conquerors wishing to pass into nirvana, With joined palms I pray: So as not to leave these wanderers in blindness, I beseech you to remain for countless eons.
examples.sa: निर्वातुकामांश्च जिनान् याचयामि कृताञ्जलिः। कल्पाननन्तांस्तिष्ठन्तु मा भूदन्धमिदं जगत्॥

examples.dm: By renouncing everything, one transcends suffering, And my mind seeks to achieve that transcendence; Since I must give everything away at once, It is best to give it to all sentient beings.
examples.gm: By giving up everything, nirvana is attained, And my mind seeks to accomplish nirvana. Since I must part with everything at once, It is best given to sentient beings.
examples.sa: सर्वत्यागश्च निर्वाणं निर्वाणार्थि च मे मनः। त्यक्तव्यं चेन्मया सर्वं वरं सत्त्वेषु दीयताम्॥

examples.dm: To the Victors who intend to pass into nirvana, I join my palms and pray: Do not leave these beings in blindness, But please remain for countless eons.
examples.gm: To the Conquerors wishing to pass into nirvana, With joined palms I pray: So as not to leave these wanderers in blindness, I beseech you to remain for countless eons.
examples.sa: निर्वातुकामांश्च जिनान् याचयामि कृताञ्जलिः। कल्पाननन्तांस्तिष्ठन्तु मा भूदन्धमिदं जगत्॥

examples.dm: O mind, though countless eons have passed while you desired to pursue your own interests, Through such great hardship, You have achieved nothing but suffering.
examples.gm: O mind, because you desired to accomplish your own purpose, Even though countless eons have passed, With such great weariness, You have accomplished only suffering.
examples.sa: अप्रमेया गताः कल्पाः स्वार्थं जिज्ञासतस्तव। श्रमेण महतानेन दुःखमेव त्वयार्जितम्॥

examples.dm: For sentient beings who are destitute and poor, May I become an inexhaustible treasure, And remain present before them As every variety of necessary provision.
examples.gm: For sentient beings who are destitute and poor, May I become an inexhaustible treasure, and As all the various kinds of needed requisites, May I remain closely present before them.
examples.sa: दरिद्राणां च सत्त्वानां निधिः स्यामहमक्षयः। नानोपकरणाकारैरुपतिष्ठेयमग्रतः॥

examples.dm: It is the supreme nectar that overcomes The Lord of Death for all beings; It is the inexhaustible treasure that dispels The poverty of all beings.
examples.gm: Destroying the Lord of Death for wandering beings, It is the supreme nectar. Dispelling the poverty of wandering beings, It is the inexhaustible treasure.
examples.sa: जगन्मृत्युविनाशाय जातमेतद्रसायनम्। जगद्दारिद्र्यशमनं निधानमिदमक्षयम्॥

examples.dm: May I be a protector for those without a protector, A guide for those traveling on the path, And for those who wish to cross over, May I be a boat, a ship, and a bridge.
examples.gm: May I be a protector for those without a protector, A guide for those who travel on the path, And a boat for those who wish to cross over, May I become a ship and a bridge.
examples.sa: अनाथानामहं नाथः सार्थवाहश्च यायिनाम्। पारेप्सूनां च नौभूतः सेतुः संक्रम एव च॥

examples.dm: Liberation comes from seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness? Because the scriptures state that without this path, There is no enlightenment.
examples.gm: "One is liberated by seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness?" Because scriptures state that without this path, There is no awakening.
examples.sa: सत्यदर्शनतो मुक्तिः शून्यतादर्शनेन किम्। न विनानेन मार्गेण बोधिरित्यागमो यतः॥

examples.dm: Today, in the presence of all the Protectors, I invite the world to the state of the Sugatas and to temporal happiness; Since I have invited you as my guests to this bliss, May the gods, asuras, and all others rejoice!
examples.gm: Today, by me, in the presence of all the protectors, Wandering beings to Sugatahood itself, and Until then, to happiness, have been invited as guests; Let gods, asuras, and others rejoice!
examples.sa: जगदद्य निमन्त्रितं मया सुगतत्वेन सुखेन चान्तरा। पुरतः खलु सर्वतायिनामभिनन्दन्तु सुरासुरादयः॥

examples.dm: Even if all the gods and demigods Were to rise up against me as enemies, They would be unable to lead me into Or cast me into the fires of the Avīci hell.
examples.gm: Even if the gods and demigods All rose up against me as enemies, Even they would not be able To lead and place me in the fire of Avīci.
examples.sa: सर्वे देवा मनुष्याश्च यदि स्युर्मम शत्रवः। तेऽपि नावीचिकं वह्निं समुदानयितुं क्षमाः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, just as I have vowed, I must respectfully fulfill it. If I do not make an effort from this moment on, I shall sink lower and lower.
examples.gm: Therefore, just as I have promised, I shall respectfully accomplish it. If from today I do not make effort, I will go lower and lower.
examples.sa: तस्माद्यथाप्रतिज्ञातं साधनीयं मयादरात्। नाद्य चेत्क्रियते यत्नस्तलेनास्मि तलं गतः॥

examples.dm: Even many who possess learning and faith, And who apply themselves with great diligence, Become defiled by the stain of downfalls, Due to the fault of lacking introspective awareness.
examples.gm: Those who are learned and have faith, And many who dedicate themselves to effort, Because they incur the fault of lacking introspection, Will become tainted by downfalls.
examples.sa: अनेके श्रुतवन्तोऽपि श्राद्धा यत्नपरा अपि। असंप्रजन्यदोषेण भवन्त्यापत्तिकश्मलाः॥

examples.dm: The appearance of a Tathāgata, the attainment of faith and a human body, And the fitness to cultivate virtue— Since such things are so rare, when will they ever be found again?
examples.gm: The appearance of the Tathāgatas, Faith, obtaining a human body, And the fitness to practice virtue, like this, Since they are rare, when will they be obtained?
examples.sa: कदा तथागतोत्पादं श्रद्धां मानुष्यमेव च। कुशलाभ्यासयोग्यत्वमेवं लप्स्येऽतिदुर्लभम्॥

examples.dm: May they be freed from all states of non-leisure, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And possessing excellent food and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.gm: Freed from all unfree states, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And perfect in sustenance and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.sa: सर्वाक्षणविनिर्मुक्ताः श्रद्धाप्रज्ञाकृपान्विताः। आकाराचारसंपन्नाः सन्तु जातिस्मराः सदा॥

examples.dm: The appearance of a Tathāgata, the attainment of faith and a human body, And the fitness to cultivate virtue— Since such things are so rare, when will they ever be found again?
examples.gm: The appearance of the Tathāgatas, Faith, obtaining a human body, And the fitness to practice virtue, like this, Since they are rare, when will they be obtained?
examples.sa: कदा तथागतोत्पादं श्रद्धां मानुष्यमेव च। कुशलाभ्यासयोग्यत्वमेवं लप्स्येऽतिदुर्लभम्॥

examples.dm: With conduct such as mine, I shall not even attain a human body again. If a human body is not attained, There will be only sin and no virtue.
examples.gm: With behavior like mine, Even a human body will not be obtained. If a human body is not obtained, There is only sin and no virtue.
examples.sa: न हीदृशैर्मच्चरितैर्मानुष्यं लभ्यते पुनः। अलभ्यमाने मानुष्ये पापमेव कुतः शुभम्॥

examples.dm: For that very reason, the Blessed One said That human status is extremely difficult to attain, Like a turtle’s neck entering the hole Of a yoke tossing upon a vast ocean.
examples.gm: For that very reason, the Bhagavan Of a yoke drifting on the great ocean, Like a turtle's neck entering the hole, Declared that the human state is extremely difficult to obtain.
examples.sa: अत एवाह भगवान्-मानुष्यमतिदुर्लभम्। महार्णवयुगच्छिद्रकूर्मग्रीवार्पणोपमम्॥

examples.dm: I have not made offerings to the Blessed One, Nor have I provided the joy of great festivals; I have not performed service for the Teachings, Nor have I fulfilled the hopes of the poor.
examples.gm: I have not made offerings to the Blessed Ones, I have not provided the happiness of great festivals, I have not performed deeds for the teaching, I have not fulfilled the wishes of the poor.
examples.sa: न प्राप्तं भगवत्पूजामहोत्सवसुखं मया। न कृता शासने कारा दरिद्राशा न पूरिता॥

examples.dm: Having experienced only that much, One will not be liberated; For while experiencing it in that way, Other sins are produced in great abundance.
examples.gm: Having experienced just that much, One will not be liberated from it, Because while experiencing it like this, Other sins are fully generated.
examples.sa: न च तन्मात्रमेवासौ वेदयित्वा विमुच्यते। तस्मात्तद्वेदयन्नेव पापमन्यत् प्रसूयते॥

examples.dm: Learn the manner of relying on a guru As described in the life story of Śrīsambhava; This and other teachings of the Buddha Are to be understood by reading the sūtras.
examples.gm: From the liberation story of Śrīsaṃbhava, One should train in the manner of relying on the guru; This and other words spoken by the Buddha, Should be known after reading the sūtras.
examples.sa: श्रीसंभवविमोक्षाच्च शिक्षेद्यद्गुरुवर्तनम्। एतच्चान्यच्च बुद्धोक्तं ज्ञेयं सूत्रान्तवाचनात्॥

examples.dm: Having found such leisure as this, If I do not habituate myself to virtue, There is no deception greater than this, And there is no folly greater than this.
examples.gm: Having found such leisure, If I do not habituate myself to virtue, There is no deception other than this, And there is no bewilderment other than this.
examples.sa: नातः परा वञ्चनास्ति न च मोहोऽस्त्यतः परः। यदीदृशं क्षणं प्राप्य नाभ्यस्तं कुशलं मया॥

examples.dm: Again, leisure is difficult to find, And the appearance of a Buddha is extremely rare. The river of afflictions is hard to abandon; Alas, suffering will continue in succession!
examples.gm: Once again, leisure is hard to find, and The appearance of a Buddha is extremely hard to encounter. The river of afflictions is hard to abandon, so Alas, suffering will continue in succession.
examples.sa: पुनश्च क्षणदौर्लभ्यं बुद्धोत्पादोऽतिदुर्लभः। क्लेशौघो दुर्निवारश्चेत्यहो दुःखपरंपरा॥

examples.dm: This powerful enemy, the mental afflictions, Can in a single instant cast me Into that fire which, upon meeting even Mount Meru, Would not leave even its ashes behind.
examples.gm: This powerful enemy of the afflictions, Upon meeting which, even Mount Meru Does not remain even as ashes, Casts me there in a single moment.
examples.sa: मेरोरपि यदासङ्गान्न भस्माप्युपलभ्यते। क्षणात् क्षिपन्ति मां तत्र बलिनः क्लेशशत्रवः॥

examples.dm: Reflecting again and again that after a long time I have obtained this supreme leisure, I should hold my mind as utterly unshakable as Mount Meru.
examples.gm: After a long time, the supreme leisure, Reflecting again and again on having attained it, Such a mind, like Mount Meru, Should be held completely unshakable.
examples.sa: चिरात्प्राप्तं क्षणवरं स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा मुहुर्मुहुः। धारयामीदृशं चित्तमप्रकम्प्यं सुमेरुवत्॥

examples.dm: When I vowed to liberate all beings, As far as the limits of space in the ten directions, From their afflictions, I myself was not yet freed from those very afflictions.
examples.gm: Reaching the ends of space in the ten directions, To liberate wandering beings from afflictions, When I promised this, I myself Was not liberated from afflictions.
examples.sa: दशदिग्व्योमपर्यन्तजगत्क्लेशविमोक्षणे। प्रतिज्ञाय मदात्मापि न क्लेशेभ्यो विमोचितः॥

examples.dm: For the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings, Reaching to the very limits of space in the ten directions, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.
examples.gm: As far as the limits of space in the ten directions, In order to accomplish the aims of all sentient beings, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.
examples.sa: दशदिग्व्योमपर्यन्तसर्वसत्त्वार्थसाधने। यथा चरति मञ्जुश्रीः सैव चर्या भवेन्मम॥

examples.dm: The afflictions do not reside in sense objects, nor in the collection of faculties, nor in between them; If they do not exist elsewhere either, then where do they dwell to harm the entire world? They are like an illusion; therefore, to abandon fear in your heart, apply yourself to understanding them. Why do you pointlessly inflict harm upon yourself in the hells and other such realms?
examples.gm: Afflictions do not reside in the objects, nor in the sense faculties, nor in between. Nor elsewhere; if so, where do they reside and harm all wandering beings? They are like an illusion; therefore, banish fear in the heart and rely on effort for the sake of knowledge. Why should I be harmed meaninglessly in hells and so forth?
examples.sa: न क्लेशा विषयेषु नेन्द्रियगणे नाप्यन्तराले स्थिता नातोऽन्यत्र कुह स्थिताः पुनरमी मथ्नन्ति कृत्स्नं जगत्। मायैवेयमतो विमुञ्च हृदयं त्रासं भजस्वोद्यमं प्रज्ञार्थं किमकाण्ड एव नरकेष्वात्मानमाबाधसे॥

examples.dm: Since seeing and even touching Are of the nature of dreams and illusions, And arise simultaneously with the mind, That feeling is not seen by it.
examples.gm: Seeing or even touching, Have a nature like a dream or an illusion. Because it arises simultaneously with the mind, Feeling is not perceived by it.
examples.sa: दृश्यते स्पृश्यते चापि स्वप्नमायोपमात्मना। चित्तेन सहजातत्वाद्वेदना तेन नेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: The afflictions do not reside in sense objects, nor in the collection of faculties, nor in between them; If they do not exist elsewhere either, then where do they dwell to harm the entire world? They are like an illusion; therefore, to abandon fear in your heart, apply yourself to understanding them. Why do you pointlessly inflict harm upon yourself in the hells and other such realms?
examples.gm: Afflictions do not reside in the objects, nor in the sense faculties, nor in between. Nor elsewhere; if so, where do they reside and harm all wandering beings? They are like an illusion; therefore, banish fear in the heart and rely on effort for the sake of knowledge. Why should I be harmed meaninglessly in hells and so forth?
examples.sa: न क्लेशा विषयेषु नेन्द्रियगणे नाप्यन्तराले स्थिता नातोऽन्यत्र कुह स्थिताः पुनरमी मथ्नन्ति कृत्स्नं जगत्। मायैवेयमतो विमुञ्च हृदयं त्रासं भजस्वोद्यमं प्रज्ञार्थं किमकाण्ड एव नरकेष्वात्मानमाबाधसे॥

examples.dm: If it does not exist because it has not been born, Then at that time, what could have the desire to be born? Since it is always distracted by sense objects, It is also not something that could cease.
examples.gm: If it does not exist prior to arising, At that time, what wishes to arise? Since it would be permanently distracted by objects, It would also never cease.
examples.sa: अनुत्पन्नं हि तन्नास्ति क इच्छेद्भवितुं तदा। विषयव्यापृतत्वाच्च निरोद्धुमपि नेहते॥

examples.dm: By letting the elephant of the mind run wild, It inflicts the torments of the Incessant Hell; An untamed, mad elephant in this world Cannot cause such harm.
examples.gm: Letting the elephant of the mind wander loose Causes harm in the Avīci hell; An untamed, maddened elephant Does not cause such harm here.
examples.sa: अदान्ता मत्तमातङ्गा न कुर्वन्तीह तां व्यथाम्। करोति यामवीच्यादौ मुक्तश्चित्तमतङ्गजः॥

examples.dm: If the elephant of the mind is firmly bound With the rope of total mindfulness, All fears will vanish, And every virtue will fall into one's hands.
examples.gm: With the rope of mindfulness on all sides, If the elephant of the mind is tightly bound, All fears will cease to exist, And all virtues will come into one's hands.
examples.sa: बद्धश्चेच्चित्तमातङ्गः स्मृतिरज्ज्वा समन्ततः। भयमस्तंगतं सर्वं कृत्स्नं कल्याणमागतम्॥

examples.dm: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, Snakes, and all enemies, The guardians of the hell realms, And likewise sorcerers and demons—
examples.gm: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, Snakes, and all enemies, The guardians of the hells for sentient beings, Evil sorcerers, and likewise rākṣasas—
examples.sa: व्याघ्राः सिंहा गजा ऋक्षाः सर्पाः सर्वे च शत्रवः। सर्वे नरकपालाश्च डाकिन्यो राक्षसास्तथा॥

examples.dm: May medicines be potent, And may the recitation of secret mantras be successful. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with a mind of compassion.
examples.gm: May medicines be endowed with potency, And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with minds of compassion.
examples.sa: शक्ता भवन्तु चौषध्यो मन्त्राः सिध्यन्तु जापिनाम्। भवन्तु करुणाविष्टा डाकिनीराक्षसादयः॥

examples.dm: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, Snakes, and all enemies, The guardians of the hell realms, And likewise sorcerers and demons—
examples.gm: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, Snakes, and all enemies, The guardians of the hells for sentient beings, Evil sorcerers, and likewise rākṣasas—
examples.sa: व्याघ्राः सिंहा गजा ऋक्षाः सर्पाः सर्वे च शत्रवः। सर्वे नरकपालाश्च डाकिन्यो राक्षसास्तथा॥

examples.dm: Who intentionally created The weapons of the hell beings? Who created the floor of burning iron, And from what did those masses of fire arise?
examples.gm: The weapons of the hells for sentient beings, Who intentionally created them? Who created the burning iron ground? From what did those masses of fire arise?
examples.sa: शस्त्राणि केन नरके घटितानि प्रयत्नतः। तप्तायःकुट्टिमं केन कुतो जाताश्च ताः स्त्रियः॥

examples.dm: The Sage has taught that all such things Are the result of a sinful mind. Thus, within the three worlds, There is no other fear besides the mind.
examples.gm: All such things Were taught by the Sage to be the sinful mind. Thus, in the three worlds, There is no fear other than the mind.
examples.sa: पापचित्तसमुद्भूतं तत्तत्सर्वं जगौ मुनिः। तस्मान्न कश्चित् त्रैलोक्ये चित्तादन्यो भयानकः॥

examples.dm: If you desire for sentient beings to attain Buddhahood, Which is honored by the three worlds, Why are you distressed when you see them Receive even a meager amount of honor and respect?
examples.gm: To awaken into Buddhahood worshipped by the three worlds, If you desire for sentient beings, Having seen them receive mere meager respect, Why do you become tormented by that?
examples.sa: त्रैलोक्यपूज्यं बुद्धत्वं सत्त्वानां किल वाञ्छसि। सत्कारमित्वरं दृष्ट्वा तेषां किं परिदह्यसे॥

examples.dm: Even if one practices recitations and all kinds of austerities For a very long period of time, The Knower of Reality has said that if they are performed With a mind distracted elsewhere, they are useless.
examples.gm: All recitations and ascetic practices, Even if practiced for a long time, If done with a mind distracted elsewhere, Are taught by the Knower of Reality to be meaningless.
examples.sa: जपास्तपांसि सर्वाणि दीर्घकालकृतान्यपि। अन्यचित्तेन मन्देन वृथैवेत्याह सर्ववित्॥

examples.dm: May medicines be potent, And may the recitation of secret mantras be successful. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with a mind of compassion.
examples.gm: May medicines be endowed with potency, And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with minds of compassion.
examples.sa: शक्ता भवन्तु चौषध्यो मन्त्राः सिध्यन्तु जापिनाम्। भवन्तु करुणाविष्टा डाकिनीराक्षसादयः॥

examples.dm: If one dwells in the midst of a boisterous crowd, One should be attentive, just as one protects a wound. Even when dwelling among wicked people, One should always guard this wound of the mind.
examples.gm: When dwelling in the midst of a wild crowd, Just as one carefully protects a wound, So too, when dwelling in the midst of bad people, One should always guard this wound of the mind.
examples.sa: यथा चपलमध्यस्थो रक्षति व्रणमादरात्। एवं दुर्जनमध्यस्थो रक्षेच्चित्तव्रणं सदा॥

examples.dm: If one protects a wound out of fear of even its slight pain, Then why, fearing the crushing of the Samghāta and Raurava hells, Does one not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.gm: Because of the minor suffering of a wound, If one who is afraid carefully protects the wound, Those who fear the Crushing and Destroying Hells, Why do they not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.sa: व्रणदुःखलवाद्भीतो रक्षामि व्रणमादरात्। संघातपर्वताघाताद्भीतश्चित्तव्रणं न किम्॥

examples.dm: If one protects a wound out of fear of even its slight pain, Then why, fearing the crushing of the Samghāta and Raurava hells, Does one not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.gm: Because of the minor suffering of a wound, If one who is afraid carefully protects the wound, Those who fear the Crushing and Destroying Hells, Why do they not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.sa: व्रणदुःखलवाद्भीतो रक्षामि व्रणमादरात्। संघातपर्वताघाताद्भीतश्चित्तव्रणं न किम्॥

examples.dm: May those heaps of glowing coals become heaps of jewels; May the scorched earth be spread as a crystal floor; May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also become Celestial palaces of offerings, filled with Sugatas.
examples.gm: May those heaps of coal become heaps of jewels. May the burning ground be paved as a crystal ground. May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also, of offerings Become immeasurable palaces, filled with Sugatas.
examples.sa: सोऽङ्गारराशिर्मणिराशिरस्तु तप्ता च भूः स्फाटिककुट्टिमं स्यात्। भवन्तु संघातमहीधराश्च पूजाविमानाः सुगतप्रपूर्णाः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, mindfulness should never be allowed To stray from the gateway of the mind. If it should stray, one should bring it back By recollecting the sufferings of the lower realms.
examples.gm: Therefore, mindfulness from the door of the mind, Should never be let go. Even if it departs, recalling the harms of the lower realms, It should be closely maintained.
examples.sa: तस्मात्स्मृतिर्मनोद्वारान्नापनेया कदाचन। गतापि प्रत्युपस्थाप्या संसंमृत्त्यापायिकीं व्यथाम्॥

examples.dm: When mindfulness stands at the gateway of the mind For the purpose of guarding it, At that time alertness will arrive, And even that which had slipped away will return.
examples.gm: When mindfulness from the door of the mind, Remains for the sake of guarding, At that time introspection will come, And even what has gone will return.
examples.sa: संप्रजन्यं तदायाति न च यात्यागतं पुनः। स्मृतिर्यदा मनोद्वारे रक्षार्थमवतिष्ठते॥

examples.dm: If there is agitation or mockery, Or if there is pride and arrogance, Or the intention to expose others' faults, Or if there is divisiveness and deceit,
examples.gm: With wildness and mockery, Or if one possesses pride and arrogance, And the intention to expose faults, Or if there is an evasive or deceptive mind,
examples.sa: उद्धतं सोपहासं वा यदा मानमदान्वितम्। सोत्प्रासातिशयं वक्रं वञ्चकं च मनो भवेत्॥

examples.dm: Having abandoned the supreme joy of the sublime Dharma, Which is a boundless cause of delight, Why do you delight in distractions, Frivolity, and the like, which are the causes of suffering?
examples.gm: Which is a boundless cause of joy, Having abandoned the supreme joy of the holy Dharma, In distraction by the causes of suffering, And in frivolity and the like, why do you delight?
examples.sa: मुक्त्वा धर्मरतिं श्रेष्ठामनन्तरतिसंततिम्। रतिरौद्धत्यहास्यादौ दुःखहेतौ कथं तव॥

examples.dm: Whenever one is intent on self-praise, Or on disparaging others, Or if one becomes abusive or filled with remorse, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Whenever one is devoted to self-praise, Or the very disparaging of others, Or becoming abusive and resentful, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: यदात्मोत्कर्षणाभासं परपंसनमेव वा। साधिक्षेपं ससंरम्भं स्थातव्यं काष्ठवत्तदा॥

examples.dm: If one associates with the childish, then from such childishness, Self-praise, the disparagement of others, And talk that delights in cyclic existence and the like, All manner of non-virtue will certainly arise.
examples.gm: If one associates with the childish, Praising oneself and disparaging others, And talking about the joys of cyclic existence and so forth, Non-virtue will certainly arise in every way.
examples.sa: आत्मोत्कर्षः परावर्णः संसाररतिसंकथा। इत्याद्यवश्यमशुभं किंचिद्बालस्य बालतः॥

examples.dm: Whenever one is intent on self-praise, Or on disparaging others, Or if one becomes abusive or filled with remorse, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Whenever one is devoted to self-praise, Or the very disparaging of others, Or becoming abusive and resentful, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: यदात्मोत्कर्षणाभासं परपंसनमेव वा। साधिक्षेपं ससंरम्भं स्थातव्यं काष्ठवत्तदा॥

examples.dm: If one associates with the childish, then from such childishness, Self-praise, the disparagement of others, And talk that delights in cyclic existence and the like, All manner of non-virtue will certainly arise.
examples.gm: If one associates with the childish, Praising oneself and disparaging others, And talking about the joys of cyclic existence and so forth, Non-virtue will certainly arise in every way.
examples.sa: आत्मोत्कर्षः परावर्णः संसाररतिसंकथा। इत्याद्यवश्यमशुभं किंचिद्बालस्य बालतः॥

examples.dm: Regarding the state of one's body and mind, One should examine them again and again; This alone, in brief, Is the definition of guarding introspection.
examples.gm: The states of the body and mind, Should be examined again and again; That alone, in brief, Is the defining characteristic of guarding introspection.
examples.sa: एतदेव समासेन संप्रजन्यस्य लक्षणम्। यत्कायचित्तावस्थायाः प्रत्यवेक्षा मुहुर्मुहुः॥

examples.dm: This concludes the fifth chapter, "Guarding Introspection," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the fifth chapter: Guarding Introspection.

examples.dm: There is no evil like hatred, And no austerity like patience. Therefore, one should diligently practice patience In various ways.
examples.gm: There is no misdeed like hatred; There is no ascetic practice like patience. Therefore, earnestly upon patience, One should meditate in various ways.
examples.sa: न च द्वेषसमं पापं न च क्षान्तिसमं तपः। तस्मात्क्षान्तिं प्रयत्नेन भावयेद्विविधैर्नयैः॥

examples.dm: For that very reason, one should meditate On this analytical investigation as its antidote; The meditative concentration arising from the field of such analysis Is the food of the yogi.
examples.gm: For this very reason, the antidote to this Is to meditate on this analytical discernment; That which arises from the field of analysis Is the food of the yogi's concentration.
examples.sa: अत एव विचारोऽयं प्रतिपक्षोऽस्य भाव्यते। विकल्पक्षेत्रसंभूतध्यानाहारा हि योगिनः॥

examples.dm: If one harbors a mind of stinging hatred, The mind will not experience the taste of peace; One will find neither joy nor happiness, Will not sleep, and will become unstable.
examples.gm: If one holds a mind with the dart of hatred, The mind does not experience peace, Neither joy nor happiness is obtained, Sleep does not come, and one becomes unsteady.
examples.sa: मनः शमं न गृह्णाति न प्रीतिसुखमश्नुते। न निद्रां न धृतिं याति द्वेषशल्ये हृदि स्थिते॥

examples.dm: If one is never sated by sensual desires, Which are like honey on the edge of a razor, Then how could one ever be sated by merit, Which ripens into peace and happiness?
examples.gm: Like honey smeared on a razor's edge, If one is not satiated by sensual desires, Having a ripening of happiness and peace, How could one ever be satiated with merit?
examples.sa: कामैर्न तृप्तिः संसारे क्षुरधारामधूपमैः। पुण्यामृतैः कथं तृप्तिर्विपाकमधुरैः शिवैः॥

examples.dm: Finding its fuel in the mental unease Caused by the occurrence of the unwanted And the obstruction of what is desired, Hatred flourishes and then destroys me.
examples.gm: From doing what is undesired and Hindering what is desired, there arises Mental unhappiness; having found this food, Hatred grows strong and destroys me.
examples.sa: अनिष्टकरणाज्जातमिष्टस्य च विघातनात्। दौर्मनस्याशनं प्राप्य द्वेषो दृप्तो निहन्ति माम्॥

examples.dm: Physical suffering, mental unhappiness, Various kinds of fear, And separation from what is desired— All these arise from the practice of misdeeds.
examples.gm: Suffering and mental unhappiness, Various kinds of fears, And separation from what is desired Will arise from engaging in misdeeds.
examples.sa: दुःखानि दौर्मनस्यानि भयानि विविधानि च। अभिलाषविघाताश्च जायन्ते पापकारिणाम्॥

examples.dm: The followers of Durgā and the people of Karṇapa Endure the sensations of being burned, cut, and so forth; Why then am I so cowardly, When my goal is liberation?
examples.gm: Devotees of asceticism and the Karṇapas Endure the sensations of burning, cutting, and so forth Pointlessly; for the sake of liberation, Why am I cowardly?
examples.sa: दुर्गापुत्रककर्णाटा दाहच्छेदादिवेदनाम्। वृथा सहन्ते मुक्त्यर्थमहं कस्मात्तु कातरः॥

examples.dm: When sentient beings are liberated, What ocean of joy could be greater? Is that not sufficient in itself? What is the use of desiring liberation for oneself?
examples.gm: When sentient beings are liberated, The ocean of joy that exists— Is that itself not sufficient? What is the use of desiring liberation?
examples.sa: मुच्यमानेषु सत्त्वेषु ये ते प्रामोद्यसागराः। तैरेव ननु पर्याप्तं मोखेणारसिकेन किम्॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, the qualities of suffering are: Through weariness, it dispels arrogance, Compassion arises for those in cyclic existence, One avoids misdeeds and delights in virtue.
examples.gm: Furthermore, the quality of suffering is That through sorrow, arrogance is dispelled, Compassion arises for those in cyclic existence, Sin is shunned, and virtue is delighted in.
examples.sa: गुणोऽपरश्च दुःखस्य यत्संवेगान्मदच्युतिः। संसारिषु च कारुण्यं पापाद्भीतिर्जिने स्पृहा॥

examples.dm: The former time when you could ruin me Was another matter; Now that I see you, where can you go? I shall crush all of your pride.
examples.gm: The former times when you ruined me Were a different time; Now I see you, where will you go? I shall destroy all your arrogance.
examples.sa: क्व यास्यसि मया दृष्टः सर्वदर्पान्निहन्मि ते। अन्त्योऽसौ पूर्वकः कालस्त्वया यत्रास्मि नाशितः॥

examples.dm: Since one does not feel anger toward the great sources of suffering Such as bile and the like, Why be angry with sentient beings? They too are all impelled by conditions.
examples.gm: Towards bile and so forth, which are Great sources of suffering, without being angry, Why be angry at those with minds? They too are all incited by conditions.
examples.sa: पित्तादिषु न मे कोपो महादुःखकरेष्वपि। सचेतनेषु किं कोपः तेऽपि प्रत्ययकोपिताः॥

examples.dm: Since harm is inflicted upon embodied beings By both those with minds and those without, Why single out and bear a grudge against those with minds? Therefore, you should endure all harm.
examples.gm: To embodied beings, animate And inanimate things both do harm; Why single out the animate and hold resentment? Therefore, be patient with harm.
examples.sa: चेतनाचेतनकृता देहिनां नियता व्यथा। सा व्यथा चेतने दृष्टा क्षमस्वैनां व्यथामतः॥

examples.dm: Alternatively, if this fault is adventitious And sentient beings are gentle by nature, It is still inappropriate to be angry, Just as it is to resent the sky for being filled with smoke.
examples.gm: But if that fault is adventitious, And the nature of sentient beings is gentle, Even then it is illogical to become angry, Like resenting space when smoke arises in it.
examples.sa: अथ दोषोऽयमागन्तुः सत्त्वाः प्रकृतिपेशलाः। तथाप्ययुक्तस्तत्कोपः कटुधूमे यथाम्बरे॥

examples.dm: This [self] is faulty by nature, So do not praise it for any fleeting qualities. Act in such a way that no one at all Will ever know of its virtues.
examples.gm: This one is of a faulty nature, Do not praise it for its adventitious good qualities. By all means, regarding its good qualities, Act so that no one at all will know them.
examples.sa: नागन्तुकगुणांशेन स्तुत्यो दोषमयो ह्ययम्। यथा कश्चिन्न जानीयाद्गुणमस्य तथा कुरु॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the guardians of hell And the forest of sword-leaves are produced By one's own karma, At whom should I be angry?
examples.gm: Like the guardians of hell, And the forest of sword-leaves, This is produced by my own karma, So at whom should I be angry?
examples.sa: असिपत्रवनं यद्वद्यथा नारकपक्षिणः। मत्कर्मजनिता एव तथेदं कुत्र कुप्यते॥

examples.dm: May the forest of sword-leaves Become for them a dense sandalwood grove; May the Shalmali trees likewise Grow into wish-fulfilling trees.
examples.gm: May the forest of sword-leaves also Become a dense sandalwood forest for them. May the trunks of the śālmali trees also Grow as wish-fulfilling trees.
examples.sa: असिपत्रवनं तेषां स्यान्नन्दनवनद्युति। कूटशाल्मलिवृक्षाश्च जायन्तां कल्पपादपाः॥

examples.dm: However, if I retaliate with harm, They will not be protected, And my own conduct will also be ruined; Thus, my ascetic practice will be destroyed.
examples.gm: But if I cause harm in return, They will not be protected, And my conduct will also decline; Thus my ascetic practice will be destroyed.
examples.sa: अथ प्रत्यपकारी स्यां तथाप्येते न रक्षिताः। हीयते चापि मे चर्या तस्मान्नष्टास्तपस्विनः॥

examples.dm: For the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings, Reaching to the very limits of space in the ten directions, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.
examples.gm: As far as the limits of space in the ten directions, In order to accomplish the aims of all sentient beings, Just as Mañjuśrī acts, May my conduct also be like that.
examples.sa: दशदिग्व्योमपर्यन्तसर्वसत्त्वार्थसाधने। यथा चरति मञ्जुश्रीः सैव चर्या भवेन्मम॥

examples.dm: For both of those who have awakened, That happiness never returns. Whether one’s life is long or short, At the time of death, it is exactly the same.
