examples.gm: For both of those who awaken, That happiness will not return; For both a long life and a short life, At the time of death they end up just the same.
examples.sa: ननु (नूनं ?) निवर्तते सौख्यं द्वयोरपि विबुद्धयोः। सैवोपमा मृत्युकाले चिरजीव्यल्पजीविनोः॥

examples.dm: Desiring results without exertion, And being thin-skinned, you are beset by many harms; Though seized by death, you act like an immortal; Alas, you are destroyed by your own sufferings!
examples.gm: Desiring the result without exerting effort, Being fragile and experiencing many harms, Yet acting like a god while seized by death— Alas, you will be destroyed by sufferings!
examples.sa: निरुद्यम फलाकाङ्क्षिन् सुकुमार बहुव्यथ। मृत्युग्रस्तोऽमराकार हा दुःखित विहन्यसे॥

examples.dm: If you think, "I shall live on my gains And, while doing so, exhaust my sins and perform merit," Yet you become angry for the sake of that gain, Will your merit not be exhausted and will you not incur sin?
examples.gm: If you say, "By living on account of gains, I will exhaust negative actions and perform merit," If I become angry for the sake of gains, Will not merit be exhausted and negative actions created?
examples.sa: पापक्षयं च पुण्यं च लाभाज्जीवन् करोमि चेत्। पुण्यक्षयश्च पापं च लाभार्थं क्रुध्यतो ननु॥

examples.dm: Some commit misdeeds out of delusion; If others, being deluded, become angry, Who among them is without fault, And who is the one who is at fault?
examples.gm: Some commit faults through ignorance, And some, being ignorant, become angry. Among them, who is to be considered faultless? And who is to be considered at fault?
examples.sa: मोहादेकेऽपराध्यन्ति कुप्यन्त्यन्ये विमोहिताः। ब्रूमः कमेषु निर्दोषं कम वा ब्रूमोऽपराधिनम्॥

examples.dm: Since harm is inflicted upon embodied beings By both those with minds and those without, Why single out and bear a grudge against those with minds? Therefore, you should endure all harm.
examples.gm: To embodied beings, animate And inanimate things both do harm; Why single out the animate and hold resentment? Therefore, be patient with harm.
examples.sa: चेतनाचेतनकृता देहिनां नियता व्यथा। सा व्यथा चेतने दृष्टा क्षमस्वैनां व्यथामतः॥

examples.dm: If the qualities do not exist, then even the existence Of sound and so forth becomes extremely remote. It is also impossible for pleasure and the like To exist in insentient things such as clothing.
examples.gm: If the qualities do not exist, sound and so forth Would be very far from existing. In insentient objects like cloth and so forth, It is impossible for pleasure and so forth to exist.
examples.sa: गुणाभावे च शब्दादेरस्तित्वमतिदूरतः। अचेतने च वस्त्रादौ सुखादेरप्यसंभवः॥

examples.dm: Having seen this, I shall strive in every way To gather merit, so that all beings May come to have a mind of mutual love For one another.
examples.gm: Seeing this to be so, by all means, So that everyone will have loving thoughts towards one another, In order to bring this about, I will Exert myself in meritorious deeds.
examples.sa: एवं बुद्ध्‍वा तु पुण्येषु तथा यत्नं करोम्यहम्। येन सर्वे भविष्यन्ति मैत्रचित्ताः परस्परम्॥

examples.dm: Whatever offerings are made to one who possesses a loving mind, That is the very greatness of sentient beings. Whatever merit comes from faith in the Buddhas, That too is the very greatness of the Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whatever offering is made to one possessing a loving mind, That is the greatness of sentient beings. Whatever merit comes from faith in the Buddha, That too is the greatness of the Buddha.
examples.sa: मैत्र्याशयश्च यत्पूज्यः सत्त्वमाहात्म्यमेव तत्। बुद्धप्रसादाद्यत्पुण्यं बुद्धमाहात्म्यमेव तत्॥

examples.dm: Praise and the like distract me; They also destroy my sense of disillusionment. They cause envy toward those with good qualities, And they destroy my excellence as well.
examples.gm: Praise and the like distract me, And also destroy my disillusionment; They cause jealousy toward those with good qualities, And destroy excellence as well.
examples.sa: स्तुत्यादयश्च मे क्षेमं संवेगं नाशयन्त्यमी। गुणवत्सु च मात्सर्यं संपत्कोपं च कुर्वते॥

examples.dm: If one harms others for the sake of oneself, One will be tormented in the hells and other lower realms. If one harms oneself for the sake of others, One will attain all forms of excellence.
examples.gm: If, for one's own sake, one harms others, One will be tormented in hell and so forth. If, for others' sake, one harms oneself, One will obtain all excellences.
examples.sa: आत्मार्थं पीडयित्वान्यं नरकादिषु पच्यते। आत्मानं पीडयित्वा तु परार्थं सर्वसंपदः॥

examples.dm: Since it was accomplished by both him and me, The fruit of this patience Should be offered to him first, For in this way, he is the cause of patience.
examples.gm: Since it is accomplished by this one and myself, Therefore, the fruit of patience Should first be offered to them, For they are the cause of patience.
examples.sa: मया चानेन चोपात्तं तस्मादेतत् क्षमाफलम्। एतस्मै प्रथमं देयमेतत्पूर्वा क्षमा यतः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, since patience arises In dependence upon a mind of intense malice, That very person is the cause of patience, And is as worthy of honor as the sublime Dharma.
examples.gm: Therefore, since patience arises In dependence on a very hateful mind, Because they are the very cause of patience, They are worthy of veneration just like the sublime Dharma.
examples.sa: तद्दुष्टाशयमेवातः प्रतीत्योत्पद्यते क्षमा। स एवातः क्षमाहेतुः पूज्यः सद्धर्मवन्मया॥

examples.dm: Since the attainment of the Buddha's qualities Depends equally upon sentient beings and the Victors, Why is it that you do not show the same respect To sentient beings as you do to the Victors?
examples.gm: From sentient beings and from the Conquerors, The accomplishment of a Buddha's qualities is alike. Just as one respects the Conquerors, Why is it not the practice to do so for sentient beings?
examples.sa: सत्त्वेभ्यश्च जिनेभ्यश्च बुद्धधर्मागमे समे। जिनेषु गौरवं यद्वन्न सत्त्वेष्विति कः क्रमः॥

examples.dm: Since they possess a share in accomplishing the qualities of a Buddha, They are therefore asserted to be equal. Yet no one is equal to the Buddhas, Who are infinite oceans of excellence.
examples.gm: Because they have a share in accomplishing a Buddha's qualities, Therefore they are asserted to be equal. Yet, regarding the boundless ocean of qualities, No one is equal to the Buddhas.
examples.sa: बुद्धधर्मागमांशेन तस्मात्सत्त्वा जिनैः समाः। न तु बुद्धैः समाः केचिदनन्तांशैर्गुणार्णवैः॥

examples.dm: Whatever offerings are made to one who possesses a loving mind, That is the very greatness of sentient beings. Whatever merit comes from faith in the Buddhas, That too is the very greatness of the Buddhas.
examples.gm: Whatever offering is made to one possessing a loving mind, That is the greatness of sentient beings. Whatever merit comes from faith in the Buddha, That too is the greatness of the Buddha.
examples.sa: मैत्र्याशयश्च यत्पूज्यः सत्त्वमाहात्म्यमेव तत्। बुद्धप्रसादाद्यत्पुण्यं बुद्धमाहात्म्यमेव तत्॥

examples.dm: May those heaps of glowing coals become heaps of jewels; May the scorched earth be spread as a crystal floor; May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also become Celestial palaces of offerings, filled with Sugatas.
examples.gm: May those heaps of coal become heaps of jewels. May the burning ground be paved as a crystal ground. May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also, of offerings Become immeasurable palaces, filled with Sugatas.
examples.sa: सोऽङ्गारराशिर्मणिराशिरस्तु तप्ता च भूः स्फाटिककुट्टिमं स्यात्। भवन्तु संघातमहीधराश्च पूजाविमानाः सुगतप्रपूर्णाः॥

examples.dm: If even a mere fraction of the qualities belonging to that unique collection of supreme excellence Appears in someone, Then offering the entire threefold world to honor them Would still be too little.
examples.gm: Of the unique collection of supreme qualities, If merely a fraction of those qualities Appears in someone, in order to venerate them, Even offering the three realms would be too small.
examples.sa: गुणसारैकराशीनां गुणोऽणुरपि चेत्क्वचित्। दृश्यते तस्य पूजार्थं त्रैलोक्यमपि न क्षमम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, with a steadfast mind, I shall overcome all downfalls; For if I am defeated by a downfall, My wish to conquer the three realms will become a mockery.
examples.gm: Therefore, with a steadfast mind, I shall conquer the downfalls; If I am defeated by downfalls, My desire to conquer the three realms becomes a laughingstock.
examples.sa: तस्माद्दृढेन चित्तेन करोम्यापदमापदः। त्रैलोक्यविजिगीषुत्वं हास्यमापज्जितस्य मे॥

examples.dm: What is diligence? It is delighting in the virtuous. Its opposing factors should be explained: Laziness, attachment to what is base, And the despondency of self-contempt.
examples.gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.
examples.sa: किं वीर्यं कुशलोत्साहस्तद्विपक्षः क उच्यते। आलस्यं कुत्सितासक्तिर्विषादात्मावमन्यना॥

examples.dm: Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors, One should strive to increase diligence through the powers of aspiration, pride, joy, relinquishment, Earnest application, and mastery.
examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.
examples.sa: एवं विपक्षमुन्मूल्य यतेतोत्साहवृद्धये। छन्दमानरतित्यागतात्पर्यवशिताबलैः॥

examples.dm: Having been caught by the hunters of the afflictions, And having entered the snare of rebirth, You have walked into the jaws of the Lord of Death; How can you still not realize this?
examples.gm: Having been snared by the fowler of afflictions, Having entered the net of birth, And having gone into the mouth of the Lord of Death, How is it that you still do not know?
examples.sa: क्लेशवागुरिकाघ्रातः प्रविष्टो जन्मवागुराम्। किमद्यापि न जानासि मृत्योर्वदनमागतः॥

examples.dm: If, however, it exists after the object of knowledge, Then from what would consciousness arise? In this way, the arising of all phenomena Cannot be understood.
examples.gm: Or if it exists after the object of knowledge, Then from what does consciousness arise? In this way, of all phenomena, Arising cannot be realized.
examples.sa: अथ ज्ञेयाद्भवेत् पश्चात् तदा ज्ञानं कुतो भवेत्। एवं च सर्वधर्माणामुत्पत्तिर्नावसीयते॥

examples.dm: Without despondency, with an army of forces, With earnest application and self-mastery, Practice the equality of self and others, And practice the exchange of self and others.
examples.gm: Without despondency, and with the forces, Applying oneself earnestly, and mastering oneself, Equalizing self and other, And exchanging self and other, you should practice!
examples.sa: अविषादबलव्यूहतात्पर्यात्मविधेयता। परात्मसमता चैव परात्मपरिवर्तनम्॥

examples.dm: One should first strive to meditate On the equality of oneself and others; Since all are equal in happiness and suffering, One should protect everyone just as one does oneself.
examples.gm: The equality of self and other One should first strive to meditate upon. Since happiness and suffering are equal, All should be protected like oneself.
examples.sa: परात्मसमतामादौ भावयेदेवमादरात्। समदुःखसुखाः सर्वे पालनीया मयात्मवत्॥

examples.dm: Because this, through the power of the awakening mind, Exhausts previous misdeeds And gathers an ocean of merit, It is explained as superior to the Hearers.
examples.gm: Because through the power of this awakening mind Former misdeeds are exhausted, And because it gathers an ocean of merit, It is explained to be supreme over the Hearers.
examples.sa: क्षपयन् पूर्वपापानि प्रतीच्छन् पुण्यसागरान्। बोधिचित्तबलादेव श्रावकेभ्योऽपि शीघ्रगः॥

examples.dm: Likewise, may the Pratyekabuddhas And the Śrāvakas also be happy.
examples.gm: Likewise, may the pratyekabuddhas And the śrāvakas also be happy.
examples.sa: प्रत्येकबुद्धाः सुखिनो भवन्तु श्रावकास्तथा। देवासुरनरैर्नित्यं पूज्यमानाः सगौरवैः॥

examples.dm: To accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, one's forces are aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated by fearing suffering and contemplating its benefits.
examples.gm: The forces to accomplish the benefit of sentient beings Are aspiration, firmness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering And contemplating its benefits.
examples.sa: छन्दस्थामरतिमुक्तिबलं सत्त्वार्थसिद्धये। छन्दं दुःखभयात्कुर्यादनुशंसांश्च भावयन्॥

examples.dm: Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors, One should strive to increase diligence through the powers of aspiration, pride, joy, relinquishment, Earnest application, and mastery.
examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.
examples.sa: एवं विपक्षमुन्मूल्य यतेतोत्साहवृद्धये। छन्दमानरतित्यागतात्पर्यवशिताबलैः॥

examples.dm: To accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, one's forces are aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated by fearing suffering and contemplating its benefits.
examples.gm: The forces to accomplish the benefit of sentient beings Are aspiration, firmness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering And contemplating its benefits.
examples.sa: छन्दस्थामरतिमुक्तिबलं सत्त्वार्थसिद्धये। छन्दं दुःखभयात्कुर्यादनुशंसांश्च भावयन्॥

examples.dm: Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors, One should strive to increase diligence through the powers of aspiration, pride, joy, relinquishment, Earnest application, and mastery.
examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.
examples.sa: एवं विपक्षमुन्मूल्य यतेतोत्साहवृद्धये। छन्दमानरतित्यागतात्पर्यवशिताबलैः॥

examples.dm: I must eliminate the immeasurable faults of both myself and others; Since for each and every one of these faults, It would take an ocean of eons to exhaust them.
examples.gm: The faults of myself and others, Being immeasurable, I must destroy; Wherein for even each single fault, An ocean of eons will be exhausted.
examples.sa: अप्रमेया मया दोषा हन्तव्याः स्वपरात्मनोः। एकैकस्यापि दोषस्य यत्र कल्पार्णवैः क्षयः॥

examples.dm: I must accomplish many virtues for both myself and others; Yet if even for a single virtue, One must train for an ocean of eons,
examples.gm: The good qualities of myself and others, Being many, I must accomplish; Wherein if for even each single quality One must familiarize for an ocean of eons,
examples.sa: गुणा मयार्जनीयाश्च बहवः स्वपरात्मनोः। तत्रैकैकगुणाभ्यासो भवेत्कल्पार्णवैर्न वा॥

examples.dm: The Sage has taught that aspiration is the root of all virtuous qualities; Its own root, in turn, is constant meditation upon the results of karmic ripening.
examples.gm: Of all wholesome factors, The Sage has stated that the root is aspiration, And its root constantly is Meditating on the ripened results.
examples.sa: कुशलानां च सर्वेषां छन्दं मूलं मुनिर्जगौ। तस्यापि मूलं सततं विपाकफलभावना॥

examples.dm: Therefore, even when acting for the benefit of others, There is no conceit or sense of wonder; Because one is single-mindedly devoted to the welfare of others, There is no hope for a ripening result.
examples.gm: Therefore, even when acting for the benefit of others, There is no conceit or amazement. Delighting solely in the benefit of others, There is no hope for a ripened result.
examples.sa: अतः परार्थं कृत्वापि न मदो न च विस्मयः। न विपाकफलाकाङ्क्षा परार्थैकान्ततृष्णया॥

examples.dm: With their skin entirely flayed by the henchmen of Yama, they are utterly tormented, And molten copper, melted by a searing fire, is poured over their bodies; Pierced by flaming swords and spears until their flesh is torn into hundreds of pieces, They fall upon the intensely blazing iron ground as a result of their many non-virtues.
examples.gm: Utterly tormented by the henchmen of Yama stripping away one's skin entirely, Molten copper melted by intensely hot fire poured onto one's body, Pierced by blazing swords and short spears, one's flesh scattered in a hundred pieces, Through many unwholesome deeds, one falls onto a ground of intensely blazing iron.
examples.sa: यमपुरुषापनीतसकलच्छविरार्तरवो हुतवहतापविद्रुतकताम्रनिषिक्ततनुः। ज्वलदसिशक्तिघातशतशातितमांसदलःपतति सुतप्तलोहधरणीष्वशुभैर्बहुशः॥

examples.dm: If one associates with the childish, then from such childishness, Self-praise, the disparagement of others, And talk that delights in cyclic existence and the like, All manner of non-virtue will certainly arise.
examples.gm: If one associates with the childish, Praising oneself and disparaging others, And talking about the joys of cyclic existence and so forth, Non-virtue will certainly arise in every way.
examples.sa: आत्मोत्कर्षः परावर्णः संसाररतिसंकथा। इत्याद्यवश्यमशुभं किंचिद्बालस्य बालतः॥

examples.dm: Those beings who are overcome by pride are afflicted; They do not possess the pride of which I speak. The truly proud do not fall under the power of the enemy, Whereas those others are under the power of the enemy of pride.
examples.gm: Any being who is overcome by pride Is afflicted, not self-confident; The self-confident do not fall under the power of the enemy, They fall under the power of the enemy of pride.
examples.sa: ये सत्त्वा मानविजिता वरकास्ते न मानिनः। मानी शत्रुवशं नैति मानशत्रुवशाश्च ते॥

examples.dm: Whoever maintains pride in order to conquer the enemy of pride Is the truly proud one, the victorious hero; For they have certainly vanquished the burgeoning enemy of pride, And as they wish, they bring the fruit of the Conquerors to perfection for all beings.
examples.gm: Whoever holds self-confidence to conquer the enemy of pride, He is the truly self-confident one and the victorious hero. Whoever definitively destroys the thriving enemy of pride, Perfects the fruit of victory according to the desires of beings.
examples.sa: ते मानिनो विजयिनश्च त एव शूरा ये मानशत्रुविजयाय वहन्ति मानम्। ये तं स्फुरन्तमपि मानरिपुं निहत्य कामं जने जयफलं प्रतिपादयन्ति॥

examples.dm: The foolish, the ugly, and the weak, Are held in contempt everywhere; If even those ascetics who are puffed up with pride Are counted among the conceited, Then tell me, how much more pathetic are the lowly?
examples.gm: Stupid, ugly, and weak, They will be despised everywhere. If ascetics puffed up with pride Are also included among the proud, Tell me, what kind of wretched beings are they?
examples.sa: सर्वतः परिभूताश्च मानस्तब्धास्तपस्विनः। तेऽपि चेन्मानिनां मध्ये दीनास्तु वद कीदृशाः॥

examples.dm: May those sentient beings who have little splendor Come to possess great splendor. May those ascetics who are physically unattractive Become endowed with perfect, beautiful forms.
examples.gm: Whatever sentient beings have little splendor, May they become endowed with great splendor. Whatever ascetics have poor forms, May they become endowed with perfect, beautiful forms.
examples.sa: अल्पौजसश्च ये सत्त्वास्ते भवन्तु महौजसः। भवन्तु रूपसंपन्ना ये विरूपास्तपस्विनः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, just as one would swiftly spring up If a snake crawled into one's lap, So too, when sleep and lethargy approach, One should quickly repel them.
examples.gm: Therefore, if a snake comes into one's lap, Just as one would quickly jump up, Likewise, if sleep and lethargy come, One should quickly repel them.
examples.sa: तस्मादुत्सङ्गगे सर्पे यथोत्तिष्ठति सत्वरम्। निद्रालस्यागमे तद्वत् प्रतिकुर्वीत सत्वरम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, enough of childish behavior! Following in the footsteps of the wise, And recalling the instructions on conscientiousness, I shall dispel sleep and mental dullness.
examples.gm: Therefore, enough with childish behavior! I shall follow in the footsteps of the wise, And, remembering the teachings on conscientiousness, I shall turn away from sleep and lethargy.
examples.sa: तेनालं लोकचरितैः पण्डिताननुयाम्यहम्। अप्रमादकथां स्मृत्वा स्त्यानमिद्धं निवारयन्॥

examples.dm: Through solitude of body and mind, Distractions will not arise. Therefore, one should renounce the world And completely cast aside discursive thoughts.
examples.gm: Through the isolation of body and mind, Distraction does not arise. Therefore, one should abandon the worldly life And completely discard discursive thoughts.
examples.sa: कायचित्तविवेकेन विक्षेपस्य न संभवः। तस्माल्लोकं परित्यज्य वितर्कान् परिवर्जयेत्॥

examples.dm: Thus, when a son dies in a dream, The conceptual thought that he does not exist Is an obstacle to the conceptual thought that he exists, And yet that [thought] is also false.
examples.gm: Thus, when a child dies in a dream, The conceptualization thinking, "He does not exist," For the conceptualization of his existence Is the block, and that is also false.

examples.dm: Because the childish find no pleasure Unless their own interests are served, The Tathāgatas have said that no childish person is a friend; Thus have the Tathāgatas spoken.
examples.gm: Because the childish do not experience joy Unless it is for their own benefit, "None of the childish are true friends," Thus the Tathāgatas have spoken.
examples.sa: न बालः कस्यचिन्मित्रमिति चोक्तं तथागतैः। न स्वार्थेन विना प्रीतियरस्माद्बालस्य जायते॥

examples.dm: Having made myself free of friends and free of enemies, This body shall dwell alone in a secluded place; Regarding myself as already dead, There will be no mourning even when I actually die.
examples.gm: Having made no friends and no enemies, This body dwelling alone in solitude, Having considered it as already dead, Even when dying, there is no mourning.
examples.sa: असंस्तवाविरोधाभ्यामेक एव शरीरकः। पुर्वमेव मृतो लोके म्रियमाणो न शोचति॥

examples.dm: Although this body arose as a single entity, The flesh and bones that were born with it Will disintegrate and separate; What need is there to mention other loved ones?
examples.gm: Although this body arose as one, The flesh and bones that were born together Will perish and separate from one another; What need to mention other friends?
examples.sa: अस्यैकस्यापि कायस्य सहजा अस्थिखण्डकाः। पृथक् पृथग्गमिष्यन्ति किमुतान्यः प्रियो जनः॥

examples.dm: One is born alone, And likewise, one dies alone; Since others do not take a share of one's suffering, What use are friends who only create obstacles?
examples.gm: When born, one is born alone, And when dying, one dies alone; Since no other takes a share of the suffering, What is the use of friends who are hindrances?
examples.sa: एक उत्पद्यते जन्तुर्म्रियते चैक एव हि। नान्यस्य तद्व्यथाभागः किं प्रियैर्विघ्नकारकैः॥

examples.dm: Abandoning all other thoughts, With a mind focused only on myself, I shall strive to settle the mind in meditative equipoise And to bring it under discipline.
examples.gm: Having abandoned all other thoughts, With a single-pointed intention, In order to settle the mind in equipoise And to subdue it, I shall strive.
examples.sa: सर्वान्यचिन्तानिर्मुक्तः स्वचित्तैकाग्रमानसः। समाधानाय चित्तस्य प्रयतिष्ये दमाय च॥

examples.dm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, I shall withdraw my mind from mistaken paths, And always rest it in meditative equipoise Upon the perfect object of focus.
examples.gm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, Having withdrawn the mind from wrong paths, Constantly upon the perfect object, I shall rest in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: स्मादावरणं हन्तुं समाधानं करोम्यहम्। विमार्गाच्चित्तमाकृष्य स्वालम्बननिरन्तरम्॥

examples.dm: That face of your affliction, Is now revealed just as it is; Now that you see it being uncovered by the vultures, Why do you flee from it?
examples.gm: That face which tormented you, Just as it has now become manifest, Having seen it unveiled by vultures, Why do you flee from it now?
examples.sa: तन्मुखं त्वत्परिक्लेशमसहद्भिरिवाधुना। गृध्रैर्व्यक्तीकृतं पश्य किमिदानीं पलायसे॥

examples.dm: Seeing this heap of flesh being eaten by vultures and others, Why do you honor the food of others with flower garlands, Sandalwood, and ornaments?
examples.gm: Seeing this heap of flesh, When vultures and others eat it, Why do you offer to the food of others Garlands of flowers, sandalwood, and ornaments?
examples.sa: मांसोच्छ्रयमिमं दृष्ट्वा गृध्रैरन्यैश्च भक्षितम्। आहारः पूज्यतेऽन्येषां स्रक्‍चन्दनविभूषणैः॥

examples.dm: You yourself contain plenty of filth, And you constantly wallow in that; Yet, out of a craving for the impure, You also desire other bags of filth.
examples.gm: You yourself contain much filth, Which you continually make use of, Yet for other bags of filth as well, Out of a craving for filth, you desire them.
examples.sa: स्वमेव बह्वमेध्यं ते तेनैव धृतिमाचर। अमेध्यभस्त्रामपरां गूथघस्मर विस्मर॥

examples.dm: Not only do you not feel revulsion For your own impurity, But out of a craving for filth, You also desire other bags of impurity.
examples.gm: Towards your own filth, Not only do you not disparage it, But out of craving for filth, You desire another bag of filth.
examples.sa: न केवलममेध्यत्वमात्मीयं न जुगुप्ससि। अमेध्यभाण्डानपरान् गूथघस्मर वाञ्छसि॥

examples.dm: You yourself contain plenty of filth, And you constantly wallow in that; Yet, out of a craving for the impure, You also desire other bags of filth.
examples.gm: You yourself contain much filth, Which you continually make use of, Yet for other bags of filth as well, Out of a craving for filth, you desire them.
examples.sa: स्वमेव बह्वमेध्यं ते तेनैव धृतिमाचर। अमेध्यभस्त्रामपरां गूथघस्मर विस्मर॥

examples.dm: Not only do you not feel revulsion For your own impurity, But out of a craving for filth, You also desire other bags of impurity.
examples.gm: Towards your own filth, Not only do you not disparage it, But out of craving for filth, You desire another bag of filth.
examples.sa: न केवलममेध्यत्वमात्मीयं न जुगुप्ससि। अमेध्यभाण्डानपरान् गूथघस्मर वाञ्छसि॥

examples.dm: Just as the body, despite its many different parts like the hands and so forth, Is protected as a single entity, So too are all diverse beings, with their various joys and sorrows, One in their equal desire for happiness, just as I am.
examples.gm: Although the divisions of hands and so forth are many, Just as they are one as a body to be fully protected, Likewise, the different migrating beings, with their happiness and suffering, Are all one in equally desiring happiness, like oneself.
examples.sa: हस्तादिभेदेन बहुप्रकारः कायो यथैकः परिपालनीयः। तथा जगद्भिन्नमभिन्नदुःख-सुखात्मकं सर्वमिदं तथैव॥

examples.dm: Pleasure and pain have arisen from karma since beginningless time. Tell me, what is it that is created by him? If there is no beginning to the cause, How could there be a beginning to the effect?
examples.gm: Happiness and suffering are from beginningless karma; Tell me, what was produced by him? If the cause has no beginning, How can the effect have a beginning?
examples.sa: कर्मणः सुखदुःखे च वद किं तेन निर्मितम्। हेतोरादिर्न चेदस्ति फलस्यादिः कुतो भवेत्॥

examples.dm: If my own suffering Does not cause harm to the bodies of others, Nevertheless, because I cling to it as "mine," That suffering is unbearable to me.
examples.gm: If my suffering Does not harm the bodies of others, Even so, that suffering is mine, Unbearable due to clinging to self.
examples.sa: यद्यप्यन्येषु देहेषु मद्दुःखं न प्रबाधते। तथापि तद्दुःखमेव ममात्मस्नेहदुःसहम्॥

examples.dm: Likewise, although the suffering of others Does not fall upon me, Nevertheless, because of attachment to a self, That suffering is difficult to bear.
examples.gm: Likewise, although the sufferings of others Do not fall upon me, Even so, that suffering is mine, Difficult to bear due to clinging to self.
examples.sa: तथा यद्यप्यसंवेद्यमन्यद्दुःखं मयात्मना। तथापि तस्य तद्दुःखमात्मस्नेहेन दुःसहम्॥

examples.dm: If you argue that even if it is illogical, One acts in this way because of grasping at a self, Then whatever is illogical regarding self and others Is precisely what should be abandoned as much as possible.
examples.gm: If you say, "Though it is illogical, here One engages through grasping at self," That which is illogical regarding self and others Is to be abandoned to the best of one's ability.
examples.sa: अयुक्तमपि चेदेतदहंकारात्प्रवर्तते। तदयुक्तं निवर्त्यं तत्स्वमन्यच्च यथाबलम्॥

examples.dm: Whatever harm exists in the world, And however many fears and sufferings there may be, If they all arise from grasping at a self, Then what use is that great demon to me?
examples.gm: Whatever harm there is in the world, and However much fear and suffering there is, If all of that arises from grasping at a self, What use is that great demon to me?
examples.sa: उपद्रवा ये च भवन्ति लोके यावन्ति दुःखानि भयानि चैव। सर्वाणि तान्यात्मपरिग्रहेण तत्किं ममानेन परिग्रहेण॥

examples.dm: Looking at one who is equal to himself, In order to make himself superior, He will certainly secure his own gain and honor, Even through contention.
examples.gm: Having looked at those equal to me, In order to make myself superior, My wealth and respect Will definitely be established even through dispute.
examples.sa: सममात्मानमालोक्य यतः स्वाधिक्यवृद्धये। कलहेनापि संसाध्यं लाभसत्कारमात्मनः॥

examples.dm: May the teaching—the sole medicine for the suffering of beings And the source of all happiness— Endure for a long time, Together with support and honor.
examples.gm: The sole medicine for the suffering of beings, The source of all happiness, May the teaching, along with gain and honor, Remain for a long time.
examples.sa: जगद्दुःखैकभैषज्यं सर्वसंपत्सुखाकरम्। लाभसत्कारसहितं चिरं तिष्ठतु शासनम्॥

examples.dm: Chapter Nine: The Perfection of Wisdom
examples.gm: Chapter Nine: The Perfection of Wisdom

examples.dm: The ninth chapter of the Engaging in the Bodhisattva Deeds, the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, this is the ninth chapter, on the Perfection of Wisdom.

examples.dm: The conventional and the ultimate: These are held to be the two truths. The ultimate is not an object of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the conventional.
examples.gm: The relative and the ultimate— These are asserted to be the two truths. The ultimate is not the domain of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the relative.
examples.sa: संवृतिः परमार्थश्च सत्यद्वयमिदं मतम्। बुद्धेरगोचरस्तत्त्वं बुद्धिः संवृतिरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: Nowhere is there any single condition That has the power to produce everything. If ultimate reality is nirvana And cyclic existence is the conventional, then
examples.gm: That a single condition has the capacity for everything Nowhere exists. "If the ultimate is nirvāṇa, And saṃsāra is the relative, in that case,
examples.sa: नैकस्य सर्वसामर्थ्यं प्रत्ययस्यास्ति कुत्रचित्। निर्वृतः परमार्थेन संवृत्या यदि संसरेत्॥

examples.dm: In killing an illusory person and the like, There is no sin because they lack a mind; But in the case of one who possesses an illusory mind, Merit and sin do arise.
examples.gm: In killing an illusory person and so forth, Because there is no mind, there is no sin; But regarding that which possesses an illusory mind, Merit and sin arise.
examples.sa: मायापुरुषघातादौ चित्ताभावान्न पापकम्। चित्तमायासमेते तु पापपुण्यसमुद्भवः॥

examples.dm: Because mantras and such lack the capacity, An illusory mind does not arise from them. Arising from various conditions, That illusion is itself of various kinds.
examples.gm: Because mantras and so forth lack the capacity, Illusory minds do not arise. Arising from various conditions, Illusions themselves are also various.
examples.sa: मन्त्रादीनामसामर्थ्यान्न मायाचित्तसंभवः । सापि नानाविधा माया नानाप्रत्ययसंभवा॥

examples.dm: When, for you, the illusion itself Does not exist, then what is perceived? If it were something else in reality, That aspect would be the mind itself.
examples.gm: When, for you, even the illusion itself Does not exist, then what is perceived? "If it exists as another in reality, That aspect is the mind itself."
examples.sa: यदा मायैव ते नास्ति तदा किमुपलभ्यते। चित्तस्यैव स आकारो यद्यप्यन्योऽस्ति तत्त्वतः॥

examples.dm: When neither entities nor non-entities Remain before the mind, Then, since there is no other aspect, It is thoroughly pacified in non-apprehension.
examples.gm: When both entities and non-entities Do not remain before the mind, At that time, since there is no other aspect, It is completely pacified, without an object of focus.
examples.sa: यदा न भावो नाभावो मतेः संतिष्ठते पुरः। तदान्यगत्यभावेन निरालम्बा प्रशाम्यति॥

examples.dm: When, for you, the illusion itself Does not exist, then what is perceived? If it were something else in reality, That aspect would be the mind itself.
examples.gm: When, for you, even the illusion itself Does not exist, then what is perceived? "If it exists as another in reality, That aspect is the mind itself."
examples.sa: यदा मायैव ते नास्ति तदा किमुपलभ्यते। चित्तस्यैव स आकारो यद्यप्यन्योऽस्ति तत्त्वतः॥

examples.dm: When the mind itself is an illusion, Then what is seen, and by what is it seen? The Protector of the World has also said That the mind does not see the mind.
examples.gm: If the mind itself is an illusion, Then what is seen by what? Even the Protector of the World Stated that the mind does not see the mind.
examples.sa: चित्तमेव यदा माया तदा किं केन दृश्यते। उक्तं च लोकनाथेन चित्तं चित्तं न पश्यति॥

examples.dm: The creator of such things is an object of knowledge, For the latencies of the afflictions have not been abandoned. Therefore, when one sees that object, The latency for emptiness is very weak.
examples.gm: Her creator has not abandoned The latent tendencies of the afflictions toward objects of knowledge; Therefore, when he sees her, His latent tendencies for emptiness are weak.
examples.sa: अप्रहीणा हि तत्कर्तुर्ज्ञेयसंक्लेशवासना। तद्दृष्टिकाले तस्यातो दुर्बला शून्यवासना॥

examples.dm: By habituating the latency for emptiness, The latency for substantial things will be abandoned; And by habituating the thought that "nothing exists," Even that will later be abandoned.
examples.gm: By familiarizing with the latent tendencies of emptiness, The latent tendencies of entities will be abandoned; By familiarizing with "there is nothing at all," That too will later be abandoned.
examples.sa: शून्यतावासनाधानाद्धीयते भाववासना। किंचिन्नास्तीति चाभ्यासात्सापि पश्चात्प्रहीयते॥

examples.dm: For example, just as a Garuḍa shrine, Once established, remains even after the practitioner has passed away, And continues to pacify poisons and the like Even though a long time has elapsed since his passing.
examples.gm: For example, when a garuḍa shrine Has been accomplished and its creator has passed away, Even though a long time has passed since his death, It pacifies poison and so forth.
examples.sa: यथा गारुडिकः स्तम्भं साधयित्वा विनश्यति। स तस्मिंश्चिरनष्टेऽपि विषादीनुपशामयेत्॥

examples.dm: Constructing a shrine to the Victorious One In accordance with the conduct of enlightenment Accomplishes all purposes, even though The Bodhisattva has passed into nirvana.
examples.gm: In accordance with the bodhisattva's conduct, The shrine of the Victorious One is also accomplished; Even when the Bodhisattva has passed Into nirvāṇa, he accomplishes all aims.
examples.sa: बोधिचर्यानुरूप्येण जिनस्तम्भोऽपि साधितः। करोति सर्वकार्याणि बोधिसत्त्वेऽपि निर्वृते॥

examples.dm: Craving is conditioned by feeling, and they also possess those feelings. A mind that possesses an object of observation will remain fixed upon something.
examples.gm: Craving occurs due to the condition of feeling; Those ones also have feelings. A mind that is endowed with apprehension Will rest upon something.
examples.sa: वेदनाप्रत्यया तृष्णा वेदनैषां च विद्यते। सालम्बनेन चित्तेन स्थातव्यं यत्र तत्र वा॥

examples.dm: When, by respectfully accumulating the collection of merit In a manner free from conceptual reference, Shall I teach emptiness to those Who are ruined by their conceptual grasping?
examples.gm: When, in a non-apprehending manner, Having respectfully gathered the accumulation of merit, To those who are ruined by apprehension, Will I teach emptiness?
examples.sa: कदोपलम्भदृष्टिभ्यो देशयिष्यामि शून्यताम्। संवृत्यानुपलम्भेन पुण्यसंभारमादरात्॥

examples.dm: Thus, it is not reasonable To direct refutations toward the position of emptiness. Therefore, without harboring any doubt, One should meditate upon emptiness.
examples.gm: Thus, toward the side of emptiness, Refutation is not appropriate. Therefore, without hesitation, One should meditate on emptiness.
examples.sa: तदेवं शून्यतापक्षे दूषणं नोपपद्यते। तस्मान्निर्विचिकित्सेन भावनीयैव शून्यता॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, in that state, Māra exerts himself To make one fall into the great miserable realms. There, the wrong paths are numerous, And it is difficult to transcend even doubt.
examples.gm: Even there, into the great lower realms, Māra exerts himself to make them fall. There, wrong paths are many, and It is hard to overcome even doubt.
examples.sa: तत्रापि मारो यतते महापायप्रपातने। तत्रासन्मार्गबाहुल्याद्विचिकित्सा च दुर्जया॥

examples.dm: In this way, sattva, rajas, and tamas Are neither son nor father. They are not observed to have a nature That possesses the apprehension of sound.
examples.gm: Thus, sattva, rajas, and Tamas are neither son nor father; And it is not seen to have a nature Possessing the apprehension of sound.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमो वापि न पुत्रो न पिता यतः। शब्दग्रहणयुक्तस्तु स्वभावस्तस्य नेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: The equilibrium of the qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas Is proclaimed to be the Primal Substance; Their disequilibrium is said to be the world.
examples.gm: The qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, Abiding in equilibrium, Are termed Pradhāna; In disequilibrium, they are said to be beings.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति गुणा अविषमस्थिताः। प्रधानमिति कथ्यन्ते विषमैर्जगदुच्यते॥

examples.dm: In this way, sattva, rajas, and tamas Are neither son nor father. They are not observed to have a nature That possesses the apprehension of sound.
examples.gm: Thus, sattva, rajas, and Tamas are neither son nor father; And it is not seen to have a nature Possessing the apprehension of sound.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमो वापि न पुत्रो न पिता यतः। शब्दग्रहणयुक्तस्तु स्वभावस्तस्य नेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: The equilibrium of the qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas Is proclaimed to be the Primal Substance; Their disequilibrium is said to be the world.
examples.gm: The qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, Abiding in equilibrium, Are termed Pradhāna; In disequilibrium, they are said to be beings.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति गुणा अविषमस्थिताः। प्रधानमिति कथ्यन्ते विषमैर्जगदुच्यते॥

examples.dm: To see a cause existing simultaneously with its result Is not possible; It is by relying on a single continuum That the "agent" and "experiencer" are taught.
examples.gm: That the one possessing the cause also possesses the result— To see this is impossible. It is in dependence upon a single continuum That an agent and an experiencer are taught.
examples.sa: हेतुमान् फलयोगीति दृश्यते नैष संभवः। संतानस्यैक्यमाश्रित्य कर्ता भोक्तेति देशितम्॥

examples.dm: Īśvara is not space, because space is inert; He is not the self, as that has already been refuted. And if the creator is also inconceivable, What is the point of speaking of him as "inconceivable"?
examples.gm: Īśvara is not space, because it is devoid of movement; He is not the self, because it was already refuted before; And as for a creator who is inconceivable, What is the use of speaking of the inconceivable?
examples.sa: नाकाशमीशोऽचेष्टत्वात् नात्मा पूर्वनिषेधतः। अचिन्त्यस्य च कर्तृत्वमप्यचिन्त्यं किमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: If there is a gap between the sense faculty and the object, Where would those two meet? If there is no gap, they are but one; What, then, could meet with what?
examples.gm: If there is a gap between the sense faculties and objects, Where would they meet? Even if there is no gap, they are a single entity, So what would meet with what?
examples.sa: सान्तराविन्द्रियार्थौ चेत्संसर्गः कुत एतयोः। निरन्तरत्वेऽप्येकत्वं कस्य केनास्तु संगतिः॥

examples.dm: The mind does not abide in the sense faculties, Nor in forms and so forth, nor in between them. It is not the mind within, nor is it without, Nor is it to be found anywhere else.
examples.gm: The mind does not abide in the sense faculties, Nor in forms and so forth, nor in between them. The mind is not inside, nor is it outside, And it is not found anywhere else.
examples.sa: नेन्द्रियेषु न रूपादौ नान्तराले मनः स्थितम्। नाप्यन्तर्न बहिश्चित्तमन्यत्रापि न लभ्यते॥

examples.dm: An atom cannot enter another atom, For it has no space and they are equal in size. Without entering, there is no mingling, And without mingling, there is no contact.
examples.gm: An atom does not enter an atom, For they have no empty space and are of equal size. Without entering, there is no mixing, And without mixing, there is no meeting.
examples.sa: नाणोरणौ प्रवेशोऽस्ति निराकाशः समश्च सः। अप्रवेशे न मिश्रत्वममिश्रत्वे न संगतिः॥

examples.dm: Those who claim that atoms are eternal Have already been refuted previously. The Sāṃkhyas assert that a permanent Primal Substance Is the cause of the world.
examples.gm: As for those who assert permanent atoms, They have also already been refuted earlier. The permanent Pradhāna is the cause of beings; This is what the Sāṃkhyas assert.
examples.sa: येऽपि नित्यानणूनाहुस्तेऽपि पूर्वं निवारिताः। सांख्याः प्रधानमिच्छन्ति नित्यं लोकस्य कारणम्॥

examples.dm: For a consciousness that is formless, Contact is not at all logical. A collection also lacks substantial reality, Just as was previously analyzed.
examples.gm: For consciousness, which has no body, Meeting is not reasonable at all. Neither is it for an aggregation, because it does not exist as a real entity, Just as was analytically examined before.
examples.sa: विज्ञानस्य त्वमूर्तस्य संसर्गो नैव युज्यते। समूहस्याप्यवस्तुत्वाद्यथा पूर्वं विचारितम्॥

examples.dm: If he depends on something, then the collection of conditions Is the cause, and not Īśvara. When the collection is present, he has no power not to produce, And without it, he has no power to produce.
examples.gm: If he depends, then the collection itself Would be the cause, and not Īśvara. When assembled, there is no power not to produce, And without them, there is no power to produce.
examples.sa: अपेक्षते चेत्सामग्रीं हेतुर्न पुनरीश्वरः। नाकर्तुमीशः सामग्र्यां न कर्तुं तदभावतः॥

examples.dm: When there is no experiencer at all, And feeling itself does not exist, Then, having seen this situation, Why does craving not turn away?
examples.gm: When there is no feeler at all, And feeling also does not exist, At that time, having seen this situation, Why would craving not be turned away?
examples.sa: यदा न वेदकः कश्चिद्वेदना च न विद्यते। तदावस्थामिमां दृष्ट्वा तृष्णे किं न विदीर्यसे॥

examples.dm: There is no experiencer at all, And therefore, feeling itself does not exist. Thus, how can this collection, Which is devoid of a self, be harmed by this?
examples.gm: There is no feeler at all, Therefore, feeling itself is not real. Thus, for this selfless aggregate, How could it be harmed by this?
examples.sa: न चास्ति वेदकः कश्चिद्वेदनातो न तत्त्वतः। निरात्मके कलापेऽस्मिन् क एवं बाध्यतेऽनया॥

examples.dm: Just as a sprout is produced from a seed, And the seed itself is known by that very sprout, Why is the existence of the object of knowledge not realized By the consciousness that arises from it?
examples.gm: A sprout arises from a seed, and Just as that very seed is known by it, By consciousness, which arises from the object of knowledge, Why is the existence of that [object] not known?
examples.sa: अङ्कुरो जायते बीजाद्बीजं तेनैव सूच्यते। ज्ञेयाज्ज्ञानेन जातेन तत्सत्ता किं न गम्यते॥

examples.dm: If a consciousness other than the sprout Realizes that the seed exists, Then by what means is the existence of that consciousness, Which realizes that object of knowledge, itself realized?
examples.gm: By a consciousness that is other than the sprout, If the existence of the seed is known, By which that object of knowledge is known, From what is the existence of the consciousness itself known?
examples.sa: अङ्कुरादन्यतो ज्ञानाद्बीजमस्तीति गम्यते। ज्ञानास्तित्वं कुतो ज्ञातं ज्ञेयं यत्तेन गम्यते॥

examples.dm: If you ask what created the variety of causes, It is from the very variety of preceding causes. Why is a cause able to produce an effect? It is from the very power of the preceding cause.
examples.gm: If one asks, what made the variations of causes? From the variations of prior causes themselves. Why are causes able to produce effects? From the power of prior causes themselves.
examples.sa: किंकृतो हेतुभेदश्चेत् पूर्वहेतुप्रभेदतः। कस्माच्चेत्फलदो हेतुः पूर्वहेतुप्रभावतः॥

examples.dm: Then even if you do not wish it, The arising of a manifest state from what was non-existent remains a fact. If the effect exists within the cause, Then one who eats food would be eating filth.
examples.gm: The arising of what is unmanifest Remains, even though you do not assert it. If the result abides in the cause, One who eats food would eat excrement.
examples.sa: व्यक्तस्यासत उत्पत्तिरकामस्यापि ते स्थिता। अन्नादोऽमेध्यभक्षः स्यात् फलं हेतौ यदि स्थितम्॥

examples.dm: Those who claim that atoms are eternal Have already been refuted previously. The Sāṃkhyas assert that a permanent Primal Substance Is the cause of the world.
examples.gm: As for those who assert permanent atoms, They have also already been refuted earlier. The permanent Pradhāna is the cause of beings; This is what the Sāṃkhyas assert.
examples.sa: येऽपि नित्यानणूनाहुस्तेऽपि पूर्वं निवारिताः। सांख्याः प्रधानमिच्छन्ति नित्यं लोकस्य कारणम्॥

examples.dm: Pleasure and the like arise from clothing and such; Since those do not exist, pleasure and the like do not exist. Furthermore, a state in which pleasure and the rest are permanent Is never observed at any time.
examples.gm: Pleasure and so forth are from cloth and so forth; Since they do not exist, pleasure and so forth do not exist. Moreover, permanent pleasure and so forth Are never observed.
examples.sa: पटादेस्तु सुखादि स्यात्तदभावात्सुखाद्यसत्। सुखादीनां च नित्यत्वं कदाचिन्नोपलभ्यते॥

examples.dm: By abandoning the coarse and becoming subtle, Those coarse and subtle states are themselves impermanent. Why, then, do you not accept that All things are likewise impermanent?
examples.gm: Since it becomes subtle after abandoning coarseness, That coarseness and subtlety are impermanent. Likewise, why do you not assert That all things are impermanent?
examples.sa: स्थौल्यं त्यक्त्वा भवेत्सूक्ष्ममनित्ये स्थौल्यसूक्ष्मते। सर्वस्य वस्तुनस्तद्वत्किं नानित्यत्वमिष्यते॥

examples.dm: If the coarse state is not other than the pleasure, Then the manifest pleasure is itself impermanent. If you claim that nothing non-existent can ever arise Because it lacks being,
examples.gm: If coarseness is not other than pleasure, Manifest pleasure is impermanent. If you assert that nothing nonexistent Arises, because it does not exist,
examples.sa: न स्थौल्यं चेत्सुखादन्यत् सुखस्यानित्यता स्फुटम्। नासदुत्पद्यते किंचिदसत्त्वादिति चेन्मतम्॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, in that state, Māra exerts himself To make one fall into the great miserable realms. There, the wrong paths are numerous, And it is difficult to transcend even doubt.
examples.gm: Even there, into the great lower realms, Māra exerts himself to make them fall. There, wrong paths are many, and It is hard to overcome even doubt.
examples.sa: तत्रापि मारो यतते महापायप्रपातने। तत्रासन्मार्गबाहुल्याद्विचिकित्सा च दुर्जया॥

examples.dm: May they never be separated from the mind of enlightenment, May they be devoted to the conduct of awakening, May they be cared for by the Buddhas, And may they abandon the activities of Māra.
examples.gm: Never separating from the awakening mind, And dedicating themselves to the bodhisattva conduct, May they be fully embraced by the buddhas, And abandon the actions of Māra.
examples.sa: बोधिचित्ताविरहिता बोधिचर्यापरायणाः। बुद्धैः परिगृहीताश्च मारकर्मविवर्जिताः॥

examples.dm: Chapter Ten: Dedication
examples.gm: Chapter Ten: Dedication

examples.dm: This concludes the tenth chapter, entitled "Dedication," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: The tenth chapter, called Dedication, from Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva.

examples.dm: When a rain of flowers falls, mingled with scented water, And they see the glowing embers of hell extinguished with a hiss, They wonder, "What is this that has suddenly satiated us with bliss?" And thus may the denizens of hell behold Padmapāṇi.
examples.gm: Through the falling of a rain of flowers mixed with scented water, Seeing the burning embers of hell sizzling and being extinguished, And thinking, "What is this sudden satisfaction of happiness?" May the hell beings see Padmapāṇi.
examples.sa: पतति कमलवृष्टिर्गन्धपानीयमिश्रा-च्छमिति नरकवह्निं दृश्यते नाशयन्ती। किमिदमिति सुखेनाह्लादितानामकस्मा-द्भवतु कमलपाणेर्दर्शनं नारकाणाम्॥

examples.dm: The crowns of a hundred gods offer worship to his lotus feet, His eyes are moist with compassion, and a rain of various flowers falls upon his head; Look at him, accompanied by the songs of praise from thousands of goddesses in lovely celestial palaces! Having seen such a Mañjughoṣa, may the denizens of hell now break into cries of joy.
examples.gm: See how the crowns of hundreds of gods make offerings to his lotus feet, His eyes moistened with compassion, and a rain of multitudes of flowers falling upon his head, In delightful tiered palaces containing thousands of goddesses proclaiming songs of praise!" Seeing Mañjughoṣa like this, may the hell beings now cry out in joy.
examples.sa: पश्यन्त्वेनं भवन्तः सुरशतमुकुटैरर्च्यमानाङ्घ्रिपद्मं कारूण्यादार्द्रदृष्टिं शिरसि निपतितानेकपुष्पौघवृष्टिम्। कूटागारैर्मनोज्ञैः स्तुतिमुखरसुरस्त्रीसहस्रोपगीतै-र्दृष्ट्वाग्रे मञ्जुघोषं भवतु कलकलः सांप्रतं नारकाणाम्॥

examples.dm: May the nuns be endowed with requisites, And may they abandon quarreling and harm. Likewise, may all those who have gone forth Never let their ethical discipline decline.
examples.gm: May nuns be endowed with provisions, And may they abandon quarrels and harm. Likewise, may all who are ordained Remain with unblemished discipline.
examples.sa: लाभिन्यः सन्तु भिक्षुण्यः कलहायासवर्जिताः। भवन्त्वखण्डशीलाश्च सर्वे प्रव्रजितास्तथा॥

examples.dm: Through the kindness of Mañjuśrī, Until I attain the Ground of Supreme Joy, May I always remember my past lives, And may I obtain the state of a renunciate.
examples.gm: And through the kindness of Mañjuśrī, Until I attain the ground of Perfect Joy, May I always remember my past lives And attain ordination.
examples.sa: जातिस्मरत्वं प्रव्रज्यामहं च प्राप्नुयां सदा। यावत्प्रमुदिताभूमिं मञ्जुघोषपरिग्रहात्॥

examples.dm: In the language of India: *Bodhicaryāvatāra*.
examples.gm: In the Indian language: Bodhisattvacaryāvatāra.

examples.dm: Respectfully bowing to the Sugatas who possess the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, and to all who are worthy of veneration, I shall describe the engagement in the vows of the Sugatas' heirs, Having condensed them in accordance with the scriptures.
examples.gm: To the Sugatas, endowed with the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, And to all who are worthy of homage, I respectfully bow down; Then, entering into the vows of the heirs of the Sugatas, I shall explain it concisely in accordance with scripture.
examples.sa: सुगतान् ससुतान् सधर्मकायान् प्रणिपत्यादरतोऽखिलांश्च वन्द्यान्। सुगतात्मजसंवरावतारं कथयिष्यामि यथागमं समासात्॥

examples.dm: Respectfully bowing to the Sugatas who possess the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, and to all who are worthy of veneration, I shall describe the engagement in the vows of the Sugatas' heirs, Having condensed them in accordance with the scriptures.
examples.gm: To the Sugatas, endowed with the Dharmakāya, along with their heirs, And to all who are worthy of homage, I respectfully bow down; Then, entering into the vows of the heirs of the Sugatas, I shall explain it concisely in accordance with scripture.
examples.sa: सुगतान् ससुतान् सधर्मकायान् प्रणिपत्यादरतोऽखिलांश्च वन्द्यान्। सुगतात्मजसंवरावतारं कथयिष्यामि यथागमं समासात्॥

examples.dm: This leisure and endowment is extremely difficult to find. Having attained that which can accomplish the purpose of a human being, If one does not accomplish what is beneficial in this life, How could such a perfect opportunity ever be found again?
examples.gm: These freedoms and advantages are extremely hard to find; Since the attainment that fulfills human purpose has been found, If one does not accomplish what is beneficial in this life, How will such a perfect opportunity arise again later?
examples.sa: क्षणसंपदियं सुदुर्लभा प्रतिलब्धा पुरुषार्थसाधनी। यदि नात्र विचिन्त्यते हितंपुनरप्येष समागमः कुतः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, virtue is always extremely weak, While sin is of great strength and utterly unbearable. Except for the mind of perfect enlightenment, What other virtue could ever overcome it?
examples.gm: Thus virtue is perpetually feeble, While evil is extremely powerful and unbearable; If it were not for the mind of perfect awakening, What other virtue could overcome it?
examples.sa: तस्माच्छुभं दुर्बलमेव नित्यं बलं तु पापस्य महत्सुघोरम्। तज्जीयतेऽन्येन शुभेन केन संबोधिचित्तं यदि नाम न स्यात्॥

examples.dm: The Lords of Sages, who have deeply contemplated for many eons, Have seen that this alone is beneficial. By this, the boundless multitudes of beings Will easily attain the supreme bliss.
examples.gm: The Lords of Sages, who have contemplated for many eons, Have seen that this alone is beneficial; By this, immeasurable multitudes of beings Will easily attain the supreme bliss.
examples.sa: कल्पाननल्पान् प्रविचिन्तयद्भि-र्दृष्टं मुनीन्द्रैर्हितमेतदेव। यतः सुखेनैव सुखं प्रवृद्ध-मुत्प्लावयत्यप्रमिताञ्जनौघान्॥

examples.dm: Like the supreme form of an alchemical elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it into the priceless Jewel of a Victor’s body; therefore, firmly grasp That which is called the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Like the supreme form of the gold-making elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it Into the priceless jewel of a Conqueror's body; Therefore, firmly hold to this so-called mind of awakening.
examples.sa: अशुचिप्रतिमामिमां गृहीत्वा जिनरत्नप्रतिमां करोत्यनर्घाम्। रसजातमतीव वेधनीयं सुदृढं गृह्णत बोधिचित्तसंज्ञम्॥

examples.dm: Like the supreme form of an alchemical elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it into the priceless Jewel of a Victor’s body; therefore, firmly grasp That which is called the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Like the supreme form of the gold-making elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it Into the priceless jewel of a Conqueror's body; Therefore, firmly hold to this so-called mind of awakening.
examples.sa: अशुचिप्रतिमामिमां गृहीत्वा जिनरत्नप्रतिमां करोत्यनर्घाम्। रसजातमतीव वेधनीयं सुदृढं गृह्णत बोधिचित्तसंज्ञम्॥

examples.dm: Like the supreme form of an alchemical elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it into the priceless Jewel of a Victor’s body; therefore, firmly grasp That which is called the awakening mind.
examples.gm: Like the supreme form of the gold-making elixir, It takes this impure body and transforms it Into the priceless jewel of a Conqueror's body; Therefore, firmly hold to this so-called mind of awakening.
examples.sa: अशुचिप्रतिमामिमां गृहीत्वा जिनरत्नप्रतिमां करोत्यनर्घाम्। रसजातमतीव वेधनीयं सुदृढं गृह्णत बोधिचित्तसंज्ञम्॥

examples.dm: Since the sole Guide of beings, through his immeasurable intellect, Has thoroughly examined it and seen its great value, Those who wish to escape the realms of cyclic existence Should firmly grasp this precious awakening mind.
examples.gm: Since the sole captain of beings, with limitless intellect, Has thoroughly examined it and found it to be highly precious, Those who wish to be separated from the states of wandering Should perfectly and firmly hold the precious mind of awakening.
examples.sa: सुपरीक्षितमप्रमेयधीभि-र्बहुमूल्यं जगदेकसार्थवाहैः। गतिपत्तनविप्रवासशीलाःसुदृढं गृह्णत बोधिचित्तरत्नम्॥

examples.dm: Like the fire at the end of an eon, it will surely Incinerate great sins in a single instant. Its immeasurable benefits were explained By the wise Protector Maitreya to Sudhana.
examples.gm: Like the fire at the end of time, it Certainly burns up great evils in a single instant; Its immeasurable benefits Were explained to Sudhana by the wise Lord Maitreya.
examples.sa: युगान्तकालानलवन्महान्ति पापानि यन्निर्दहति क्षणेन। यस्यानुशंसानमितानुवाच मैत्रेयनाथः सुधनाय धीमान्॥

examples.dm: Like the fire at the end of an eon, it will surely Incinerate great sins in a single instant. Its immeasurable benefits were explained By the wise Protector Maitreya to Sudhana.
examples.gm: Like the fire at the end of time, it Certainly burns up great evils in a single instant; Its immeasurable benefits Were explained to Sudhana by the wise Lord Maitreya.
examples.sa: युगान्तकालानलवन्महान्ति पापानि यन्निर्दहति क्षणेन। यस्यानुशंसानमितानुवाच मैत्रेयनाथः सुधनाय धीमान्॥

examples.dm: To summarize that awakening mind, It should be understood as being of two types: The mind that aspires for awakening, and The mind that engages in awakening.
examples.gm: In brief, that mind of awakening Should be understood as being of two types: The mind aspiring to awakening, and The mind entering awakening itself.
examples.sa: तद्बोधिचित्तं द्विविधं विज्ञातव्यं समासतः। बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तं च बोधिप्रस्थानमेव च॥

examples.dm: Although great fruits arise from the aspiring mind While wandering in cyclic existence, It does not produce a continuous flow of merit In the way that the engaging mind does.
examples.gm: From the mind aspiring to awakening, Great fruits arise while in cyclic existence, but Unlike the mind entering awakening, A continuous stream of merit does not arise.
examples.sa: बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तस्य संसारेऽपि फलं महत्। न त्वविच्छिन्नपुण्यत्वं यथा प्रस्थानचेतसः॥

examples.dm: From the moment one has correctly adopted that mind With an irreversible resolve In order to thoroughly liberate The infinite realms of sentient beings,
examples.gm: From the moment that, In order to completely free the infinite realms of beings, With a mind that does not turn back, One perfectly takes up that mind,
examples.sa: यतः प्रभृत्यपर्यन्तसत्त्वधातुप्रमोक्षणे। समाददाति तच्चित्तमनिवर्त्येन चेतसा॥

examples.dm: From the moment one has correctly adopted that mind With an irreversible resolve In order to thoroughly liberate The infinite realms of sentient beings,
examples.gm: From the moment that, In order to completely free the infinite realms of beings, With a mind that does not turn back, One perfectly takes up that mind,
examples.sa: यतः प्रभृत्यपर्यन्तसत्त्वधातुप्रमोक्षणे। समाददाति तच्चित्तमनिवर्त्येन चेतसा॥

examples.dm: This is reasonable, and as it was Requested by Subāhu, For the sake of beings with lesser aspirations, The Tathāgata himself has spoken.
examples.gm: Along with the reasoning for this, In the Questions of Subāhu, For the sake of beings of lesser inclination, It was taught by the Tathāgata himself.
examples.sa: इदं सुबाहुपृच्छायां सोपपत्तिकमुक्तवान्। हीनाधिमुक्तिसत्त्वार्थं स्वयमेव तथागतः॥

examples.dm: This is reasonable, and as it was Requested by Subāhu, For the sake of beings with lesser aspirations, The Tathāgata himself has spoken.
examples.gm: Along with the reasoning for this, In the Questions of Subāhu, For the sake of beings of lesser inclination, It was taught by the Tathāgata himself.
examples.sa: इदं सुबाहुपृच्छायां सोपपत्तिकमुक्तवान्। हीनाधिमुक्तिसत्त्वार्थं स्वयमेव तथागतः॥

examples.dm: Whether it be a father or even a mother, Who else possesses such a benevolent intention? Do even the gods or the sages possess it? Does even Brahmā have such a mind?
examples.gm: Whether it be a father or even a mother, Who has such a beneficial mind? Do the gods or the sages, Or even Brahmā have this?
examples.sa: कस्य मातुः पितुर्वापि हिताशंसेयमीदृशी। देवतानामृषीणां वा ब्रह्मणां वा भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: Whether it be a father or even a mother, Who else possesses such a benevolent intention? Do even the gods or the sages possess it? Does even Brahmā have such a mind?
examples.gm: Whether it be a father or even a mother, Who has such a beneficial mind? Do the gods or the sages, Or even Brahmā have this?
examples.sa: कस्य मातुः पितुर्वापि हिताशंसेयमीदृशी। देवतानामृषीणां वा ब्रह्मणां वा भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: What need is there to mention one who constantly bestows Upon an infinite number of sentient beings for an endless duration The unsurpassed bliss of the Sugatas, Which fulfills every heartfelt aspiration?
examples.gm: To limitless numbers of sentient beings for a long time, The unsurpassable bliss of the Sugatas, Which fulfills all the wishes in their minds, What need is there to mention constantly giving?
examples.sa: किमु निरवधिसत्त्वसंख्यया निरवधिकालमनुप्रयच्छतः। गगनजनपरिक्षयाक्षयं सकलमनोरथसंप्रपूरणम्॥

examples.dm: In order to fully embrace that precious mind, I make excellent offerings to the Tathāgatas, To the stainless Jewel of the sublime Dharma, And to the Sons of the Buddha, those oceans of virtue.
examples.gm: In order to take hold of that precious mind, To the Tathāgatas and the holy Dharma, The stainless Jewel, and the Children of the Buddhas, Who are oceans of qualities, I make excellent offerings.
examples.sa: तच्चित्तरत्नग्रहणाय सम्यक् पूजां करोम्येष तथागतानाम्। सद्धर्मरत्नस्य च निर्मलस्य बुद्धात्मजानां च गुणोदधीनाम्॥

examples.dm: In order to fully embrace that precious mind, I make excellent offerings to the Tathāgatas, To the stainless Jewel of the sublime Dharma, And to the Sons of the Buddha, those oceans of virtue.
examples.gm: In order to take hold of that precious mind, To the Tathāgatas and the holy Dharma, The stainless Jewel, and the Children of the Buddhas, Who are oceans of qualities, I make excellent offerings.
examples.sa: तच्चित्तरत्नग्रहणाय सम्यक् पूजां करोम्येष तथागतानाम्। सद्धर्मरत्नस्य च निर्मलस्य बुद्धात्मजानां च गुणोदधीनाम्॥

examples.dm: In the worlds of the gods and others, there are fragrances, Incense, wish-fulfilling trees, and jewel trees, Various kinds of harvests that grow without being sown, And all other ornaments worthy of being offered;
examples.gm: Fragrances in the worlds of gods and others, Incense, wish-fulfilling trees, and jewel trees, Various crops that grow without being plowed, And other ornaments worthy of being offered,
examples.sa: देवादिलोकेषु च गन्धधूपाः कल्पद्रुमा रत्नमयाश्च वृक्षाः। सरांसि चाम्भोरुहभूषणानिहंसस्वनात्यन्तमनोहराणि॥

examples.dm: I take up with my mind and offer them well to the Munis, the supreme beings, Together with their spiritual heirs; O sublime objects of offering, you who are filled with great compassion, Regard me with affection and accept these offerings of mine.
examples.gm: Taking them with my mind, to the Capable Ones, the supreme of beings, And to their Children, I make excellent offerings; May those holy objects of offering, the ones of great compassion, Think of me with love and accept these things of mine.
examples.sa: आदाय बुद्ध्या मुनिपुंगवेभ्यो निर्यातयाम्येष सपुत्रकेभ्यः। गृह्णन्तु तन्मे वरदक्षिणीया महाकृपा मामनुकम्पमानाः॥

examples.dm: To the Victors and their spiritual heirs, I offer my entire body forever. O Supreme Beings, please accept me completely; With devotion, I shall become your servant.
examples.gm: To the Conquerors and their Children, I Offer my entire body forever. Supreme Beings, please accept me completely; With devotion I will become your subject.
examples.sa: ददामि चात्मानमहं जिनेभ्यः सर्वेण सर्वं च तदात्मजेभ्यः। परिग्रहं मे कुरुताग्रसत्त्वा युष्मासु दासत्वमुपैमि भक्त्या॥

examples.dm: Since I have been fully accepted by you, I shall be fearless in existence and act for the benefit of sentient beings. I shall perfectly transcend my previous misdeeds, And shall commit no further sins hereafter.
examples.gm: Because I am completely accepted by you, I will not fear in cyclic existence and will benefit sentient beings. I will perfectly overcome my previous negative deeds, And I will not commit other negative deeds henceforth.
examples.sa: परिग्रहेणास्मि भवत्कृतेन निर्भीर्भवे सत्त्वहितं करोमि। पूर्वं च पापं समतिक्रमामिनान्यच्च पापं प्रकरोमि भूयः॥

examples.dm: Since I have been fully accepted by you, I shall be fearless in existence and act for the benefit of sentient beings. I shall perfectly transcend my previous misdeeds, And shall commit no further sins hereafter.
examples.gm: Because I am completely accepted by you, I will not fear in cyclic existence and will benefit sentient beings. I will perfectly overcome my previous negative deeds, And I will not commit other negative deeds henceforth.
examples.sa: परिग्रहेणास्मि भवत्कृतेन निर्भीर्भवे सत्त्वहितं करोमि। पूर्वं च पापं समतिक्रमामिनान्यच्च पापं प्रकरोमि भूयः॥

examples.dm: To the Tathāgatas and their spiritual heirs, I offer a bath from many precious vases, Beautifully filled with delightful, scented water, Accompanied by manifold songs and music.
examples.gm: To the Tathāgatas and their Children, With many jeweled vases of scented water, Beautifully and perfectly filled, alongside songs And various music, I offer a bath.
examples.sa: मनोज्ञगन्धोदकपुष्पपूर्णैः कुम्भैर्महारत्नमयैरनेकैः। स्नानं करोम्येष तथागतानां तदात्मजानां च सगीतिवाद्यम्॥

examples.dm: With various fine garments, thin and soft, And hundreds of those most sublime ornaments, I shall adorn the noble Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and the rest.
examples.gm: With various fine garments, thin and soft, And with hundreds of those supreme ornaments, The noble Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and others, I will adorn.
examples.sa: दिव्यैर्मृदुश्लक्ष्णविचित्रशोभै-र्वस्त्रैरलंकारवरैश्च तैस्तैः। समन्तभद्राजितमञ्जुघोष-लोकेश्वरादीनपि मण्डयामि॥

examples.dm: With various fine garments, thin and soft, And hundreds of those most sublime ornaments, I shall adorn the noble Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and the rest.
examples.gm: With various fine garments, thin and soft, And with hundreds of those supreme ornaments, The noble Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and others, I will adorn.
examples.sa: दिव्यैर्मृदुश्लक्ष्णविचित्रशोभै-र्वस्त्रैरलंकारवरैश्च तैस्तैः। समन्तभद्राजितमञ्जुघोष-लोकेश्वरादीनपि मण्डयामि॥

examples.dm: With the finest perfumes, whose fragrance pervades The entire billion-fold world system, I shall anoint the bodies of all the Lords of Sages, Which blaze with a radiant luster like burnished, refined gold.
examples.gm: With fragrances whose scent wafts throughout the three thousandfold world systems, By these supreme perfumes, the bodies of all the Lords of Capable Ones, Like purified and polished refined gold, Radiant and blazing, I will anoint.
examples.sa: सर्वत्रिसाहस्रविसारिगन्धै-र्गन्धोत्तमैस्ताननुलेपयामि। सूत्तप्तसून्मृष्टसुधौतहेम-प्रभोज्ज्वलान् सर्वमुनीन्द्रकायान्॥

examples.dm: To the Lords of Sages, the supreme objects of veneration, I offer delightful Mandārava flowers, lotuses, Utpalas, and all other fragrant blossoms, As well as beautifully arranged and enchanting garlands.
examples.gm: To the Lords of Capable Ones, the supreme objects of offering, with pleasing Mandāra flowers and lotuses, Utpalas, and all fragrant things, And beautifully strung, pleasing garlands, I make offerings.
examples.sa: मान्दारवेन्दीवरमल्लिकाद्यैः सर्वैः सुगन्धैः कुसुमैर्मनोज्ञैः। अभ्यर्चयाभ्यर्च्यतमान् मुनीन्द्रान् स्रग्भिश्च संस्थानमनोरमाभिः॥

examples.dm: To the Lords of Sages, the supreme objects of veneration, I offer delightful Mandārava flowers, lotuses, Utpalas, and all other fragrant blossoms, As well as beautifully arranged and enchanting garlands.
examples.gm: To the Lords of Capable Ones, the supreme objects of offering, with pleasing Mandāra flowers and lotuses, Utpalas, and all fragrant things, And beautifully strung, pleasing garlands, I make offerings.
examples.sa: मान्दारवेन्दीवरमल्लिकाद्यैः सर्वैः सुगन्धैः कुसुमैर्मनोज्ञैः। अभ्यर्चयाभ्यर्च्यतमान् मुनीन्द्रान् स्रग्भिश्च संस्थानमनोरमाभिः॥

examples.dm: To the Lords of Sages, the supreme objects of veneration, I offer delightful Mandārava flowers, lotuses, Utpalas, and all other fragrant blossoms, As well as beautifully arranged and enchanting garlands.
examples.gm: To the Lords of Capable Ones, the supreme objects of offering, with pleasing Mandāra flowers and lotuses, Utpalas, and all fragrant things, And beautifully strung, pleasing garlands, I make offerings.
examples.sa: मान्दारवेन्दीवरमल्लिकाद्यैः सर्वैः सुगन्धैः कुसुमैर्मनोज्ञैः। अभ्यर्चयाभ्यर्च्यतमान् मुनीन्द्रान् स्रग्भिश्च संस्थानमनोरमाभिः॥

examples.dm: I also offer clouds of the finest incense, Captivating and pervasive in their scent. I shall also offer divine feasts Consisting of various kinds of foods and drinks.
examples.gm: Supreme incense with a captivating, pervasive fragrance, Masses of clouds of its vapor I also offer to them; With meals comprising various foods and drinks, Divine feasts I will also offer to them.
examples.sa: स्फीतस्फुरद्गन्धमनोरमैश्च तान् धूपमेघैरुपधूपयामि। भोज्यैश्च खाद्यैर्विविधैश्च पेयै-स्तेभ्यो निवेद्यं च निवेदयामि॥

examples.dm: I also offer clouds of the finest incense, Captivating and pervasive in their scent. I shall also offer divine feasts Consisting of various kinds of foods and drinks.
examples.gm: Supreme incense with a captivating, pervasive fragrance, Masses of clouds of its vapor I also offer to them; With meals comprising various foods and drinks, Divine feasts I will also offer to them.
examples.sa: स्फीतस्फुरद्गन्धमनोरमैश्च तान् धूपमेघैरुपधूपयामि। भोज्यैश्च खाद्यैर्विविधैश्च पेयै-स्तेभ्यो निवेद्यं च निवेदयामि॥

examples.dm: I shall also offer precious lamps Arranged in rows upon golden lotuses. Upon the ground, smoothed and anointed with perfume, I shall scatter beautiful loose flowers.
examples.gm: Arranged in rows of golden lotuses, Jeweled lamps I will also offer. On the cleared ground anointed with incense, I shall scatter pleasing loose flowers.
examples.sa: रत्नप्रदीपांश्च निवेदयामि सुवर्णपद्मेषु निविष्टपङ्क्तीन्। गन्धोपलिप्तेषु च कुट्टिमेषु किरामि पुष्पप्रकरान् मनोज्ञान्॥

examples.dm: Immeasurable palaces resonant with delightful songs of praise, Beautifully ablaze with hanging ornaments of pearls and jewels— These, which have become the ornaments of infinite space, I offer to those whose very nature is compassion.
examples.gm: Immeasurable palaces possessing pleasing songs of praise, Beautifully blazing with hanging ornaments of pearls and jewels, Which have become ornaments of boundless space, these too I will offer to those whose nature is compassion.
examples.sa: प्रलम्बमुक्तामणिहारशोभा-नाभास्वरान् दिङ्मुखमण्डनांस्तान्। विमानमेघान् स्तुतिगीतरम्यान् मैत्रीमयेभ्योऽपि निवेदयामि॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, may a multitude of other offerings, Possessed of music and sweet, captivating melodies, And clouds that soothe the suffering of sentient beings, Remain in their respective places.
examples.gm: Besides those, masses of offerings, Accompanied by pleasing, sweet sounds of music, Which soothe the suffering of sentient beings, May clouds of these remain individually.
examples.sa: अतः परं प्रतिष्ठन्तां पूजामेघा मनोरमाः। तूर्यसंगीतिमेघाश्च सर्वसत्त्वप्रहर्षणाः॥

examples.dm: To all the Buddhas of the three times, And to the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With as many bodies as there are atoms in the realms, I bow down and pay homage.
examples.gm: To all the Buddhas who have gone in the three times, Along with the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With bodies as numerous as all the atoms in the fields, Bowing down, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वक्षेत्राणुसंख्यैश्च प्रणामैः प्रणमाम्यहम्। सर्वत्र्यध्वगतान् बुद्धान् सहधर्मगणोत्तमान्॥

examples.dm: To all the Buddhas of the three times, And to the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With as many bodies as there are atoms in the realms, I bow down and pay homage.
examples.gm: To all the Buddhas who have gone in the three times, Along with the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With bodies as numerous as all the atoms in the fields, Bowing down, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वक्षेत्राणुसंख्यैश्च प्रणामैः प्रणमाम्यहम्। सर्वत्र्यध्वगतान् बुद्धान् सहधर्मगणोत्तमान्॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to the foundations of the awakening mind and to the reliquaries; I prostrate to the preceptors, the masters, And to those who maintain the supreme ascetic discipline.
examples.gm: To the bases of the awakening mind, And to the stūpas, I pay homage. To the preceptors and likewise the teachers, And to the supreme practitioners, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वचैत्यानि वन्देऽहं बोधिसत्त्वाश्रयांस्तथा। नमः करोम्युपाध्यायानभिवन्द्यान् यतींस्तथा॥

examples.dm: Until I reach the heart of enlightenment, I take refuge in the Buddhas; Likewise, I take refuge in the Dharma And in the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: Until reaching the essence of awakening, I go for refuge to the Buddhas; To the Dharma and the Bodhisattvas' Assembly, likewise, I go for refuge.
examples.sa: बुद्धं गच्छामि शरणं यावदा बोधिमण्डतः। धर्मं गच्छामि शरणं बोधिसत्त्वगणं तथा॥

examples.dm: To the fully enlightened Buddhas and Bodhisattvas Who dwell in all directions, And who possess great compassion, I join my palms and pray:
examples.gm: To those who reside in all directions, The perfect Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, Who possess great compassion, Joining my palms, I make this request:
examples.sa: विज्ञापयामि संबुद्धान् सर्वदिक्षु व्यवस्थितान्। महाकारुणिकांश्चापि बोधिसत्त्वान् कृताञ्जलिः॥

examples.dm: Overwhelmed by the confusion of ignorance, And whatever I have rejoiced in— Having seen those faults, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.gm: And, overcome by the confusion of ignorance, Whatever I have rejoiced in, Having seen these mistakes, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.sa: यच्चानुमोदितं किंचिदात्मघाताय मोहतः। तदत्ययं देशयामि पश्चात्तापेन तापितः॥

examples.dm: Whatever sins I, a sinner stained by many faults, Have committed through my many transgressions, Those extremely unbearable deeds, I confess to all the Guides.
examples.gm: Defiled by many faults, Whatever non-virtues I, a sinner, Have committed that are extremely unbearable, I confess them all to the Guides.
examples.sa: अनेकदोषदुष्टेन मया पापेन नायकाः। यत्कृतं दारुणं पापं तत्सर्वं देशयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: I am terrified that I might die Before my sins have been purified. Please protect me with all haste, So that I may be certain to be liberated from this.
examples.gm: Before my non-virtues are purified, I may meet my death. So that I may definitely be freed from them, I pray you, protect me swiftly!
examples.sa: कथं च निःसराम्यस्मान्नित्योद्वेगोऽस्मि नायकाः । मा भून्मे मृत्युरचिरादक्षीणे पापसंचये॥

examples.dm: I am terrified that I might die Before my sins have been purified. Please protect me with all haste, So that I may be certain to be liberated from this.
examples.gm: Before my non-virtues are purified, I may meet my death. So that I may definitely be freed from them, I pray you, protect me swiftly!
examples.sa: कथं च निःसराम्यस्मान्नित्योद्वेगोऽस्मि नायकाः । मा भून्मे मृत्युरचिरादक्षीणे पापसंचये॥

examples.dm: Therefore, to the Victors, the protectors of beings, Who strive for the purpose of shielding all wanderers, And who, possessing great power, dispel every fear, From this very day, I go for refuge.
examples.gm: Therefore, in the Victors, the protectors of beings, Who strive for the purpose of protecting beings, The mighty ones who clear away all fear, From today onward, I take refuge.
examples.sa: अद्यैव शरणं यामि जगन्नाथान् महाबलान्। जगद्रक्षार्थमुद्युक्तान् सर्वत्रासहरान् जिनान्॥

examples.dm: To the Dharma realized within their hearts, Which dispels the terrors of cyclic existence, And likewise to the assembly of Bodhisattvas, I also go for refuge perfectly.
examples.gm: In the Dharma that they have realized, Which clears away the fears of saṃsāra, And in the assembly of Bodhisattvas, Likewise, I perfectly take refuge.
examples.sa: तैश्चाप्यधिगतं धर्मं संसारभयनाशनम्। शरणं यामि भावेन बोधिसत्त्वगणं तथा॥

examples.dm: To the protector Avalokiteśvara, Whose compassionate conduct is never mistaken, I cry out with a piteous voice: "Please protect this sinful one!"
examples.gm: Whose compassionate deeds are unerring, To the protector Avalokiteśvara as well, With an anguished cry, I call out: "Please protect me, a sinner!"
examples.sa: तं चावलोकितं नाथं कृपाव्याकुलचारिणम्। विरौम्यार्तरवं भीतः स मां रक्षतु पापिनम्॥

examples.dm: To the noble Ākāśagarbha, And to Kṣitigarbha as well, And to all the great compassionate protectors, I cry out from my heart, seeking refuge.
examples.gm: To the noble Ākāśagarbha, And to Kṣitigarbha, And to all the greatly compassionate protectors, Seeking refuge, I call out from my heart.
examples.sa: आर्यमाकाशगर्भं च क्षितिगर्भं च भावतः। सर्वान् महाकृपांश्चापि त्राणान्वेषी विरौम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: At the sight of whom, the messengers of Yama And other hostile beings flee in terror To the four directions, I go for refuge to the Wielder of the Vajra.
examples.gm: Seeing whom, the messengers of Yama And other malicious beings Flee in terror to the four directions, I take refuge in the Vajra-wielder.
examples.sa: यं दृष्ट्वैव च संत्रस्ताः पलायन्ते चतुर्दिशम्। यमदूतादयो दुष्टास्तं नमस्यामि वज्रिणम्॥

examples.dm: If, when frightened by an ordinary illness, One must act according to a physician's advice, Then what need is there to mention those Constantly afflicted by the diseases of a hundred faults, such as desire?
examples.gm: Even if frightened by an ordinary illness, One must act according to the doctor's words; Of a hundred faults such as attachment and the like, When constantly stricken by their disease, what need to mention?
examples.sa: इत्वरव्याधिभीतोऽपि वैद्यवाक्यं न लङ्घयेत्। किमु व्याधिशतैर्ग्रस्तश्चतुर्भिश्चतुरुत्तरैः॥

examples.dm: If even one of these could destroy All the people living in Jambudvīpa, And no other medicine to cure them Can be found anywhere in any direction,
examples.gm: Even by just one of them, in Jambudvīpa All the people dwelling there are destroyed; And if other medicines to cure them Are not found anywhere in all directions,
examples.sa: एकेनापि यतः सर्वे जम्बुद्वीपगता नराः। नश्यन्ति येषां भैषज्यं सर्वदिक्षु न लभ्यते॥

examples.dm: Then the intention not to act according to the instructions Of the Omniscient Physician, who removes every pain, Is a state of extreme delusion And is truly contemptible.
examples.gm: In that case, of the omniscient physician Who draws out all pain— The intention not to act according to his commands Is utterly foolish and an object of reproach.
examples.sa: तत्र सर्वज्ञवैद्यस्य सर्वशल्यापहारिणः। वाक्यमुल्लङ्घयामीति धिङ् मामत्यन्तमोहितम्॥

examples.dm: If one must remain cautious Even at a small, ordinary precipice, What need is there to mention the long-lasting abyss That falls for a thousand leagues?
examples.gm: Even on a small, ordinary precipice, If one must remain careful, Of falling a thousand yojanas On a long-lasting precipice, what need to mention?
examples.sa: अत्यप्रमत्तस्तिष्ठामि प्रपातेष्वितरेष्वपि। किमु योजनसाहस्रे प्रपाते दीर्घकालिके॥

examples.dm: From non-virtue, suffering arises. Thinking, "How can I be certain of escaping this?" It is right that I should constantly, Day and night, think only of this.
examples.gm: From non-virtue suffering arises. "How will I definitely escape from that?" Constantly, day and night, by me Just this alone is right to be pondered.
examples.sa: इयमेव तु मे चिन्ता युक्ता रात्रिंदिवं तदा। अशुभान्नियतं दुःखं निःसरेयं ततः कथम्॥

examples.dm: Because of my ignorance and delusion, Whatever natural misdeeds Or proscribed sins I have committed, Whatever they may be,
