examples.gm: Because I am ignorant and foolish, Natural misdeeds or Whatever proscribed negative deeds— Whichever ones I have done,
examples.sa: मया बालेन मूढेन यत्किंचित्पापमाचितम्। प्रकृत्या यच्च सावद्यं प्रज्ञप्त्यावद्यमेव च॥

examples.dm: Because of my ignorance and delusion, Whatever natural misdeeds Or proscribed sins I have committed, Whatever they may be,
examples.gm: Because I am ignorant and foolish, Natural misdeeds or Whatever proscribed negative deeds— Whichever ones I have done,
examples.sa: मया बालेन मूढेन यत्किंचित्पापमाचितम्। प्रकृत्या यच्च सावद्यं प्रज्ञप्त्यावद्यमेव च॥

examples.dm: In the presence of the Protectors, openly, With palms joined and a mind fearful of suffering, I prostrate again and again, And I confess all of these.
examples.gm: Directly in the presence of the protectors, With palms joined and a mind terrified of suffering, Bowing down again and again, I will confess all of them.
examples.sa: तत्सर्वं देशयाम्येष नाथानामग्रतः स्थितः। कृताञ्जलिर्दुःखभीतः प्रणिपत्य पुनः पुनः॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.bo: བྱང་ཆུབ་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་དགེ་བསགས་པ། ། དེ་ལ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། ལུས་ཅན་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས། ། ངེས་པར་ཐར་ལ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། སྐྱོབ་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་། ། རྒྱལ་སྲས་ས་ལའང་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། །
examples.dm: I rejoice in the accumulation of virtue That has become the cause for enlightenment. I rejoice in the definite liberation Of embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence. I rejoice in the enlightenment of the Protectors, And also in the levels of the Bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: In the accumulated virtue that becomes the cause of awakening, In that I rejoice. From the suffering of samsara for embodied beings, In the definite liberation I rejoice. In the awakening of the protectors and In the stages of the Conquerors' sons too, I rejoice.
examples.sa: संसारदुःखनिर्मोक्षमनुमोदे शरीरिणाम्। बोधिसत्त्वत्वबुद्धत्वमनुमोदे च तायिनाम्॥

examples.dm: I joyfully rejoice in the ocean of virtue That is the generation of the mind of awakening, which brings happiness to all sentient beings, And in the deeds that benefit all sentient beings, With a heart full of delight.
examples.gm: Bringing happiness to all sentient beings, In the ocean of virtue of generating the awakening mind, and In the deeds that benefit sentient beings, With joy I rejoice.
examples.sa: चित्तोत्पादसमुद्रांश्च सर्वसत्त्वसुखावहान्। सर्वसत्त्वहिताधानाननुमोदे च शासिनाम्॥

examples.dm: To the Buddhas of all directions, I join my palms and pray: For those wandering in the darkness of suffering, Please kindle the lamp of the Dharma.
examples.gm: To the Buddhas of all directions, With joined palms I pray: For sentient beings confused in the darkness of suffering, I beseech you to light the lamp of Dharma.
examples.sa: सर्वासु दिक्षु संबुद्धान् प्रार्थयामि कृताञ्जलिः। धर्मप्रदीपं कुर्वन्तु मोहाद्दुःखप्रपातिनाम्॥

examples.dm: By raining down showers of food and drink, May I dispel the suffering of hunger and thirst; During the intermediate eon of famine, May I myself become food and drink.
examples.gm: Bringing down a rain of food and drink, May I dispel the suffering of hunger and thirst. During the intermediate eon of famine, May I myself become food and drink.
examples.sa: क्षुत्पिपासाव्यथां हन्यामन्नपानप्रवर्षणैः। दुर्भिक्षान्तरकल्पेषु भवेयं पानभोजनम्॥

examples.dm: My body, and likewise my possessions, And all my virtues of the three times, I shall give away without a sense of loss, To accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: My body and likewise my wealth, and All virtues of the three times, In order to accomplish the welfare of all sentient beings, I shall give away without regret.
examples.sa: आत्मभावांस्तथा भोगान् सर्वत्र्यध्वगतं शुभम्। निरपेक्षस्त्यजाम्येष सर्वसत्त्वार्थसिद्धये॥

examples.dm: May I be a wish-fulfilling jewel, a vase of excellence, A perfected mantra, and a great medicine, And may I be a wish-granting tree, And a cow of plenty for all embodied beings.
examples.gm: A wish-fulfilling jewel and a fine vase, An accomplished knowledge-mantra and great medicine, And wish-granting trees, May I become a cow of plenty for embodied beings.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिर्भद्रघटः सिद्धविद्या महौषधिः। भवेयं कल्पवृक्षश्च कामधेनुश्च देहिनाम्॥

examples.dm: May I be a wish-fulfilling jewel, a vase of excellence, A perfected mantra, and a great medicine, And may I be a wish-granting tree, And a cow of plenty for all embodied beings.
examples.gm: A wish-fulfilling jewel and a fine vase, An accomplished knowledge-mantra and great medicine, And wish-granting trees, May I become a cow of plenty for embodied beings.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिर्भद्रघटः सिद्धविद्या महौषधिः। भवेयं कल्पवृक्षश्च कामधेनुश्च देहिनाम्॥

examples.dm: May I be a wish-fulfilling jewel, a vase of excellence, A perfected mantra, and a great medicine, And may I be a wish-granting tree, And a cow of plenty for all embodied beings.
examples.gm: A wish-fulfilling jewel and a fine vase, An accomplished knowledge-mantra and great medicine, And wish-granting trees, May I become a cow of plenty for embodied beings.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिर्भद्रघटः सिद्धविद्या महौषधिः। भवेयं कल्पवृक्षश्च कामधेनुश्च देहिनाम्॥

examples.dm: May I be a wish-fulfilling jewel, a vase of excellence, A perfected mantra, and a great medicine, And may I be a wish-granting tree, And a cow of plenty for all embodied beings.
examples.gm: A wish-fulfilling jewel and a fine vase, An accomplished knowledge-mantra and great medicine, And wish-granting trees, May I become a cow of plenty for embodied beings.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिर्भद्रघटः सिद्धविद्या महौषधिः। भवेयं कल्पवृक्षश्च कामधेनुश्च देहिनाम्॥

examples.dm: May I be a wish-fulfilling jewel, a vase of excellence, A perfected mantra, and a great medicine, And may I be a wish-granting tree, And a cow of plenty for all embodied beings.
examples.gm: A wish-fulfilling jewel and a fine vase, An accomplished knowledge-mantra and great medicine, And wish-granting trees, May I become a cow of plenty for embodied beings.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिर्भद्रघटः सिद्धविद्या महौषधिः। भवेयं कल्पवृक्षश्च कामधेनुश्च देहिनाम्॥

examples.dm: Just as the great elements, such as earth, And like space itself, may I always be The basis for the various means of subsistence For immeasurable sentient beings.
examples.gm: Just like earth and the other great elements, And like space, permanently, For limitless sentient beings, May I also be the ground of manifold sustenance.
examples.sa: पृथिव्यादीनि भूतानि निःशेषाकाशवासिनाम्। सत्त्वानामप्रमेयाणां यथाभोगान्यनेकधा॥

examples.dm: Likewise, for the realms of sentient beings Extending to the very ends of space, May I be the cause of their sustenance in every way, Until all have passed beyond sorrow.
examples.gm: Likewise, extending to the limits of space, For the realm of sentient beings in all ways, Until they all attain nirvana, May I also be the cause of their sustenance.
examples.sa: एवमाकाशनिष्ठस्य सत्त्वधातोरनेकधा। भवेयमुपजीव्योऽहं यावत्सर्वे न निर्वृताः॥

examples.dm: Just as the Sugatas of former times Generated the mind of enlightenment, And in the Bodhisattva trainings Abided and trained in successive order,
examples.gm: Just as the previous Sugatas Generated the awakening mind, And in the trainings of the bodhisattvas, Just as they progressively abided,
examples.sa: यथा गृहीतं सुगतैर्बोधिचित्तं पुरातनैः। ते बोधिसत्त्वशिक्षायामानुपूर्व्या यथा स्थिताः॥

examples.dm: Today my life has become fruitful; I have well obtained this human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; I have now become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.gm: Today my life is fruitful; I have well obtained a human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; Today I have become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: अद्य मे सफलं जन्म सुलब्धो मानुषो भवः। अद्य बुद्धकुले जातो बुद्धपुत्रोऽस्मि सांप्रतम्॥

examples.dm: Today my life has become fruitful; I have well obtained this human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; I have now become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.gm: Today my life is fruitful; I have well obtained a human existence. Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; Today I have become a child of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: अद्य मे सफलं जन्म सुलब्धो मानुषो भवः। अद्य बुद्धकुले जातो बुद्धपुत्रोऽस्मि सांप्रतम्॥

examples.dm: It is the supreme nectar that overcomes The Lord of Death for all beings; It is the inexhaustible treasure that dispels The poverty of all beings.
examples.gm: Destroying the Lord of Death for wandering beings, It is the supreme nectar. Dispelling the poverty of wandering beings, It is the inexhaustible treasure.
examples.sa: जगन्मृत्युविनाशाय जातमेतद्रसायनम्। जगद्दारिद्र्यशमनं निधानमिदमक्षयम्॥

examples.dm: It is the supreme medicine that completely Pacifies the illnesses of all beings; It is the shade tree of rest for beings Weary from wandering the paths of cyclic existence.
examples.gm: Completely pacifying the illnesses of wandering beings, It is the supreme medicine. For wandering beings wandering and weary on the path of existence, It is the tree of rest.
examples.sa: जगद्व्याधिप्रशमनं भैषज्यमिदमुत्तमम्। भवाध्वभ्रमणश्रान्तजगद्विश्रामपादपः॥

examples.dm: It is the universal bridge that delivers All beings from the lower realms; It is the rising moon of the mind that dispels The heat of the afflictions of all beings.
examples.gm: For all wandering beings, from the lower realms It is the universal bridge that liberates. Dispelling the torment of the afflictions of wandering beings, It is the rising moon of the mind.
examples.sa: दुर्गत्युत्तरणे सेतुः सामान्यः सर्वयायिनाम्। जगत्क्लेशोपशमन उदितश्चित्तचन्द्रमाः॥

examples.dm: It is the great sun that completely dispels The dimness of ignorance of wandering beings; It is the essence of butter extracted From churning the milk of the sublime Dharma.
examples.gm: The dimness of ignorance of wandering beings, It is the great sun that uproots it. From churning the milk of the true Dharma, It is the essence of butter that has emerged.
examples.sa: जगदज्ञानतिमिरप्रोत्सारणमहारविः। सद्धर्मक्षीरमथनान्नवनीतं समुत्थितम्॥

examples.dm: Having thus firmly grasped the Awakening Mind, The children of the Conquerors Must always, without distraction, Strive never to transgress the trainings.
examples.gm: The son of the Conquerors, in that way, Having very firmly taken hold of the awakening mind, Unwaveringly and always, Should strive not to transgress the trainings.
examples.sa: एवं गृहीत्वा सुदृढं बोधिचित्तं जिनात्मजः। शिक्षानतिक्रमे यत्नं कुर्यान्नित्यमतन्द्रितः॥

examples.dm: Having thus firmly grasped the Awakening Mind, The children of the Conquerors Must always, without distraction, Strive never to transgress the trainings.
examples.gm: The son of the Conquerors, in that way, Having very firmly taken hold of the awakening mind, Unwaveringly and always, Should strive not to transgress the trainings.
examples.sa: एवं गृहीत्वा सुदृढं बोधिचित्तं जिनात्मजः। शिक्षानतिक्रमे यत्नं कुर्यान्नित्यमतन्द्रितः॥

examples.dm: Then, having sincerely invited all beings To the unsurpassed bliss, If I were to deceive all those beings, How could I ever go to a happy realm?
examples.gm: To unsurpassable happiness, Having invited them from the depths of my heart, If I deceive all wandering beings, How will I go to the higher realms?
examples.sa: किमुतानुत्तरं सौख्यमुच्चैरुद्धुष्य भावतः। जगत्सर्वं विसंवाद्य का गतिर्मे भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: Even if one abandons the bodhicitta, The way in which those are liberated Is an inconceivable karmic process, Known only to the Omniscient One.
examples.gm: Even though some people give up the awakening mind, As for their being liberated, The way of karma is inconceivable; Only the Omniscient One knows.
examples.sa: वेत्ति सर्वज्ञ एवैतामचिन्त्यां कर्मणो गतिम्। यद्बोधिचित्तत्यागेऽपि मोचयत्येवं तां नरान्॥

examples.dm: Even if one abandons the bodhicitta, The way in which those are liberated Is an inconceivable karmic process, Known only to the Omniscient One.
examples.gm: Even though some people give up the awakening mind, As for their being liberated, The way of karma is inconceivable; Only the Omniscient One knows.
examples.sa: वेत्ति सर्वज्ञ एवैतामचिन्त्यां कर्मणो गतिम्। यद्बोधिचित्तत्यागेऽपि मोचयत्येवं तां नरान्॥

examples.dm: If my body were to be burned for a long time By the unbearable fires of hell, There is no doubt that my mind would be tormented By the blazing fire of unbearable remorse.
examples.gm: If the unbearable fire of hell for a long time Burns my body, Due to the blazing fire of unbearable regret, My mind will doubtless be tormented.
examples.sa: चिरं धक्ष्यति मे कायं नारकाग्निः सुदुःसहः। पश्चात्तापानलश्चित्तं चिरं धक्ष्यत्यशिक्षितम्॥

examples.dm: If my body were to be burned for a long time By the unbearable fires of hell, There is no doubt that my mind would be tormented By the blazing fire of unbearable remorse.
examples.gm: If the unbearable fire of hell for a long time Burns my body, Due to the blazing fire of unbearable regret, My mind will doubtless be tormented.
examples.sa: चिरं धक्ष्यति मे कायं नारकाग्निः सुदुःसहः। पश्चात्तापानलश्चित्तं चिरं धक्ष्यत्यशिक्षितम्॥

examples.dm: Even if all the gods and demigods Were to rise up against me as enemies, They would be unable to lead me into Or cast me into the fires of the Avīci hell.
examples.gm: Even if the gods and demigods All rose up against me as enemies, Even they would not be able To lead and place me in the fire of Avīci.
examples.sa: सर्वे देवा मनुष्याश्च यदि स्युर्मम शत्रवः। तेऽपि नावीचिकं वह्निं समुदानयितुं क्षमाः॥

examples.dm: The afflictions do not reside in sense objects, nor in the collection of faculties, nor in between them; If they do not exist elsewhere either, then where do they dwell to harm the entire world? They are like an illusion; therefore, to abandon fear in your heart, apply yourself to understanding them. Why do you pointlessly inflict harm upon yourself in the hells and other such realms?
examples.gm: Afflictions do not reside in the objects, nor in the sense faculties, nor in between. Nor elsewhere; if so, where do they reside and harm all wandering beings? They are like an illusion; therefore, banish fear in the heart and rely on effort for the sake of knowledge. Why should I be harmed meaninglessly in hells and so forth?
examples.sa: न क्लेशा विषयेषु नेन्द्रियगणे नाप्यन्तराले स्थिता नातोऽन्यत्र कुह स्थिताः पुनरमी मथ्नन्ति कृत्स्नं जगत्। मायैवेयमतो विमुञ्च हृदयं त्रासं भजस्वोद्यमं प्रज्ञार्थं किमकाण्ड एव नरकेष्वात्मानमाबाधसे॥

examples.dm: This concludes the fourth chapter, "Showing Heedfulness," from the *Entering the Bodhisattva's Conduct*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the fourth chapter, called the Teaching on Conscientiousness.

examples.dm: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, Snakes, and all enemies, The guardians of the hell realms, And likewise sorcerers and demons—
examples.gm: Tigers, lions, elephants, bears, Snakes, and all enemies, The guardians of the hells for sentient beings, Evil sorcerers, and likewise rākṣasas—
examples.sa: व्याघ्राः सिंहा गजा ऋक्षाः सर्पाः सर्वे च शत्रवः। सर्वे नरकपालाश्च डाकिन्यो राक्षसास्तथा॥

examples.dm: In this way, all fears And immeasurable sufferings as well Arise from the mind; Thus it was taught by the Speaker of Truth.
examples.gm: Thus, all fears and Immeasurable sufferings too, That they arise from the mind Was taught by the Speaker of Truth Himself.
examples.sa: यस्माद्भयानि सर्वाणि दुःखान्यप्रमितानि च। चित्तादेव भवन्तीति कथितं तत्त्ववादिना॥

examples.dm: The Sage has taught that all such things Are the result of a sinful mind. Thus, within the three worlds, There is no other fear besides the mind.
examples.gm: All such things Were taught by the Sage to be the sinful mind. Thus, in the three worlds, There is no fear other than the mind.
examples.sa: पापचित्तसमुद्भूतं तत्तत्सर्वं जगौ मुनिः। तस्मान्न कश्चित् त्रैलोक्ये चित्तादन्यो भयानकः॥

examples.dm: The perfection of generosity is said to be the mind Of relinquishing all possessions, together with their results, To all beings; Therefore, it is the mind itself.
examples.gm: All possessions together with their fruits, By the mind giving them to all people, The perfection of generosity is taught; Therefore, it is simply the mind itself.
examples.sa: फलेन सह सर्वस्वत्यागचित्ताज्जनेऽखिले। दानपारमिता प्रोक्ता तस्मात्सा चित्तमेव तु॥

examples.dm: To what place could fish and other creatures be moved So that they would not be killed? The perfection of ethical discipline is explained As the attainment of the mind of renunciation.
examples.gm: Where could fish and so forth Be driven away so that they are not killed? From attaining the mind of renunciation, The perfection of moral discipline is explained.
examples.sa: मत्स्यादयः क्व नीयन्तां मारयेयं यतो न तान्। लब्धे विरतिचित्ते तु शीलपारमिता मता॥

examples.dm: To what place could fish and other creatures be moved So that they would not be killed? The perfection of ethical discipline is explained As the attainment of the mind of renunciation.
examples.gm: Where could fish and so forth Be driven away so that they are not killed? From attaining the mind of renunciation, The perfection of moral discipline is explained.
examples.sa: मत्स्यादयः क्व नीयन्तां मारयेयं यतो न तान्। लब्धे विरतिचित्ते तु शीलपारमिता मता॥

examples.dm: Unruly sentient beings are like space; It is impossible to overcome them all. But if this single mind of anger is overcome, It is the same as overcoming all those enemies.
examples.gm: Unruly sentient beings are like space; They can never be entirely overcome. If this single mind of anger is overcome, It is equivalent to overcoming all those enemies.
examples.sa: कियतो मारयिष्यामि दुर्जनान् गगनोपमान्। मारिते क्रोधचित्ते तु मारिताः सर्वशत्रवः॥

examples.dm: Likewise, I am unable to turn back All external phenomena; But I shall turn back this mind of mine; What need is there to turn back anything else?
examples.gm: Likewise, external phenomena too, Cannot be turned back by me, But I will turn back this mind of mine; What need is there to turn back others?
examples.sa: बाह्या भावा मया तद्वच्छक्या वारयितुं न हि। स्वचित्तं वारयिष्यामि किं ममान्यैर्निवारितैः॥

examples.dm: Just as the result of generating a single clear mind Is birth as a Brahmā or the like, The results of body and speech are not such, Because their conduct is weak.
examples.gm: Whatever result is generated by a single clear mind, Such as Brahmā and so forth, The results of body and speech, Because of weak conduct, are not like that.
examples.sa: सहापि वाक्शरीराभ्यां मन्दवृत्तेर्न तत्फलम्। यत्पटोरेककस्यापि चित्तस्य ब्रह्मतादिकम्॥

examples.dm: Just as the result of generating a single clear mind Is birth as a Brahmā or the like, The results of body and speech are not such, Because their conduct is weak.
examples.gm: Whatever result is generated by a single clear mind, Such as Brahmā and so forth, The results of body and speech, Because of weak conduct, are not like that.
examples.sa: सहापि वाक्शरीराभ्यां मन्दवृत्तेर्न तत्फलम्। यत्पटोरेककस्यापि चित्तस्य ब्रह्मतादिकम्॥

examples.dm: Even if one practices recitations and all kinds of austerities For a very long period of time, The Knower of Reality has said that if they are performed With a mind distracted elsewhere, they are useless.
examples.gm: All recitations and ascetic practices, Even if practiced for a long time, If done with a mind distracted elsewhere, Are taught by the Knower of Reality to be meaningless.
examples.sa: जपास्तपांसि सर्वाणि दीर्घकालकृतान्यपि। अन्यचित्तेन मन्देन वृथैवेत्याह सर्ववित्॥

examples.dm: Those who do not understand this secret of the mind, The supreme essence of the Dharma, Will wander aimlessly and in vain, Even though they wish to attain happiness and destroy suffering.
examples.gm: If someone, regarding the supreme principal of Dharma, Does not know this secret of the mind, Even though they wish to attain happiness and overcome suffering, They will wander meaninglessly and in vain.
examples.sa: दुःखं हन्तुं सुखं प्राप्तुं ते भ्रमन्ति मुधाम्बरे। यैरेतद्धर्मसर्वस्वं चित्तं गुह्यं न भावितम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, I shall firmly grasp And properly guard this mind of mine. Apart from the ascetic discipline of guarding the mind, What is the use of many other disciplines?
examples.gm: Therefore, this mind of mine, I shall hold it well and guard it well. Except for the discipline of guarding the mind, What is the use of many disciplines?
examples.sa: तस्मात्स्वधिष्ठितं चित्तं मया कार्यं सुरक्षितम्। चित्तरक्षाव्रतं मुक्त्त्वा बहुभिः किं मम व्रतैः॥

examples.dm: If one protects a wound out of fear of even its slight pain, Then why, fearing the crushing of the Samghāta and Raurava hells, Does one not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.gm: Because of the minor suffering of a wound, If one who is afraid carefully protects the wound, Those who fear the Crushing and Destroying Hells, Why do they not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.sa: व्रणदुःखलवाद्भीतो रक्षामि व्रणमादरात्। संघातपर्वताघाताद्भीतश्चित्तव्रणं न किम्॥

examples.dm: If one conducts oneself in this manner, Whether dwelling among wicked people Or even in the midst of women, The steady practitioner of discipline will not degenerate.
examples.gm: If one acts with such conduct, Whether dwelling in the midst of bad people, Or even dwelling in the midst of women, The steadfast observer of vows will not decline.
examples.sa: अनेन हि विहारेण विहरन् दुर्जनेष्वपि। प्रमदाजनमध्येऽपि यतिर्धीरो न खण्ड्यते॥

examples.dm: By reflecting in this way, one should maintain A sense of shame, respect, and likewise fear. Consequently, the recollection of the Buddha Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.gm: Thinking like this, with shame, Respect, and fear, one should dwell. Thus, the recollection of the Buddhas, Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.sa: इति ध्यात्वा तथा तिष्ठेत् त्रपादरभयान्वितः। बुद्धानुस्मृतिरप्येवं भवेत्तस्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥

examples.dm: By reflecting in this way, one should maintain A sense of shame, respect, and likewise fear. Consequently, the recollection of the Buddha Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.gm: Thinking like this, with shame, Respect, and fear, one should dwell. Thus, the recollection of the Buddhas, Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.sa: इति ध्यात्वा तथा तिष्ठेत् त्रपादरभयान्वितः। बुद्धानुस्मृतिरप्येवं भवेत्तस्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥

examples.dm: The intoxicated elephant of the mind Must be bound to the great pillar of reflecting on the Dharma; One should examine with all diligence So that it does not escape from how it is tied.
examples.gm: The mad elephant of the mind, To the great pillar of thinking on the Dharma, So that it does not escape from how it is tied, Thus, it should be examined with all effort.
examples.sa: निरूप्यः सर्वयत्नेन चित्तमत्तद्विपस्तथा। धर्मचिन्तामहास्तम्भे यथा बद्धो न मुच्यते॥

examples.dm: In such a way, one should strive So that meditative concentration does not slip away for even a single moment; One should individually examine the mind, Thinking, "Where is this mind of mine wandering?"
examples.gm: So that one striving in concentration Does not stray even for a single moment, "Where is this mind of mine engaged?" Thus, one should individually examine the mind.
examples.sa: कुत्र मे वर्तत इति प्रत्यवेक्ष्यं तथा मनः। समाधानधुरं नैव क्षणमप्युत्सृजेद्यथा॥

examples.dm: In such a way, one should strive So that meditative concentration does not slip away for even a single moment; One should individually examine the mind, Thinking, "Where is this mind of mine wandering?"
examples.gm: So that one striving in concentration Does not stray even for a single moment, "Where is this mind of mine engaged?" Thus, one should individually examine the mind.
examples.sa: कुत्र मे वर्तत इति प्रत्यवेक्ष्यं तथा मनः। समाधानधुरं नैव क्षणमप्युत्सृजेद्यथा॥

examples.dm: If one is unable to do so due to involvement in dangers, festivities, and the like, one should act as is appropriate; For it is taught that at times such as when practicing generosity, the rules of discipline may be set aside in equanimity.
examples.gm: When involved with dangers and festivities and so forth, If one is unable, one should act at ease. Thus, at times of giving, It is taught to treat ethical discipline with equanimity.
examples.sa: भयोत्सवादिसंबन्धे यद्यशक्तो यथासुखम्। दानकाले तु शीलस्य यस्मादुक्तमुपेक्षणम्॥

examples.dm: If one acts in this way, all is well performed; Otherwise, neither task will be achieved. If there is no introspection, the secondary afflictions Will not fail to increase.
examples.gm: In that way, everything is well done; Otherwise, neither will happen. The secondary affliction of lacking introspection, In that way, will not increase.
examples.sa: एवं हि सुकृतं सर्वमन्यथा नोभयं भवेत्। असंप्रजन्यक्लेशोऽपि वृद्धिं चैवं गमिष्यति॥

examples.dm: If there is agitation or mockery, Or if there is pride and arrogance, Or the intention to expose others' faults, Or if there is divisiveness and deceit,
examples.gm: With wildness and mockery, Or if one possesses pride and arrogance, And the intention to expose faults, Or if there is an evasive or deceptive mind,
examples.sa: उद्धतं सोपहासं वा यदा मानमदान्वितम्। सोत्प्रासातिशयं वक्रं वञ्चकं च मनो भवेत्॥

examples.dm: Whenever one is intent on self-praise, Or on disparaging others, Or if one becomes abusive or filled with remorse, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Whenever one is devoted to self-praise, Or the very disparaging of others, Or becoming abusive and resentful, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: यदात्मोत्कर्षणाभासं परपंसनमेव वा। साधिक्षेपं ससंरम्भं स्थातव्यं काष्ठवत्तदा॥

examples.dm: If one desires gain, honor, or fame, Or if one seeks a circle of attendants, Or if one's mind desires to be served, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Desiring gain, honor, and fame, Or desiring to seek attendants and retinues, If one's mind desires to be served, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: लाभसत्कारकीर्त्यर्थि परिवारार्थि वा पुनः। उपस्थानार्थे मे चित्तं तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: If one desires gain, honor, or fame, Or if one seeks a circle of attendants, Or if one's mind desires to be served, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Desiring gain, honor, and fame, Or desiring to seek attendants and retinues, If one's mind desires to be served, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.

examples.dm: When impatience, laziness, or fear arise, And likewise when impudence or idle chatter, Or attachment to one's own side arises, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Intolerance, laziness, and fear, Likewise shamelessness and senseless talk, If a mind attached to one's own side arises, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: असहिष्ण्वलसं भीतं प्रगल्भं मुखरं तथा। स्वपक्षाभिनिविष्टं च तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.gm: Intolerance, laziness, and fear, Likewise shamelessness and senseless talk, If a mind attached to one's own side arises, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.

examples.dm: Having thus examined the mind for afflictions And for strivings toward meaningless things, At that time, the heroic one should firmly Restrain it by means of the antidote.
examples.gm: Thus, completely afflicted, Having examined the mind striving for meaningless things, At that time, the hero, by means of an antidote, Should hold it firmly.
examples.sa: एवं संक्लिष्टमालोक्य निष्फलारम्भि वा मनः। निगृह्णीयाद् दृढं शूरः प्रतिपक्षेण तत्सदा॥

examples.dm: With deep certainty and supreme faith, With steadfastness, respect, and courtesy, With a sense of shame and dread of blame, Be peaceful and strive to bring joy to others.
examples.gm: With utmost certainty and excellent faith, Steadfast, respectful, and courteous, With a sense of shame and with apprehension, Peaceful, and striving to make others happy.
examples.sa: सुनिश्चितं सुप्रसन्नं धीरं सादरगौरवम्। सलज्जं सभयं शान्तं पराराधनतत्परम्॥

examples.gm: With utmost certainty and excellent faith, Steadfast, respectful, and courteous, With a sense of shame and with apprehension, Peaceful, and striving to make others happy.

examples.dm: Do not be weary of the conflicting Desires of the childish, But be compassionate, thinking, "These arise from their afflictions."
examples.gm: Of the childish who are mutually discordant, Not being disheartened by their desires, 'From these arisen afflictions, This mind has arisen,' thinking thus, being endowed with compassion, and
examples.sa: परस्परविरुद्धाभिर्बालेच्छाभिरखेदितम्। क्लेशोत्पादादिदं ह्येतदेषामिति दयान्वितम्॥

examples.dm: In matters that are naturally blameless, For the sake of myself and other beings, I should always maintain this mind Without a sense of self, like an emanation.
examples.gm: Regarding faultless things, Having mastered myself and sentient beings, Without "I", like an apparition, This mind should always be held.
examples.sa: आत्मसत्त्ववशं नित्यमनवद्येषु वस्तुषु। निर्माणमिव निर्मानं धारयाम्येष मानसम्॥

examples.dm: Reflecting again and again that after a long time I have obtained this supreme leisure, I should hold my mind as utterly unshakable as Mount Meru.
examples.gm: After a long time, the supreme leisure, Reflecting again and again on having attained it, Such a mind, like Mount Meru, Should be held completely unshakable.
examples.sa: चिरात्प्राप्तं क्षणवरं स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वा मुहुर्मुहुः। धारयामीदृशं चित्तमप्रकम्प्यं सुमेरुवत्॥

examples.dm: First, with your own intellect, peel away this layer of skin; Then, with the blade of wisdom, Separate the flesh from the lattice of bones.
examples.gm: First, this layer of skin, Separate it with your own intellect. And the flesh from the network of bones, Separate it aside with the weapon of wisdom.
examples.sa: इमं चर्मपुटं तावत्स्वबुद्ध्यैव पृथक्कुरु। अस्थिपञ्जरतो मांसं प्रज्ञाशस्त्रेण मोचय॥

examples.dm: At best, it is only fit to be guarded as food for foxes and vultures; This human body is meant only to be put to use.
examples.gm: At best, by foxes and vultures, This is fit to be guarded for the sake of food. This human body Is fit only to be employed.
examples.sa: युक्तं गृध्रशृगालादेराहारार्थं तु रक्षितुम्। कर्मोपकरणं त्वेतन्मनुष्याणां शरीरकम्॥

examples.dm: Regarding the body as a boat, a mere support for coming and going, Think of it as a vessel, And in order to accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, Transform it into a wish-fulfilling body.
examples.gm: Merely as a support for going and coming, Conceive of the body as a boat, and In order to accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, Transform it into a wish-fulfilling body.
examples.sa: काये नौबुद्धिमाधाय गत्यागमननिश्रयात्॥ यथाकामंगमं कायं कुरु सत्त्वार्थसिद्धये॥

examples.dm: Having understood this, one should always Remain diligent in working for the welfare of others. Because the Compassionate One sees far ahead, He permits even those things that were prohibited.
examples.gm: Having understood thus, for the benefit of others, One should always remain striving. By the Compassionate One who sees far, Even prohibited actions have been permitted for that.
examples.sa: एवं बुद्ध्‍वा परार्थेषु भवेत्सततमुत्थितः। निषिद्धमप्यनुज्ञातं कृपालोरर्थदर्शिनः॥

examples.dm: One should share with those who have fallen into wrong paths, the protectorless, And those established in ascetic vows; One should eat only in moderation, And give away everything except for the three religious robes.
examples.gm: To those fallen into ruin, the unprotected, And those abiding in ascetic practice, one should share; One should eat only a moderate amount, And give away everything except the three Dharma robes.
examples.sa: विनिपातगतानाथव्रतस्थान् संविभज्य च। भुञ्जीत मध्यमां मात्रां त्रिचीवरबहिस्त्यजेत्॥

examples.dm: Although the conduct of Bodhisattvas Is said to be immeasurable, One should certainly practice those activities That serve to train the mind.
examples.gm: The practices of the Bodhisattvas Are taught to be limitless; The practice of purifying the mind, One should definitely practice at least that much.
examples.sa: आचारो बोधिसत्त्वानामप्रमेय उदाहृतः। चित्तशोधनमाचारं नियतं तावदाचरेत्॥

examples.dm: Three times during the day and three times at night, One should recite the Three Heaps Sūtra; By relying on the Victors and the spirit of awakening, One should pacify the remaining downfalls.
examples.gm: Three times during the day and night, One should recite the Triskandha; By relying on the Conquerors and the awakening mind, One should pacify the remainder of downfalls thereby.
examples.sa: रात्रिंदिवं च त्रिस्कन्धं त्रिष्कालं च प्रवर्तयेत्। शेषापत्तिशमस्तेन बोधिचित्तजिनाश्रयात्॥

examples.dm: Whether directly or indirectly, Do nothing other than act for the benefit of sentient beings; Solely for the sake of sentient beings, Dedicate everything toward enlightenment.
examples.gm: Whether directly or else indirectly, One should do nothing other than the benefit of sentient beings; For the sake of sentient beings alone, One should dedicate everything for awakening.
examples.sa: पारंपर्येण साक्षाद्वा सत्त्वार्थं नान्यदाचरेत्। सत्त्वानामेव चार्थाय सर्वं बोधाय नामयेत्॥

examples.dm: One should never forsake a spiritual friend Who is learned in the meaning of the Mahāyāna And possesses the supreme conduct of a Bodhisattva, Even at the cost of one's own life.
examples.gm: Always, the virtuous spiritual friend, Who is skilled in the meaning of the Mahāyāna, And the supreme discipline of the bodhisattvas, Should not be given up even for the sake of one's life.
examples.sa: सदा कल्याणमित्रं च जीवितार्थेऽपि न त्यजेत्। बोधिसत्त्वव्रतधरं महायानार्थकोविदम्॥

examples.dm: Learn the manner of relying on a guru As described in the life story of Śrīsambhava; This and other teachings of the Buddha Are to be understood by reading the sūtras.
examples.gm: From the liberation story of Śrīsaṃbhava, One should train in the manner of relying on the guru; This and other words spoken by the Buddha, Should be known after reading the sūtras.
examples.sa: श्रीसंभवविमोक्षाच्च शिक्षेद्यद्गुरुवर्तनम्। एतच्चान्यच्च बुद्धोक्तं ज्ञेयं सूत्रान्तवाचनात्॥

examples.dm: The trainings are revealed within the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, in particular, Should be looked at first of all.
examples.gm: The trainings appear in the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, Should be looked at from the very beginning.
examples.sa: शिक्षाः सूत्रेषु दृश्यन्ते तस्मात्सूत्राणि वाचयेत्। आकाशगर्भसूत्रे च मूलापत्तीर्निरूपयेत्॥

examples.dm: Because it extensively demonstrates What must be practiced at all times, The Śikṣāsamuccaya as well Should certainly be looked at again and again.
examples.gm: Because what is to be practiced constantly Is extensively taught in that, The Śikṣāsamuccaya, too, Should definitely be looked at again and again.
examples.sa: शिक्षासमुच्चयोऽवश्यं द्रष्टव्यश्च पुनः पुनः। विस्तरेण सदाचारो यस्मात्तत्र प्रदर्शितः॥

examples.dm: Alternatively, for the time being, one should look at the concise Compendium of Sūtras; Both works composed by the noble Nāgārjuna should also be studied with diligence.
examples.gm: Or else, for the time being, the brief Sūtrasamuccaya should be looked at; And the two composed by the Noble Nāgārjuna Should also be looked at with effort.
examples.sa: संक्षेपेणाथवा तावत्पश्येत्सूत्रसमुच्चयम्। आर्यनागार्जुनाबद्धं द्वितीयं च प्रयत्नतः॥

examples.dm: Alternatively, for the time being, one should look at the concise Compendium of Sūtras; Both works composed by the noble Nāgārjuna should also be studied with diligence.
examples.gm: Or else, for the time being, the brief Sūtrasamuccaya should be looked at; And the two composed by the Noble Nāgārjuna Should also be looked at with effort.
examples.sa: संक्षेपेणाथवा तावत्पश्येत्सूत्रसमुच्चयम्। आर्यनागार्जुनाबद्धं द्वितीयं च प्रयत्नतः॥

examples.dm: Alternatively, for the time being, one should look at the concise Compendium of Sūtras; Both works composed by the noble Nāgārjuna should also be studied with diligence.
examples.gm: Or else, for the time being, the brief Sūtrasamuccaya should be looked at; And the two composed by the Noble Nāgārjuna Should also be looked at with effort.
examples.sa: संक्षेपेणाथवा तावत्पश्येत्सूत्रसमुच्चयम्। आर्यनागार्जुनाबद्धं द्वितीयं च प्रयत्नतः॥

examples.dm: Alternatively, for the time being, one should look at the concise Compendium of Sūtras; Both works composed by the noble Nāgārjuna should also be studied with diligence.
examples.gm: Or else, for the time being, the brief Sūtrasamuccaya should be looked at; And the two composed by the Noble Nāgārjuna Should also be looked at with effort.
examples.sa: संक्षेपेणाथवा तावत्पश्येत्सूत्रसमुच्चयम्। आर्यनागार्जुनाबद्धं द्वितीयं च प्रयत्नतः॥

examples.dm: Whatever virtuous deeds have been accumulated, Such as generosity and offerings to the Sugatas, Over a thousand eons, A single moment of anger destroys them all.
examples.gm: Accumulated over a thousand eons, Generosity, offerings to the Sugatas, and so forth— Whatever good conduct there is, all of that, A single moment of anger destroys.
examples.sa: सर्वमेतत्सुचरितं दानं सुगतपूजनम्। कृतं कल्पसहस्रैर्यत्प्रतिघः प्रतिहन्ति तत्॥

examples.dm: Whatever virtuous deeds have been accumulated, Such as generosity and offerings to the Sugatas, Over a thousand eons, A single moment of anger destroys them all.
examples.gm: Accumulated over a thousand eons, Generosity, offerings to the Sugatas, and so forth— Whatever good conduct there is, all of that, A single moment of anger destroys.
examples.sa: सर्वमेतत्सुचरितं दानं सुगतपूजनम्। कृतं कल्पसहस्रैर्यत्प्रतिघः प्रतिहन्ति तत्॥

examples.dm: The causes of happiness occur only occasionally, While the causes of suffering are extremely numerous. Without suffering, there is no renunciation; Therefore, O mind, remain steadfast.
examples.gm: The causes of happiness occur sometimes; The causes of suffering are very many. Without suffering, there is no renunciation. Therefore, mind, resolve to be steadfast!
examples.sa: कथंचिल्लभ्यते सौख्यं दुःखं स्थितमयत्नतः। दुःखेनैव च निःसारः चेतस्तस्माद् दृढीभव॥

examples.dm: The followers of Durgā and the people of Karṇapa Endure the sensations of being burned, cut, and so forth; Why then am I so cowardly, When my goal is liberation?
examples.gm: Devotees of asceticism and the Karṇapas Endure the sensations of burning, cutting, and so forth Pointlessly; for the sake of liberation, Why am I cowardly?
examples.sa: दुर्गापुत्रककर्णाटा दाहच्छेदादिवेदनाम्। वृथा सहन्ते मुक्त्यर्थमहं कस्मात्तु कातरः॥

examples.dm: The followers of Durgā and the people of Karṇapa Endure the sensations of being burned, cut, and so forth; Why then am I so cowardly, When my goal is liberation?
examples.gm: Devotees of asceticism and the Karṇapas Endure the sensations of burning, cutting, and so forth Pointlessly; for the sake of liberation, Why am I cowardly?
examples.sa: दुर्गापुत्रककर्णाटा दाहच्छेदादिवेदनाम्। वृथा सहन्ते मुक्त्यर्थमहं कस्मात्तु कातरः॥

examples.dm: Since one does not feel anger toward the great sources of suffering Such as bile and the like, Why be angry with sentient beings? They too are all impelled by conditions.
examples.gm: Towards bile and so forth, which are Great sources of suffering, without being angry, Why be angry at those with minds? They too are all incited by conditions.
examples.sa: पित्तादिषु न मे कोपो महादुःखकरेष्वपि। सचेतनेषु किं कोपः तेऽपि प्रत्ययकोपिताः॥

examples.dm: Through heedlessness, people even harm themselves With thorns and the like; For the sake of obtaining women and other such objects, They are consumed by craving and engage in fasting and the like.
examples.gm: Due to carelessness, even to themselves, They do harm with thorns and so forth; In order to obtain women and the like, They become obsessed and starve themselves and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रमादादात्मनात्मानं बाधन्ते कण्टकादिभिः। भक्तच्छेदादिभिः कोपाद्दुरापस्त्र्यादिलिप्सया॥

examples.dm: Through heedlessness, people even harm themselves With thorns and the like; For the sake of obtaining women and other such objects, They are consumed by craving and engage in fasting and the like.
examples.gm: Due to carelessness, even to themselves, They do harm with thorns and so forth; In order to obtain women and the like, They become obsessed and starve themselves and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रमादादात्मनात्मानं बाधन्ते कण्टकादिभिः। भक्तच्छेदादिभिः कोपाद्दुरापस्त्र्यादिलिप्सया॥

examples.dm: Some hang themselves or leap from cliffs, Consume poison or unwholesome food, And through non-meritorious conduct, They inflict harm upon themselves.
examples.gm: Some hang themselves or jump from cliffs, Eat poison or unwholesome food, And through non-meritorious conduct, They bring harm upon themselves.
examples.sa: उद्बन्धनप्रपातैश्च विषापथ्यादिभक्षणैः। निघ्नन्ति केचिदात्मानपुण्याचरणेन च॥

examples.dm: Impelled by my own past actions, Those who harm me have arisen; If by this they go to the hells, Have I not been the one to ruin them?
examples.gm: Instigated by my own karma, Those who harm me appear; If because of this they go to hell, Have I not ruined them?
examples.sa: मत्कर्मचोदिता एव जाता मय्यपकारिणः। येन यास्यन्ति नरकान्मयैवामी हता ननु॥

examples.dm: I am the one who causes them harm, And they are the ones who benefit me; Why, then, O wicked mind, Do you perversely become angry?
examples.gm: I am the one who harms them, While they are the ones who benefit me; Why perversely, O wicked mind, do you become angry?
examples.sa: अहमेवापकार्येषां ममैते चोपकारिणः। कस्माद्विपर्ययं कृत्वा खलचेतः प्रकुप्यसि॥

examples.dm: If I possess the virtue of a patient intention, I shall not go to the hells; If I protect myself, What harm has been done to them in this?
examples.gm: If I possess the good qualities Of intention, I will not go to hell; If I protect myself, What will happen to them here?
examples.sa: भवेन्ममाशयगुणो न यामि नरकान् यदि। एषामत्र किमायातं यद्यात्मा रक्षितो मया॥

examples.dm: Since the mind is not a physical entity, No one can destroy it anywhere; Because of intense attachment to the body, The body is afflicted by sufferings.
examples.gm: Because the mind is bodiless, No one can destroy it anywhere; Because of deep attachment to the body, The body is harmed by sufferings.
examples.sa: मनो हन्तुममूर्तत्वान्न शक्यं केनचित्क्वचित्। शरीराभिनिवेशात्तु चित्तं दुःखेन बाध्यते॥

examples.dm: If contempt, harsh speech, And unpleasant words Do not cause any harm to the body, Why, O mind, do you become so angry?
examples.gm: Contempt, speaking harsh words, And those unpleasant words— Since they do not harm the body, O mind, why do you become so angry?
examples.sa: न्यक्कारः परुषं वाक्यमयशश्चेत्ययं गणः। कायं न बाधते तेन चेतः कस्मात्प्रकुप्यसि॥

examples.dm: If the dislike that others have for me Does not consume me in this life or in other lives, Why should I be averse to it?
examples.gm: That others dislike me, Since that, in this life or another, Will not consume me, Why do I dislike it?
examples.sa: मय्यप्रसादो योऽन्येषां स मां किं भक्षयिष्यति। इह जन्मान्तरे वापि येनासौ मेऽनभीप्सितः॥

examples.dm: If I am averse to this because it creates obstacles to my gain, My gains will be discarded in this world, But my sins will remain firm.
examples.gm: Because it hinders my gain, If I do not desire this, My gain will be left behind here, But my negative actions will remain steadfast.
examples.sa: लाभान्तरायकारित्वाद् यद्यसौ मेऽनभीप्सितः। नङ्क्ष्यतीहैव मे लाभः पापं तु स्थास्यति ध्रुवम्॥

examples.dm: It is better that I die this very day Than to live a long life through wrong livelihood; Even if I were to remain for a long time, The suffering of death will be exactly the same.
examples.gm: It is better that I die this very day, Than to live long by wrong livelihood; Even if I remain for a long time, The suffering of death will be just the same.
examples.sa: वरमद्यैव मे मृत्युर्न मिथ्याजीवितं चिरम्। यस्माच्चिरमपि स्थित्वा मृत्युदुःखं तदेव मे॥

examples.dm: It is better that I die this very day Than to live a long life through wrong livelihood; Even if I were to remain for a long time, The suffering of death will be exactly the same.
examples.gm: It is better that I die this very day, Than to live long by wrong livelihood; Even if I remain for a long time, The suffering of death will be just the same.
examples.sa: वरमद्यैव मे मृत्युर्न मिथ्याजीवितं चिरम्। यस्माच्चिरमपि स्थित्वा मृत्युदुःखं तदेव मे॥

examples.dm: This happiness of your rejoicing Is a source of bliss that is blameless; It is permitted by those endowed with excellence, And is the supreme way of attracting others.
examples.gm: This joy of your rejoicing Produces happiness and has no blame; It is approved by those possessing good qualities, And is also supreme in gathering others.
examples.sa: इदं च ते हृष्टिसुखं निरवद्यं सुखोदयम्। न वारितं च गुणिभिः परावर्जनमुत्तमम्॥

examples.dm: If you do not desire this happiness Thinking, "In that way, the other person would be happy," Then by ceasing to give wages and the like, You will be ruined in both this life and the next.
examples.gm: Thinking, "Others will become happy in that way," If you do not want this happiness, Because you forsake giving wages and so forth, You will be ruined in the seen and the unseen.
examples.sa: तस्यैव सुखमित्येवं तवेदं यदि न प्रियम्। भृतिदानादिविरतेर्दृष्टादृष्टं हतं भवेत्॥

examples.dm: Since you have generated the mind of enlightenment Out of a desire for all sentient beings to be happy, Why do you become angry When sentient beings find happiness for themselves?
examples.gm: Because you desire happiness for all sentient beings, Having generated the mind of awakening, If sentient beings find happiness themselves, Why do you become angry because of that?
examples.sa: बोधिचित्तं समुत्पाद्य सर्वसत्त्वसुखेच्छया। स्वयं लब्धसुखेष्वद्य कस्मात्सत्त्वेषु कुप्यसि॥

examples.dm: If you desire for sentient beings to attain Buddhahood, Which is honored by the three worlds, Why are you distressed when you see them Receive even a meager amount of honor and respect?
examples.gm: To awaken into Buddhahood worshipped by the three worlds, If you desire for sentient beings, Having seen them receive mere meager respect, Why do you become tormented by that?
examples.sa: त्रैलोक्यपूज्यं बुद्धत्वं सत्त्वानां किल वाञ्छसि। सत्कारमित्वरं दृष्ट्वा तेषां किं परिदह्यसे॥

examples.dm: If you desire for sentient beings to attain Buddhahood, Which is honored by the three worlds, Why are you distressed when you see them Receive even a meager amount of honor and respect?
examples.gm: To awaken into Buddhahood worshipped by the three worlds, If you desire for sentient beings, Having seen them receive mere meager respect, Why do you become tormented by that?
examples.sa: त्रैलोक्यपूज्यं बुद्धत्वं सत्त्वानां किल वाञ्छसि। सत्कारमित्वरं दृष्ट्वा तेषां किं परिदह्यसे॥

examples.dm: Whether that person receives it from another, Or it remains in the benefactor's house, In either case, it is not yours; So what does it matter to you whether it is given or not?
examples.gm: If he receives that from him, Or if it remains in the benefactor's house, In all ways, since you do not have it, What does it matter whether it is given or not given?
examples.sa: यदि तेन न तल्लब्धं स्थितं दानपतेर्गृहे। सर्वथापि न तत्तेऽस्ति दत्तादत्तेन तेन किम्॥

examples.dm: Even if an enemy is unhappy, What reason is there for you to rejoice in that? Your mere wishful thinking Will not become a cause of harm to them.
examples.gm: Even if an enemy is unhappy, What is there for you to rejoice in? Merely by your wishing, It does not become a cause of harm to them.
examples.sa: जातं चेदप्रियं शत्रोस्त्वत्तुष्ट्या किं पुनर्भवे। त्वदाशंसनमात्रेण न चाहेतुर्भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: This hook cast by the fisherman of the afflictions Is an unbearable barb; Having been caught by it, you will surely be boiled In the cauldrons of hell by the hell-guardians.
examples.gm: This hook, cast by the fisherman of the afflictions, Is an unbearable barb. Caught by it, in the cauldrons of hell, The guardians of hell will boil me.
examples.sa: एतद्धि बडिशं घोरं क्लेशबाडिशिकार्पितम्। यतो नरकपालास्त्वां क्रीत्वा पक्ष्यन्ति कुम्भिषु॥

examples.dm: The honors of praise and fame Do not become merit, nor do they become long life; They do not become strength, nor are they health, And they do not even bring physical comfort.
examples.gm: Praise, fame, and honor Will not become merit, nor will they become long life; Will not become my strength, and are not health; Nor will they make the body comfortable.
examples.sa: स्तुतिर्यशोऽथ सत्कारो न पुण्याय न चायुषे। न बलार्थं न चारोग्ये न च कायसुखाय मे॥

examples.dm: The honors of praise and fame Do not become merit, nor do they become long life; They do not become strength, nor are they health, And they do not even bring physical comfort.
examples.gm: Praise, fame, and honor Will not become merit, nor will they become long life; Will not become my strength, and are not health; Nor will they make the body comfortable.
examples.sa: स्तुतिर्यशोऽथ सत्कारो न पुण्याय न चायुषे। न बलार्थं न चारोग्ये न च कायसुखाय मे॥

examples.dm: When their sandcastles crumble, Children weep in despair; Likewise, when praise and fame decline, My own mind is just like a child's.
examples.gm: When a sandcastle collapses, Children howl in despair. Likewise, when praise and fame decline, My own mind is like a child.
examples.sa: यथा पांशुगृहे भिन्ने रोदित्यार्तरवं शिशुः। तथा स्तुतियशोहानौ स्वचित्तं प्रतिभाति मे॥

examples.dm: Praise and the like distract me; They also destroy my sense of disillusionment. They cause envy toward those with good qualities, And they destroy my excellence as well.
examples.gm: Praise and the like distract me, And also destroy my disillusionment; They cause jealousy toward those with good qualities, And destroy excellence as well.
examples.sa: स्तुत्यादयश्च मे क्षेमं संवेगं नाशयन्त्यमी। गुणवत्सु च मात्सर्यं संपत्कोपं च कुर्वते॥

examples.dm: For me, who seeks liberation, I do not need the shackles of gain and honor. How could I be angry with those Who act to release me from my bonds?
examples.gm: Since I seek liberation, I do not need the bonds of gain and honor. Those who free me from being bound— How could I be angry at them?
examples.sa: मुक्त्यर्थिनश्चायुक्तं मे लाभसत्कारबन्धनम्। ये मोचयन्ति मां बन्धाद्द्‍वेषस्तेषु कथं मम॥

examples.dm: For me, who wishes to enter into suffering, They are like a blessing from the Buddha; They have become the very door that prevents my fall, So how could I be angry with them?
examples.gm: When I wish to enter into suffering, Like the blessing of the Buddha, They become a gate that prevents me from passing. How could I be angry at them?
examples.sa: दुःखं प्रवेष्टुकामस्य ये कपाटत्वमागताः। बुद्धाधिष्ठानत इव द्वेषस्तेषु कथं मम॥

examples.dm: If, due to my own faults, I do not practice patience toward this person, I am merely creating an obstacle for myself Regarding this cause of merit that has arrived.
examples.gm: If, through my own fault, I do not practice patience here, When the cause of merit is present, I am solely the one making an obstacle to it.
examples.sa: अथाहमात्मदोषेण न करोमि क्षमामिह। मयैवात्र कृतो विघ्नः पुण्यहेतावुपस्थिते॥

examples.dm: A beggar who arrives at the proper time Is not an obstacle to generosity; And one who enables the taking of vows Cannot be called an obstacle to ordination.
examples.gm: By a beggar who arrives at the right time, No obstacle to giving is created; One who grants ordination Cannot be called an obstacle to ordination.
examples.sa: न हि कालोपपन्नेन दानविघ्नः कृतोऽर्थिना। न च प्रव्राजके प्राप्ते प्रव्रज्याविघ्न उच्यते॥

examples.dm: Since it was accomplished by both him and me, The fruit of this patience Should be offered to him first, For in this way, he is the cause of patience.
examples.gm: Since it is accomplished by this one and myself, Therefore, the fruit of patience Should first be offered to them, For they are the cause of patience.
examples.sa: मया चानेन चोपात्तं तस्मादेतत् क्षमाफलम्। एतस्मै प्रथमं देयमेतत्पूर्वा क्षमा यतः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, since patience arises In dependence upon a mind of intense malice, That very person is the cause of patience, And is as worthy of honor as the sublime Dharma.
examples.gm: Therefore, since patience arises In dependence on a very hateful mind, Because they are the very cause of patience, They are worthy of veneration just like the sublime Dharma.
examples.sa: तद्दुष्टाशयमेवातः प्रतीत्योत्पद्यते क्षमा। स एवातः क्षमाहेतुः पूज्यः सद्धर्मवन्मया॥

examples.dm: For this reason, the Sage has spoken of the "field of sentient beings" And the "field of the Victors." Many who have pleased them have, In this way, reached the perfection of excellence.
examples.gm: Therefore, the field of sentient beings And the field of the Conquerors, the Sage has proclaimed. By pleasing them, many Have thus reached the far shore of excellence.
examples.sa: सत्त्वक्षेत्रं जिनक्षेत्रमित्यतो मुनिनोदितम्। एतानाराध्य बहवः संपत्पारं यतो गताः॥

examples.dm: For this reason, the Sage has spoken of the "field of sentient beings" And the "field of the Victors." Many who have pleased them have, In this way, reached the perfection of excellence.
examples.gm: Therefore, the field of sentient beings And the field of the Conquerors, the Sage has proclaimed. By pleasing them, many Have thus reached the far shore of excellence.
examples.sa: सत्त्वक्षेत्रं जिनक्षेत्रमित्यतो मुनिनोदितम्। एतानाराध्य बहवः संपत्पारं यतो गताः॥

examples.dm: For this reason, the Sage has spoken of the "field of sentient beings" And the "field of the Victors." Many who have pleased them have, In this way, reached the perfection of excellence.
examples.gm: Therefore, the field of sentient beings And the field of the Conquerors, the Sage has proclaimed. By pleasing them, many Have thus reached the far shore of excellence.
examples.sa: सत्त्वक्षेत्रं जिनक्षेत्रमित्यतो मुनिनोदितम्। एतानाराध्य बहवः संपत्पारं यतो गताः॥

examples.dm: If even a mere fraction of the qualities belonging to that unique collection of supreme excellence Appears in someone, Then offering the entire threefold world to honor them Would still be too little.
examples.gm: Of the unique collection of supreme qualities, If merely a fraction of those qualities Appears in someone, in order to venerate them, Even offering the three realms would be too small.
examples.sa: गुणसारैकराशीनां गुणोऽणुरपि चेत्क्वचित्। दृश्यते तस्य पूजार्थं त्रैलोक्यमपि न क्षमम्॥

examples.dm: Since sentient beings possess a share in the arising of the supreme Buddha-Dharma, It is reasonable, based on this mere correspondence, To consider sentient beings as objects of worship.
examples.gm: A fraction of generating the supreme qualities of a Buddha Is possessed by sentient beings; therefore, In accordance with just this fraction, It is fitting to venerate sentient beings.
examples.sa: बुद्धधर्मोदयांशस्तु श्रेष्ठः सत्त्वेषु विद्यते। एतदंशानुरूप्येण सत्त्वपूजा कृता भवेत्॥

examples.dm: In order to please the Tathāgatas, From this day forth I shall remain a servant to the world. Even if many beings should kick me or trample upon my head, Or even kill me, I shall not retaliate; may the Protectors of the World be pleased.
examples.gm: In order to please the Tathāgatas, From today onward I shall be a servant to the world. Even if the multitudes of wandering beings strike my head with their feet, Or kill me, I will not retaliate; may the protectors of the world be pleased!
examples.sa: आराधनायाद्य तथागतानां सर्वात्मना दास्यमुपैमि लोके। कुर्वन्तु मे मूर्घ्नि पदं जनौघा विघ्नन्तु वा तुष्यतु लोकनाथः॥

examples.dm: This alone is what pleases the Tathāgatas, This is also the perfect accomplishment of one's own welfare, This alone dispels the suffering of the world; Therefore, I shall always make this my practice.
examples.gm: This alone is what pleases the Tathāgatas; This alone is also the perfect accomplishment of my own purpose; This alone is also what dispels the suffering of the world; Therefore, I should always practice this alone.
examples.sa: तथागताराधनमेतदेव स्वार्थस्य संसाधनमेतदेव। लोकस्य दुःखापहमेतदेव तस्मान्ममास्तु व्रतमेतदेव॥

examples.dm: For the guardians of hell and the compassionate ones are their allies. Therefore, just as subjects placate a fierce king, One should please all sentient beings.
examples.gm: Because the wardens of hell And the compassionate ones are their forces; Therefore, just as subjects please a fierce king, I should please sentient beings.
examples.sa: यस्मान्नरकपालाश्च कृपावन्तश्च तद्बलम्। तस्मादाराधयेत्सत्त्वान् भृत्यश्चण्डनृपं यथा॥

examples.dm: In the cycle of existence, through patience one attains beauty and the like, As well as health and renown, A very long life, And the extensive happiness of a universal monarch.
examples.gm: While in saṃsāra, through patience, beauty and the like, Health, and fame, An extremely long life, and The vast happiness of a universal monarch are attained.
examples.sa: प्रासादिकत्वमारोग्यं प्रामोद्यं चिरजीवितम्। चक्रवर्तिसुखं स्फीतं क्षमी प्राप्नोति संसरन्॥

examples.dm: This concludes the sixth chapter, entitled "The Teaching on Patience," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the sixth chapter, named "Teaching Patience."

examples.dm: This concludes the sixth chapter, entitled "The Teaching on Patience," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the sixth chapter, named "Teaching Patience."

examples.dm: What is diligence? It is delighting in the virtuous. Its opposing factors should be explained: Laziness, attachment to what is base, And the despondency of self-contempt.
examples.gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.
examples.sa: किं वीर्यं कुशलोत्साहस्तद्विपक्षः क उच्यते। आलस्यं कुत्सितासक्तिर्विषादात्मावमन्यना॥

examples.dm: What is diligence? It is delighting in the virtuous. Its opposing factors should be explained: Laziness, attachment to what is base, And the despondency of self-contempt.
examples.gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.

examples.gm: What is diligence? It is delight in virtue. Its opposing factors shall be explained: Laziness, clinging to what is bad, and Despondency, which is self-contempt.
examples.sa: किं वीर्यं कुशलोत्साहस्तद्विपक्षः क उच्यते। आलस्यं कुत्सितासक्तिर्विषादात्मावमन्यना॥

examples.dm: Through savoring the taste of idle pleasure, And the craving that relies on sleep, One does not feel weariness for the suffering of cyclic existence; From these, laziness fully arises.
examples.gm: Tasting the pleasure of idleness, and Craving that relies on sleep; From feeling no weariness toward the sufferings of saṃsāra, Laziness comes to arise.
examples.sa: अव्यापारसुखास्वादनिद्रापाश्रयतृष्णया। संसारदुःखानुद्वेगादालस्यमुपजायते॥

examples.dm: Without despondency, with an army of forces, With earnest application and self-mastery, Practice the equality of self and others, And practice the exchange of self and others.
examples.gm: Without despondency, and with the forces, Applying oneself earnestly, and mastering oneself, Equalizing self and other, And exchanging self and other, you should practice!
examples.sa: अविषादबलव्यूहतात्पर्यात्मविधेयता। परात्मसमता चैव परात्मपरिवर्तनम्॥

examples.dm: Without despondency, with an army of forces, With earnest application and self-mastery, Practice the equality of self and others, And practice the exchange of self and others.
examples.gm: Without despondency, and with the forces, Applying oneself earnestly, and mastering oneself, Equalizing self and other, And exchanging self and other, you should practice!

examples.dm: One should not be discouraged, thinking, "How could I ever attain enlightenment?" For the Tathāgata, the Speaker of Truth, Has spoken this truth.
examples.gm: Thinking, "How could I attain enlightenment?" I should not be despondent, For in this way the Tathāgata, Who speaks the truth, has spoken this truth:
examples.sa: नैवावसादः कर्तव्यः कुतो मे बोधिरित्यतः। यस्मात्तथागतः सत्यं सत्यवादीदमुक्तवान्॥

examples.dm: Even those who have become flies, gadflies, bees, Or likewise those who have become insects, If they develop the power of diligence, Will attain the supreme enlightenment so difficult to find.
examples.gm: "Flies, mosquitoes, and bees, And likewise whatever is born as a worm, Even they, if they generate the power of effort, Will attain unsurpassable enlightenment, which is hard to find."
examples.sa: तेऽप्यासन् दंशमशका मक्षिकाः कृमयस्तथा। यैरुत्साहवशात् प्राप्ता दुरापा बोधिरुत्तमा॥

examples.dm: The Supreme Physician does not employ Common medical treatments such as these; Through extremely gentle procedures, He heals immeasurable and grievous illnesses.
examples.gm: Such ordinary medical treatments Are not performed by the supreme physician; With an extremely gentle method, He cures immeasurable great diseases.
examples.sa: क्रियामिमामप्युचितां वरवैद्यो न दत्तवान्। मधुरेणोपचारेण चिकित्सति महातुरान्॥

examples.dm: Because non-virtue is abandoned, there is no suffering; Because of wisdom, there is no unhappiness. In this way, it is through distorted conceptions And non-virtue that the mind and body are harmed.
examples.gm: By abandoning misdeeds, there is no suffering; By being wise, there is no displeasure. Thus, wrong conceptualizations And misdeeds harm the mind and body.
examples.sa: न दुःखी त्यक्तपापत्वात्पण्डितत्वान्न दुर्मनाः। मिथ्याकल्पनया चित्ते पापात्काये यतो व्यथा॥

examples.dm: If the body is at ease through merit, And the mind is at ease through wisdom, Then even while remaining in samsara for the sake of others, Why would those with compassion ever be weary?
examples.gm: Through merit, the body is at ease, And through wisdom, the mind is at ease. Even while remaining in cyclic existence for the sake of others, Why would the compassionate ones become weary?
examples.sa: पुण्येन कायः सुखितः पाण्डित्येन मनः सुखि। तिष्ठन् परार्थं संसारे कृपालुः केन खिद्यते॥

examples.dm: Because this, through the power of the awakening mind, Exhausts previous misdeeds And gathers an ocean of merit, It is explained as superior to the Hearers.
examples.gm: Because through the power of this awakening mind Former misdeeds are exhausted, And because it gathers an ocean of merit, It is explained to be supreme over the Hearers.
examples.sa: क्षपयन् पूर्वपापानि प्रतीच्छन् पुण्यसागरान्। बोधिचित्तबलादेव श्रावकेभ्योऽपि शीघ्रगः॥

examples.dm: To accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, one's forces are aspiration, steadfastness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated by fearing suffering and contemplating its benefits.
examples.gm: The forces to accomplish the benefit of sentient beings Are aspiration, firmness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering And contemplating its benefits.
examples.sa: छन्दस्थामरतिमुक्तिबलं सत्त्वार्थसिद्धये। छन्दं दुःखभयात्कुर्यादनुशंसांश्च भावयन्॥

examples.gm: The forces to accomplish the benefit of sentient beings Are aspiration, firmness, joy, and relinquishment. Aspiration is generated through the fear of suffering And contemplating its benefits.

examples.dm: Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors, One should strive to increase diligence through the powers of aspiration, pride, joy, relinquishment, Earnest application, and mastery.
examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.
examples.sa: एवं विपक्षमुन्मूल्य यतेतोत्साहवृद्धये। छन्दमानरतित्यागतात्पर्यवशिताबलैः॥

examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.

examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.

examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.

examples.dm: If I do not perceive in myself even a fraction of the effort Needed to begin exhausting these faults, Then as a vessel of immeasurable suffering, Why does my heart not burst?
examples.gm: Of that initiation of exhausting faults, If I do not see even a fraction in myself, Being an abode of immeasurable suffering, Why does my heart not burst?
examples.sa: तत्र दोषक्षयारम्भे लेशोऽपि मम नेक्ष्यते। अप्रमेयव्यथाभाज्ये नोरः स्फुटति मे कथम्॥

examples.dm: I have not made offerings to the Blessed One, Nor have I provided the joy of great festivals; I have not performed service for the Teachings, Nor have I fulfilled the hopes of the poor.
examples.gm: I have not made offerings to the Blessed Ones, I have not provided the happiness of great festivals, I have not performed deeds for the teaching, I have not fulfilled the wishes of the poor.
examples.sa: न प्राप्तं भगवत्पूजामहोत्सवसुखं मया। न कृता शासने कारा दरिद्राशा न पूरिता॥

examples.dm: I have not granted fearlessness to the frightened, Nor have I given comfort to the distressed; I have merely produced the pain and suffering Of the womb of my mother.
examples.gm: Not having given fearlessness to the fearful, And not having given happiness to the afflicted, I have merely produced the pangs And suffering of my mother's womb.
examples.sa: भीतेभ्यो नाभयं दत्तमार्ता न सुखिनः कृताः। दुःखाय केवलं मातुर्गतोऽस्मि गर्भशल्यताम्॥

examples.dm: The Sage has taught that aspiration is the root of all virtuous qualities; Its own root, in turn, is constant meditation upon the results of karmic ripening.
examples.gm: Of all wholesome factors, The Sage has stated that the root is aspiration, And its root constantly is Meditating on the ripened results.
examples.sa: कुशलानां च सर्वेषां छन्दं मूलं मुनिर्जगौ। तस्यापि मूलं सततं विपाकफलभावना॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should aspire to virtue, And cultivate it with genuine respect. Having undertaken the rite of the Vajradhvaja, One should cultivate the pride of self-confidence.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should aspire to the wholesome, And meditate upon it with reverence; According to the method of the Vajradhvaja, Having begun, one should meditate on self-confidence.
examples.sa: तस्मात्कार्यः शुभच्छन्दो भावयित्वैवमादरात्। वज्रध्वजस्थविधिना मानं त्वारभ्य भावयेत्॥

examples.dm: First, examine your resources, And then decide whether to begin or not. It is best not to begin at all, But once begun, one should not turn back.
examples.gm: First, having examined one's capacity, One should either begin or not begin; Not beginning is best, But having begun, one should not turn back.
examples.sa: पूर्वं निरूप्य सामग्रीमारभेन्नारभेत वा। अनारम्भो वरं नाम न त्वारभ्य निवर्तनम्॥

examples.dm: By becoming habituated to this in other lives, Sin and suffering will increase. Furthermore, the time for the result will be inferior, And even that goal will not be achieved.
examples.gm: Becoming accustomed to that in other lives, Misdeeds and suffering will increase; Other deeds and the time of results as well Will become inferior, and that will not be accomplished either.
examples.sa: जन्मान्तरेऽपि सोऽभ्यासः पापाद्दुःखं च वर्धते। अन्यच्च कार्यकालं च हीनं तच्च न साधितम्॥

examples.dm: One should apply pride to these three: Actions, afflictions, and ability. Thinking, "I alone shall do it," This is the pride of action.
examples.gm: Actions, afflictions, and capacity: One should generate self-confidence regarding these three. Thinking, "I shall do this alone," This is the self-confidence of action.
examples.sa: त्रिषु मानो विधातव्यः कर्मोपक्लेशशक्तिषु। मयैवैकेन कर्तव्यमित्येषा कर्ममानिता॥

examples.dm: When encountering a dying snake, Even a crow acts like a Garuda. If I am weak and feeble, Even a minor downfall will cause me harm.
examples.gm: When encountering a dead snake, Even a crow acts like a garuda. If I myself am weak, Even a minor downfall will cause harm.
examples.sa: मृतं दुण्डुभमासाद्य काकोऽपि गरुडायते। आपदाबाधतेऽल्पापि मनो मे यदि दुर्बलम्॥

examples.dm: For one who is despondent and has abandoned effort, How could there be liberation from misfortune? By generating the pride of exertion, Even the great will find it difficult to overcome you.
examples.gm: For one who is despondent and casts aside effort, Is there liberation from destitution? But by generating self-confidence and effort, One is difficult to defeat even by the great.
examples.sa: विषादकृतनिश्चेष्टे आपदः सुकरा ननु। व्युत्थितश्चेष्टमानस्तु महतामपि दुर्जयः॥

examples.dm: I shall triumph over everything; None shall triumph over me. As a son of the Lion-like Conqueror, I shall abide in this pride.
examples.gm: I shall conquer all, And no one shall conquer me. I, a son of the Victorious Lion, Should abide in this self-confidence.
examples.sa: मया हि सर्वं जेतव्यमहं जेयो न केनचित्। मयैष मानो वोढव्यो जिनसिंहसुतो ह्यहम्॥

examples.dm: Inflated by the pride of the afflictions, They are led by that pride to the lower realms; Their human joy is destroyed, and They become slaves eating the food of others,
examples.gm: Those inflated by the affliction of pride Are led to the lower realms by pride, Destroying their human joys, And becoming slaves who eat others' food,
examples.sa: मानेन दुर्गतिं नीता मानुष्येऽपि हतोत्सवाः। परपिण्डाशिनो दासा मूर्खा दुर्दर्शनाः कृशा॥

examples.dm: Whoever maintains pride in order to conquer the enemy of pride Is the truly proud one, the victorious hero; For they have certainly vanquished the burgeoning enemy of pride, And as they wish, they bring the fruit of the Conquerors to perfection for all beings.
examples.gm: Whoever holds self-confidence to conquer the enemy of pride, He is the truly self-confident one and the victorious hero. Whoever definitively destroys the thriving enemy of pride, Perfects the fruit of victory according to the desires of beings.
examples.sa: ते मानिनो विजयिनश्च त एव शूरा ये मानशत्रुविजयाय वहन्ति मानम्। ये तं स्फुरन्तमपि मानरिपुं निहत्य कामं जने जयफलं प्रतिपादयन्ति॥

examples.dm: If one is never sated by sensual desires, Which are like honey on the edge of a razor, Then how could one ever be sated by merit, Which ripens into peace and happiness?
examples.gm: Like honey smeared on a razor's edge, If one is not satiated by sensual desires, Having a ripening of happiness and peace, How could one ever be satiated with merit?
examples.sa: कामैर्न तृप्तिः संसारे क्षुरधारामधूपमैः। पुण्यामृतैः कथं तृप्तिर्विपाकमधुरैः शिवैः॥

examples.dm: Just as one carrying a vessel filled with mustard oil, Followed by a man with a drawn sword threatening to kill him, Is terrified of spilling it, so should the practitioner be focused.
examples.gm: Just as one carrying a vessel filled with mustard oil, With a sword-bearer standing nearby, Fearing the threat of death if it spills, An ascetic should likewise exert himself.
examples.sa: तैलपात्रधरो यद्वदसिहस्तैरधिष्ठितः। स्खलिते मरणत्रासात्तत्परः स्यात्तथा व्रती॥

examples.dm: Therefore, just as one would swiftly spring up If a snake crawled into one's lap, So too, when sleep and lethargy approach, One should quickly repel them.
examples.gm: Therefore, if a snake comes into one's lap, Just as one would quickly jump up, Likewise, if sleep and lethargy come, One should quickly repel them.
examples.sa: तस्मादुत्सङ्गगे सर्पे यथोत्तिष्ठति सत्वरम्। निद्रालस्यागमे तद्वत् प्रतिकुर्वीत सत्वरम्॥

examples.dm: Just as a tuft of cotton is moved to and fro By the coming and going of the wind, So should I be governed by enthusiasm; In that way, success will be achieved.
examples.gm: Just as the going and Coming of the wind control the cotton fluff, Likewise, being controlled by joy, In that way, success will be achieved.
examples.sa: यथैव तूलकं वायोर्गमनागमने वशम्। तथोत्साहवशं यायादृद्धिश्चैवं समृध्यति॥

examples.dm: Having thus generated diligence, One should place the mind in meditative concentration. A person whose mind is distracted Dwells between the fangs of the mental afflictions.
examples.gm: Having thus generated joyous effort, One should place the mind in meditative concentration. A person whose mind is distracted Dwells between the fangs of the afflictions.
examples.sa: वर्धयित्वैवमुत्साहं समाधौ स्थापयेन्मनः। विक्षिप्तचित्तस्तु नरः क्लेशदंष्ट्रान्तरे स्थितः॥

examples.dm: Through solitude of body and mind, Distractions will not arise. Therefore, one should renounce the world And completely cast aside discursive thoughts.
examples.gm: Through the isolation of body and mind, Distraction does not arise. Therefore, one should abandon the worldly life And completely discard discursive thoughts.
examples.sa: कायचित्तविवेकेन विक्षेपस्य न संभवः। तस्माल्लोकं परित्यज्य वितर्कान् परिवर्जयेत्॥

examples.dm: Through special insight thoroughly conjoined with calm abiding, One should understand that the mental afflictions are completely destroyed. Therefore, one should first seek calm abiding; This is achieved by those who find genuine delight in detachment from the world.
examples.gm: By special insight completely endowed with calm abiding, Knowing that the afflictions are destroyed, One should first seek calm abiding; and that too Is accomplished by joyful detachment from the world.
examples.sa: शमथेन विपश्यनासुयुक्तः कुरुते क्लेशविनाशमित्यवेत्य। शमथः प्रथमं गवेषणीयःस च लोके निरपेक्षयाभिरत्या॥

examples.dm: Through special insight thoroughly conjoined with calm abiding, One should understand that the mental afflictions are completely destroyed. Therefore, one should first seek calm abiding; This is achieved by those who find genuine delight in detachment from the world.
examples.gm: By special insight completely endowed with calm abiding, Knowing that the afflictions are destroyed, One should first seek calm abiding; and that too Is accomplished by joyful detachment from the world.
examples.sa: शमथेन विपश्यनासुयुक्तः कुरुते क्लेशविनाशमित्यवेत्य। शमथः प्रथमं गवेषणीयःस च लोके निरपेक्षयाभिरत्या॥

examples.dm: Through special insight thoroughly conjoined with calm abiding, One should understand that the mental afflictions are completely destroyed. Therefore, one should first seek calm abiding; This is achieved by those who find genuine delight in detachment from the world.
examples.gm: By special insight completely endowed with calm abiding, Knowing that the afflictions are destroyed, One should first seek calm abiding; and that too Is accomplished by joyful detachment from the world.
examples.sa: शमथेन विपश्यनासुयुक्तः कुरुते क्लेशविनाशमित्यवेत्य। शमथः प्रथमं गवेषणीयःस च लोके निरपेक्षयाभिरत्या॥

examples.dm: If they are not seen, there is no joy, And the mind will not remain in meditative equipoise; Even if they are seen, there is no satisfaction, And one is tormented by craving just as before.
examples.gm: Not seeing them, one will not be joyful, And the mind will not rest in equipoise. Even seeing them, one will not be satisfied, And will be tormented by craving as before.
examples.sa: अपश्यन्नरतिं याति समाधौ न च तिष्ठति। न च तृप्यति दृष्ट्वापि पूर्ववद्बाध्यते तृषा॥

examples.dm: If one is attached to sentient beings, The perfect reality is completely obscured. It destroys even a mind of disillusionment, And in the end, one will be tormented by grief.
examples.gm: If one forms attachments to sentient beings, Ultimate reality is completely obscured, The mind of disillusionment is also destroyed, And in the end, one will be tormented by sorrow.
examples.sa: न पश्यति यथाभूतं संवेगादवहीयते। दह्यते तेन शोकेन प्रियसंगमकाङ्क्षया॥

examples.dm: By thinking only of them, This life will pass away in vain. Through impermanent friendships, Even the eternal Dharma is destroyed.
examples.gm: By merely thinking about them, This life will pass away meaninglessly. Because of impermanent friends and relatives, Even the eternal Dharma will be destroyed.
examples.sa: तच्चिन्तया मुधा याति ह्रस्वमायुर्मुहुर्मुहुः। अशाश्वतेन धर्मेण धर्मो भ्रश्यति शाश्वतः॥

examples.dm: By thinking only of them, This life will pass away in vain. Through impermanent friendships, Even the eternal Dharma is destroyed.
examples.gm: By merely thinking about them, This life will pass away meaninglessly. Because of impermanent friends and relatives, Even the eternal Dharma will be destroyed.
examples.sa: तच्चिन्तया मुधा याति ह्रस्वमायुर्मुहुर्मुहुः। अशाश्वतेन धर्मेण धर्मो भ्रश्यति शाश्वतः॥

examples.dm: In a single instant they become friends, And in a mere moment they turn into enemies. Because they react with anger toward things that should bring joy, Ordinary beings are difficult to please.
examples.gm: In a single instant they become friends, And in a brief moment they even become enemies. Since they become angry at causes for joy, Ordinary people are difficult to please.
examples.sa: क्षणाद्भवन्ति सुहृदो भवन्ति रिपवः क्षणात्। तोषस्थाने प्रकुप्यन्ति दुराराधाः पृथग्जनाः॥

examples.dm: If I harbor such pride, thinking, "I have many gains and honors, And many people are fond of me," Then fear will arise after death.
examples.gm: "I have much gain and respect," "Many are fond of me"— If one harbors such conceit, Fear will arise after death.
examples.sa: लाभी च सत्कृतश्चाहमिच्छन्ति बहवश्च माम्। इति मर्त्यस्य संप्राप्तान्मरणाज्जायते भयम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, the wise should not form attachments, For from attachment, fear is born. Since these things are by nature subject to loss, Remain steadfast and understand this well.
examples.gm: Therefore, the wise should not be attached; From attachment, fear arises. Since these will naturally be left behind, Remain steadfast and fully understand this.
examples.sa: तस्मात्प्राज्ञो न तामिच्छेदिच्छातो जायते भयम्। स्वयमेव च यात्येतद्धैर्यं कृत्वा प्रतीक्षताम्॥

examples.dm: Though one may acquire many gains, And though fame and renown may arise, Even with a collection of gain and fame, There is no knowing where one will go.
examples.gm: Even if many gains are acquired, And fame and a good reputation arise, Together with the collection of gains and fame, There is no knowing where one will go.
examples.sa: बहवो लाभिनोऽभूवन् बहवश्च यशस्विनः। सह लाभयशोभिस्ते न ज्ञाताः क्व गता इति॥

examples.dm: If there are others who disparage me, What reason is there for me to be pleased by praise? If there are others who praise me, What reason is there for me to be displeased by disparagement?
examples.gm: If there are others who disparage me, What joy is there for me in praise? If there are others who praise me, What displeasure is there in disparagement?
examples.sa: मामेवान्ये जुगुप्सन्ति किं प्रहृष्याम्यहं स्तुतः। मामेवान्ये प्रशंसन्ति किं विषीदामि निन्दितः॥
