examples.dm: If there are others who disparage me, What reason is there for me to be pleased by praise? If there are others who praise me, What reason is there for me to be displeased by disparagement?
examples.gm: If there are others who disparage me, What joy is there for me in praise? If there are others who praise me, What displeasure is there in disparagement?
examples.sa: मामेवान्ये जुगुप्सन्ति किं प्रहृष्याम्यहं स्तुतः। मामेवान्ये प्रशंसन्ति किं विषीदामि निन्दितः॥

examples.dm: Possessing only a few items such as an alms bowl, And wearing clothes that no one else desires, When shall I come to dwell without fear, Even without attempting to conceal this body?
examples.gm: With merely a begging bowl and the like, Wearing garments unwanted by anyone, And not even concealing this body, When will I dwell fearlessly?
examples.sa: मृत्पात्रमात्रविभवश्चौरासंभोगचीवरः। निर्भयो विहरिष्यामि कदा कायमगोपयन्॥

examples.dm: Just as travelers on a road Take up a temporary lodging, So too do those on the path of existence Take up a place of birth.
examples.gm: Just as those who enter upon a journey Take up a place to stay, In the same way, those entered on the path of existence Fully take up a place of birth.
examples.sa: अध्वानं प्रतिपन्नस्य यथावासपरिग्रहः। तथा भवाध्वगस्यापि जन्मावासपरिग्रहः॥

examples.dm: Since there is no one nearby To cause the harm of mourning, No one at all will distract me From such practices as the recollection of the Buddha.
examples.gm: Since there is no one staying nearby To cause grief or harm, By this, the recollection of the Buddha and so forth Will not be distracted by anyone.
examples.sa: न चान्तिकचराः केचिच्छोचन्तः कुर्वते व्यथाम्। बुद्धाद्यनुस्मृतिं चास्य विक्षिपन्ति न केचन॥

examples.dm: If they are nothing but skeletons and nothing else, And are neither independent nor a self, Why, after desiring them intensely and becoming thoroughly attached, Do you not go to the state beyond sorrow?
examples.gm: Are nothing but skeletons, nothing else. Being neither independent nor a self, Strongly desiring and fully clinging to them, Why do you not proceed to nirvāṇa?
examples.sa: तान्येवास्थीनि नान्यानि स्वाधीनान्यममानि च। प्रकामं संपरिष्वज्य किं न गच्छसि निर्वृतिम्॥

examples.dm: That face of your affliction, Is now revealed just as it is; Now that you see it being uncovered by the vultures, Why do you flee from it?
examples.gm: That face which tormented you, Just as it has now become manifest, Having seen it unveiled by vultures, Why do you flee from it now?
examples.sa: तन्मुखं त्वत्परिक्लेशमसहद्भिरिवाधुना। गृध्रैर्व्यक्तीकृतं पश्य किमिदानीं पलायसे॥

examples.dm: Even when others merely looked with their eyes, You kept it thoroughly guarded; While it is being devoured by them, Why, O miser, do you not protect it?
examples.gm: Even when others looked at it with their eyes, It was completely guarded; Now that it is being eaten by them, Miser, why do you not guard it?
examples.sa: परचक्षुर्निपातेभ्योऽप्यासीद्यत्परिरक्षितम्। तदद्य भक्षितं यावत् किमीर्ष्यालो न रक्षसि॥

examples.dm: Seeing this heap of flesh being eaten by vultures and others, Why do you honor the food of others with flower garlands, Sandalwood, and ornaments?
examples.gm: Seeing this heap of flesh, When vultures and others eat it, Why do you offer to the food of others Garlands of flowers, sandalwood, and ornaments?
examples.sa: मांसोच्छ्रयमिमं दृष्ट्वा गृध्रैरन्यैश्च भक्षितम्। आहारः पूज्यतेऽन्येषां स्रक्‍चन्दनविभूषणैः॥

examples.dm: Seeing it as nothing but a heap of bones, If you are terrified even when it is motionless, Why are you not afraid when it is moved by someone, Like a reanimated corpse?
examples.gm: Having seen it as merely a heap of bones, If you are terrified even when it does not move, When it was moved by something, like a zombie, Why were you not afraid?
examples.sa: निश्चलादपि ते त्रासः कङ्कालादेवमीक्षितात्। वेतालेनेव केनापि चाल्यमानाद्भयं न किम्॥

examples.dm: Since both excrement and saliva arise from the very same food, Why do you dislike the excrement, And yet, why do you delight in the saliva?
examples.gm: From a single food alone, If feces and saliva are produced, Out of these, you dislike the feces, So why do you delight in the saliva?
examples.sa: एकस्मादशनादेषां लालामेध्यं च जायते । तत्रामेध्यमनिष्टं ते लालापानं कथं प्रियम् ॥

examples.dm: Since both excrement and saliva arise from the very same food, Why do you dislike the excrement, And yet, why do you delight in the saliva?
examples.gm: From a single food alone, If feces and saliva are produced, Out of these, you dislike the feces, So why do you delight in the saliva?
examples.sa: एकस्मादशनादेषां लालामेध्यं च जायते । तत्रामेध्यमनिष्टं ते लालापानं कथं प्रियम् ॥

examples.dm: If you have no attachment to what is impure, Why do you embrace in your lap another, A cage of bones bound together by sinews, And plastered over with the mud of flesh?
examples.gm: If you have no attachment to filth, To a cage of bones tied together with sinews And plastered with the mud of flesh, Why do you embrace another in your lap?
examples.sa: यदि ते नाशुचौ रागः कस्मादालिङ्गसेऽपरम्। मांसकर्दमसंलिप्तं स्नायुबद्धास्थिपञ्जरम्॥

examples.dm: If you say, "I am fond of this flesh," And desire to touch and look at it, Then why do you not desire flesh In its natural, insentient state?
examples.gm: Saying, "I delight in this flesh," If you desire to touch and look at it, Which is of a mindless nature, How can you desire the flesh?
examples.sa: मांसप्रियोऽहमस्येति द्रष्टुं स्प्रष्टुं च वाञ्छसि। अचेतनं स्वभावेन मांसं त्वं कथमिच्छसि॥

examples.dm: Having abandoned the young lotus Opened by the rays of a cloudless sun, Why does your mind, with its attachment to the impure, Take delight in a cage of filth?
examples.gm: Opened by the rays of a cloudless sun, Abandoning a fresh lotus, With a mind attached to filth, Why do you delight in a cage of filth?
examples.sa: विघनार्कांशुविकचं मुक्त्वा तरुणपङ्कजम्। अमेध्यशौण्डचित्तस्य का रतिर्गूथपञ्जरे॥

examples.dm: If you have no attachment to what is impure, Then why do you embrace in your lap another Who was produced by that seed And arose from an impure field?
examples.gm: If you have no attachment to filth, Arisen from a field of filth, And generated by its seed, Why do you embrace another in your lap?
examples.sa: यदि ते नाशुचौ रागः कस्मादालिङ्गसे परम्। अमेध्यक्षेत्रसंभूतं तद्बीजं तेन वर्धितम्॥

examples.dm: You do not desire even a tiny worm That arises from filth, Yet you desire a body that is a mass of many impurities And was likewise born from filth.
examples.gm: A filth-worm arisen from filth, Even a tiny one, you do not desire, Yet a body whose nature is much filth, And born of filth, you desire.
examples.sa: अमेध्यभवमल्पत्वान्न वाञ्छस्यशुचिं कृमिम्। बह्वमेध्यमयं कायममेध्यजमपीच्छसि॥

examples.dm: Even pleasant things like camphor, Or boiled rice and vegetables, Once taken into the mouth and spat out, Make even the ground foul and unclean.
examples.gm: Even pleasing things like camphor, Or cooked rice and vegetables, If put into the mouth and spat out, Make even the ground foul and filthy.
examples.sa: कर्पूरादिषु हृद्येषु शाल्यन्नव्यञ्जनेषु वा। मुखक्षिप्तविसृष्टेषु भूमिरप्यशुचिर्मता॥

examples.dm: Through the torments of accumulating, guarding, and losing, One should understand that wealth is an endless source of ruin. Those who are distracted by their attachment to wealth Have no opportunity to be liberated from the suffering of cyclic existence.
examples.gm: Through the torments of amassing, protecting, and losing it, Wealth should be known as endless ruin. Those who are distracted by attachment to wealth Have no opportunity for liberation from the miseries of existence.
examples.sa: अर्जनरक्षणनाशविषादै-रर्थमनर्थमनन्तमवेहि। व्यग्रतया धनसक्तमतीनां नावसरो भवदुःखविमुक्तेः॥

examples.dm: Through the torments of accumulating, guarding, and losing, One should understand that wealth is an endless source of ruin. Those who are distracted by their attachment to wealth Have no opportunity to be liberated from the suffering of cyclic existence.
examples.gm: Through the torments of amassing, protecting, and losing it, Wealth should be known as endless ruin. Those who are distracted by attachment to wealth Have no opportunity for liberation from the miseries of existence.
examples.sa: अर्जनरक्षणनाशविषादै-रर्थमनर्थमनन्तमवेहि। व्यग्रतया धनसक्तमतीनां नावसरो भवदुःखविमुक्तेः॥

examples.dm: For those possessed by desire, such faults are many and the benefits are few; It is like a beast of burden pulling a cart, That eats only a few mouthfuls of grass.
examples.gm: For those with desires, these and so forth Are the many disadvantages and little benefit, Just like beasts of burden drawing a chariot Eating a few mouthfuls of grass.
examples.sa: एवमादीनवो भूयानल्पास्वादस्तु कामिनाम्। शकटं वहतो यद्वत्पशोर्घासलवग्रहः॥

examples.dm: Thus, having become weary of desires, One should generate a delight in solitude, Within peaceful forests That are empty of strife and afflictions.
examples.gm: Having thus generated revulsion for desires, Generate joy for solitude. Empty of disputes and afflictions, In the peaceful forests,
examples.sa: एवमुद्विज्य कामेभ्यो विवेके जनयेद्रतिम्। कलहायासशून्यासु शान्तासु वनभूमिषु॥

examples.dm: Acting with independence and without attachment, Having no connection with anyone at all, That joy of contentment, whatever it may be, Is difficult even for Indra to find.
examples.gm: Acting independently and without attachment, Unconnected to anyone at all, Whatever is the joyful conduct of contentment, Even Indra has difficulty finding it.
examples.sa: स्वच्छन्दचार्यनिलयः प्रतिबद्धो न कस्यचित्। यत्संतोषसुखं भुङ्क्ते तदिन्द्रस्यापि दुर्लभम्॥

examples.dm: Acting with independence and without attachment, Having no connection with anyone at all, That joy of contentment, whatever it may be, Is difficult even for Indra to find.
examples.gm: Acting independently and without attachment, Unconnected to anyone at all, Whatever is the joyful conduct of contentment, Even Indra has difficulty finding it.
examples.sa: स्वच्छन्दचार्यनिलयः प्रतिबद्धो न कस्यचित्। यत्संतोषसुखं भुङ्क्ते तदिन्द्रस्यापि दुर्लभम्॥

examples.dm: The conceptual thought that "I" will experience that Is a mistaken conception, For the one who dies is one, And the one who is born is another.
examples.gm: The thought that "I will experience it" Is a false conception; Thus, the one who dies is another, And the one who is born is another.
examples.sa: अहमेव तदापीति मिथ्येयं परिकल्पना। अन्य एव मृतो यस्मादन्य एव प्रजायते॥

examples.dm: Therefore, although Supuṣpacandra Knew of the harm the king would inflict, He did not avert his own suffering, So that the suffering of many might be exhausted.
examples.gm: Therefore, Supuṣpacandra, Even while knowing the king's harm, Did not dispel his own suffering, So that the suffering of many would be exhausted.
examples.sa: अतः सुपुष्पचन्द्रेण जानतापि नृपापदम्। आत्मदुःखं न निहतं बहूनां दुःखिनां व्ययात्॥

examples.dm: Through the power of habituation, One comes to perceive the drops Of another's semen and blood as "I," Even though they are not inherently one's own.
examples.gm: Through habituation, regarding others' Drops of semen and blood, Even though they lack any entity, Just as one apprehends them as "I,"
examples.sa: अभ्यासादन्यदीयेषु शुक्रशोणितबिन्दुषु। भवत्यहमिति ज्ञानमसत्यपि हि वस्तुनि॥

examples.dm: Having recognized oneself as being full of faults And others as an ocean of virtues, One should practice completely discarding self-grasping And adopting others.
examples.gm: Knowing oneself to be flawed, and others To be an ocean of qualities, Completely discarding grasping at self And taking up others should be meditated upon.
examples.sa: ज्ञात्वा सदोषमात्मानं परानपि गुणोदधीन्। आत्मभावपरित्यागं परादानं च भावयेत्॥

examples.dm: Just as the thought of "I" has arisen Toward this selfless body through habituation, Why should the thought of "I" not likewise Arise toward other sentient beings through habituation?
examples.gm: Just as towards this selfless body The mind of "I" has arisen through habituation, Likewise, towards other sentient beings as well, Why would the mind of "I" not arise through habituation?
examples.sa: यथात्मबुद्धिरभ्यासात्स्वकायेऽस्मिन्निरात्मके। परेष्वपि तथात्मत्वं किमभ्यासान्न जायते॥

examples.dm: Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, In order to dispel the fears of beings in cyclic existence, Blessed even his own name.
examples.gm: Therefore, the protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, for transmigratory beings, In order to dispel the fears of the assembly, Blessed even his own name.
examples.sa: अध्यतिष्ठदतो नाथः स्वनामाप्यवलोकितः। पर्षच्छारद्यभयमप्यपनेतुं जनस्य हि॥

examples.dm: Whoever wishes to quickly provide protection For both themselves and others, Should practice the supreme secret: The exchanging of oneself and others.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding oneself and others, Wishes to quickly protect them, The exchange of self and others, Which is the supreme secret, should be practiced.
examples.sa: आत्मानं चापरांश्चैव यः शीघ्रं त्रातुमिच्छति। स चरेत्परमं गुह्यं परात्मपरिवर्तनम्॥

examples.dm: Whoever wishes to quickly provide protection For both themselves and others, Should practice the supreme secret: The exchanging of oneself and others.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding oneself and others, Wishes to quickly protect them, The exchange of self and others, Which is the supreme secret, should be practiced.
examples.sa: आत्मानं चापरांश्चैव यः शीघ्रं त्रातुमिच्छति। स चरेत्परमं गुह्यं परात्मपरिवर्तनम्॥

examples.dm: Thinking, "If I give this away, what will I have to enjoy?" Is the way of a demon, thinking only of one's own benefit. Thinking, "If I use this myself, what will I have to give?" Is the Dharma of the gods, thinking of the welfare of others.
examples.gm: "If I give, what will I consume?"— Thinking of one's own purpose is the way of a demon. "If I consume, what will I give?"— Thinking of others' purpose is the quality of a deity.
examples.sa: यदि दास्यामि किं भोक्ष्ये इत्यात्मार्थे पिशाचता। यदि भोक्ष्ये किं ददामीति परार्थे देवराजता॥

examples.dm: Thinking, "If I give this away, what will I have to enjoy?" Is the way of a demon, thinking only of one's own benefit. Thinking, "If I use this myself, what will I have to give?" Is the Dharma of the gods, thinking of the welfare of others.
examples.gm: "If I give, what will I consume?"— Thinking of one's own purpose is the way of a demon. "If I consume, what will I give?"— Thinking of others' purpose is the quality of a deity.
examples.sa: यदि दास्यामि किं भोक्ष्ये इत्यात्मार्थे पिशाचता। यदि भोक्ष्ये किं ददामीति परार्थे देवराजता॥

examples.dm: If one employs others for one's own benefit, One will experience servitude and the like. If one employs oneself for the benefit of others, One will experience lordship and the like.
examples.gm: If one employs others for one's own purpose, One will experience servitude and so forth. If one uses oneself for the purpose of others, One will experience lordship and so forth.
examples.sa: आत्मार्थं परमाज्ञप्य दासत्वाद्यनुभूयते। परार्थं त्वेनमाज्ञप्य स्वामित्वाद्यनुभूयते॥

examples.dm: If one does not truly exchange One's own happiness for the suffering of others, Buddhahood will not be attained, And there will be no happiness even in cyclic existence.
examples.gm: One's own happiness and the sufferings of others, If one does not perfectly exchange them, One will not achieve Buddhahood, and Even in cyclic existence there will be no happiness.
examples.sa: न नाम साध्यं बुद्धत्वं संसारेऽपि कुतः सुखम्। स्वसुखस्यान्यदुःखेन परिवर्तमकुर्वतः॥

examples.dm: Setting aside the next life, Even the goals of this life will not be achieved, Just as a servant will not do his work And a master will not pay his wages.
examples.gm: Let alone the next world, With servants not doing their work and Masters not paying wages, Even the purpose of this life will not be accomplished.
examples.sa: आस्तां तावत्परो लोके दृष्टोऽप्यर्थो न सिध्यति। भृत्यस्याकुर्वतः कर्म स्वामिनोऽददतो भृतिम्॥

examples.dm: Whatever harm exists in the world, And however many fears and sufferings there may be, If they all arise from grasping at a self, Then what use is that great demon to me?
examples.gm: Whatever harm there is in the world, and However much fear and suffering there is, If all of that arises from grasping at a self, What use is that great demon to me?
examples.sa: उपद्रवा ये च भवन्ति लोके यावन्ति दुःखानि भयानि चैव। सर्वाणि तान्यात्मपरिग्रहेण तत्किं ममानेन परिग्रहेण॥

examples.dm: If I do not completely let go of the self, I will be unable to abandon suffering, Just as one who does not let go of fire Is unable to avoid being burned.
examples.gm: If one does not completely let go of oneself, One cannot abandon suffering, Just as if one does not let go of fire, One cannot avoid being burned.
examples.sa: आत्मानमपरित्यज्य दुःखं त्यक्तुं न शक्यते। यथाग्निमपरित्यज्य दाहं त्यक्तुं न शक्यते॥

examples.dm: Having identified oneself with those who are inferior and so forth, And having identified others as oneself, With a mind free of conceptual doubt, Meditate on envy, rivalry, and pride.
examples.gm: Having made the lower and so forth into oneself, and Having made oneself into the other, With a mind free of conceptualization, I should meditate on jealousy, rivalry, and pride.
examples.sa: हीनादिष्वात्मतां कृत्वा परत्वमपि चात्मनि। भावयेर्ष्यां च मानं च निर्विकल्पेन चेतसा॥

examples.dm: The decline of my ethical discipline, views, and so forth, Is due to the power of the afflictions and is not under my control. I must be healed as much as possible, And I shall even accept the hardship involved.
examples.gm: The decline of discipline, view, and so forth Is due to the power of afflictions; it is not under my control. I should be healed as much as possible, and I will willingly accept even harm.
examples.sa: शीलदृष्टिविपत्त्यादिक्लेशशक्त्या न मद्वशात्। चिकित्स्योऽहं यथाशक्ति पीडाप्यङ्गीकृता मया॥

examples.dm: It is said that this miserable one is even competing with me. But is he my equal in learning, wisdom, Physical appearance, lineage, or wealth?
examples.gm: This miserable one is even renowned To be contending together with me. Are his learning and wisdom, or Form, caste, and wealth equal to mine?
examples.sa: अस्यापि हि वराकस्य स्पर्धा किल मया सह। किमस्य श्रुतमेतावत् प्रज्ञा रूपं कुलं धनम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, just as you have grasped as "I" these drops of others' semen and blood, You should likewise habituate yourself to regarding others in the same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, just as Upon the drops of semen and blood of others, You have grasped as "I", Likewise make it a habit with others too.
examples.sa: तस्माद्यथान्यदीयेषु शुक्रशोणितबिन्दुषु। चकर्थ त्वमहंकारं तथान्येष्वपि भावय॥

examples.dm: When one desires the impossible, afflictions and a shattered peace of mind will arise; However, for one who is independent of all such things, their excellence is inexhaustible.
examples.gm: Desiring the impossible brings afflictions, And disappointed hopes will also arise. But for one who does not depend on anything, Their excellence knows no exhaustion.
examples.sa: अशक्यमिच्छतः क्लेश आशाभङ्गश्च जायते। निराशो यस्तु सर्वत्र तस्य संपदजीर्णिका॥

examples.dm: Ultimately ending in ashes, it is inert and moved by others; Why do I grasp this unbearable, impure form as a self?
examples.gm: Ultimately ending in ashes, Motionless, to be moved by others, An unbearable, impure form— Why do I grasp at this as 'I'?
examples.sa: भस्मनिष्ठावसानेयं निश्चेष्टान्येन चाल्यते। अशुचिप्रतिमा घोरा कस्मादत्र ममाग्रहः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, enough of childish behavior! Following in the footsteps of the wise, And recalling the instructions on conscientiousness, I shall dispel sleep and mental dullness.
examples.gm: Therefore, enough with childish behavior! I shall follow in the footsteps of the wise, And, remembering the teachings on conscientiousness, I shall turn away from sleep and lethargy.
examples.sa: तेनालं लोकचरितैः पण्डिताननुयाम्यहम्। अप्रमादकथां स्मृत्वा स्त्यानमिद्धं निवारयन्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, I shall withdraw my mind from mistaken paths, And always rest it in meditative equipoise Upon the perfect object of focus.
examples.gm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, Having withdrawn the mind from wrong paths, Constantly upon the perfect object, I shall rest in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: स्मादावरणं हन्तुं समाधानं करोम्यहम्। विमार्गाच्चित्तमाकृष्य स्वालम्बननिरन्तरम्॥

examples.dm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, I shall withdraw my mind from mistaken paths, And always rest it in meditative equipoise Upon the perfect object of focus.
examples.gm: Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations, Having withdrawn the mind from wrong paths, Constantly upon the perfect object, I shall rest in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: स्मादावरणं हन्तुं समाधानं करोम्यहम्। विमार्गाच्चित्तमाकृष्य स्वालम्बननिरन्तरम्॥

examples.dm: This concludes the eighth chapter, titled "The Explanation of Meditative Concentration," from the *Entering the Conduct of a Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the eighth chapter, called The Teaching on Meditative Concentration.

examples.dm: All of these various branches Were taught by the Sage for the sake of wisdom. Therefore, those who wish to pacify suffering Should generate wisdom.
examples.gm: All these branches The Sage taught for the sake of wisdom. Therefore, those who wish to pacify Suffering should generate wisdom.
examples.sa: इमं परिकरं सर्वं प्रज्ञार्थं हि मुनिर्जगौ। तस्मादुत्पादयेत्प्रज्ञां दुःखनिवृत्तिकाङ्क्षया॥

examples.dm: The conventional and the ultimate: These are held to be the two truths. The ultimate is not an object of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the conventional.
examples.gm: The relative and the ultimate— These are asserted to be the two truths. The ultimate is not the domain of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the relative.
examples.sa: संवृतिः परमार्थश्च सत्यद्वयमिदं मतम्। बुद्धेरगोचरस्तत्त्वं बुद्धिः संवृतिरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: The worldly perceive things and conceptualize them As being truly real, rather than like an illusion; It is on this point that The yogis and the worldly dispute.
examples.gm: People of the world see entities, And conceptualize them as truly real, Not as being like illusions; therefore, here, Yogis and the world dispute.
examples.sa: लोकेन भावा दृश्यन्ते कल्प्यन्ते चापि तत्त्वतः। न तु मायावदित्यत्र विवादो योगिलोकयोः॥

examples.dm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Exists by worldly renown, not by valid cognition. This is as false as the common renown Of purity in things that are actually impure.
examples.gm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Is through convention, not through valid cognition. That is false, just like the convention Of being clean and so forth regarding what is unclean and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रत्यक्षमपि रूपादि प्रसिद्ध्या न प्रमाणतः। अशुच्यादिषु शुच्यादिप्रसिद्धिरिव सा मृषा॥

examples.dm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Exists by worldly renown, not by valid cognition. This is as false as the common renown Of purity in things that are actually impure.
examples.gm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Is through convention, not through valid cognition. That is false, just like the convention Of being clean and so forth regarding what is unclean and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रत्यक्षमपि रूपादि प्रसिद्ध्या न प्रमाणतः। अशुच्यादिषु शुच्यादिप्रसिद्धिरिव सा मृषा॥

examples.dm: For the sake of engaging the world, The Protector taught these things as if they were real; If you object that they are not even momentary, And that this is contradictory even in conventional truth,
examples.gm: "For the sake of guiding the world, The Protector taught entities. In reality, They are not momentary." If one says, "This contradicts even the relative,"
examples.sa: लोकावतारणार्थं च भावा नाथेन देशिताः। तत्त्वतः क्षणिका नैते संवृत्या चेद्विरुध्यते॥

examples.dm: There is no fault in the conventional truth of the yogis, For they see reality in relation to the world; Otherwise, the world's perception would invalidate The realization that a woman's body is impure.
examples.gm: There is no fault in the yogi's relative; In relation to the world, they see reality. Otherwise, the apprehension of women as unclean Would be invalidated by the world.
examples.sa: न दोषो योगिसंवृत्या लोकात्ते तत्त्वदर्शिनः। अन्यथा लोकबाधा स्यादशुचिस्त्रीनिरूपणे॥

examples.dm: How can merit from an illusory Conqueror Be the same as if he were truly existent? If sentient beings are like illusions, Then how are they reborn after death?
examples.gm: Merit from a Victorious One who is like an illusion Is just as it is for one who truly exists. "If sentient beings are like illusions, How are they born after dying?"
examples.sa: मायोपमाज्जिनात्पुण्यं सद्भावेऽपि कथं यथा। यदि मायोपमः सत्त्वः किं पुनर्जायते मृतः॥

examples.dm: As long as the conditions are assembled, For that long even an illusion will arise. How can a sentient being be truly existent Merely because their continuity lasts a long time?
examples.gm: As long as conditions are assembled, For that long, even illusions will occur. How, merely through a long continuum, Does a sentient being truly exist?
examples.sa: यावत्प्रत्ययसामग्री तावन्मायापि वर्तते। दीर्घसंतानमात्रेण कथं सत्त्वोऽस्ति सत्यतः॥

examples.dm: In killing an illusory person and the like, There is no sin because they lack a mind; But in the case of one who possesses an illusory mind, Merit and sin do arise.
examples.gm: In killing an illusory person and so forth, Because there is no mind, there is no sin; But regarding that which possesses an illusory mind, Merit and sin arise.
examples.sa: मायापुरुषघातादौ चित्ताभावान्न पापकम्। चित्तमायासमेते तु पापपुण्यसमुद्भवः॥

examples.dm: But since the continuity of conditions is severed, It does not arise even conventionally. When even the confusion itself does not exist, By what means can an illusion be perceived?
examples.gm: But because the continuum of conditions is severed, It does not arise even relatively. "When even the deceptive mind does not exist, By what is the illusion perceived?"
examples.sa: प्रत्ययानां तु विच्छेदात्संवृत्यापि न संभवः। यदा न भ्रान्तिरप्यस्ति माया केनोपलभ्यते॥

examples.dm: When, for you, the illusion itself Does not exist, then what is perceived? If it were something else in reality, That aspect would be the mind itself.
examples.gm: When, for you, even the illusion itself Does not exist, then what is perceived? "If it exists as another in reality, That aspect is the mind itself."
examples.sa: यदा मायैव ते नास्ति तदा किमुपलभ्यते। चित्तस्यैव स आकारो यद्यप्यन्योऽस्ति तत्त्वतः॥

examples.dm: Since it is never seen by anyone at all, Whether it is clear or not clear, Is like the graceful posturing of a barren woman's daughter; It is meaningless even to speak of it.
examples.gm: If it is not seen by anyone at all, Whether it is luminous or not luminous, Like the alluring pose of a barren woman's daughter, Expressing it is meaningless.
examples.sa: प्रकाशा वाप्रकाशा वा यदा दृष्टा न केनचित्। वन्ध्यादुहितृलीलेव कथ्यमानापि सा मुधा॥

examples.dm: If self-awareness does not exist, How can consciousness be remembered? Memory arises through a connection to the experience of something else, Just like the venom of a rat.
examples.gm: "If self-awareness does not exist, How is consciousness remembered?" It is remembered from its connection to experiencing another, Like the poison of a rat.
examples.sa: यदि नास्ति स्वसंवित्तिर्विज्ञानं स्मर्यते कथम्। अन्यानुभूते संबन्धात् स्मृतिराखुविषं यथा॥

examples.dm: If it were self-luminous because it is seen When endowed with other conditions, Then, just as a vase is seen through the application of a perfected eye-salve, The eye-salve itself would not be the vase that is seen.
examples.gm: "Endowed with other conditions, Because it sees, it illuminates itself." Through the application of accomplished eye-ointment, A vase is seen, but not the eye-ointment itself.
examples.sa: प्रत्ययान्तरयुक्तस्य दर्शनात्स्वं प्रकाशते। सिद्धाञ्जनविधेर्दृष्टो घटो नैवाञ्जनं भवेत्॥

examples.dm: Whatever is seen, heard, or known, Is not what is to be negated here; What is to be overturned here is the conceptualization of them as true, Which is the cause of suffering.
examples.gm: How things are seen, heard, and known Is not to be refuted here; Here, what becomes the cause of suffering, The conceptualization of true existence, is to be reversed.
examples.sa: यथा दृष्टं श्रुतं ज्ञातं नैवेह प्रतिषिध्यते। सत्यतः कल्पना त्वत्र दुःखहेतुर्निवार्यते॥

examples.dm: Whatever is seen, heard, or known, Is not what is to be negated here; What is to be overturned here is the conceptualization of them as true, Which is the cause of suffering.
examples.gm: How things are seen, heard, and known Is not to be refuted here; Here, what becomes the cause of suffering, The conceptualization of true existence, is to be reversed.
examples.sa: यथा दृष्टं श्रुतं ज्ञातं नैवेह प्रतिषिध्यते। सत्यतः कल्पना त्वत्र दुःखहेतुर्निवार्यते॥

examples.dm: When the mind is free from a perceived object, At that time, all are Tathāgatas. That being the case, what excellence is there In the conceptual construction of "Mind Only"?
examples.gm: When the mind is free of an apprehended object, At that time, all are Tathāgatas. Even in that case, in Mind Only, What merit is there in conceptualizing it?
examples.sa: ग्राह्यमुक्तं यदा चित्तं तदा सर्वे तथागताः। एवं च को गुणो लब्धश्चित्तमात्रेऽपि कल्पिते॥

examples.dm: When the mind is free from a perceived object, At that time, all are Tathāgatas. That being the case, what excellence is there In the conceptual construction of "Mind Only"?
examples.gm: When the mind is free of an apprehended object, At that time, all are Tathāgatas. Even in that case, in Mind Only, What merit is there in conceptualizing it?
examples.sa: ग्राह्यमुक्तं यदा चित्तं तदा सर्वे तथागताः। एवं च को गुणो लब्धश्चित्तमात्रेऽपि कल्पिते॥

examples.dm: Even if one knows things are like an illusion, How will the afflictions be averted? For even the creator of an illusory woman May feel desire for her.
examples.gm: Even if one knows things to be like an illusion, How are the afflictions repelled? Since, toward an illusory woman, Even her creator generates attachment.
examples.sa: मायोपमत्वेऽपि ज्ञाते कथं क्लेशो निवर्तते। यदा मायास्त्रियां रागस्तत्कर्तुरपि जायते॥

examples.dm: By habituating the latency for emptiness, The latency for substantial things will be abandoned; And by habituating the thought that "nothing exists," Even that will later be abandoned.
examples.gm: By familiarizing with the latent tendencies of emptiness, The latent tendencies of entities will be abandoned; By familiarizing with "there is nothing at all," That too will later be abandoned.
examples.sa: शून्यतावासनाधानाद्धीयते भाववासना। किंचिन्नास्तीति चाभ्यासात्सापि पश्चात्प्रहीयते॥

examples.dm: By habituating the latency for emptiness, The latency for substantial things will be abandoned; And by habituating the thought that "nothing exists," Even that will later be abandoned.
examples.gm: By familiarizing with the latent tendencies of emptiness, The latent tendencies of entities will be abandoned; By familiarizing with "there is nothing at all," That too will later be abandoned.
examples.sa: शून्यतावासनाधानाद्धीयते भाववासना। किंचिन्नास्तीति चाभ्यासात्सापि पश्चात्प्रहीयते॥

examples.dm: When neither entities nor non-entities Remain before the mind, Then, since there is no other aspect, It is thoroughly pacified in non-apprehension.
examples.gm: When both entities and non-entities Do not remain before the mind, At that time, since there is no other aspect, It is completely pacified, without an object of focus.
examples.sa: यदा न भावो नाभावो मतेः संतिष्ठते पुरः। तदान्यगत्यभावेन निरालम्बा प्रशाम्यति॥

examples.dm: When neither entities nor non-entities Remain before the mind, Then, since there is no other aspect, It is thoroughly pacified in non-apprehension.
examples.gm: When both entities and non-entities Do not remain before the mind, At that time, since there is no other aspect, It is completely pacified, without an object of focus.
examples.sa: यदा न भावो नाभावो मतेः संतिष्ठते पुरः। तदान्यगत्यभावेन निरालम्बा प्रशाम्यति॥

examples.dm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel or a wish-granting tree Completely fulfills all hopes, Likewise, through the power of the aspirations of those to be trained, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.gm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree Completely fulfill hopes, Likewise, due to those to be tamed and prayers of aspiration, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिः कल्पतरुर्यथेच्छापरिपूरणः। विनेयप्रणिधानाभ्यां जिनबिम्बं तथेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel or a wish-granting tree Completely fulfills all hopes, Likewise, through the power of the aspirations of those to be trained, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.gm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree Completely fulfill hopes, Likewise, due to those to be tamed and prayers of aspiration, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिः कल्पतरुर्यथेच्छापरिपूरणः। विनेयप्रणिधानाभ्यां जिनबिम्बं तथेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel or a wish-granting tree Completely fulfills all hopes, Likewise, through the power of the aspirations of those to be trained, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.gm: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree Completely fulfill hopes, Likewise, due to those to be tamed and prayers of aspiration, The form of the Victorious One appears.
examples.sa: चिन्तामणिः कल्पतरुर्यथेच्छापरिपूरणः। विनेयप्रणिधानाभ्यां जिनबिम्बं तथेक्ष्यते॥

examples.dm: For example, just as a Garuḍa shrine, Once established, remains even after the practitioner has passed away, And continues to pacify poisons and the like Even though a long time has elapsed since his passing.
examples.gm: For example, when a garuḍa shrine Has been accomplished and its creator has passed away, Even though a long time has passed since his death, It pacifies poison and so forth.
examples.sa: यथा गारुडिकः स्तम्भं साधयित्वा विनश्यति। स तस्मिंश्चिरनष्टेऽपि विषादीनुपशामयेत्॥

examples.dm: Liberation comes from seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness? Because the scriptures state that without this path, There is no enlightenment.
examples.gm: "One is liberated by seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness?" Because scriptures state that without this path, There is no awakening.
examples.sa: सत्यदर्शनतो मुक्तिः शून्यतादर्शनेन किम्। न विनानेन मार्गेण बोधिरित्यागमो यतः॥

examples.dm: Liberation comes from seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness? Because the scriptures state that without this path, There is no enlightenment.
examples.gm: "One is liberated by seeing the truths; What is the use of seeing emptiness?" Because scriptures state that without this path, There is no awakening.
examples.sa: सत्यदर्शनतो मुक्तिः शून्यतादर्शनेन किम्। न विनानेन मार्गेण बोधिरित्यागमो यतः॥

examples.dm: Whatever conditions make you believe in that, They are the same for the Mahāyāna as well. If it were true because two others accept it, Then the Vedas and so forth would also be true.
examples.gm: By whatever conditions you believe in that, That is the same for the Mahāyāna too. If it is true because two others accept it, The Vedas and so forth would also become true.
examples.sa: यत्प्रत्यया च तत्रास्था महायानेऽपि तां कुरु। अन्योभयेष्टसत्यत्वे वेदादेरपि सत्यता॥

examples.dm: If you say it is because the Mahāyāna is contested, Since your own scriptures are contested by non-Buddhists, And other scriptures are contested by your own and other schools, They would also have to be rejected because they are contested.
examples.gm: If you say the Mahāyāna is subject to dispute, The scriptures are disputed by non-Buddhists, And other scriptures are disputed by ourselves and others; Since they are subject to dispute, they would have to be discarded.
examples.sa: सविवादं महायानमिति चेदागमं त्यज। तीर्थिकैः सविवादत्वात्स्वैः परैश्चागमान्तरम्॥

examples.dm: If the root of the teaching is the monkhood itself, Then even being a monk is a difficult state to maintain. For those whose minds are still directed toward objects, Even nirvana is a difficult state to maintain.
examples.gm: If being a monk is the root of the teaching, Even being a monk is difficult to establish. For those whose minds have apprehension, Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.
examples.sa: शासनं भिक्षुतामूलं भिक्षुतैव च दुःस्थिता। सावलम्बनचित्तानां निर्वाणमपि दुःस्थितम्॥

examples.dm: If you argue that for the time being it is certain that there is no craving that constitutes grasping, Then why should this craving not exist—just like their confusion—even if it is not of an afflicted nature?
examples.gm: As for the craving for appropriation, If you say it is certain that it does not exist; Even if that craving is not an affliction, Why would it not exist, like ignorance?
examples.sa: तृष्णा तावदुपादानं नास्ति चेत्संप्रधार्यते। किमक्लिष्टापि तृष्णैषां नास्ति संमोहवत् सती॥

examples.dm: If you argue that for the time being it is certain that there is no craving that constitutes grasping, Then why should this craving not exist—just like their confusion—even if it is not of an afflicted nature?
examples.gm: As for the craving for appropriation, If you say it is certain that it does not exist; Even if that craving is not an affliction, Why would it not exist, like ignorance?
examples.sa: तृष्णा तावदुपादानं नास्ति चेत्संप्रधार्यते। किमक्लिष्टापि तृष्णैषां नास्ति संमोहवत् सती॥

examples.dm: If you argue that for the time being it is certain that there is no craving that constitutes grasping, Then why should this craving not exist—just like their confusion—even if it is not of an afflicted nature?
examples.gm: As for the craving for appropriation, If you say it is certain that it does not exist; Even if that craving is not an affliction, Why would it not exist, like ignorance?
examples.sa: तृष्णा तावदुपादानं नास्ति चेत्संप्रधार्यते। किमक्लिष्टापि तृष्णैषां नास्ति संमोहवत् सती॥

examples.dm: A mind that is devoid of emptiness, even if it has ceased, will arise once again, Just like the meditative absorption of non-perception; Therefore, one should meditate on emptiness.
examples.gm: A mind separated from emptiness, Though ceased, will arise again, Like the meditative absorption without discrimination; Therefore, one should meditate on emptiness.
examples.sa: विना शून्यतया चित्तं बद्धमुत्पद्यते पुनः। यथासंज्ञिसमापत्तौ भावयेत्तेन शून्यताम्॥

examples.dm: A mind that is devoid of emptiness, even if it has ceased, will arise once again, Just like the meditative absorption of non-perception; Therefore, one should meditate on emptiness.
examples.gm: A mind separated from emptiness, Though ceased, will arise again, Like the meditative absorption without discrimination; Therefore, one should meditate on emptiness.
examples.sa: विना शून्यतया चित्तं बद्धमुत्पद्यते पुनः। यथासंज्ञिसमापत्तौ भावयेत्तेन शून्यताम्॥

examples.dm: Regarding those words whose depth could not be fathomed By the likes of the great Mahākāśyapa, Because you have not understood them, Who are you to say they should not be accepted?
examples.gm: Any speech whose depth was unfathomed By Mahākāśyapa and the rest, Just because you do not understand it, Who would make it unacceptable?
examples.sa: महाकाश्यपमुख्यैश्च यद्वाक्यं नावगाह्यते । तत्त्वयानवबुद्धत्वादग्राह्यं कः करिष्यति ॥

examples.dm: Thus, it is not reasonable To direct refutations toward the position of emptiness. Therefore, without harboring any doubt, One should meditate upon emptiness.
examples.gm: Thus, toward the side of emptiness, Refutation is not appropriate. Therefore, without hesitation, One should meditate on emptiness.
examples.sa: तदेवं शून्यतापक्षे दूषणं नोपपद्यते। तस्मान्निर्विचिकित्सेन भावनीयैव शून्यता॥

examples.dm: Thus, it is not reasonable To direct refutations toward the position of emptiness. Therefore, without harboring any doubt, One should meditate upon emptiness.
examples.gm: Thus, toward the side of emptiness, Refutation is not appropriate. Therefore, without hesitation, One should meditate on emptiness.
examples.sa: तदेवं शून्यतापक्षे दूषणं नोपपद्यते। तस्मान्निर्विचिकित्सेन भावनीयैव शून्यता॥

examples.dm: Emptiness is the antidote To the darkness of the afflictive and cognitive obscurations. Why, then, would those who desire to swiftly attain omniscience Not meditate upon it?
examples.gm: Of the obscurations of afflictions and knowables, Emptiness is the antidote to the darkness. By one who wishes to quickly become omniscient, How could one not meditate on it?
examples.sa: क्लेशज्ञेयावृतितमःप्रतिपक्षो हि शून्यता। शीघ्रं सर्वज्ञताकामो न भावयति तां कथम्॥

examples.dm: Flesh and skin are not the self; Heat and wind are also not the self. The orifices are not the self in any way; The six consciousnesses are also not the self.
examples.gm: Flesh and skin are not the self, And warmth and wind are not the self. The cavities are not the self, and in all ways The six consciousnesses are not the self either.
examples.sa: नाहं मांसं न च स्नायु नोष्मा वायुरहं न च। न च च्छिद्राण्यहं नापि षड् विज्ञानानि सर्वथा॥

examples.dm: How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound Become that which apprehends form? One person being designated as both father and son Is not the ultimate reality.
examples.gm: How could that which has the nature of apprehending sound Become the apprehender of form? One being both father and son Is designated, but it is not ultimate reality.
examples.sa: शब्दग्रहणरूपं यत्तद्रूपग्रहणं कथम्। एकः पिता च पुत्रश्च कल्प्यते न तु तत्त्वतः॥

examples.dm: If the self does not exist, The connection between action and result is illogical; Since the action perishes after being performed, Whose action would it be?
examples.gm: If the self does not exist, The connection between actions and results is not logical, Because if one perishes after performing an action, Whose action will it be?
examples.sa: न कर्मफलसंबन्धो युक्तश्चेदात्मना विना। कर्म कृत्वा विनष्टे हि फलं कस्य भविष्यति॥

examples.dm: To see a cause existing simultaneously with its result Is not possible; It is by relying on a single continuum That the "agent" and "experiencer" are taught.
examples.gm: That the one possessing the cause also possesses the result— To see this is impossible. It is in dependence upon a single continuum That an agent and an experiencer are taught.
examples.sa: हेतुमान् फलयोगीति दृश्यते नैष संभवः। संतानस्यैक्यमाश्रित्य कर्ता भोक्तेति देशितम्॥

examples.dm: If sentient beings do not exist, Then for whom should one feel compassion? It is directed toward those imputed by delusion, Which are accepted for the sake of the result.
examples.gm: If sentient beings do not exist, Toward whom does one practice compassion? Toward whatever is imputed by the delusion That is accepted for the sake of the result.
examples.sa: यदि सत्त्वो न विद्येत कस्योपरि कृपेति चेत्। कार्यार्थमभ्युपेतेन यो मोहेन प्रकल्पितः॥

examples.dm: As long as the collection of conditions remains, The body appears like a person; Likewise, as long as the hands and so forth are present, The body will appear to exist therein.
examples.gm: As long as the collection of conditions lasts, The body appears like a person. Likewise, as long as it is present in the hands and so forth, For that long, the body appears there.
examples.sa: यावत्प्रत्ययसामग्री तावत्कायः पुमानिव। एवं करादौ सा यावत्तावत्कायोऽत्र दृश्यते॥

examples.dm: Even the parts are reduced to atoms, And those atoms are divided into directional facets. Since the directional facets are also devoid of parts, They are like space; therefore, even atoms do not exist.
examples.gm: And the part also by its division into particles, And that particle also by its division into directional parts, And since the division of directions is devoid of parts, It is like space; therefore, even particles do not exist.
examples.sa: अंशा अप्यणुभेदेन सोऽप्यणुर्दिग्विभागतः। दिग्विभागो निरंशत्वादाकाशं तेन नास्त्यणुः॥

examples.dm: Even the parts are reduced to atoms, And those atoms are divided into directional facets. Since the directional facets are also devoid of parts, They are like space; therefore, even atoms do not exist.
examples.gm: And the part also by its division into particles, And that particle also by its division into directional parts, And since the division of directions is devoid of parts, It is like space; therefore, even particles do not exist.
examples.sa: अंशा अप्यणुभेदेन सोऽप्यणुर्दिग्विभागतः। दिग्विभागो निरंशत्वादाकाशं तेन नास्त्यणुः॥

examples.dm: If it is argued that it is not experienced because it is overwhelmed by something more powerful, How can that which is not of the nature of experience Be a sensation?
examples.gm: If it is because it is overshadowed by something stronger That it is not experienced, How can that which is not of the nature of experience Be a feeling?
examples.sa: बलीयसाभिभूतत्वाद्यदि तन्नानुभूयते। वेदनात्वं कथं तस्य यस्य नानुभवात्मता॥

examples.dm: If you say that suffering exists in a subtle state And its gross form has merely been removed, Then that is simply a state of joy other than that; If you say it is subtle, then that too is of the same nature.
examples.gm: "Suffering exists in a subtle state; Has its gross state not been removed?" If you say, "That is merely a joy distinct from that," Then that subtle state too is [a state] of that [joy].
examples.sa: अस्ति सूक्ष्मतया दुःखं स्थौल्यं तस्य हृतं ननु। तुष्टिमात्रापरा चेत्स्यात्तस्मात् साप्यस्य सूक्ष्मता॥

examples.dm: If, because an opposing condition has arisen, Suffering is not produced, Then is it not established that what is considered "feeling" Is merely a stubborn conceptual attachment?
examples.gm: If, because a contrary condition has arisen, Suffering does not arise, Is it not established that the conception of feeling Is merely conceptual clinging?
examples.sa: विरुद्धप्रत्ययोत्पत्तौ दुःखस्यानुदयो यदि। कल्पनाभिनिवेशो हि वेदनेत्यागतं ननु॥

examples.dm: If, because an opposing condition has arisen, Suffering is not produced, Then is it not established that what is considered "feeling" Is merely a stubborn conceptual attachment?
examples.gm: If, because a contrary condition has arisen, Suffering does not arise, Is it not established that the conception of feeling Is merely conceptual clinging?
examples.sa: विरुद्धप्रत्ययोत्पत्तौ दुःखस्यानुदयो यदि। कल्पनाभिनिवेशो हि वेदनेत्यागतं ननु॥

examples.dm: How could it be logical to speak of "contact" Between things that have no parts? If you have ever seen contact occurring without parts, Then please demonstrate it.
examples.gm: How could it be reasonable to say That what is partless can meet? If meeting and being partless Have been seen together, show it!
examples.sa: निरंशस्य च संसर्गः कथं नामोपपद्यते। संसर्गे च निरंशत्वं यदि दृष्टं निदर्शय॥

examples.dm: If, in this way, there is no contact, From what could feeling arise? For what purpose is all this toil? What could cause harm to what?
examples.gm: Thus, if contact does not exist, From what would feeling arise? What is the purpose of this weariness? What would harm what?
examples.sa: तदेवं स्पर्शनाभावे वेदनासंभवः कुतः। किमर्थमयमायासः बाधा कस्य कुतो भवेत्॥

examples.dm: If in that way the conventional does not exist, How could there be the two truths? Furthermore, if that conventional exists through another, How could sentient beings pass into nirvana?
examples.gm: If, in this way, conventional reality does not exist, How could the two truths exist in that? And if that is due to another conventional reality, How could sentient beings pass into nirvāṇa?
examples.sa: यद्येवं संवृतिर्नास्ति ततः सत्यद्वयं कुतः। अथ साप्यन्यसंवृत्या स्यात्सत्त्वो निर्वृतः कुतः॥

examples.dm: Conceptual thought and the object to be analyzed Are both mutually dependent. Based upon what is renowned in the world, All analytical investigations are expressed.
examples.gm: Conception and the object to be conceived, The two are mutually dependent. Relying on what is conventionally known, All analyses are expressed.
examples.sa: कल्पना कल्पितं चेति द्वयमन्योन्यनिश्रितम्। यथाप्रसिद्धमाश्रित्य विचारः सर्व उच्यते॥

examples.dm: Conceptual thought and the object to be analyzed Are both mutually dependent. Based upon what is renowned in the world, All analytical investigations are expressed.
examples.gm: Conception and the object to be conceived, The two are mutually dependent. Relying on what is conventionally known, All analyses are expressed.
examples.sa: कल्पना कल्पितं चेति द्वयमन्योन्यनिश्रितम्। यथाप्रसिद्धमाश्रित्य विचारः सर्व उच्यते॥

examples.dm: When the object of analysis is thoroughly analyzed, There is no basis remaining for the analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that is described as nirvana.
examples.gm: If the object of analysis has been analyzed, There is no basis for analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that too is expressed as nirvāṇa.
examples.sa: विचारिते विचार्ये तु विचारस्यास्ति नाश्रयः। निराश्रितत्वान्नोदेति तच्च निर्वाणमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: For those who hold that these two are real, Their position is extremely difficult to maintain. If the object is established through the power of consciousness, What basis is there for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.gm: According to those who hold these two to be true, That very position rests in great difficulty. If the object is established by the power of consciousness, What is the basis for the existence of consciousness itself?
examples.sa: यस्य त्वेतद्द्वयं सत्यं स एवात्यन्तदुःस्थितः। यदि ज्ञेयवशादर्थो ज्ञानास्तित्वे तु का गतिः॥

examples.dm: For the time being, through worldly direct perception, All causes are seen. The distinctions in the lotus stalk and so forth Are produced by the distinctions among their causes.
examples.gm: For now, by worldly direct perception, All causes are seen. The variations such as the stalk of the lotus Are produced by the variations of causes.
examples.sa: लोकः प्रत्यक्षतस्तावत्सर्वं हेतुमुदीक्षते। पद्मनालादिभेदो हि हेतुभेदेन जायते॥

examples.dm: If Īśvara is the cause of the world, Then for a start, explain who Īśvara is. If you say he is the elements, that may be so; But why weary yourself over a mere name?
examples.gm: If Īśvara is the cause of beings, Tell me, for now, what is Īśvara? If one says it is the elements, so be it; But what is the use of exhausting oneself over a mere name?
examples.sa: ईश्वरो जगतो हेतुः वद कस्तावदीश्वरः। भूतानि चेद्भवत्वेवं नाममात्रेऽपि किं श्रमः॥

examples.dm: Īśvara is not space, because space is inert; He is not the self, as that has already been refuted. And if the creator is also inconceivable, What is the point of speaking of him as "inconceivable"?
examples.gm: Īśvara is not space, because it is devoid of movement; He is not the self, because it was already refuted before; And as for a creator who is inconceivable, What is the use of speaking of the inconceivable?
examples.sa: नाकाशमीशोऽचेष्टत्वात् नात्मा पूर्वनिषेधतः। अचिन्त्यस्य च कर्तृत्वमप्यचिन्त्यं किमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: Pleasure and pain have arisen from karma since beginningless time. Tell me, what is it that is created by him? If there is no beginning to the cause, How could there be a beginning to the effect?
examples.gm: Happiness and suffering are from beginningless karma; Tell me, what was produced by him? If the cause has no beginning, How can the effect have a beginning?
examples.sa: कर्मणः सुखदुःखे च वद किं तेन निर्मितम्। हेतोरादिर्न चेदस्ति फलस्यादिः कुतो भवेत्॥

examples.dm: Those who claim that atoms are eternal Have already been refuted previously. The Sāṃkhyas assert that a permanent Primal Substance Is the cause of the world.
examples.gm: As for those who assert permanent atoms, They have also already been refuted earlier. The permanent Pradhāna is the cause of beings; This is what the Sāṃkhyas assert.
examples.sa: येऽपि नित्यानणूनाहुस्तेऽपि पूर्वं निवारिताः। सांख्याः प्रधानमिच्छन्ति नित्यं लोकस्य कारणम्॥

examples.dm: The equilibrium of the qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas Is proclaimed to be the Primal Substance; Their disequilibrium is said to be the world.
examples.gm: The qualities known as Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, Abiding in equilibrium, Are termed Pradhāna; In disequilibrium, they are said to be beings.
examples.sa: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति गुणा अविषमस्थिताः। प्रधानमिति कथ्यन्ते विषमैर्जगदुच्यते॥

examples.dm: If pleasure and the rest were manifest as existing entities, Why is their experience not perceived? If that itself becomes subtle, How can it be both coarse and subtle?
examples.gm: If the manifestation of pleasure and so forth exists, Why is the experience not apprehended? If that itself becomes subtle, How can it be both coarse and subtle?
examples.sa: सत्यामेव सुखव्यक्तौ संवित्तिः किं न गृह्यते। तदेव सूक्ष्मतां याति स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं च तत्कथम्॥

examples.dm: If pleasure and the rest were manifest as existing entities, Why is their experience not perceived? If that itself becomes subtle, How can it be both coarse and subtle?
examples.gm: If the manifestation of pleasure and so forth exists, Why is the experience not apprehended? If that itself becomes subtle, How can it be both coarse and subtle?
examples.sa: सत्यामेव सुखव्यक्तौ संवित्तिः किं न गृह्यते। तदेव सूक्ष्मतां याति स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं च तत्कथम्॥

examples.dm: If pleasure and the rest were manifest as existing entities, Why is their experience not perceived? If that itself becomes subtle, How can it be both coarse and subtle?
examples.gm: If the manifestation of pleasure and so forth exists, Why is the experience not apprehended? If that itself becomes subtle, How can it be both coarse and subtle?
examples.sa: सत्यामेव सुखव्यक्तौ संवित्तिः किं न गृह्यते। तदेव सूक्ष्मतां याति स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं च तत्कथम्॥

examples.dm: By abandoning the coarse and becoming subtle, Those coarse and subtle states are themselves impermanent. Why, then, do you not accept that All things are likewise impermanent?
examples.gm: Since it becomes subtle after abandoning coarseness, That coarseness and subtlety are impermanent. Likewise, why do you not assert That all things are impermanent?
examples.sa: स्थौल्यं त्यक्त्वा भवेत्सूक्ष्ममनित्ये स्थौल्यसूक्ष्मते। सर्वस्य वस्तुनस्तद्वत्किं नानित्यत्वमिष्यते॥

examples.dm: If the coarse state is not other than the pleasure, Then the manifest pleasure is itself impermanent. If you claim that nothing non-existent can ever arise Because it lacks being,
examples.gm: If coarseness is not other than pleasure, Manifest pleasure is impermanent. If you assert that nothing nonexistent Arises, because it does not exist,
examples.sa: न स्थौल्यं चेत्सुखादन्यत् सुखस्यानित्यता स्फुटम्। नासदुत्पद्यते किंचिदसत्त्वादिति चेन्मतम्॥

examples.dm: If a valid authority is not valid, Would that which is measured by it not be false? In that case, the meditation On emptiness would be untenable.
examples.gm: If valid cognition is not valid, Is what is measured by it not false? In reality, emptiness; Meditating on it therefore becomes untenable.
examples.sa: प्रमाणमप्रमाणं चेन्ननु तत्प्रमितं मृषा। तत्त्वतः शून्यता तस्माद्भावानां नोपपद्यते॥

examples.dm: Without contacting the imagined entity, Its non-existence cannot be apprehended. Therefore, whatever entity is false, Its non-existence is clearly false as well.
examples.gm: Without contacting the imputed entity, Its nonentity is not apprehended. Therefore, whatever entity is false, Its nonentity is clearly false.
examples.sa: कल्पितं भावमस्पृष्ट्वा तदभावो न गृह्यते। तस्माद्भावो मृषा यो हि तस्याभावः स्फुटं मृषा॥

examples.dm: Therefore, when analyzed in such a manner, Nothing at all exists without a cause, Nor does it abide within conditions, Whether they be individual or assembled.
examples.gm: Therefore, by analyzing in this way, Nothing whatever exists without a cause. In individual or assembled Conditions, it also does not abide.
examples.sa: तस्मादेवं विचारेण नास्ति किंचिदहेतुतः। न च व्यस्तसमस्तेषु प्रत्ययेषु व्यवस्थितम्॥

examples.dm: Whatever is seen through the proximity of something else, And does not exist without it, Is like a fabricated reflection; How could there be any true reality in that?
examples.gm: Whatever, through the proximity of something, Is seen, and is not when that is absent, Is artificial and similar to a reflection; How can there be true existence in that?
examples.sa: यदन्यसंनिधानेन दृष्टं न तदभावतः। प्रतिबिम्बसमे तस्मिन् कृत्रिमे सत्यता कथम्॥

examples.dm: Whatever is seen through the proximity of something else, And does not exist without it, Is like a fabricated reflection; How could there be any true reality in that?
examples.gm: Whatever, through the proximity of something, Is seen, and is not when that is absent, Is artificial and similar to a reflection; How can there be true existence in that?
examples.sa: यदन्यसंनिधानेन दृष्टं न तदभावतः। प्रतिबिम्बसमे तस्मिन् कृत्रिमे सत्यता कथम्॥

examples.dm: Even by means of hundreds of millions of causes, A non-existent thing cannot be transformed. How could that state ever be an entity? And what else could possibly become an entity?
examples.gm: Even by a hundred million causes, A nonentity cannot be transformed. How could that state be an entity? And what else could become an entity?
examples.sa: नाभावस्य विकारोऽस्ति हेतुकोटिशतैरपि। तदवस्थ कथं भावः को वान्यो भावतां गतः॥

examples.dm: Thus, there is no cessation, And likewise, there is no existence. Therefore, all these wandering beings Are eternally unborn and unceasing.
examples.gm: Thus, there is no cessation, And there is no entity; therefore, All these migrating beings Are always unproduced and unceased.
examples.sa: एवं न च निरोधोऽस्ति न च भावोऽस्ति सर्वदा। अजातमनिरुद्धं च तस्मात्सर्वमिदं जगत्॥

examples.dm: Thus, there is no cessation, And likewise, there is no existence. Therefore, all these wandering beings Are eternally unborn and unceasing.
examples.gm: Thus, there is no cessation, And there is no entity; therefore, All these migrating beings Are always unproduced and unceased.
examples.sa: एवं न च निरोधोऽस्ति न च भावोऽस्ति सर्वदा। अजातमनिरुद्धं च तस्मात्सर्वमिदं जगत्॥

examples.dm: Thus, when things are empty, What is there to gain and what is there to lose? Who is there to show respect, And what is there to be held in utter contempt?
examples.gm: Thus, with entities being empty, What is there to be gained, what is there to be lost? Who is there to do honor, Or what is there to completely despise?
examples.sa: एवं शून्येषु धर्मेषु किं लब्धं किं हृतं भवेत्। सत्कृतः परिभूतो वा केन कः संभविष्यति॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, that ocean of unbearable suffering Is beyond compare and without end. In that state, one's strength is likewise feeble, And there, one's lifespan is also very short.
examples.gm: Furthermore, there is the incomparable and unbearable Boundless ocean of suffering. There, one thus has little strength, And there, life is also short.
examples.sa: तत्र चानुपमास्तीव्रा अनन्ता दुःखसागराः। तत्रैवमल्पबलता तत्राप्यल्पत्वमायुषः॥

examples.dm: Life passes by quickly and meaninglessly, And analytical discernment is extremely difficult to find. Moreover, when one is habituated to such distractions, Where is there any means to turn them back?
examples.gm: Life passes quickly and meaninglessly; Discernment is extremely hard to find. And there, as for habituation to distraction, Where is the method to reverse it?
examples.sa: वृथैवायुर्वहत्याशु विवेकस्तत्र दुर्लभः। तत्राप्यभ्यस्तविक्षेपनिवारणगतिः कुतः॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, in that state, Māra exerts himself To make one fall into the great miserable realms. There, the wrong paths are numerous, And it is difficult to transcend even doubt.
examples.gm: Even there, into the great lower realms, Māra exerts himself to make them fall. There, wrong paths are many, and It is hard to overcome even doubt.
examples.sa: तत्रापि मारो यतते महापायप्रपातने। तत्रासन्मार्गबाहुल्याद्विचिकित्सा च दुर्जया॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, in that state, Māra exerts himself To make one fall into the great miserable realms. There, the wrong paths are numerous, And it is difficult to transcend even doubt.
examples.gm: Even there, into the great lower realms, Māra exerts himself to make them fall. There, wrong paths are many, and It is hard to overcome even doubt.
examples.sa: तत्रापि मारो यतते महापायप्रपातने। तत्रासन्मार्गबाहुल्याद्विचिकित्सा च दुर्जया॥

examples.dm: Again, leisure is difficult to find, And the appearance of a Buddha is extremely rare. The river of afflictions is hard to abandon; Alas, suffering will continue in succession!
examples.gm: Once again, leisure is hard to find, and The appearance of a Buddha is extremely hard to encounter. The river of afflictions is hard to abandon, so Alas, suffering will continue in succession.
examples.sa: पुनश्च क्षणदौर्लभ्यं बुद्धोत्पादोऽतिदुर्लभः। क्लेशौघो दुर्निवारश्चेत्यहो दुःखपरंपरा॥

examples.dm: Even though they are in such extreme misery, Those who do not see their own suffering While remaining in this river of pain— Alas, they are worthy of compassion!
examples.gm: Although suffering so extremely like this, Those who do not see their own suffering, These beings dwelling in the river of suffering, Alas, are worthy of sorrow.
examples.sa: अहो बतातिशोच्यत्वमेषां दुःखौघवर्तिनाम्। ये नेक्षन्ते स्वदौःस्थित्यमेवमप्यतिदुःस्थिताः॥

examples.dm: Thus, by behaving as if they will never grow old or die, They are first of all killed in these very places, And then the unbearable fall into the lower realms occurs.
examples.gm: Thus, as if there were no aging and death, To those who live behaving in such a way, First of all, having been killed, The unbearable fall into the lower realms will come.
examples.sa: अजरामरलीलानामेवं विहरतां सताम्। आयास्यन्त्यापदो घोराः कृत्वा मरणमग्रतः॥

examples.dm: When shall I be able to pacify those tormented by the fires of suffering With a cooling rain of my own bliss, Which has arisen from the clouds of merit, And thus become a source of peace?
examples.gm: Thus, for those tormented by the fire of suffering, Well-arisen from the clouds of merit, With the rain of my own accumulation of happiness, When will I pacify them?
examples.sa: एवं दुःखाग्नितप्तानां शान्तिं कुर्यामहं कदा। पुण्यमेघसमुद्भूतैः सुखोपकरणैः स्वकैः॥

examples.dm: When, by respectfully accumulating the collection of merit In a manner free from conceptual reference, Shall I teach emptiness to those Who are ruined by their conceptual grasping?
examples.gm: When, in a non-apprehending manner, Having respectfully gathered the accumulation of merit, To those who are ruined by apprehension, Will I teach emptiness?
examples.sa: कदोपलम्भदृष्टिभ्यो देशयिष्यामि शून्यताम्। संवृत्यानुपलम्भेन पुण्यसंभारमादरात्॥

examples.dm: When, by respectfully accumulating the collection of merit In a manner free from conceptual reference, Shall I teach emptiness to those Who are ruined by their conceptual grasping?
examples.gm: When, in a non-apprehending manner, Having respectfully gathered the accumulation of merit, To those who are ruined by apprehension, Will I teach emptiness?
examples.sa: कदोपलम्भदृष्टिभ्यो देशयिष्यामि शून्यताम्। संवृत्यानुपलम्भेन पुण्यसंभारमादरात्॥

examples.dm: In all the world systems, However many hells there may be, May the embodied beings within them Rejoice in the happiness of Sukhavati.
examples.gm: In the realms of the world, the hells, However many there are, In them, may embodied beings Rejoice with the happiness of Sukhāvatī.
examples.sa: यावन्तो नरकाः केचिद्विद्यन्ते लोकधातुषु। सुखावतीसुखामोद्यैर्मोदन्तां तेषु देहिनः॥

examples.dm: In all the world systems, However many hells there may be, May the embodied beings within them Rejoice in the happiness of Sukhavati.
examples.gm: In the realms of the world, the hells, However many there are, In them, may embodied beings Rejoice with the happiness of Sukhāvatī.
examples.sa: यावन्तो नरकाः केचिद्विद्यन्ते लोकधातुषु। सुखावतीसुखामोद्यैर्मोदन्तां तेषु देहिनः॥

examples.dm: May the forest of sword-leaves Become for them a dense sandalwood grove; May the Shalmali trees likewise Grow into wish-fulfilling trees.
examples.gm: May the forest of sword-leaves also Become a dense sandalwood forest for them. May the trunks of the śālmali trees also Grow as wish-fulfilling trees.
examples.sa: असिपत्रवनं तेषां स्यान्नन्दनवनद्युति। कूटशाल्मलिवृक्षाश्च जायन्तां कल्पपादपाः॥

examples.dm: May those heaps of glowing coals become heaps of jewels; May the scorched earth be spread as a crystal floor; May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also become Celestial palaces of offerings, filled with Sugatas.
examples.gm: May those heaps of coal become heaps of jewels. May the burning ground be paved as a crystal ground. May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also, of offerings Become immeasurable palaces, filled with Sugatas.
examples.sa: सोऽङ्गारराशिर्मणिराशिरस्तु तप्ता च भूः स्फाटिककुट्टिमं स्यात्। भवन्तु संघातमहीधराश्च पूजाविमानाः सुगतप्रपूर्णाः॥

examples.dm: May those submerged in the fordless river, which is like a pit of fire, Their flesh all decayed and their skeletons the color of white kunda flowers, Attain celestial bodies through the power of my merit, And dwell with goddesses by the gently flowing waters.
examples.gm: May those sinking in the unfordable river that is like a fire pit, Their flesh all destroyed, with bones the color of jasmine flowers, By the power of my virtue attain the bodies of gods, And abide together with goddesses in the Mandākinī.
examples.sa: पतितसकलमांसाः कुन्दवर्णास्थिदेहा दहनसमजलायां वैतरण्यां निमग्नाः। मम कुशलबलेन प्राप्तदिव्यात्मभावाः सह सुरवनिताभिः सन्तु मन्दाकिनीस्थाः॥

examples.dm: Why are the terrifying minions of Yama, the crows, and the vultures afraid here? Thinking, "Whose excellent power is this that dispels darkness everywhere and generates blissful joy?" They look upward and behold the blazing Vajrapāṇi dwelling in the midst of the sky; Through the force of their intense joy, may they be freed from sin and dwell in his company.
examples.gm: "Why are the men of Yama, and the unbearable crows and vultures terrified here? Whose noble power is this, that entirely dispels darkness and generates joy and happiness?" Thinking thus, Looking upward and seeing the blazing Vajrapāṇi residing in the center of the sky, Freed from negativity through the force of intense joy, may they depart together with him.
examples.sa: त्रस्ताः पश्यन्त्वकस्मादिह यमपुरुषाः काकगृध्राश्च घोरा ध्वान्तं ध्वस्तं समन्तात्सुखरतिजननी कस्य सौम्या प्रभेयम्। इत्यूर्ध्वं प्रेक्षमाणा गगनतलगतं वज्रपाणिं ज्वलन्तं दृष्ट्वा प्रामोद्यवेगाद्व्यपगतदुरिता यान्तु तेनैव सार्धम्॥

examples.dm: When a rain of flowers falls, mingled with scented water, And they see the glowing embers of hell extinguished with a hiss, They wonder, "What is this that has suddenly satiated us with bliss?" And thus may the denizens of hell behold Padmapāṇi.
examples.gm: Through the falling of a rain of flowers mixed with scented water, Seeing the burning embers of hell sizzling and being extinguished, And thinking, "What is this sudden satisfaction of happiness?" May the hell beings see Padmapāṇi.
examples.sa: पतति कमलवृष्टिर्गन्धपानीयमिश्रा-च्छमिति नरकवह्निं दृश्यते नाशयन्ती। किमिदमिति सुखेनाह्लादितानामकस्मा-द्भवतु कमलपाणेर्दर्शनं नारकाणाम्॥

examples.dm: Friends, cast away your fear and come here quickly to our side! Who is this radiant youth with five knots of hair who has arrived to grant us fearlessness— The compassionate Bodhisattva who thoroughly protects all beings, And through whose power we are freed from all suffering and reach the heights of joy?
examples.gm: "Friends, cast away your fear and come quickly here to us! By whose power we are freed from all suffering and the force of joy has arrived, The one who entirely protects all wandering beings, who has given rise to bodhicitta and compassion, The blazing youth with a topknot who makes us fearless, has arrived!
examples.sa: आयातायात शीघ्रं भयमपनयत भ्रातरो जीविताः स्मः संप्राप्तोऽस्माकमेष ज्वलदभयकरः कोऽपि चीरीकुमारः। सर्वं यस्यानुभावाद्व्यसनमपगतं प्रीतिवेगाः प्रवृत्ताः जातं संबोधिचित्तं सकलजनपरित्राणमाता दया च॥

examples.dm: Friends, cast away your fear and come here quickly to our side! Who is this radiant youth with five knots of hair who has arrived to grant us fearlessness— The compassionate Bodhisattva who thoroughly protects all beings, And through whose power we are freed from all suffering and reach the heights of joy?
examples.gm: "Friends, cast away your fear and come quickly here to us! By whose power we are freed from all suffering and the force of joy has arrived, The one who entirely protects all wandering beings, who has given rise to bodhicitta and compassion, The blazing youth with a topknot who makes us fearless, has arrived!
examples.sa: आयातायात शीघ्रं भयमपनयत भ्रातरो जीविताः स्मः संप्राप्तोऽस्माकमेष ज्वलदभयकरः कोऽपि चीरीकुमारः। सर्वं यस्यानुभावाद्व्यसनमपगतं प्रीतिवेगाः प्रवृत्ताः जातं संबोधिचित्तं सकलजनपरित्राणमाता दया च॥

examples.dm: Thus, through my roots of virtue, may they see clouds of unobstructed Bodhisattvas such as Samantabhadra, Like clouds of bliss, raining down cool and fragrant showers; Upon seeing this, May those denizens of hell be filled with manifest joy.
examples.gm: Likewise, by my roots of virtue, seeing Samantabhadra and other Bodhisattvas' unobstructed pleasant clouds, Letting fall a cool and fragrant rain, May those sentient beings in hell become truly joyful.
examples.sa: इति मत्कुशलैः समन्तभद्र-प्रमुखानावृतबोधिसत्त्वमेघान्। सुखशीतसुगन्धवातवृष्टी-नभिनन्दन्तु विलोक्य नारकास्ते॥

examples.dm: May animals be free from the fear Of preying upon one another; And just like the people of the Northern Continent, May the hungry ghosts become happy.
examples.gm: May animals be freed From the fear of eating one another. Just like the humans of Uttarakuru, May the hungry ghosts become happy.
examples.sa: शाम्यन्तु वेदनास्तीव्रा नारकाणां भयानि च। दुर्गतिभ्यो विमुच्यन्तां सर्वदुर्गतिवासिनः॥

examples.dm: May animals be free from the fear Of preying upon one another; And just like the people of the Northern Continent, May the hungry ghosts become happy.
examples.gm: May animals be freed From the fear of eating one another. Just like the humans of Uttarakuru, May the hungry ghosts become happy.
examples.sa: शाम्यन्तु वेदनास्तीव्रा नारकाणां भयानि च। दुर्गतिभ्यो विमुच्यन्तां सर्वदुर्गतिवासिनः॥

examples.dm: By the stream of milk flowing From the hand of the noble Avalokiteśvara, May the hungry ghosts be satisfied, And by bathing in it, may they be forever cooled.
examples.gm: Of noble Avalokiteśvara, By the stream of milk flowing from his hands, May the hungry ghosts be satisfied, And having bathed, may they always be cooled.
examples.sa: अन्योन्यभक्षणभयं तिरश्चामपगच्छतु। भवन्तु सुखिनः प्रेता यथोत्तरकुरौ नराः॥

examples.dm: May the blind see forms, And may the deaf always hear sounds; Just like the goddess Māyādevī, May pregnant women also give birth without harm.
examples.gm: May the blind see with their eyes, And the deaf always hear sounds. Just as with the goddess Māyā, May pregnant women give birth without harm.
examples.sa: संतर्प्यन्तां प्रेताः स्नाप्यन्तां शीतला भवन्तु सदा। आर्यावलोकितेश्वरकरगलितक्षीरधाराभिः॥

examples.dm: May they be freed from all states of non-leisure, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And possessing excellent food and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.gm: Freed from all unfree states, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And perfect in sustenance and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.sa: सर्वाक्षणविनिर्मुक्ताः श्रद्धाप्रज्ञाकृपान्विताः। आकाराचारसंपन्नाः सन्तु जातिस्मराः सदा॥

examples.dm: May they be freed from all states of non-leisure, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And possessing excellent food and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.gm: Freed from all unfree states, Endowed with faith, wisdom, and compassion, And perfect in sustenance and conduct, May they always remember their past lives.
examples.sa: सर्वाक्षणविनिर्मुक्ताः श्रद्धाप्रज्ञाकृपान्विताः। आकाराचारसंपन्नाः सन्तु जातिस्मराः सदा॥

examples.dm: May all have inexhaustible enjoyments, Just like the treasury of space. Without dispute and without harm, May they act with complete freedom.
examples.gm: Like the treasury of space, May their enjoyments be inexhaustible, And without dispute and without harm, May they enjoy them independently.
examples.sa: भवन्त्वक्षयकोशाश्च यावद्गगनगञ्जवत्। निर्द्वन्द्वा निरुपायासाः सन्तु स्वाधीनवृत्तयः॥

examples.dm: May they never be separated from the mind of enlightenment, May they be devoted to the conduct of awakening, May they be cared for by the Buddhas, And may they abandon the activities of Māra.
examples.gm: Never separating from the awakening mind, And dedicating themselves to the bodhisattva conduct, May they be fully embraced by the buddhas, And abandon the actions of Māra.
examples.sa: बोधिचित्ताविरहिता बोधिचर्यापरायणाः। बुद्धैः परिगृहीताश्च मारकर्मविवर्जिताः॥

examples.dm: May they never be separated from the mind of enlightenment, May they be devoted to the conduct of awakening, May they be cared for by the Buddhas, And may they abandon the activities of Māra.
examples.gm: Never separating from the awakening mind, And dedicating themselves to the bodhisattva conduct, May they be fully embraced by the buddhas, And abandon the actions of Māra.
examples.sa: बोधिचित्ताविरहिता बोधिचर्यापरायणाः। बुद्धैः परिगृहीताश्च मारकर्मविवर्जिताः॥

examples.dm: May the ground everywhere Be free from pebbles and the like, And remain naturally smooth, As level as the palm of a hand and of the nature of lapis lazuli.
examples.gm: Everywhere, may the ground Be free of gravel and the like, As even as the palm of a hand, and of lapis lazuli, May its nature remain soft.
examples.sa: शर्करादिव्यपेता च समा पाणितलोपमा। मृद्वी च वैडूर्यमयी भूमिः सर्वत्र तिष्ठतु॥

examples.dm: In all the various circles of retinues, May many Bodhisattvas Dwell, having adorned the surface of the earth With their own excellence.
examples.gm: In all the circles of retinues that exist, May many bodhisattvas Adorn the surface of the earth with their excellence, And remain dwelling there.
examples.sa: बोधिसत्त्वमहापर्षन्मण्डलानि समन्ततः। निषीदन्तु स्वशोभाभिर्मण्डयन्तु महीतलम्॥

examples.dm: May all embodied beings continuously hear The sound of the Dharma from birds, From trees, from all rays of light, And even from the sky itself.
examples.gm: By all embodied beings, from birds, Trees, and all rays of light, And even from space, may the sound of the Dharma Be heard unceasingly.
examples.sa: पक्षिभ्यः सर्ववृखेभ्यो रश्मिभ्यो गगनादपि। धर्मध्वनिरविश्रामं श्रूयतां सर्वदेहिभिः॥

examples.dm: May they always meet with the Buddhas And the sons of the Buddhas. With infinite clouds of offerings, May they worship the teachers of the world.
examples.gm: May they always encounter buddhas And the children of buddhas. With boundless clouds of offerings, May they make offerings to the gurus of the world.
examples.sa: बुद्धबुद्धसुतैर्नित्यं लभन्तां ते समागमम्। पूजामेघैरनन्तैश्च पूजयन्तु जगद्गुरुम्॥

examples.dm: May they always meet with the Buddhas And the sons of the Buddhas. With infinite clouds of offerings, May they worship the teachers of the world.
examples.gm: May they always encounter buddhas And the children of buddhas. With boundless clouds of offerings, May they make offerings to the gurus of the world.
examples.sa: बुद्धबुद्धसुतैर्नित्यं लभन्तां ते समागमम्। पूजामेघैरनन्तैश्च पूजयन्तु जगद्गुरुम्॥

examples.dm: May the gods also send rain at the proper time, And may the harvests be bountiful. May kings act in accordance with the Dharma, And may the world also flourish.
examples.gm: May the gods send rain on time, And may the harvests be perfect. May kings act in accordance with the Dharma, And may the world also prosper.
examples.sa: देवो वर्षतु कालेन सस्यसंपत्तिरस्तु च। स्फीतो भवतु लोकश्च राजा भवतु धार्मिकः॥

examples.dm: May medicines be potent, And may the recitation of secret mantras be successful. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with a mind of compassion.
examples.gm: May medicines be endowed with potency, And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with minds of compassion.
examples.sa: शक्ता भवन्तु चौषध्यो मन्त्राः सिध्यन्तु जापिनाम्। भवन्तु करुणाविष्टा डाकिनीराक्षसादयः॥

examples.dm: May medicines be potent, And may the recitation of secret mantras be successful. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with a mind of compassion.
examples.gm: May medicines be endowed with potency, And may the recitation of secret mantras be accomplished. May ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, and the like Be endowed with minds of compassion.
examples.sa: शक्ता भवन्तु चौषध्यो मन्त्राः सिध्यन्तु जापिनाम्। भवन्तु करुणाविष्टा डाकिनीराक्षसादयः॥

examples.dm: May temples be well-established, Adorned with study and recitation. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the purposes of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
examples.gm: May monasteries, with reading and Recitation, remain well adorned. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the goals of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
examples.sa: पाठस्वाध्यायकलिला विहाराः सन्तु सुस्थिताः। नित्यं स्यात्संघसामग्री संघकार्यं च सिध्यतु॥

examples.dm: May temples be well-established, Adorned with study and recitation. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the purposes of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
examples.gm: May monasteries, with reading and Recitation, remain well adorned. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the goals of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
examples.sa: पाठस्वाध्यायकलिला विहाराः सन्तु सुस्थिताः। नित्यं स्यात्संघसामग्री संघकार्यं च सिध्यतु॥

examples.dm: May temples be well-established, Adorned with study and recitation. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the purposes of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
examples.gm: May monasteries, with reading and Recitation, remain well adorned. May the Saṅgha always be in harmony, And may the goals of the Saṅgha be accomplished.
examples.sa: पाठस्वाध्यायकलिला विहाराः सन्तु सुस्थिताः। नित्यं स्यात्संघसामग्री संघकार्यं च सिध्यतु॥

examples.dm: May the nuns be endowed with requisites, And may they abandon quarreling and harm. Likewise, may all those who have gone forth Never let their ethical discipline decline.
examples.gm: May nuns be endowed with provisions, And may they abandon quarrels and harm. Likewise, may all who are ordained Remain with unblemished discipline.
examples.sa: लाभिन्यः सन्तु भिक्षुण्यः कलहायासवर्जिताः। भवन्त्वखण्डशीलाश्च सर्वे प्रव्रजितास्तथा॥

examples.dm: May the wise be honored, And may they also receive alms. May their mental continuums be completely purified, And may they be renowned in all directions.
examples.gm: May the learned be honored And also receive alms. May their mindstreams be completely pure, And may they be renowned in all directions.
examples.sa: पण्डिताः संस्कृताः सन्तु लाभिनः पैण्डपातिकाः। भवन्तु शुद्धसंतानाः सर्वदिक्ख्यातकीर्तयः॥

examples.dm: May they not experience the suffering of the lower realms, And even without undergoing hardships, With bodies superior even to the gods, May they swiftly achieve Buddhahood.
examples.gm: Without experiencing the sufferings of the lower realms, And without engaging in hardships, With bodies superior to those of the gods, May they swiftly attain buddhahood.
examples.sa: अभुक्त्वापायिकं दुःखं विना दुष्करचर्यया। दिव्येनैकेन कायेन जगद्बुद्धत्वमाप्नुयात्॥

examples.dm: May the Bodhisattvas Fulfill their intentions to benefit wandering beings. Whatever the Protectors have intended, May that be attained by all sentient beings.
examples.gm: May the bodhisattvas Accomplish their intentions for the welfare of beings. Whatever the protectors intend, May that be accomplished for sentient beings.
examples.sa: सिध्यन्तु बोधिसत्त्वानां जगदर्थं मनोरथाः। यच्चिन्तयन्ति ते नाथास्तत्सत्त्वानां समृध्यतु॥

examples.dm: Likewise, may the Pratyekabuddhas And the Śrāvakas also be happy.
examples.gm: Likewise, may the pratyekabuddhas And the śrāvakas also be happy.
examples.sa: प्रत्येकबुद्धाः सुखिनो भवन्तु श्रावकास्तथा। देवासुरनरैर्नित्यं पूज्यमानाः सगौरवैः॥

examples.dm: Through the kindness of Mañjuśrī, Until I attain the Ground of Supreme Joy, May I always remember my past lives, And may I obtain the state of a renunciate.
examples.gm: And through the kindness of Mañjuśrī, Until I attain the ground of Perfect Joy, May I always remember my past lives And attain ordination.
examples.sa: जातिस्मरत्वं प्रव्रज्यामहं च प्राप्नुयां सदा। यावत्प्रमुदिताभूमिं मञ्जुघोषपरिग्रहात्॥

examples.dm: May I be sustained and live, Even on a diet of the simplest food. In all my lives, may I obtain Perfect circumstances for living in solitude.
examples.gm: May I, even with simple food, Live endowed with vitality. In all my lifetimes, May I attain the perfection of solitary places.
examples.sa: येन तेनासनेनाहं यापयेयं बलान्वितः। विवेकवाससामग्रीं प्राप्नुयां सर्वजातिषु॥

examples.dm: Whatever sufferings sentient beings have, May they all ripen upon me. Through the assembly of Bodhisattvas, May all beings enjoy happiness.
examples.gm: Whatever suffering there is for beings, May it all ripen upon me. Through the sangha of bodhisattvas, May beings experience happiness.
examples.sa: यत्किंचिज्जगतो दुःखं तत्सर्वं मयि पच्यताम्। बोधिसत्त्वशुभैः सर्वैर्जगत्सुखितमस्तु च॥

examples.dm: May the teaching—the sole medicine for the suffering of beings And the source of all happiness— Endure for a long time, Together with support and honor.
examples.gm: The sole medicine for the suffering of beings, The source of all happiness, May the teaching, along with gain and honor, Remain for a long time.
examples.sa: जगद्दुःखैकभैषज्यं सर्वसंपत्सुखाकरम्। लाभसत्कारसहितं चिरं तिष्ठतु शासनम्॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to Mañjughoṣa, Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises. I also prostrate to my spiritual friend, Through whose kindness I have flourished.
examples.gm: Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises, I prostrate to Mañjuśrī. Through whose kindness I have grown, I also prostrate to the spiritual friend.
examples.sa: मञ्जुघोषं नमस्यामि यत्प्रसादान्मतिः शुभे। कल्याणमित्रं वन्देऽहं यत्प्रसादाच्च वर्धते॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to Mañjughoṣa, Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises. I also prostrate to my spiritual friend, Through whose kindness I have flourished.
examples.gm: Through whose kindness a virtuous mind arises, I prostrate to Mañjuśrī. Through whose kindness I have grown, I also prostrate to the spiritual friend.
examples.sa: मञ्जुघोषं नमस्यामि यत्प्रसादान्मतिः शुभे। कल्याणमित्रं वन्देऽहं यत्प्रसादाच्च वर्धते॥

examples.dm: The *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*, composed by the master Śāntideva, is hereby completed.
examples.gm: Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, composed by the master Śāntideva, is complete.
examples.sa: ॥बोधिचर्यावतारे परिणामनापरिच्छेदो दशमः॥ ^10-a ॥समाप्तोऽयं बोधिचर्यावतारः। कृतिराचार्यशान्तिदेवस्य॥
